President Donald Trump has announced an agreement with Greenland, in which the U.S. will take permanent control of the Arctic island’s security.

“I am pleased to announce that the United States of America has entered into an Agreement with The Kingdom of Denmark, and Greenland, that gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland, completely addressing ALL of our many U.S. concerns,” Trump wrote on Truth Social Friday evening.

The president has eyed Greenland since before he returned to the White House in January 2025, arguing that the U.S. needed to control the semi-autonomous Danish territory for national security purposes.

Trump said that the agreement means the U.S. “will FOREVER have the complete ability to do what is necessary in Greenland in order to secure and defend the security of Greenland, and the United States of America.”

open image in gallery President Donald Trump has announced an agreement with Greenland, in which the U.S. will take permanent control of the Arctic island’s security ( Getty Images )

It’s unclear what exactly is in the agreement Trump claims to have struck with Denmark and Greenland, but he did highlight one major point — U.S. adversaries such as Russia and China will need his approval to work with Greenland militarily and economically.

“From now on, no U.S. adversary can EVER have a base in Greenland, have a military presence in Greenland, or make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval,” Trump said.

The president had warned Russia and China would take Greenland if he didn’t step in.

“It's so strategic. Right now, Greenland is covered with Russian and Chinese ships all over the place,” Trump claimed during a press gaggle aboard Air Force One in January. “We need Greenland from the standpoint of national security — and Denmark is not going to be able to do it.”

open image in gallery The president has eyed Greenland since before he returned to the White House in January 2025, arguing that the U.S. needed to control the semi-autonomous Danish territory for national security purposes ( Getty Images )

Trump boasted about his role in the new agreement with Greenland that he said would be “cherished by the American People.”

“For over 100 years, Presidents have known the strategic importance of Greenland, but NONE of them were able to do anything about it. I am proud to be the President that permanently and conclusively addressed this very important situation,” he wrote on Truth Social.

“We will immediately begin the process of developing a large Military presence in the appropriate part of Greenland, of which there are many. We will work with the people of Greenland in its development and construction,” he added.

Denmark’s prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, and the leader of Greenland’s government, Jens-Frederik Nielsen, released statements on Friday night saying that the agreement was expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly next week.

”It is encouraging that we are about to make an agreement that will ensure and strengthen the security of Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark, the United States, and the Western Alliance. The agreement recognizes Greenland’s interests and our place in the international cooperation. It is to the benefit of us all,” said Nielsen.

Frederiksen added: ”I am glad that we are about to make a great agreement for Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark, and the United States. An agreement which strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic Area and therefore is great for NATO and Europe as well. And an agreement which at the same time recognizes the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the Greenlandic people’s right to self-determination.”

Since Trump began pushing to acquire Greenland, he has been met with opposition, not just from the people of the Arctic island and Denmark, but also from America’s European allies.

“Greenland belongs to its people. It is for Denmark and Greenland, and them only, to decide on matters concerning Denmark and Greenland,” a joint statement from seven European leaders read.

open image in gallery As part of the agreement, Trump said U.S. adversaries such as Russia and China will need his approval to work with Greenland militarily and economically ( AFP via Getty Images )

In the January 6 statement, leaders from France, Germany, the United Kingdom and other U.S. allies said, “We and many other Allies have increased our presence, activities and investments, to keep the Arctic safe and to deter adversaries.”

They said that since Denmark is a part of NATO, “security in the Arctic must therefore be achieved collectively...by upholding the principles of the UN Charter, including sovereignty, territorial integrity and the inviolability of borders.”

Days later, Trump threatened to impose a 10 percent tariff on imports from European allies, several of which were part of the earlier joint statement, “until such time as a Deal is reached for the Complete and Total purchase of Greenland.”

Trump quickly backed down from his tariff threats, claiming to have “formed the framework of a future deal with respect to Greenland” with NATO chief Mark Rutte.

open image in gallery Fifty-eight percent of Americans opposed a U.S. takeover of Greenland in a January poll, when tensions between America and Europe were at a high over the issue ( Getty Images )

Even with the new agreement between government officials, it is doubtful that Trump will sway those in Greenland opposed to American intervention.

The day Trump threatened tariffs against European nations if he did not strike a deal to acquire Greenland, protesters in Nuuk held Greenlandic flags and a banner that read “Make America Go Away” and “We Are Not Property!”

“I think he should mind his own business,” Greenlander Lars Vintner, a heating engineer, told the Associated Press in January.

“What’s he going to do with Greenland? He speaks of Russians and Chinese and everything in Greenlandic waters or in our country,” he said. “Every summer we go sailing and we go hunting and I never saw Russian or Chinese ships here in Greenland.”

A majority of Americans are also not sold on the idea of gaining control of Greenland.

Fifty-eight percent of Americans oppose a U.S. takeover of the Arctic island while 21 percent favor it and 20 percent are unsure, according to a Pew Research Center poll from January.

President Donald Trump on Friday claimed to have “banned” three of the country’s most prominent news outlets from the White House, taking a page from authoritarian leaders by attempting to limit coverage of his administration by legitimate journalists as his and his party’s popularity continue to crumble as the midterm elections approach.

Writing on Truth Social, the president said he would “effective immediately” be “banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW ... and Politico ... from the White House as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS.”

“Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America. Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow,” he added.

All of the outlets mentioned by the president are legitimate and reputable news organizations with long histories of aggressive and independent reporting under both Republican and Democratic administrations.

It’s unclear what, if anything, specifically led to the president’s outburst, but Trump has had a years-long feud with CNN dating back to his first campaign for the presidency and his first term in the White House. And in an unrelated Oval Office press availability, he doubled down shortly after.

open image in gallery US President Donald J. Trump makes an announcement on healthcare in the Oval Office ( Reuters )

The president launched into a lengthy rant in the Oval Office in which he repeated a bogus claim that Politico had received a subsidy from the Biden administration — actually subscription revenues from government agencies — and suggested that other outlets could also face similar fates if they do not write positive stories about his administration.

“Something is wrong with a country that can allow people to write purposely negative stories,” the president said. “If they want to write them, that’s fine. I don’t have to let them into the people’s house.

“They purposely write negative news, and they do that because want to try and diminish the Republicans and a Republican administration,” he continued. “And honestly, we've done a fantastic job.

“Look at the numbers. Look at the economic numbers. We have more money coming into our country today than ever before, we have the highest employment that we've ever had in history ... we have the best poverty rate, the lowest poverty rate in the history of our country, and people are making more money today than they ever had.”

The president does not actually possess the authority to arbitrarily ban entire outlets from the White House based on the content those outlets publish.

Not only does the First Amendment to the U.S. Constitution protect the right of journalists to report without government interference, but a 1977 District of Columbia Circuit Court case, Sherill v. Knight, states that “bona fide journalists” cannot be denied access to White House press facilities except in cases when a journalist seeking a press credential to enter the White House “presents a potential source of physical danger to the President and/or his immediate family so serious as to justify his exclusion.”

That decades-old precedent was upheld during Trump’s first term after he attempted to revoke the credentials of CNN’s then-chief White House correspondent, Jim Acosta, and later a columnist for Playboy, Brian Karem, for behavior the White House considered to be inappropriate.

In both cases, the DC Circuit Court upheld lower court orders directing the White House to restore both journalists’ White House press passes.

open image in gallery Trump takes questions from reporters Friday after saying he will ban certain media outlets that do not flatter him from having access to the White House in the future ( Reuters )

“If President Trump means to expel these news organizations from the White House press pool, his action is doubly unconstitutional because the press pool is a ‘public forum’ under the First Amendment, which means the president can’t exclude journalists from it on the basis of their viewpoints,” Jameel Jaffer, the executive director of the Knight First Amendment Institute at Columbia University, told the New York Times.

Trump has nonetheless pushed to punish news outlets by restricting their access to the White House during his second term.

Last year, his administration seized control of the press pool that had for decades been organized by the White House Correspondents’ Association in order to punish the Associated Press for refusing to change its’ widely used style guide to reflect his administration’s attempt to rename the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America.”

His handpicked Pentagon boss, ex-Fox News presenter turned Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, has instituted sweeping restrictions on the Pentagon’s own press corps that led nearly every legitimate media outlet covering the Defense Department to turn in their credentials.

It is not clear whether anyone from the White House has attempted to enforce the president’s purported “ban” on CNN, MSNOW and Politico.

As of Friday afternoon, CNN’s press workspace was fully staffed and multiple camera and sound technicians from the network were present on the White House campus.

“CNN stands fully behind our White House team and their fair and accurate reporting. We have a right under the U.S. Constitution to do that reporting without hindrance or interference from the government,” the network said in a statement.

“Should the ban which President Trump threatened go ahead, it would be an illegal assault on that fundamental and constitutionally-protected right.”

CNN star Jake Tapper took to X on Friday evening and slammed Trump for the ban attempt.

“Less than an hour after @KristenhCNN did this report about the WH announcement of lower drug prices, President Trump complained CNN would never cover such a thing and banned us from the White House. In addition to being unconstitutional, it’s so ill-informed,” he wrote.”

In a statement, Politico said it “will continue to fairly report on this White House and future ones. We will vigorously defend our First Amendment rights against any attempt to restrict them. The claims that POLITICO received government subsidies are false and have been thoroughly debunked."

Asked how he could justify attempting to ban news outlets when he has taken an oath to uphold the U.S. Constitution, Trump replied: “Because they're fake news, and you get so tired of reading and seeing fake news.”

Very little of what the president said was actually accurate. For one, the highest-ever recorded U.S. employment rate was 64.7 percent, 26 years ago in April 2000.

Asked about his prior attempts to ban individual reporters, Trump suggested a different judge would have been more amenable to his authoritarian push to restrict a free press.

“To be honest with you, I don't think that a court should allow fake news to be written day after day after day, I think that somebody has a right to keep them away if they're going to write false stories all the time,” he said.

He continued complaining that the coverage of his administration by legitimate news organizations is not fawning in the manner practiced by Breitbart News and other partisan outlets.

When a reporter attempted to ask Sanders — who was actually in the Oval Office for the event in her new role as Governor of Arkansas — whether she agreed with Trump’s push to ban entire news organizations, he interjected and repeated himself.

“I don't think somebody should be allowed to come in and write fake stories, fake news, and that's why they have no credibility,” he said.

“They never write a good story ... it's sick. I mean, there's something wrong with a country that can allow people to write purposely negative stories. Now, if they want to write them, that's fine. But I don't have to let them into my — into the people's house.”

He also complained that two of the nation’s largest papers — The New York Times and The Washington Post — were “fake” and “disgusting,” but he did not indicate that he would attempt to bar their reporters from the White House.

Bruce Brown, president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, said in a statement: “A ban like this would be flatly unconstitutional. The First Amendment is clear that once the White House invites in some journalists, it can’t ban others because it doesn’t like their reporting.”

Jacqui Heinrich, president of the White House Correspondents Association, also addressed the ban.

“The president said it plainly in the Oval Office, describing his own planned action as a “ban on the free press.” The Constitution protects the freedom of the press from government interference. That protection does not depend on whether the president likes a news organization’s coverage, agrees with its reporting, or approves of the questions its journalists ask.

“This is about more than the rights of journalists. It is about the right of the American people to receive a full and independent account of the activities, policies and decisions of whoever occupies the nation’s highest office. The WHCA stands in defense of our colleagues at CNN, MSNOW, and Politico who are being singled out for doing their jobs.”

The late Queen reacted “tetchily” to the news that Princess Diana had been in a car crash before she knew of its severity, Earl Spencer has claimed.

In his most recent extract from his memoir on Friday, Diana’s brother said: “When the Queen had heard the first news of Diana being in a traffic accident, she had asked tetchily, ‘What is she up to now?’ This, before the seriousness of it all became clear.”

The Earl has insisted he is being truthful about his claims, following backlash from Buckingham Palace, which said that the King is mindful that “grief can cloud reason”.

In an earlier excerpt, he also claimed that the Queen considered restoring his sister’s Her Royal Highness title, which she lost when she divorced Charles.

It’s the latest in a string of bombshell allegations made against the royal family and King Charles.

The Earl told the BBC on Friday that he was “telling the truth” after claiming that Charles had said his sister would be forgotten “soon enough” on the phone with him in the days after Diana’s death.

“I can tell you here and now, those are exactly the words he said.”

News.title: Investigation launched after beheaded sea lion is found along San Francisco shore
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

Police are investigating after a sea lion was found beheaded on San Francisco’s Ocean Beach, according to local reports.

Wildlife experts believe the animal was decapitated after it had already died.

"Maybe the person who did this didn't know that it was illegal, or maybe they did," Sue Pemberton of the California Academy of Sciences told ABC 7 San Francisco.

She said that sometimes the “legality of it doesn’t really stop people.”

“I don't really know what this person was thinking, but people might collect them for the novelty of having a trophy of some sort," she said.

A sea lion in San Francisco was found decapitated. Local officials determined the animal's head was removed after it had already died, but warned the public that interfering with the carcasses of dead marine mammals is a federal crime ( Getty )

It's not the first time something like this has happened. Another sea lion was found without its head further down the coast on a beach in Pacific Grove last year, according to SFist.

The individual involved in that incident reportedly tried to carry the head away in a Ziploc bag.

Officials said that interfering with the carcasses of marine mammals is a federal offense carrying serious penalties.

Under the Marine Mammal Protection Act, taking parts from a sea lion carcass is illegal and can be punished with up to $36,000 in fines and a year in prison.

Beachgoers who encounter a dead or stranded marine mammal are urged to leave it alone and report the sighting to local wildlife officials or the Marine Mammal Stranding Network.

The White House has tried to take credit for Wendy’s switching back to a classic look, but social media users aren’t buying it.

Wendy’s announced this week that it was kicking it old school with its iconic yellow packaging, tapping into a wave of 90s nostalgia as millennials and Gen Z seek childhood comforts.

When the fast-food joint first opened in Columbus, Ohio, in 1969, it used yellow cups and boxes to serve nuggets, fries and its signature Frostys. Over time, Wendy’s got rid of the yellow packaging for its now-familiar red and white boxes and cups.

Now, the yellow packaging is back at Wendy’s for a limited time, and if you ask the White House, it’s all thanks to President Donald Trump, a known lover of rival fast-food joint McDonald's.

In response to an X post about Wendy’s yellow packaging comeback, the White House account wrote on Thursday, “Thank you, President Trump!!!!!”

open image in gallery The White House has tried to take credit for Wendy’s switching back to its classic yellow packaging, but social media users aren’t buying it ( Wendy's )

But people in the comment section either couldn’t see how Trump could have a hand in the decision or mocked him for claiming a fast-food refresh as one of his accomplishments.

“Trump has nothing to do with that. What are you smoking? You should say ‘Thank you, [Wendy’s founder] Dave [Thomas]’ and thank the customers who demanded it back,” one X user said.

Another wrote: “The level of delusion actually scares me.”

“Imagine having so few actual wins that you have to fabricate fake ones about fast food,” a third posted.

Wendy’s, meanwhile, said the reason for the switch-up was that its customers have been begging for it.

open image in gallery In response to Wendy’s yellow packaging comeback, the White House publicly thanked President Donald Trump, a known lover of rival fast-food joint McDonald's ( Getty Images )

“Fans have been asking for its return for years, making it one of the most requested comebacks in Wendy’s history,” a company spokesperson told TODAY.com. “Yellow has been part of Wendy’s since the very beginning and is something many fans instantly recognize.”

The yellow packaging will return on September 28 and continue into 2027, Wendy’s told USA TODAY.

When asked by The Independent to clarify what it meant by its comment thanking Trump for the yellow packaging revival, the White House just said: “America is back!”

People on X also took issue with White House’s post, given that Americans are struggling to afford basic necessities, with even something once considered cheap, like fast food, hitting their wallets hard.

The cost of food was up 2.7 percent in August from the year before, according to the federal government’s Consumer Price Index. The cost of energy has skyrocketed during Trump’s Iran war, rising 16.3 percent in August from the previous year.

“Nobody can afford it, but thank you President Trump!” one person wrote.

Another said: “Anything on gas, grocery, rent or electricity prices there President Trump?”

“Hey we want affordable gas and groceries, not iconic fast food,” one person wrote.

Wendy’s move to bring back its nostalgic yellow packaging came after one of its largest franchise operators filed for bankruptcy.

Meritage Hospitality Group Inc., a major restaurant operator based in Grand Rapids, Michigan, that runs more than 300 Wendy’s restaurants, announced the decision Thursday.

“The filing follows a candid assessment of the financial pressures facing the Company, including the sustained system-wide headwinds affecting the broader Wendy’s brand over the past few years,” the company wrote in a news release. “The Company has a high level of confidence in the opportunity for a brand turnaround.”

The government has been urged to commit £6bn at the upcoming Budget to tackle unaffordable UK rents faced by millions across the UK.

More than 1.1 million low-income tenants are facing a “cost of housing crunch”, according to a new report from the Resolution Foundation, as the gap between rental costs and housing benefits continues to hit record highs.

The influential think tank is calling on Andy Burnham and new chancellor John Healey to use next month’s Budget to intervene by relinking the benefit rates to local market prices.

The formula used to calculate housing benefit levels – the Local Housing Allowance (LHA) – has been frozen since April 2024. The mechanism is designed to ensure benefit levels are in line with at least the lowest 30 per cent of rents in any local area.

But market rents have continued to surge, the shortfall between LHA rates and the affordable rents is set to hit a record 23.3 per cent in October, the Resolution report warns. This means a shortfall of around £200 a month for renters in London, and £100 a month for the rest of the UK.

open image in gallery Over 1.1 million low-income tenants are facing a “cost of housing crunch” according to a new report from the Resolution Foundation ( Getty/iStock )

If left unchecked, this gap could rise to 30 per cent by early 2028, researchers forecast, increasing the London shortfall to £260 a month and the UK-wide figure to £130.

Recent research from Citizens Advice and Crisis found that less than 2 per cent of properties in the UK are now considered affordable for renters on housing benefits.

Official findings show that renters are increasingly being forced to forgo the essentials to meet costs, with over half (58 per cent) of working-age adults in private tenancies on housing support in material deprivation in 2024/25. One in five were unable to keep their homes warm, and one in eight unable to afford three meals a day.

Addressing criticism that unfreezing the LHA would prompt landlords to hike rents, Resolution analysed the April 2024 relinking, finding that just 10p of every additional pound in support resulted in higher rents at the bottom of the market.

This increase also resulted in an immediate reduction of over 150,000 Universal Credit households struggling with a rental shortfall.

open image in gallery John Healey will deliver his first Budget as chancellor in October ( Getty )

Stephen Hunsaker, economist at the Resolution Foundation, said: “The gap between average rents and Local Housing Allowance levels is set to reach a record high this October, and failing to repeg LHA to actual rents in next month’s Budget could lock in a freeze for another year, and see the gap reach 30 per cent by March 2028.

“Rather than primarily benefitting landlords, our new analysis shows that the last time LHA was repegged to local rents in April 2024 it was tenants that benefited, with the fraction of LHA recipients facing a shortfall between their rents and the amount they could claim dropping significantly.

“With many tenants receiving housing support already going without essentials to pay their rent today, the Government should restore the automatic annual linking of LHA to relieve the pressure on low-income families in the private rented sector.”

The think tank has urged the government to spend £2bn annually to relink LHA to local market rents and restore the automatic annual adjustments. This would cost £6bn to 2029/30.

It echoes calls made by many housing campaigners, who argue that the policy continues to put pressure on renters and place them at risk of homelessness.

Mairi MacRae, director of policy and campaigns at Shelter, said: “Caught between an escalating cost-of-living crisis and skyrocketing private rents, families should be able to rely on housing benefit as a safety net to help cover costs. Yet with the freeze on housing allowance, thousands are left desperately grappling to plug the gap between their income and rent.

“Families are being forced to make impossible choices daily between feeding their family or paying their rent. Tens of thousands are stuck homeless in grim temporary accommodation for months or even years on end because there's nowhere affordable for them to move to.”

The Independent has contacted the government for comment.

News.title: GPs summoned in Frankfurt as third malaria death reported
News.content:
While malaria is treatable if caught early, the patients were likely not considered to have the disease because they lacked travel history to countries where malaria typically circulates, meaning treatment was delayed.

“This is why we alerted the medical people in Frankfurt, if you have odd cases presenting at your clinic, please also consider that there might be malaria around,” Dr Tinnemann said.

“There is this assumption that people who get sick with a nasty fever in places like Frankfurt and elsewhere that have not travelled cannot have malaria, and we don’t bother to investigate. That’s got to stop. That’s why these people die,” Joe Lines, Professor of Malaria Control and Vector Biology at the London School of Tropical Hygiene and Medicine, told The Telegraph.

Before the two cases in Schwanheim – both of which occurred at least 3 miles from the airport where the first malaria cases were reported – investigators were working on the hypothesis that just a single mosquito was responsible for the outbreak, but the new cases have cast doubt on that theory.

“We expect mosquitoes to live between one and three weeks on average,” said Dr Tinnemann.

“We had five cases in the beginning of July, then another in August - at that point, there was a good chance that potentially it could just be one bug. But now it seems at least there must be one other,” he said.

Frankfurt’s public health board have now shipped blood samples from all eight patients to a specialised lab in Antwerp, Belgium, where scientists can carry out DNA analysis to indicate if the infections came from one or multiple mosquitoes, and are awaiting results.

As temperatures warm, experts fear that several tropical mosquito-borne diseases – including malaria, dengue fever, Zika virus, and chikungunya could become established across Europe.

Earlier this month, a colony of Aedes aeypti mosquitoes – the bugs responsible for transmitting dengue and Zika virus – were found breeding in a residential area in East London for the first time.

Airfinity, the disease-monitoring company, said of the malaria outbreak in Frankfurt: “the risk to the wider public remains low but non-zero.”

“Continued vector surveillance, rapid diagnosis, and ready access to antimalarials are critical to prevent further severe outcomes.”

News.title: Global fund utilises AI to tackle malaria, TB, and HIV amid aid cuts
News.content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is helping to soften the blow from aid cuts, according to one of the world’s biggest development funds.

The Global Fund, which raises and invests billions of pounds to reduce the burden of HIV, tuberculosis (TB) and malaria globally says new AI-driven products like portable pregnancy scanners are helping to mitigate the funding gap.

“[We] have adapted pretty quickly to the changes in the funding environment; it has undoubtedly had negative impacts on health outcomes [...], but in some ways, the resilience of life-saving services has been remarkable,” Peter Sands, the executive director of the Global Fund, told The Telegraph.

The Global Fund is managing a $6 billion (£4.4bn) shortfall for the period 2026 to 2028 and has been forced to make difficult decisions to continue their work, it confirmed this week.

The gap comes as Western governments shift money from foreign aid to defence. The UK reduced its contribution to the fund by 15 per cent last year to £850 million, down from £1 billion.

But Mr Sands said investments in tools to tackle infectious diseases – including those driven by AI – are starting to pay off.

“Innovation is absolutely part of the answer when money is short. One of the few ways you can get to make the money go further is to have a better tool, a better way of doing things,” Mr Sands said.

News.title: Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players
News.content:
Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

News.title: Fiji declares national crisis as HIV epidemic escalates
News.content:
“The rollout has been slow and frustrating, and Fiji will pay for it in terms of lives lost,” said Prof Lisa Maher, an epidemiologist at the Kirby Institute in Sydney who is supporting Fiji’s response. “This is the only thing that will turn the epidemic around and stop people dying, and stop onward transmission of HIV to the general population.”

But the emergency declaration should provide political cover to introduce the needle and syringe programme, with a Cabinet subcommittee now created to remove barriers to action.

“The government is signalling that it is prepared to act in this particularly important and controversial area,” said Prof Maher. “It’s not coincidental that the draft bill [to legalise the distribution of needles and syringes for certain groups] now looks likely to go before parliament, after being blocked for 10 months… So it’s not just symbolic.”

Dr Jason Mitchell, head of Fiji’s HIV taskforce, added: “Since the government announced [the crisis], it has followed with some very rapid actions in progressing the needle and syringe programme. So that is being fast tracked through the necessary channels, and the government is determined to get that out in the next couple of weeks.

“We’ve gotten to the point where we really needed to take some really strong action,” he told The Telegraph. “This is the government realising that there have been challenges, and they need to step it up.”

It is hoped that the declaration will also turbocharge other elements of the response – for instance the scale-up of the post-exposure prophylaxis (Prep) scheme, which was introduced in May – as the virus gains a foothold in the broader population.

Although there has been a major focus on testing, treatment and education, UNAIDS still estimates that only 39 per cent of an estimated 9,100 people living with HIV in 2025 knew their positive status. Just 22 per cent were accessing antiretroviral treatment, and 117 people died in 2025, compared to 25 in 2021.

News.title: Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing
News.content:
There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

News.title: Banton shows his worth as England cruise to series victory against Sri Lanka
News.content:
A patchy Test team and a one-day international side learning on the job should not obscure the fact that under Harry Brook, England have built a formidable T20 outfit.

Missing a slew of first-choice players, they dispatched Sri Lanka with a game to spare and an emphatic show of their depth in the format, with Sonny Baker and Tom Banton – two men still finding their feet in the side – to the fore. England have now won 20 of the 23 completed T20s since Brook took over last year, and six matches in a row this summer. It is easily their best format and, as Liam Dawson said, they have “match-winners throughout” and plenty of “freak” performers.

In this six-wicket win, Baker’s one for 15 limited England’s target to a paltry 146, which Banton, a natural opener who is being recommissioned in the middle order, helped knock off with 47 balls remaining. “Tonight was a special performance, very clinical,” said Brook.

News.title: Interest rate increase ‘likely’, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Andrew Bailey has said that interest rates are likely to rise if the Middle East war rages on, warning inflation is now on course to hit 4pc.

The Bank of England opted to hold borrowing costs at 3.75pc on Thursday, the sixth time in a row it has left them unchanged.

However, the Governor said a “material” increase in energy prices since July would push up inflation to twice the Bank’s 2pc target.

He warned the outlook for inflation “continues to be on the upside” and criticised the “seeming loss of urgency to find solutions” to the war in Iran.

Oil prices are back above $100 a barrel and analysts expect average gas and electricity bills to rise above £2,000 this winter as the conflict continues.

Mr Bailey said: “So far, higher global energy costs have had a limited effect on price and wage setting in the UK.

“But the longer this volatility persists, the bigger the impact it will have on inflation, and the more likely it is we will need to raise Bank Rate to ensure that inflation falls back to our 2pc target.”

Investors expect the Bank to raise interest rates as soon as November, which has pushed average mortgage rates to their highest level in three years.

The average five-year fixed mortgage deal has risen to 5.87pc, according to Moneyfacts, which is the highest level since November 2023 and up from 4.95pc before the Iran war.

Thursday’s rate hold leaves the Bank out of step with central banks around the world after the US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank voted to raise borrowing costs this month.

However, economists said there had been a change in tone from policymakers over the threat posed by energy prices and whether this would feed into the wider economy.

The Bank of England predicted that inflation would hit 4pc early next year, just as most workers are negotiating pay rises.

Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said: “It seems as though a majority of the MPC is on the cusp of wanting to tighten policy.”

In a warning on the impending pain facing households, Mr Bailey told the Chancellor that energy bills would rise by 24pc early next year under the Ofgem price cap.

This will push up annual average bills by £413 to £2,136, which the Governor blamed on the war in the Middle East.

The Governor is required to write a formal letter to the Chancellor every time inflation is more than a percentage point above its 2pc target.

Official data showed inflation rose to 3.1pc in August.

Mr Bailey said: “The energy price shock has been the most important factor driving recent short-term movements in inflation.”

Despite expectations of higher rates, the FTSE 100 rose on Thursday at its steepest pace since July, climbing more than 1pc, as the Bank of England eased the pressure on the UK bond market.

Policymakers also confirmed a Telegraph report that the Bank will stop selling the long-dated bonds it amassed during the financial crisis and lockdown.

The Bank will continue actively selling £20bn of government bonds per year until the rest of the stockpile is wound down to zero in 2034.

The announcement triggered a sharp fall in the cost of borrowing for the Treasury, with the yield on 30-year UK gilts falling at the fastest pace since May.

News.title: Next-generation antivenom fights India’s deadliest snakes
News.content:
The process to make antivenom has barely changed in a century: snakes are milked, their venom is injected into horses, and their antibodies are harvested to form the basis of the product. The resulting treatments are difficult to administer, can trigger severe side effects, and the quality varies from batch to batch.

“The big four snakes contribute to 70 per cent of poisonous bites [in India]… so 30 per cent of poisonous snakes are not covered, even to begin with,” said Dr Yogesh Jain, a public health physician in Chhattisgarh state and a member of The Global Snakebite Taskforce.

“But there are huge quality and efficacy issues even against these 70 per cent of bites. We’re relying on a 100-year-old technique of getting antivenoms, and at least 50,000 people are dying every year,” he told The Telegraph.

“There’s a real need for new technology. We don’t have a safe and appropriate antivenom for the largest majority of people in rural India.”

Now, scientists are hopeful that they have developed a potential alternative.

In the latest study, published last week, researchers showed that an experimental antivenom cocktail with five components protected mice against lethal doses of antivenom in Indian cobras, even when delayed by up to 20 minutes – a scenario that mimics the real-world lag between a bite and treatment.

“If you go 10 years back, people didn’t think you could make sufficiently simple products with new, modern biotechnology that could cover all these different snake venoms,” said Prof Andreas Laustsen-Kiel, head of the Section of Biologics Engineering at the Technical University of Denmark and co-author of the paper.

“People simply believed it was too complex, too expensive to manufacture, and so on… But the data we are gathering is convincing enough to say this is something that could make a huge dent in the lost lives and limbs snakebite causes every year.”

The antivenom itself was based on lab-made nanobodies – antibodies derived from a group of animals including camels, llamas and some species of shark. Scientists believe their structure means they could be a more potent, more precise, more temperature-stable alternative to man-made monoclonal antibodies – and cheaper to manufacture.

“The latest study builds on an earlier discovery of nanobodies that can protect across a broad spectrum of African snakes,” said Prof Nicholas Casewell, director of the Centre for Snakebite Research and Interventions at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, who has previously collaborated with Prof Laustsen-Kiel.

“In this paper they have iterated and demonstrated that a narrow number of nanobodies can protect against Indian cobras and king cobras. This demonstration brings the nanobody technology closer to market,” he added.

But that is likely still years away, depending on how much funding the researchers can attract. The next steps – a larger animal study, scaling up manufacture, and launching human trials – are expensive.

“If money was no issue, we could probably be testing in humans in 1.5 to three years from now,” said Prof Laustsen-Kiel. “But since money is a big issue, it is more likely that human trials won’t be able to start until 2.5 to four years from now.

“But I really think that this [study shows] there’s no doubt that biotech can deliver better antivenoms. The question is whether people are willing to fund it,” he said.

Sports.title: Steve Lomas feared for his own safety after crossing Millwall-West Ham divide – but has no regrets over time as boss
Sports.content:
Next

STEVE LOMAS has no regrets about managing Millwall but admits he should never have set foot in the place.

Brave Lomas, 52, breached one of football’s most ferocious divides when he managed Millwall after spending eight years across the River Thames at despised West Ham.



Fans of both clubs burn with an overzealous mutual dislike that has spilled over into crowd trouble. The relatively few matches between the local rivals have been overshadowed by large-scale disorder.

West Ham’s relegation from the Premier League last season means they must visit The Den on Saturday for a game that will have the Metropolitan Police on high alert.



It’s an anxious enough day out for the 1,700 Hammers supporters who will make the trip to “bandit country” in south London.

Try doing it on a daily basis when you’re considered one of the enemy and you’re up against it trying to turn a club around in the face of fierce animosity.

Lomas told SunSport: “From my point of view looking back, the timing wasn’t great. Even forgetting about the West Ham issue, which was a problem.

“In hindsight, I should really have left it. Not from the point of view of it being Millwall, but from a football point of view. The squad wasn’t good enough.

“We were signing free transfers and people that other clubs didn’t want. I should have ducked it. We had too many people over 30 on decent money. We were just stale and were on our way down.

“They just about stayed up the season before I went there. The squad was aging and needed freshening up, but there just wasn’t any money.

“That year Bournemouth signed Callum Wilson for a £2.6million fee. I had about £1.8m of wages to try to turn our squad around. No money to actually buy anyone.

“There were about 18 boys already signed and about 13 of them were out of contract in my first year. I didn’t want half of them but needed them to try to keep us up.”

Four defeats in the opening six league games will pile the pressure on any new manager. But Lomas’ eight years as midfielder and captain of hated foes West Ham turned the screw quicker and tighter.

The Northern Irishman said: “It was very difficult. We had people down at the training ground. There was abuse.

“After one game we had somebody sent off after about ten minutes. It was against Derby and we got beaten 4-1 and the fans were waiting for me outside.



“But I learned more about myself as a person and a manager in those six months than I did at St Johnstone when we were flying and doing well. I learned about crisis management.

“After six games we had two points then we won four on the bounce. I nearly won manager of the month. That’s how mad it was.

“At times I worried about my safety. There’s a nasty element down there but I have never been one to be bullied. It was hairy a couple of times. I was told I had to stay behind in the ground after one game.

“Even when the crowd was dispersed there were still a few boys hanging around. But there are a lot of good Millwall people too.

“I had hundreds of letters from people telling me I must be mad to take the job because the squad was awful. That it wasn’t the DNA of a Millwall squad.”



Lomas and fearless Hammers legend Billy Bonds braved the chasm between West Ham and Millwall as managers.

The bitterness between the two sets of fans triggered a full-blown riot at West Ham’s old Upton Park ground in 2009 with one Millwall fan stabbed in the chest.

West Ham were eventually fined £115,000 for failing to control their fans while their south London visitors were exonerated.

Lomas lasted less than half a season before being sacked but holds affection for both clubs and believes the two sets of supporters are more similar than many wish to admit.



He said: “The fans of both clubs want the players to leave everything on the pitch. From that point of view they are 100 per cent similar. They will give a lot if you give everything on the pitch. That is the common denominator.

“They love their clubs and will defend for what it’s worth. Some of the times it oversteps the mark at both clubs. Hopefully that is a bygone thing and the best team wins on the pitch.

“At the old ground you had to walk out into the car park and there was just a chicken wire fence separating you from the fans. You had to get out of the car park and turn left onto Green Street,

Sports.title: Daniel Farke’s brewing something special in Yorkshire as unbeaten Leeds dream big with £200m Elland Road stadium upgrade
Sports.content:
Next

THE GOOD old boys can feel it. The fans believe it. Daniel Farke wants to achieve it.

Something else other than tea is brewing in Yorkshire. And Crystal Palace could be the latest to get swept away by the Leeds storm.



The mood at Elland Road has changed. After years in the doldrums post the early highs of the 2000s, the club’s owners and supporters are Marching on Together.

Off the pitch changes are already underway. The iconic Norman Hunter Suite outside the visitors entrance of the famous old ground has been bulldozed. Diggers and cranes are at work on the first part of transforming England’s most atmospheric stadium.



The club could have their new main stand finished by 2028, increasing the capacity by almost 10,000 to 48,000. Then the Don Revie Stand is next on the list. Once completed, that will take the capacity beyond 53,000.

The £200m Elland Road project is the biggest public show of ambition yet from Leeds’ 49ers Enterprises owners.

But for any player stepping out on a matchday, it already feels like the whole of the city is in there. It has always been a cauldron of noise. But the level has been cranked up a notch.

Newcastle were the latest to be blown apart by Farke’s monsters and the bear pit crowd. Palace are the next ones to enter the LS11 Coliseum to fight for survival.

Gary McAllister was part of the last Leeds title-winning side in 1992. The Scot, speaking on behalf of Lottoland, said: “I always use the analogy that if Leeds were playing Real Madrid tomorrow night at Elland Road, the Leeds fans would think they could win. They’re that passionate. Which is a great thing to have.”

Who can blame them? Not since the days of David O’Leary’s young side reaching the Champions League semi final in 2001 have excitement levels been so high.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

After an unbeaten start, Leeds head into the weekend sitting third. More decisively, they would be sitting fifth going back 29 games.

With the team proving a match for anybody and the stadium work underway, the Leeds faithful are daring to dream big once again.

Boss Farke is too. He said: “Yes, exciting times, there’s no doubt about this. Exciting times ahead but in order to make sure that once we can move into the full new stadium and go back hopefully to some even bigger heights, a lot of hard work is needed.”

The German has felt both sides of the passionate Leeds crowd. Despite winning promotion, he felt the wrath after a sticky start to life in the Prem. But he says that was the pull factor when he took over in 2023.

He said: “It’s a joy and why I signed a contract for this club. I wanted to be in charge for these amazing supporters. It’s also sometimes demanding to lead a club with such passion and such a big history.



“Such big dreams come along with responsibility and pressure quite often, it’s demanding and costs lots of energy, because you don’t have to lead just a group of players, but also the staff, who are also more or less very often supporters who love this club.

“It’s a responsibility to lead the whole group, even the whole fan base. After years and nearly decades of suffering, I wanted to play my little part to help bring this club back closer to the good old times.

“It will take a while to re-reach the good old times, but it’s a joy right now at the moment. You walk through the city and see the pride and joy in the supporters’ eyes and how much it means to them. Football should be the best thing in life and this feels at the moment for, for many of our fans, really like a shining light.”



Former right-back Danny Mills speaks fondly when recalling the “excitement” of being part of O’Leary’s side.

And he is not surprised by the current crowd’s excitement as he claims there has always been a pressure on to get the club back to its Don Revie heyday in the 1960s and 70s.

Speaking via BestBettingBonuses.co.uk, he said: “For us, it was sensational. Everybody was young, hungry, had a point to prove and wanted to get better. That’s what we did. Ultimately, we fell short in the end – not by a long way, but we did fall short of winning something.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But the crowd at Elland Road have always wanted, insisted on, hard work and effort. It doesn’t really matter beyond that. Even when they dropped down to the Championship and League One, the attendances were still fantastic. Leeds is synonymous with the 60s and 70s, and then obviously late 80s into the early 90s when they won the title.

“Leeds have always thrived off that dirty Leeds mentality. High tempo, energy. The crowd bounce off that, that then bounces back to the players, and you get this snowball effect.”

Sports.title: Harry Kane makes history as he scores 100th Bundesliga goal in just NINETY-EIGHT games… 30 faster than anyone else

HARRY KANE made history as the fastest-ever player to register 100 Bundesliga goals to boost his Ballon d’Or hopes.

Kane, 33, has reached a raft of milestones throughout his glittering 17-year career, including becoming the record goalscorer for England and Tottenham.



And now the star striker has cemented his legacy as a Bayern Munich and Bundesliga legend with his 100th goal in Germany’s top flight following his brace in a 7-0 thumping of Union Berlin.

The England captain became a centurion in just NINETY-EIGHT league appearances with Bayern.



That smashed Cologne legend Dieter Muller’s near 50-year record, after the Germany great set the previous landmark in 129 Bundesliga matches.

The forward celebrated his historic achievement on social media but gave immense credit to his team-mates, coaching staff and fans.



Kane tweeted: “Brilliant team performance and the perfect result before internationals.

“Personally very proud to get to 100 Bundesliga goals in record time – never possible without all the support from team-mates and staff and the fans.”

Kane has found the net once every 78.5 minutes in the league since his move to the Allianz Arena in 2023.

That’s a better record than Erling Haaland, Robert Lewandowski and Gerd Muller, who netted every 87, 100 and 105 minutes respectively.

Kane now boasts a staggering six goals and one assist in seven appearances across all competitions this term.

That adds to his whopping total of 152 goals and 34 assists in 154 appearances for Bayern.

That could increase the centre-forward’s odds of winning his first ever Ballon d’Or award.

Kane is among the favourites after leading the Bavarians to a domestic double last season and England to third place in the 2026 World Cup — their best finish since winning it in 1966.

However, the Londoner faces stiff competition from Barcelona duo Lamine Yamal and Rodri, who led Spain to World Cup glory.



But Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe and Paris Saint-Germain pair Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Ousmane Dembele also stand a good chance.

Meanwhile, Inter Miami star Lionel Messi is eyeing his ninth Ballon d’Or after taking Argentina to the World Cup final.

BRILLIANT Brentford sent Jordan Henderson and the rest of Chelsea’s Dad’s Army back home across west London with their tails between their legs.

Blues boss Xabi Alonso gave Henderson his debut against his former club alongside fellow thirty-somethings Danny Welbeck and Emi Martinez.



But the oldest Chelsea Premier League starting 11 since May 2023 produced the worst performance of the Alonso era so far.

Henderson, 36, was at fault for the decisive second goal, much to the delight of the home crowd, who chanted “Jordan, Jordan, what’s the score?”



And substitute Fabio Carvalho wrapped things up in stoppage time.

Age is just a number, and the statistics that matter are not great so far for the new Chelsea manager.



Jaidon Anthony’s first goal for Brentford, a second-half header, and Igor Thiago’s first strike of the season mean Alonso’s team have lost two and drawn one of his first five Premier League games in charge.

Changes in formation and personnel blunted Chelsea’s previously potent attack and could not prevent them succumbing to a setpiece, a weakness familiar from last season.

The Blues missed the injured Joao Pedro but Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, his partners in the tricky trio, were disappointing.

And Alonso’s team kept up the unwanted record of conceding at least twice in every league game.

With Pep Chavarria, 28, also making his first league start, Chelsea’s average age was 27 years 349 days – the best part of four years more per man than the 24 years 36 days figure from Alonso’s four previous matches.

Sports.title: 'Bullied' and 'out of control' - Chelsea's defensive issues laid bare
Sports.content:
"You need to feel it. We're not feeling it," said Xabi Alonso after Chelsea's 3-0 loss at Brentford. Yet Chelsea are stuck in a familiar feeling.

Another defeat, their 11th of the calendar year - more than they had in 2025, with three months of this year to go. At least two goals conceded for the fifth straight Premier League game under Alonso. More set-piece woe.

"We dropped our consistency, our competitive mentality needed in the second half," said Alonso. That will concern Chelsea fans the most. It was way too easy for Brentford to take over that second half.

And there's another continuing trend: Chelsea being outbattled in a match. Remember, they were outrun in the vast majority of their Premier League matches last season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Brentford and Chelsea.

The first thing you think about when you come up against Brentford is set pieces. Long throws, smart corners - the lot. And just like against Hull in their previous game, Chelsea lost control of the match by conceding once again from a set-piece.

This was the fourth goal they have conceded from a set-piece in five Premier League games - taking their overall tally since the start of last season to 23, the joint-worst out of any Premier League side.

Once again, the ball was put right on top of Emiliano Martinez towards the back post and neither the goalkeeper nor the outfield players were able to react. And the worst part of it for Chelsea? Brentford saw it coming a mile off.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jaidon Anthony heads Brentford in front against Chelsea.

"We did target [the back post] at half-time," said Vitaly Janelt to Sky Sports. "There was a big gap at the far post. We targeted that and I think it was our first corner of the second half."

And Chelsea are suffering from all these set-piece woes despite now having the best dead-ball coach in the league in Austin MacPhee. Bernardo Cueva, who was their set-piece coach before MacPhee and now has a different role at the club, was even pinched from Brentford by the Blues.

"We have not been good enough, at times we have been bullied and we need to improve at that," said Levi Colwill to Sky.

Image: Chelsea are struggling at the back

"But we trust in our set-piece coach; we are still adjusting to new things, but we do need to improve as a team."

It is not the only area where Chelsea need to improve defensively. The way they allow teams to penetrate their defensive third is among the worst in the division - they have gone 22 straight Premier League games without a clean sheet.

Image: Chelsea have been struggling all season at the back

On average, Chelsea concede 2.2 non-penalty goals per game. And they deserve to, because the xG numbers say they are expected to allow that same number of shots on target on their goal.

What doesn't help is a clear inability to protect the penalty area. Chelsea are also in the top three this season for conceding shots in their own penalty area on average, allowing around 10 per game. Their goalkeepers get used as a battering ram.

With defensive numbers like these, it's no wonder Chelsea have been unable to hold onto a lead in their last three league games.

They explode out of the blocks so quickly - this was the first Premier League game where they failed to take the lead in the opening 10 minutes of the game, but they nearly did when Pedro Neto had a good chance saved.

And then when Chelsea fall behind, they have been pegged back so many times that the bad habits kick in. "It's about everything. It's about the mentality, the football and the tactical things that we need to keep improving," said Alonso.

"We concede the first goal, you're still in the game but then we lose the shape. We were out of control."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch as Kevin Schade pushes Chelsea's Valentin Barco during Brentford's 3-0 win over Chelsea.

That control could be eased in the future when Moises Caicedo returns, but the lack of solidity they have without the Ecuadorian is a concern.

Two summer recruits in Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco started the Brentford game, but it was the Bees who looked stronger in midfield.

Keith Andrews' side arguably have the better squad depth in that area of the pitch as well - they won the match 3-0 with record signing Mamadou Sangare sat on the bench for over an hour.

Right now, Joao Pedro looks like Chelsea's most influential player from a goalscoring perspective. The 'JP Morgan' frontline was broken up for the first time this season - and Chelsea failed to score for the first time this season.

Of course, it was always going to take time for Alonso to implement his ideas at Stamford Bridge. This was a Chelsea team with seven summer signings in its starting line-up, with the Spaniard the fourth manager to take charge of the club in nine months.

"It doesn't happen overnight," former Chelsea captain Gary Cahill told Sky Sports. "I think with what you're saying he will be judged in the next five, six, seven weeks to get this right because you will have that time on the training ground and then we should start to see his methods coming through because we've seen him in an attacking sense."

"It's not just set-pieces," said Alonso on where Chelsea have to improve. "In defensive duels, build-up and controlling games." That being said, there aren't many more parts of the game besides those four.

"We've got a lot to work on over the international break," added Colwill. He can say that again.

Sports.title: How belief of Wakefield's inner sanctum led to history-making semi-final
Sports.content:
When Wakefield Trinity came back into Super League for the 2025 season, there wouldn't have been many who would have foreseen a semi-final appearance within two seasons- except those in their inner sanctum.

That inner sanctum, among others, consists of owner Matt Ellis, head of recruitment Ste Mills, and head coach Daryl Powell.

Working in tandem, they came up with a plan for how they would continually progress: they have signed raw talent, made them stars, provided a stadium that both home and away fans enjoy attending, and now brought the progressive and rapid success that their most faithful have been waiting so long to see.

An example of turning that raw talent into a shining diamond? Caleb Hamlin-Uele. Wakefield saw something in a player who was not breaking through in the NRL. They brought him into the Championship, moulded him, made him one of Super League's best props, and now he is truly in contention to represent England at the World Cup this autumn.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Emre Guler gets sent off for Wakefield Trinity against Leigh Leopards .

Of course, the biggest success of all would be a trophy. But for now, they are through to their first ever Super League semi-final after their 26-16 victory over Leigh in the Eliminators.

Wakefield's victory was down to their immense forward pack which took control early in the second half. Even with Emre Guler shown red on the hour mark for what appeared to be a punch, they had done enough to keep Leigh at arm's length and see the game home.

It is further reward for what has been a remarkable rise from Wakefield.

Image: The Wakefield Trinity faithful were delighted

Image: The full-time celebrations were a glimpse into what the moment means for Wakefield

"We are going to go where we are going to go. We are just going to prepare as best we can," Powell said.

"I think we can beat anybody.

"Wakefield have never won a play-off game - that is a box ticked.

"Now it is whether we can win a Grand Final. We have two games to do something special.

"It is difficult but doable.

"You are one game away from getting to a Grand Final that would be huge for the club.

"You have got to be excited by that. We are all excited about how good we can be as a team.

"We will do everything we need to in order to give ourselves the best chance to do that."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Caius Faatili barges through to score emphatic try for Wakefield Trinity against Leigh Leopards.

Powell has been there and done this before with a team that was not expected to be at the big dance. Castleford, back in 2017, blew everyone away, won the League Leaders' Shield, then beat St Helens with a Luke Gale drop goal to make it to Old Trafford.

They could not complete the final hurdle.

Wakefield have two more hurdles to go. A semi-final against either Wigan Warriors or Leeds Rhinos. A win in that? Then they go to the Theatre of Dreams trying to complete theirs.

If they do that, the inner sanctum's belief that raw potential can become greatness will have been achieved.

Sports.title: Littler overcomes lively crowd to beat Noppert at World Series of Darts Finals
Sports.content:
Luke Littler battled past Danny Noppert and a lively Dutch crowd to reach the second round at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

Littler, who has won every major tournament this year, reacted to effectively an away crowd twice in a dramatic contest to beat Noppert 6-4 and keep his hopes of an unprecedented clean sweep alive.

It sparked memories of several nights at this year's Premier League Darts when Littler faced whistles and jeers throughout the series on his way to winning the title, revealing afterwards he wanted to quit the invitational event.

Noppert capitalised on a slow start by Littler to break in the third leg and held a 3-1 lead but the key moment came when he made a mess of a 44 checkout in the sixth leg which allowed Littler to break back and make it 3-3.

After winning that leg, Littler let out a huge roar and put his hands to his ears, asking the crowd for more noise as they booed him loudly.

Noppert missed two darts to restore his break advantage in the next leg and Littler punished him, then the teenager took out a superb 95 checkout with tops-tops to move 5-4 ahead and broke his opponent to win the match.

"Coming back from a losing position to win is always a great feeling," said Littler, who won the World Series of Darts Finals in 2024.

"I'm not putting pressure on myself. I am just focusing on round by round."

Image: Luke Littler reacted to the crowd during the match (PDC/Kelly Deckers)

Should Littler win this weekend and win the following two tournaments, the World Grand Prix and European Championship, he would become the first player to hold every major darts title at the same time.

He would then set about trying to complete a remarkable clean sweep in November at the Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship finals, but he's taking things one match at a time and will next face Nathan Aspinall in the second round of this week's competition.

"Nathan always throws everything at me. He produces his best, I perform at my best, and hopefully it's another great game tomorrow," said Littler.

"It would be one of the best darts achievements if I could pull it off [the clean sweep], but it's still a very long way away."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stephen Bunting says Luke Littler has 'changed' Darts since bursting onto the scene a few years ago, but says he believes 'The Nuke' won't win as many world titles as darts legend Phil Taylor

A night of close matches

Unlike the first night when Michael van Gerwen was stunned by Daryl Gurney, there were no major surprises as the first round came to a conclusion on Friday.

Former world champion Gerwyn Price raced into a 5-0 lead against Brody Klinge but the Australian fought back to 5-4 before Price stumbled over the line.

It was a similar story for his compatriot Jonny Clayton as he was 4-0 up before missing several match darts on his way to a 6-3 win over Maik Kuivenhoven, who was called up as a late replacement for Lourence Ilagan after the Philippines player withdrew due to visa issues.

Image: Gerwyn Price could be the player to stop Luke Littler at the World Series of Darts Finals (PDC/Kelly Deckers)

James Wade edged out Damon Heta 6-5 after the latter missed a match dart in their deciding leg, while Aspinall fought back from 4-2 down to defeat Raymond Smith 6-4.

Having won six Players Championship events this year, Wessel Nijman is looking to turn that great form into something big on the televised stage and he started off his World Series of Darts campaign with a 6-4 win over veteran Simon Whitlock.

And there were 6-5 narrow wins for Canada's Jim Long over Australia's Adam Leek, plus Alexandra Palace cult hero Motomu Sakai against Callan Rydz.

Sports.title: Ballard heads Bristol City past Watford as they climb to fifth
Sports.content:
Bristol City moved into the Championship play-off places with a 1-0 victory over depleted Watford.

Dominic Ballard's first-half header was enough for all three points for the Robins at Ashton Gate, steering a backwards header in from Rio Cardines' ball into the box.

It was a much-needed win for Michael Skubala's side after back-to-back defeats leading into this clash on Friday night.

Bristol City now rise to fifth in the table ahead of the rest of the weekend's action and then the extended upcoming international break.

Watford, meanwhile, who have an injury-ravaged squad under Alessio Dionisi, remain in the bottom half of the table. They have picked up just a point on the road all season.

The key moments from Ashton Gate

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dom Ballard's superb header saw Bristol City go ahead in the first half against Watford.

3: BIG CHANCE! Bristol City should be ahead. Lovely work from Ballard to jink in down the left and cross into the middle. Knight arrives unmarked but he heads wide!

8: CHANCE! Now a good opening for Watford. Nabizada slinks inside and sees his shot blocked into the path of Kjerrumgaard. He then prods over from 12 yards.

11: PENALTY SHOUT! Atkinson then goes down in the box and wants a penalty after a challenge from Doumbia, but the referee is not interested. Hard to track in real time, but on replays it was clear that Doumbia got Atkinson before the ball.

31: GOAL! Bristol City have the lead that their dominance has earned! Cardines with another assist! His sixth of the season as he whips in a lovely inswinging cross and Dominic Ballard rises with his back to goal to steer a header into the corner!

80: CHANCE! Tolaj could seal it! A long ball forward from Tanner finds the run of the striker. He gets in between two Watford defenders, but then lashes over.

87: PENALTY SHOUT! Boadu feels he's having his shirt pulled in the box as he goes down! But the referee is not interested in the Watford man's protests!

The managers

Bristol City's Michael Skubala:

"Dom's got great movement in and around the box and I thought he could get down the sides of the two centre-halves. I thought he could link quite well. [Lorent] Tolaj does it well as well, but Dom's a really good mover without the ball and he creates little moments for himself.

"I think the goal is just a typical Dom Ballard goal that I've seen over the last few years.

"I was really pleased. It's not easy to come back off a couple of results that we lost, but it really showed some resilience to bounce back. A win's a win and a good clean sheet.

"I thought we showed, especially in the first half, some really good intensity with the ball. We moved it really well, shifted the play and looked really threatening. In the second half, naturally, we were a little bit lower, but we had some fast transition moments to go and get the second.

"We challenged the group with a clean sheet and making sure we defended our box solidly, and I thought the lads were great. The other thing was that I made seven changes, which is showing the squad depth. Not many people make seven changes and some of the lads put in great performances."

Watford's Alessio Dionisi:

"For a lot of matches we played with all the same players, the same line-up. Today it was difficult to ask other players.

"It's not easy because, for example, today on the bench there weren't midfielders, there weren't defenders. It was difficult.

"I'm not happy sometimes with the situation in the last 20 metres because we arrived near the box and then played back. It's not good, but we have a lot of young players.

"Today there were six young players in the line-up. Two 19-year-olds and two 20-year-olds. It's not easy, but I believe in our future because it's important.

"I speak every day with my director, with my owner, with the club. The club knows this situation well because at the start I wasn't happy. It's difficult to start when we had a few players.

"I know a lot of players arrived at the end of the [window], but now it's important to recover a lot of players.

"I spoke in the dressing room with my team. Now it's important to believe, to work together, because I believe in this team, I believe in our job."

Sports.title: Chelsea's defensive woes continue as Brentford win derby
Sports.content:
Chelsea's defensive and set-piece woes continued under Xabi Alonso as Brentford claimed an emphatic 3-0 victory in the west London derby.

It was all too easy for Brentford to win it as first Mikkel Damsgaard's corner was nodded across by Jannik Schuster, leaving Jaidon Anthony to nod home unmarked from a few yards out.

Then with Chelsea pushing for a leveller and moving to a back four, Brentford hit the Blues on the counter as Kevin Schade broke through. His one-on-one was saved by Emiliano Martinez but Igor Thiago struck home from close range to end his seven-game goal drought.

And with virtually the last kick of the game, Fabio Carvalho scored his first Premier League goal since his near-year-long injury lay-off after tucking home Schade's cross while unmarked at the far post.

Image: Igor Thiago celebrates his second

Chelsea have now conceded 12 goals - the most in the league - from five Premier League games as the wait for their first top-flight clean sheet of the season goes on.

Unimpressive in defence, but in attack, Chelsea weren't much better - clearly missing the injured Joao Pedro, with replacement Danny Welbeck failing to generate any clear chances in his place.

Moises Caicedo was another big miss, with his replacement being Jordan Henderson, who made an unsuccessful first start for the Blues at the club he joined them from.

Cole Palmer looked bright in sparks, but the Blues never really generated anything apart from Pedro Neto's ninth-minute effort, kept out by Caoimhin Kelleher.

Brentford - who have become the first team to stop Chelsea scoring this season - continue their unbeaten start to the season to go up to third. Speaking of three, that's the number of Premier League games without a win for Alonso's Chelsea.

The key moments from the Gtech...

9: SAVE! Danny Welbeck tees up Pedro Neto in the area but his shot is saved by Caoimhin Kelleher.

41: BLOCK! Morgan Rogers has a good shooting chance in the penalty area but his effort is blocked by Schuster.

50: OFF THE BAR! Anthony strikes the top of the bar with a header from inside the box. The offside flag goes up but replays showed he was level.

61: GOAL! Brentford take the advantage as Schuster heads Mikkel Damsgaard's corner across and Anthony nods in from a few yards out.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jaidon Anthony heads Brentford in front against Chelsea.

82: GOAL! Schade breaks through for a one-on-one but sees an effort saved, yet Thiago taps in the rebound to seal the points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Igor Thiago scores Brentford second against Chelsea.

90+4: GOAL! Carvalho makes it three by tapping home at the far post from Schade's wicked ball across.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fabio Carvalho scores Brentford third to seal win over Chelsea

Alonso: This is not enough from Chelsea

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso speaking to Sky Sports:

"I'm disappointed with the second half and with the result. This is not enough to compete in the Premier League.

"We were not able to maintain our level for the full 90 minutes and that's why we were punished today.

"It's about everything. It's about the mentality, the football and the tactical things that we need to keep improving. We can do much better."

On whether Joao Pedro's absence played a part:

"It's not about looking for excuses.

"We need to look at each other and know that we have to work and improve because there is still a long way to go. We have to check many things.

"We got into situations, but we were not precise enough with the final action. That's why we didn't score."

Andrews: Something was bubbling at Brentford

Brentford boss Keith Andrews speaking to Sky Sports:

"I think it's important that you enjoy these nights. There's no point hiding it. There are some tough days in the game, and you've got to enjoy the different emotions.

"I felt like there was something bubbling towards tonight. I have this unbelievable calm around the team because I trust them, so it's nice to see it come to fruition.

"I see humility and hunger within the group every day. We're very respectful of each other, but we're going to get better. We have to continue improving in this league.

"We try to push boundaries and be really open with each other. Let's continue on our journey because I'm loving it."
