Sports.title: Arteta: Dowman could go out on loan in future
Sports.content:
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has not ruled out loaning out Max Dowman in the future and says the club evaluates the 16-year-old sensation's progress every six months.

Dowman continued his rise by starting and scoring twice in Arsenal's Carabao Cup win over Ipswich this week. After the game, Gunners midfielder Mikel Merino compared the young teenager to Barcelona and Spain star Lamine Yamal.

But those 90 minutes at Portman Road have been Dowman's only minutes of the season, and he did not make Arsenal's matchday squad in the wins over Aston Villa and Sunderland.

"We haven't really listened to any of the [loan] possibilities because we were clear that we want to have him in the squad, that we wanted him to be part of the pre-season," Arteta said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We take a took at Max Dowman's remarkable rise in an Arsenal shirt so far as the youngster nets twice more in the Carabao Cup win over Ipswich to impress yet again.

"I'm going to start to see where we are from there. We will evaluate every six months where we are, what is the best thing for him to do and from there make the right decisions.

"It will depend on a lot of factors: what he needs, where the team is as well, the availability that we have in the squad, the amount of minutes that he's playing, the quality he's delivering when he's got those minutes.

"We have to be open, but now the focus is to be here and impact the team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Paul Merson says the likes of teenage sensations Max Dowman at Arsenal and JJ Gabriel, who's asked to leave Manchester United, need to be patient as they look to build their careers.

"There have been many cases of that age that they've gone [on loan] and they've been successful, some others not. Particularly, I think I was 17 when I went to Paris [Saint-Germain].

"Depending on the atmosphere that you find there, how much the coach believes in you, you go there just to be part of a squad, not to play minutes.

"Which country? Depends. But now he's in a great place. He's in a good place right now and let's keep him here."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the ProjectFootballer podcast back in 2024, Jamie Redknapp spoke about the 'special talent' held by 14-year-old Max Dowman.

Last season, Dowman became the Premier League's youngest goalscorer and starter in their title-winning campaign, as well as the youngest player in Champions League history, where they reached the final.

Over the last nine months, the Gunners have sent Ethan Nwaneri - who broke the record for the youngest ever Premier League player in 2022 at just 15 - out on loan to Marseille and Borussia Dortmund, where he is currently playing.

Bothroyd: Dowman is better than Madueke

Jay Bothroyd on Sky Sports News:

"Noni Madueke is not playing for Arsenal. For me, Max Dowman is better than Madueke now.

"If you're going to consider Madueke for England, then you definitely have to consider Dowman. And Dowman should be in that England squad right now. There's no doubt about that for me.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at some of the future Premier League stars making their mark in the third round of the Carabao Cup.

"He's going to be the future of England. He's 16 but this is his second season as a pro. Come the European Championships in 2028, he's going to be 18. He has to be in that squad and if he keeps doing what he's doing, he's going to be in that squad.

"What's the negative? If you're good enough, you're old enough. Professional players think a certain way. They're not thinking: I'm 16, I'll wait a few years. They're thinking I want to play right now, especially if they're thinking they're better than who's in there.

"Dowman needs to be considered, he's the future. The same as how Rio Ngumoha is the future, who is electric."

Sports.title: Brentford blitz Chelsea as Fábio Carvalho caps stunning second-half display
Sports.content:
Those early-season thoughts that Chelsea might be the team best-placed to challenge Arsenal are beginning to look extremely over-optimistic. The two chaotic wins with which they began were always difficult to read: they might have been useful points picked up on the way to a more solid structure, or they might have represented evidence of significant problems. After three games without a win, and 12 goals conceded in five games this season, it’s beginning to look like the latter.

At the final whistle, Keith Andrews tipped his head back and roared at the sky, celebrating Brentford’s first home win over Chelsea since 1938. They remain unbeaten, coherent and disciplined, and moved up to third in the table. The comparison is impossible not to draw: as one side flail in an orgy of structured spending, their far less wealthy neighbours thrive with a clear plan and sense of direction. “It was a performance I felt was bubbling,” said Andrews. “I could see it in the players’ eyes over the last two days. They were very focused, very determined.”

Such is the state of perpetual flux at Chelsea that the usual homilies about the benefits of stability always seem a little redundant when applied to them. With 11 new signings this summer maintaining the sense of the club as a trading hub, learning the names of everybody in the dressing room has probably been a greater priority than worrying too much about boardroom wrangling. But, still, their first game since Todd Boehly and Mark Walter agreed to sell their 12.8% stake in the club to the major shareholder Clearlake Capital felt significant. At the very least, a more harmonious boardroom should be beneficial.

Boehly, the great disruptor, who arrived blithely telling English football it was doing everything wrong, has departed having achieved very little other than splurging £300m on players who didn’t fit and giving Raheem Sterling a £325,000-a-week contract in his shambolic spell as de facto sporting director. Four years on, after 60 arrivals, do Chelsea look any more like title challengers than they did then? It was, in truth, very hard to say what this looked like, other than a team that is every much still under construction. Jordan Henderson made his full Chelsea debut at his former club, while Danny Welbeck, Pep Chavarría and Valentín Barco made their first league starts.

Barco, whose overenthusiastic celebrations after Argentina’s winner against England at the World Cup earned him a post-match slap from Jude Bellingham, was booed with impressive consistency from the home fans. The lesson was clear: if you’re going to be a major irritant while in possession of a distinctive shock of hair the colour of burnished copper, there will be consequences. Emí Martínez was jeered as well for the crime of being Argentinian. Henderson, by contrast, was treated relatively gently, his booing as a returnee more sporadic and muted, tending to the perfunctory.

View image in fullscreen Jaidon Anthony rises to head Brentford in front. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

The pattern for Chelsea was a familiar one: a fast start, fading to something a little scratchier. The opening, for the second successive game, did not produce an early goal, although Pedro Neto would have given them a ninth-minute lead had it not been for a sharp save from Caoimhín Kelleher.

“We have dropped our consistency, our competitive mentality in the second half,” said Xabi Alonso. “We have not been able to keep our level. When you lose shape you are out of control. To be able to understand and know what it takes to be competing to the end, it’s a process and it takes time.”

The longer the game went on, the less assured Chelsea looked and a Brentford opener arrived just after the hour. Perhaps inevitably, it came from a dead ball; the stats had suggested that Brentford this season had been creating significantly more chances from set plays than they had converted. As modern corner routines go it seemed very straightforward, Jannik Schuster climbing above the diminutive Barco to head Mikkel Damsgaard’s corner back across goal, where Jaidon Anthony nodded in from close range, his first goal since his summer move from Burnley.

View image in fullscreen Fábio Carvalho fires Brentford into a three-goal lead in injury time. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

Chelsea belatedly applied some pressure but, although the final minutes were played largely in the Brentford half, they created little beyond corners, as Brentford maintained their composure and structure.

The second goal arrived seven minutes from time. Damsgaard, perhaps the tidiest player in the league, led the break, playing in Kevin Schade. Martínez saved his side-footed effort but Igor Thiago guided an awkwardly bouncing ball inside the post for his first goal of the season. Fábio Carvalho made it 3-0 in added time, slamming in a cross from Schade, who had been left inexplicably unmarked on the left after a long throw was half-cleared.

As Brentford begin to consider that European qualification is a real possibility, Chelsea remain what they have been since the takeover: a work in progress – and, particularly at the back, it feels that progress has a long way to run.

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold recalled by England but with a warning from Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has told Trent Alexander-Arnold he must bring defensive solidity to the England squad after giving him a surprise recall for the upcoming Nations League matches.

The head coach has selected the Real Madrid right-back only once before – for the games against Andorra and Senegal in June last year. Tuchel made headlines when he did so by urging Alexander-Arnold to focus on the defensive side of his game or risk a slip that could undermine the team’s World Cup campaign.

Tuchel used him as a 64th-minute substitute against Andorra and Alexander-Arnold was out of the picture by the time England went to North America for the tournament. He is now back, despite starting only three of Madrid’s seven matches this season and largely going under the radar with his performances. Tuchel’s message to him has not changed.

“He has to, it’s necessary,” Tuchel said when asked whether Alexander-Arnold offered enough defensively. “My conviction is that he will but he has no choice.”

Tuchel continues to see Alexander-Arnold, who is famed for the range of his passing, as a right-back rather than a midfielder. The head coach has previously said he has Tino Livramento and Jarell Quansah ahead of Alexander-Arnold in the right-back pecking order. He has named both of them in the squad for the games against Spain (home), Czechia (home and away) and Croatia (away).

Quick Guide England's squad Show Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford, James Trafford, Jason Steele. Defenders: Trent Alexander-Arnold, Jarrod Branthwaite, Trevoh Chalobah, Marc Guéhi, Lewis Hall, Ezri Konsa, Tino Livramento, Nico O’Reilly, Jarell Quansah. Midfielders: Elliot Anderson, Jude Bellingham, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Kobbie Mainoo, Cole Palmer, Declan Rice, Alex Scott. Forwards: Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Eberechi Eze, Anthony Gordon, Harry Kane, Rio Ngumoha, Marcus Rashford, Morgan Rogers, Bukayo Saka. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Tuchel has been unable to include his first-choice right-back, Reece James, or Djed Spence, who can operate in either full-back position, because of injuries. Ben White is also injured; Tuchel said he would have considered him. The centre-half Ezri Konsa, who is in the squad, has played at right-back.

Tuchel said he had spoken to Alexander-Arnold to tell him he would not go to the World Cup but had not called him this time. “He heard the good news over the nomination,” he said. “I am not sure a lot of things have changed. I know what he is capable of. I know about his talent. I know what he is saying: that he is desperate to play for England and he will fight for his shirt. It’s a long camp and it’s a good moment to show up. It’s a chance for Trent to claim what he feels is his – his place on the right side. So here we go.”

Alexander-Arnold was the headline selection on a day when Tuchel gave further recalls to Jarrad Branthwaite, Lewis Hall, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Alex Scott, Cole Palmer and Dominic Calvert-Lewin. He also included Rio Ngumoha. Dean Henderson, John Stones, Dan Burn and Jordan Henderson miss out because of injury. Noni Madueke, Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney have been dropped.

Tuchel overlooked Levi Colwill, Adam Wharton, Phil Foden and Morgan Gibbs-White. Nor was there a recall for Harry Maguire. Tuchel gave the defender hope of involvement at the World Cup when he selected him against Uruguay and Japan in March before he ignored him for the tournament. It drew an outspoken response, Maguire using social media to pronounce himself “shocked and gutted”. His mother, Zoe, said she was “disgusted” by the decision.

Quick Guide How do I 

Of Maguire’s reaction, Tuchel said: “I will not hold it against him for the rest of his life because I’m not that type of person. I can forget easily and quickly. But I didn’t like it and it doesn’t help.”

Tuchel said he had not spoken to Maguire since.

Sports.title: Harry Kane smashes record for fastest to 100 Bundesliga goals in 98th game
Sports.content:
Harry Kane smashed the 49-year-old record for the fastest player to score 100 Bundesliga goals in Bayern Munich’s 7-0 victory over Union Berlin, his 98th league game for the club.

Cologne’s Dieter Müller set the previous mark in 1977, but it took him 129 matches and, with the England captain scoring at better than a goal a game, a new record had been inevitable for some time. Since his arrival in 2023 Kane had been averaging a Bundesliga goal every 78.5 minutes and has now scored 152 in 154 appearances in all competitions, including 61 in 51 games last term.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

He blasted home a 39th-minute penalty to take the record before nodding in a Michael Olise cross early in the second half to send Bayern top of the table before the other weekend matches.

The feat stole the spotlight from Olise, who scored his first Bayern hat-trick, and Jamal Musiala, who also scored a goal worthy of winning any game.

“I’m very proud to have now scored 100 and 101 Bundesliga goals. I haven’t been around that long. I’ve loved every second of it,” Kane told Sky Germany. “With Michael, Lucho [Luis Díaz] and Jamal I naturally get chances and today was no exception.

“So I just want to thank the team, the club, the coach, and the staff – everyone who has helped me achieve this. Let’s keep going like this. Scoring more goals in games is obviously a big step. Of course, there have been many important goals among them. I can only say that I’m enjoying every minute of it. Just like today.”

Sports.title: Women’s Super League: Lauren Hemp hits double as Manchester City see off lively Liverpool
Sports.content:
Manchester City continued their winning start to the new Women’s Super League season but the defending champions needed a 90th-minute own goal from Grace Fisk to help them edge past an ever-improving Liverpool side after an entertaining game in which Lauren Hemp scored twice.

Fisk inadvertently turned Grace Clinton’s dangerous cross into her own net to put City 3-2 up and then – with Liverpool searching for an equaliser and committing players forward deep in stoppage time – Hemp added another on the counterattack to make it 4-2 and widen the margin of victory, but that slightly masked how well the visitors had played.

Gareth Taylor – against his former side – will have taken significant encouragement from his Liverpool team’s performance, on a night when they made the league leaders dig deep.

“Playing that way, we believe we’ll win a lot of games this season,” Taylor told Sky Sports, as he praised his team’s effort. “What you saw was a more improved version of what we were towards the end of last season.”

That certainly seemed the case. Nevertheless, the result ensured that City, who had already been the only WSL side who held a 100% winning record after the opening two rounds of games and now will certainly stay top of the table for at least another week, have still not dropped any points in home league fixtures since Andrée Jeglertz took charge in the summer of 2025.

It had looked as though Jeglertz’s City were set for a routine evening when Hemp met Carlotta Wamser’s incisive inside ball and sent a controlled, low finish into the far bottom corner. It was Hemp’s first goal since scoring for England in a victory over Spain in April, her first club goal since scoring in the FA Cup in February and her first WSL goal since last November’s Manchester derby.

Moments after Hemp’s opening goal, with 13 minutes on the clock, the entire crowd rose to applaud the late Matt Beard, the former Liverpool manager, in reference to the year 2013, when he won the first of two consecutive WSL titles with Liverpool.

Supporters of clubs across the WSL and WSL2 have been invited to applaud at the same time in games across this weekend, to mark a year since Beard’s death on 20 September 2025. He was a much-loved character and hugely successful coach at Liverpool, whose performance – particularly in the remainder of the first half – would have done him proud.

View image in fullscreen Vivien Endemann puts Liverpool 2-1 up against Manchester City. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

The away side deservedly struck back and found themselves 2-1 up before the half-hour mark, as their pressing gave the defending champions a headache. First a misunderstanding between Wamser and Alex Greenwood allowed Vivien Endemann to set up Alice Bergström for the equaliser, which she calmly tucked past Ayaka Yamashita.

Soon afterwards, after City failed to clear a cross, Endemann – who had opened her Liverpool account with a debut goal at Charlton on the opening weekend – fired in a shot that Yamashita got a hand to but could only help into the net.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Khadija Shaw struck a post from a difficult angle after rounding Khiara Keating, but Shaw eventually did equalise after a goalkeeping error shortly before half-time. Keating – returning to face her former club after her summer move to Liverpool – did well to block Hemp’s strike but was unable to prevent the ball trickling into the path of the onrushing Shaw, who gratefully poked home.

Keating impressed in the second half with a fine reaction save, keeping out a Shaw effort that had looked destined for the top corner at her near post. But the hosts began to build pressure and the introduction of the lively Clinton inside the final 15 minutes boosted their attacking threat.

Her near-post cross proved too difficult for Fisk to clear and – just as they did on countless occasions last term – City lived up to Jeglertz’s mantra of “we will find a way to win”, a message that has been imprinted on the walls of their training base.

Jeglertz hinted at that again as he told Sky Sports: “I’m very pleased with the mentality of the group. They never stop believing, they keep on going and – in the end – we are winners.”

Sports.title: We wanted to let Max Dowman bloom in the shadows but he has become hard to ignore | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
The poet Jorge Luis Borges wrote a famous short story about a society that had become so good at making maps, so obsessed with capturing every detail, that its rulers decided the only way to do the job right was to make a lifesize map of its entire empire, which could then be laid out across the actual land from coast to coast. Imagine a map of Britain the exact same size as Britain, showing every branch of Greggs, every nail bar, every vape shop in perfect detail. Only then can we really see what Britain looks like, by standing on a fake Britain laid over the top of actual Britain.

Borges was writing in the 1940s, at a time when people were fascinated by the mechanised future, with its new forms of measuring out the world: the wireless, the 30mph motorcar, the rise of Big Tape Measure. And to be fair, the mega-map is a pretty accurate vision of our own fully networked present, a place where you can snoop around a village in Mozambique from your laptop in Egham, where no one ever stops committing acts of minute self-surveillance, even if they think they’re just searching “What is beetroot?” on the internet.

Borges also hated football. “Soccer is popular because stupidity is popular,” he wrote, which probably seemed a bold statement at the time. But then Borges also didn’t live to see an episode of Wow Sports Premier League Breakfast at Breakfast with Roger McRoger and a puzzled Lee Trundle. After which, perhaps less of a surprise. But the process he describes is also a good description of what football is doing to itself. Endless data, endless analysis, no spaces or free air, matches that are just schematised movement. At times it can feel like football is out there laying a lifesize real-time map on top of itself.

In Borges’s story, the land soon begins to decay beneath the massive map – which is reassessed by later generations as insane, pointless and stupid – and left to rot in the desert. We haven’t reached this point. Nobody is de-mapping football. But it does perhaps explain why everyone gets so excited when a talent emerges that seems to be playful and human, to exist outside the grid. And also why it has felt wrong to gush too soon about Max Dowman, to fear placing the hex on him. We know how this works. Here is a fluffy new thing. Let us break him. Let us heap pressure on his shoulders. Don’t talk about Max Dowman. Let Max Dowman exist, breathe, bloom in the shadows.

So, Max Dowman then. It has become quite hard to ignore him. He was brilliant against Ipswich in midweek, and brilliant in a way that seems solid and real and comfortable with itself. Most obviously there were the two goals, both a perfect snapshot of why Dowman seems equipped to survive, more state‑of‑the‑art than some other young players we’ve burdened with expectation.

The second goal is particularly good, five perfect little actions packed into six seconds of football. Arsenal have the ball on the edge of the Ipswich box. Dowman shows for a pass, sees it’s going elsewhere, changes his mind, and makes a three-yard sprint to create space. Finally he has the physical capacity to control a bouncing ball in that sliver of space, to move his feet so much quicker than the nearest defender it looks like a glitch in the machine, and to finish in a way that involves sifting the options and timing the shot, all without breaking stride.

View image in fullscreen Max Dowman leaves Cédric Kipré floundering to score his brilliant second, and Arsenal’s third, goal at Ipswich. Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

The first goal is on his other side, and involves a more classical piece of one-on-one deception. This is the same defender: Cédric Kipré, 29 years old, came through Paris Saint-Germain’s youth system. Dowman walks through him with a micro-feint and a switch of feet, then reels off another hilariously understated finish, doing it all while a second defender is still gathering himself to lunge, like a man operating in a different time signature to everyone around him.

This is the key point of difference, the ability to make everything stop, the fly-vision that means he sees what’s about to happen while everyone else is whirling about trying to read the charts, in the same way Lionel Messi (yes, sorry, sorry) always seems to have time to pass the ball into the net, like this is all a kickabout in a pair of sliders.

Our way of understanding young creative players has often seemed to lag behind where the game actually is, to be driven by nostalgia for what this thing used to look like. I remember the excitement over the 18-year-old Jack Rodwell’s physicality at the exact moment physicality was no longer going to be a thing, like proudly unveiling the latest horse‑drawn train just as the Ford Model T rolls off the production line.

Michael Owen was brilliant at 17, but he was mainly brilliant at running very fast in a straight line and smashing the ball into the net. Plus of course there was Wayne Rooney, who emerged a pale, unformed teenager composed entirely from energy drinks and white bread, out there making the game up on the fly, as though some urban foundling had come barrelling over the advert boards with a string of sausages still dangling from his mouth.

The narrative around Rooney is that he lost this vital native quality. But Rooney adapted and survived, and clearly understood what he had to be a lot better than those of us watching. And even now creative players have to exist against this. Cole Palmer is exciting because he does surprising things that seem to be striking a blow for freedom, beauty and older people who struggle to make their email work. But his real challenge is to retain just enough of this while fitting the world around him.

Dowman is a bit different. The things that make him stand out seem to speak very easily to how football is now. Being a modern creative footballer is not jinking runs, rasping drives or dribbling across a cabbage field in a pair of cowboy boots. It’s targeted energy, high-intensity semi-freedom. Lamine Yamal and Désiré Doué have the same fast-twitch foot and brain speed, the ability to operate in micro-moments, to see patterns just ahead of time. Dowman is 6ft tall and getting stronger. He won’t be kicked to pieces. He can repeat this without taking bites out of himself.

There is still the issue of his youth. But maybe this doesn’t matter so much either. The world has changed. In the age of Rooney and Owen there was no care, no data, no softness. This is where the structures of modern football are an advantage. Dowman will be GPS’d to the last decimal point. Endless physical scientists will have a say on his output and stress levels.

View image in fullscreen Wayne Rooney and Michael Owen broke through as teenagers in an age of less data and less care. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

The money is too big. The talent is too valuable. It also comes ready to plug and play. You don’t get to this level unless you can ingest systems and briefings. You’ve already been pressure-cooked and stress-tested. What you’re being asked to do in the orderly spaces of professional football is the same thing you were asked to do in the orderly spaces of academy football, just five levels up and with more people watching.

Borges was anti-football because he saw it as inauthentic, the players no longer sports people but “actors in jerseys before the TV cameras”. And this is also fine, further evidence that boomer-dad nostalgia is one of the key archetypes of human behaviour.

Life is also different now; not harder or easier, but more instant, a series of moments, the creation of rapid-fire energy. Dowman has grown up inside this. He can parcel his time out, disappear for a bit, maybe make a show of things in the spring.

And yes, this is another way of fitting him to a model, laying a lifesize map of future Max Dowman across the present. But I strongly suspect he will be fine, and that unlike so many other things out there he’s pretty well adapted to whatever the future is supposed to look like.

Sports.title: Premier League news: Carrick brushes aside questions over future, Arteta salutes ‘extraordinary’ Dowman
Sports.content:
1. Carrick insists: ‘It’s not a blame game’ Michael Carrick says it will take more than one or two defeats before he comes under internal pressure as the Manchester United head coach. United lost 3-2 to Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, having led 2-0 at Old Trafford. That followed Sunday’s 1-0 home loss to 10-man Manchester City. United also went down 2-0 at Hull on the opening day of the season and conceded a late equaliser at Everton at the beginning of the month. The results have caused Carrick to come under scrutiny and he was reminded before Sunday’s visit to Fulham that his predecessors, Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, were sacked after 30 months and 14 months, respectively, in the job. “It will be a lot longer than one or two games of results [before he is under pressure from United’s hierarchy],” Carrick said: “It’s irrelevant for me. I know the club, I know the role, I know what’s expected here in terms of playing at a certain standard. “In terms of the future and ownership and how long I’ve got, it’s totally nothing, it’s ridiculous to think that way in the position I’m in: it’s just not on the radar. It’s two or three games we haven’t had certain results. We’ve got to perform and we’ve got a lot of games to plan for.” Carrick is content to take ownership of his team’s performance. “That’s why I’m here. It’s my responsibility, I’m fine with that,” he said. “It’s not a blame game. We always search for things to look at and find the blame, sometimes it gets too much. Blame me, it’s no problem, but it’s not about blaming people. It’s about finding solutions. It’s a collective thing. I know where we want to go and we want to get there fast. We don’t like losing matches, but it doesn’t affect what we do next.” The 45-year-old was asked if he needs to show more emotion on the touchline. “I need to show more emotion? In what way?” he replied. “What do you want me to show?” On Friday JJ Gabriel travelled to Barcelona for discussions regarding potentially joining the club, with United understood to have found out via the media despite the 15-year-old being registered with them. On Tuesday Gabriel told United he wanted his registration rescinded because he wishes to join another club. Real Madrid have a firm interest and it is understood Gabriel and his advisers travelled for preliminary talks with Barcelona. Carrick said: “The situation will work itself out, whatever way it's going to work itself out. Making sure he's OK is the important thing." Jamie Jackson

2. Dowman takes step up in his stride Mikel Arteta has praised Max Dowman’s “extraordinary” transition from schoolboy to Arsenal first-team squad member and backed the teenager to make more of an impact this season. Dowman became the first 16-year-old since Wayne Rooney in October 2002 to score twice for a Premier League club in Arsenal’s victory over Ipswich in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday, after bursting on to the scene last year. That was his first appearance of the campaign, having been an unused substitute on four occasions as Arsenal have won all seven of their fixtures.



Dowman, who has been training with Arsenal’s first team since he was 14, completed his GCSEs in the summer and he will study for a BTec qualification after deciding against taking A-Levels. Arteta said Dowman’s development was still being carefully managed by Arsenal after a couple of years of having to balance his studies. “It’s not easy,” said the Arsenal manager. “That’s what tells you about the craziness of the age and the environment he still lives in with the demands and the competition he needs to face during the week. But the way he has handled it, him and the family, it has been extraordinary. If he is here, he has to be here in all conditions and we cannot treat him differently in many aspects.” Dowman is in contention to be on the bench to face Brighton on Saturday as Arsenal attempt to make it eight successive victories to start the season for the first time since 1903. Arteta is convinced more opportunities will come his way sooner rather than later.

“That’s the best way to knock on the door: to do it on the pitch, not in the office,” he said. “What Max did the other day, alongside all the players as well, that haven’t played that many minutes, it was really impressive.” View image in fullscreen Arsenal’s Max Dowman turns 17 in January when he could go out on loan. Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Every Second Media/Shutterstock Premier League regulations do not allow players under 17 to be sent out on loan but Luton are understood to have registered an interest in Dowman, who was coached by their manager, Jack Wilshere, when he played for Arsenal’s under-18s. Arteta said it was possible Dowman could be allowed to leave in January, by which point he will be 17, but that his immediate future was at Arsenal. “We haven’t really listened to any of the possibilities because we were crystal clear that we wanted to have him in the squad, that we wanted him to be part of the pre-season and then start to see where we are from there,” Arteta said. “We will evaluate every six months, where we are and what is the best thing for him to do and then make the right decision. It depends on a lot of factors – what he needs and what the team needs as well, the availability we have in the squad, the minutes that he is playing and the qualities of those minutes. We have to be open but now the focus is to be here and to impact the team.” Ed Aarons

3. De Zerbi grants Tonali time to settle Roberto De Zerbi insists Sandro Tonali is not feeling the pressure of his price tag despite a mixed start to life at Tottenham. The midfielder became the most expensive player in the club’s history when he joined from Newcastle for £92.5m in the summer. De Zerbi made a big play to sign Tonali amid interest from Manchester City and Arsenal, delivering a two-hour sales pitch to his fellow Italian to convince him to move to north London. He outlined how central Tonali would be to his plans and explained what he could expect from Spurs’ fans and the team’s style of football. Tonali has started all four Premier League games this season – in which Spurs have drawn twice and lost twice without scoring – but has produced underwhelming defensive numbers and created only three chances. De Zerbi revealed he had spoken to the 26-year-old about the weight of the price tag and claimed the player “doesn’t feel the pressure about that”. The Spurs manager pointed out that Tonali took time to adapt in his first season at Milan in 2020 before becoming one of the most sought-after young midfielders in the world once he settled there. De Zerbi said “the adaptation has been not so fast” at Tottenham “but it can happen”, adding: “It is not so easy to change city, to change everything, for the players. Sometimes the adaptation is immediate, sometimes you need more time.” View image in fullscreen Sandro Tonali has started all four Premier League games this season, but Spurs are still seeking their first win. Photograph: Chloe Knott/Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock Tottenham’s struggles in front of goal have not been helped by Tonali’s inability to create chances for the forwards. The goalless draw against Everton was the first in 140 games at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and following a 0-0 against Nottingham Forest, equalling Spurs’ tally of goalless games in the previous 181 matches. The last time they recorded three or more consecutive goalless draws in the league was 25 years ago under George Graham, when they went to four. It is a remarkable run, especially after a summer spend of more than £300m, that leaves Spurs in 17th going into Saturday’s game against Aston Villa, who have also struggled after a summer of major change. De Zerbi maintained he is happy with Tonali’s performances – even though he believes they can improve – and described him as “a complete midfielder”. “His physical characteristics are to play box to box but he started his career as a playmaker. He’s good enough with the ball, he’s good enough without the ball.” Sam Cunningham

Sports.title: Uefa and Concacaf ask Gianni Infantino to give Fifa’s billions to its member associations
Sports.content:
The presidents of Uefa and Concacaf have written to Gianni Infantino requesting that Fifa release money from its $6bn (£4.5bn) reserves to its member associations, stating that the plan to fund them via the doomed Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme was unnecessary given the cash pile it is sitting on.

Aleksander Ceferin and Victor Montagliani proposed a payout of at least $10m to each of Fifa’s 211 member associations (MAs), initially as a one-off during the 2027-2030 commercial cycle. They called for an independent review of Fifa’s financial position and said their own study “raises an important question as to whether the proposed transaction was necessary to deliver greater resources to the MAs”.

The proposed $10m would be handed out on top of money committed by Fifa’s existing Fifa Forward programme, which paid each MA about $8m over the previous four-year cycle. In a separate letter to the presidents of the Asian Football Confederation, the Confederation of African Football, Conmebol (the South American federation) and Oceania, Ceferin and Montagliani asked their counterparts to support the motion. Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, the AFC president, is expected to send an endorsement of their plan.

The leaders intend their proposal to be considered at the next Fifa Council meeting on 15 October, where Infantino is due to face Fifa’s nominal decision-making body for the first time since scandal engulfed his reign.

The letter to Infantino states: “Our analysis indicates that Fifa should make at least $10million available to each of its 211 MAs over the 2027-30 cycle for investment in infrastructure and football development – an aggregate of approximately $2.1billion. This would be a one-off release of reserves, over and above the approved Fifa Forward Programme, which would continue in full as already committed.”

It points out Fifa’s reserves would not dip below $1.5bn even after that scale of distribution, and says a larger handout could be possible “once a clearer picture of Fifa’s financial position at year-end is available”.

Ceferin and Montagliani said Fifa “already has the capacity to deliver substantially more to its MAs from its own balance sheet – without any sale of interests in its competitions, and without asking anything of the MAs in return”.

They proceeded to point out that releasing part of Fifa’s reserves would “demonstrate that MAs should not have to choose between development and good governance; between investment and integrity; or between financial support and the ability to consider proposals on their merits. Development is an institutional responsibility of Fifa – not a matter of individual discretion.”

While Fifa Forward Enterprise had promised member associations about $40m, half of that sum was an optional $20m payment for those signing up to his plan.

Infantino remains under pressure to resign but looks certain to run for re-election in March. It remains to be seen whether he will face an opponent.

Fifa was approached for comment.

Sports.title: Oxford United apologise for launching ‘United 93’ clothing range around 9/11 anniversary
Sports.content:
Oxford United have abandoned a new range of American style-sportswear after it inadvertently referenced the tragedy of September 11.

The League One club launched their new “Campus Collection” on Friday morning but had removed it from sale by lunchtime, after clothing designs were revealed to bear the slogan “United 93”. The U’s immediately published an apology that admitted to a lack of understanding of “the historical context and associations” related to the branding and made “sincere apologies for this error and any offence caused”.

“Inspired by the style and culture of American sports,” the club originally trailed the Campus Collection as launching on 11 September of this year, the 25th anniversary of the atrocity that killed nearly 3,000 people. Concerns over sensitivity saw the launch then delayed, but when the online collection was finally made available for sale on Friday, images showed models wearing an NFL-style shirt with “United 93” on the chest, in recognition of Oxford being founded in 1893.

United 93 was one of four domestic passenger jets seized by al-Qaida terrorists on 11 September 2001. A mutiny by passengers prevented hijackers from using the plane to destroy a government building in Washington DC, and it ultimately crashed into a field, killing all 44 people on board. A film titled “United 93” was also made about the tragedy.

The Campus Collection was live for approximately two hours on Friday before the webpage was deleted by the club after they realised the meaning of the phrase. “The range was released without understanding of the historical context and associations,” the club statement read. “It should not have reached the point of sale and we take full responsibility for not undertaking proper due diligence.

“We have removed the collection with immediate effect and are reviewing our approval processes to ensure nothing like this happens again. Once again, we would like to put on record our sincere apologies for this error and any offence caused.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Opinion was mixed among Oxford fans, with many outraged but others inclined to forgive the error. One user of the Yellows Forum called it a “monumental cock-up that I would expect to be sacked for if I’d signed off on it”. Another wrote: “Whilst not ideal … everyone who sees this realises there’s no malicious intent. Ultimately there was just no consideration to it at all.”

Sports.title: Chelsea told they’re ‘definitely not’ title contenders as Xabi Alonso sets unwanted record
Sports.content:
Chelsea are not going to be in the Premier League title race this season - there is so much wrong with the 'crazy club'.

Those are the thoughts of Adrian Durham, who watched on as the Blues were beaten 3-0 by Brentford on Friday night.

3 Chelsea were easily beaten by Brentford on Friday, losing away to the Bees in the Premier League for the first time Credit: Getty

Keith Andrews outclassed Xabi Alonso at the Gtech Community Stadium as his side moved up to third in the table.

Meanwhile, Chelsea dropped down to seventh after being handed their second loss of the season in just five games.

The teams went in goalless at half time, but Brentford came out the much better side in the second half, opening the scoring just after the hour mark through Jaidon Anthony.

Igor Thiago then made it two with nine minutes to go and ex-Liverpool man Fabio Carvalho added the third in stoppage time.

The impressive result handed the Bees their first-ever Premier League home victory over Chelsea.

They were winless in five meetings beforehand, but now Xabi Alonso is the first Blues manager to lose on the road against them.

Chelsea out of the Premier League title race

A 3-0 loss for Chelsea has them sitting on seven points after five games and already five points off the top of the table.

That could increase to eight if Arsenal or Manchester City win their matches across the upcoming weekend of action.

And talkSPORT's Durham has already ruled them out of challenging for the Premier League title this campaign.

Speaking after the full-time whistle, he said: "So many questions about this Chelsea performance...fundamentally, they are definitely not Premier League title contenders, we can see that.

3 Alonso has lost two of his opening five league games as Chelsea boss Credit: AFP

"I think there's so much wrong with them."

Arsenal legend Martin Keown added: "It's extremely disappointing from a Chelsea point of view, we were never really convinced.

"The wealth that the club has and the players they buy, but then you see that tonight...it wasn't particularly convincing."

He later continued: "That is a wake-up call for Chelsea."

And Durham then concluded: "They're a crazy club, Chelsea. They started with a 36-year-old in midfield and finished with a 16-year-old in midfield. That's how crazy they are."

Jordan Henderson, formerly of Brentford, made his first start for Chelsea before academy prospect Madhi Nicoll-Jazuli was brought on to join him for the final stages of the match.

3 Brentford outclassed Chelsea to leave the Blues well off the pace in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Jason Cundy's comments come back to bite him

Chelsea superfan Jason Cundy would have been watching their defeat to Brentford behind his hands on Friday.

Not only because of the poor performance, but because just before the season started, he predicted the Blues to win the title.

“I’m going to make a statement now. There is no reason why Chelsea cannot win this title. In fact, I’m going to say it. Chelsea will win the title," Cundy said at the start of August.

“There is something about Chelsea. We have got a cheat code. I’m not proud of it, but we can win the title for a number of reasons.

“Have you seen our front three? Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer - Palmer’s had a rest, Joao Pedro’s had a rest.

“Our midfield, the recruitment at the back. It almost certainly looks like we could be playing three at the back with someone in Xabi Alonso, who knows how to win a title.

“One game a week, we saw how beneficial that could be when Antonio Conte came in, went to three at the back. Win the title. History is going to repeat itself."

But after losing in such a fashion, it seems Cundy's title shout may have been a little bit too ambitious.

And Jamie O'Hara has made sure to rub it in, posting an edited image of Cundy dressed as a bee and writing: 'Up the Bees'.
