Sports.title: UEFA and CONCACAF demand Gianni Infantino hands over £7m to all FIFA members
Sports.content:
UEFA and CONCACAF have written a joint letter to Gianni Infantino calling for at least $10million from its reserves to be paid to FIFA's 211 Member Associations.

It follows Infantino's failed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plans, which intended to part-privatise world football's governing body.



4 UEFA and CONCACAF have called on Infantino and FIFA to pay their 211 members using money in their reserves Credit: Getty

The letter is signed by UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin and CONCACAF President Victor Montagliani. The latter is a potential candidate to run against Infantino in next March's election even though he has not yet publicly come forward.

"FIFA is on course to close 2023-26 with reserves of approximately $6billion," reads the letter, seen by talkSPORT. "[This is] considerably more than is required."

Infantino is asked to "make at least $10m available to each of [FIFA's] 211 member associations over the 2027-30 cycle". This would cost $2.11bn with pre-planned funding on top.



The letter backs up a belief from senior UEFA and CONCACAF figures that FIFA should invest using far more of its own reserves.

It was not lost on critics of FFE that Infantino was seeking $4.2bn from investors, including Joshua Kushner, and yet FIFA's own reserves following the 2022 World Cup were almost exactly this number.



Given the investment was offered on such favourable terms to private investors, there appears no reason why FIFA couldn’t have just used its own reserves to fund FFE allowing for 100 per cent of any profits to stay within the organisation. It’s a moot point now FFE has been shelved, but one that has led to a wider debate over how FIFA should use its reserves.

Several federations, including the English Football Association, are in favour of FIFA depleting their reserves in order to better fund members. This is due to FIFA being a not-for-profit organisation and a confidence that the organisation's revenue streams will continue to grow.



Infantino had promised federations who endorsed FFE two joining bonuses: an initial payment worth $20m, and a secondary one for the same amount.

Ceferin and Montagliani argue FIFA has more than enough money to self-fund without the need for private investors.

"FIFA currently holds billions of dollars in accumulated reserves," the letter goes on to read. "These resources belong to football and exist to serve the game and its 211 Member Associations.

4 FIFA have been told to stop withholding 'billions' that currently sit in its reserves Credit: AFP



"Prudence should not prevent a careful examination of whether a portion could responsibly be released to the extent those reserves exceed FIFA's foreseeable needs.

"Releasing part of these reserves would demonstrate that member associations should not have to choose between development and good governance; between investment and integrity; or between financial support and the ability to consider proposals on their merits.

"Development is an institutional responsibility of FIFA – not a matter of individual discretion."

UEFA and CONCACAF have been lobbying other confederations to support their motion ahead of the next FIFA Council meeting on October 15 in Zurich.



Meanwhile, Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt has called on Infantino and FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafström to release all documents relating to FFE, and to publish the reasoning behind why US striker Flo Balogun's red card against Bosnia was suspended making him eligible to play in the World Cup last sixteen tie with Belgium.

As talkSPORT exclusively revealed, Infantino was lobbied by US President Donald Trump to review the ban.

4 Infantino is under huge pressure after a controversy-filled World Cup and due to his FFE plans Credit: Getty

Infantino has been under significant pressure to stand down following both that incident and the ill-fated FFE proposal. Yet the FIFA President has vowed to fight on, and no candidate has yet come forward to stand against him.



That could change between now and the November 18 deadline, according to UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister. The former Wales international has been one of the leading voices within UEFA pushing for FIFA reforms, including a new president.

'There has to be a challenger for Infantino'

"In the weeks since the exposure of FFE, we have seen a gradual seeping lack of confidence in the leadership of Gianni Infantino," McAllister told talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs at the World Football Summit in Madrid.

"It wasn't just about that initiative, there have been a series of episodes or incidents over recent months and years that have undermined the confidence in his leadership.

"Most recently, there was the overturning of the red card of Balogun at the World Cup, and the FIFA Peace Prize over which there was no consultation… despite it being hugely political.



"There has to be a challenger to Infantino because he will certainly, as he already said, be a candidate in the election unless something dramatic happens in the coming weeks. Of course, it could do, but legal processes [including UEFA putting together a criminal case against Infantino and FIFA] take a long time, so let's not hold our breath over that.

4 UEFA's vice president, McAllister, believes a candidate has to rival Infantino for FIFA presidency Credit: Getty

"There has to be a candidate who, first of all, can command the support of all modernisers beyond just Europe. Football doesn't belong to Europe. Yes, we [UEFA] are a very powerful confederation and, yes, we generate a lot of funds, but football belongs to every single federation and club across the world. On this, I agree with Infantino that football doesn't belong to anyone in any geographical location.

"We have to unite people around a candidate, or maybe more than one candidate, and that candidate, whoever he or she is, has to stand on a manifesto of agreed reform: of greater transparency or greater accountability, of less political interference and must recognise the role of the FIFA President should be to run football, and not [like Infantino] to involve himself in other ventures, whether that's via the private or political sectors.



"I hope very much there will be a candidate [to rival Infantino] and I think that's where we are at the moment. Lots of work is happening behind the scenes. But we need a candidate with an ethos of credibility and modernisation, showing why they should win the election next March."

Behind the scenes, both Infantino and prospective candidates, including Montagliani, are doing the maths to determine where the votes lie.

Infantino went into the 2026 World Cup with 200+ letters of endorsement. Several of these have been revoked, but the FIFA President currently still has more than 106 Member Associations on side despite a wave of withdrawals of support from Europe.

That’s why Infantino remains so bullish about winning another term, but the landscape could yet change if another candidate emerges to rival him.

Sports.title: Harry Kane creates Bundesliga history as he smashes 49-year record for Bayern Munich
Sports.content:
Harry Kane creates Bundesliga history as he smashes 49-year record for Bayern Munich

Harry Kane has become the fastest Bundesliga player in history to hit 100 goals.

The England captain scored twice for Bayern Munich in a 7-0 win over Union Berlin on Friday night to set a German top-flight record.



3 Kane tucked away a penalty for Bayern to reach 100 Bundesliga goals on Friday night Credit: AFP

Kane found the target for the 100th time in the Bundesliga since his 2023 move from Tottenham Hotspur.

He managed to reach a century of goals in just 98 appearances by tucking away a penalty in the 39th minute of the game.

This has smashed the record previously held by German icon Dieter Muller, who took 129 matches to score 100 in 1977 for FC Cologne.



He then went on to score a second time and reach 101 goals, netting another after 54 minutes at the Allianz Arena.

Since joining Bayern three years ago, Kane has remarkably scored a goal every 78.5 minutes in the Bundesliga.



That is a better rate than Erling Haaland and Robert Lewandowski.

In Bayern's last match, a 2-1 win over Elversberg, Kane became the fastest player in their history to hit 150 goals too.

The 33-year-old managed to do so in his 153rd Bayern appearance.

Last season, he scored 61 goals in 51 matches across all competitions and won the European Golden Boot with 36 league strikes.



Closing in on the Ballon d'Or?

Kane is in a strong position for the Ballon d'Or title, with the striker one of the favourites to be crowned at next month's ceremony.

3 Kane smashed home from the spot to reach a century faster than any other player Credit: Getty

Should he win, he would become the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to receive the honour.

And his record-breaking strike is sure to have increased his chances of pipping Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the post.



However, speaking ahead of Friday night's game, where he has made history, he wasn't keen on speaking about the award.

Kane told Marca: “I don’t like to speak about myself… 73 goals speak for themselves.

“It’s been the best season of my life, by far.”

Bayern led 3-0 at half time against Union Berlin, with Kane's penalty the second of the evening in Munich.

3 Kane and Bayern thrashed Union Berlin at the Allianz Arena, with Olise scoring a hat-trick Credit: Getty



Jamal Musiala opened the scoring after 18 minutes before Michael Olise added the third just before the break.

And then Kane added another to double his tally and put Bayern 4-0 up and cruising - but the scoring didn't stop there.

Olise would go on to score a hat-trick and Ismael Saibari also got in on the act, as Bayern thrashed Union Berlin 7-0.

Sports.title: History-making WSL side building new training ground ‘better than most Premier League clubs’
Sports.content:
London City Lionesses owner Michele Kang believes their new training ground will be better than Premier League teams' facilities.

The WSL club, who are the first-ever team not affiliated with a men's side to reach the top flight, are building a new training centre.



3 London City Lionesses are building a new state-of-the-art training ground that will compete with Premier League clubs' Credit: Getty

It is expected to open within the next year, as they continue to take big strides in the women's game under Kang's ownership.

Kang has invested a huge amount of money into the women's football sphere and has transformed London City Lionesses.

Within 18 months of taking over in 2023, they achieved promotion to the WSL, and they've gone from strength to strength since.



Last summer, they broke the women's transfer world record by signing Grace Geyoro from Paris Saint-Germain, before going on to bring in multiple other new superstars this year.

London City Lionesses incredibly brought two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas to the club from Barcelona, also signing her teammate Mapi Leon and ex-England goalkeeper Mary Earps.



As well as investing on the pitch, the club are now in the process of building a new training ground - and it's going to be special.

New training ground 'better than Premier League clubs'

Kang told BBC Sport: "We're building a state-of-the-art training centre for our female athletes dedicated to them, built and designed for them, which will open in less than a year.



"Our architect, who has built several Premier League training centres, told me that by the time the London City training centre is up and running, it would be better than the majority of Premier League men's teams' training centres."

On the importance of making sure the women's game is equal to the men's, she added: "We have to take care of our female players better so that they can train, perform, and thrive as female athletes, not small men.

"You drive your boy to a state-of-the-art training centre and then, if you're lucky enough to have a facility nearby, you drive your girl somewhere else. Why would you accept that?"

3 Two-time Ballon d'Or winner Putellas is London City Lionesses' captain amid investment on and off the pitch Credit: Getty



3 Owner Kang believes the club's new facility will rival some of the best in English football as a whole Credit: Getty

London City Lionesses' new training facility will also help in research into injury rates in the women's game going forward.

"There are more ACL injuries among female players. Two or three times more female players get ACL injuries than male players," Kang continued.

"Something like 94 per cent of all science medical research is dedicated to men. So there's just fundamentally so little known about the female body."



How are London City Lionesses doing this season?

Two games into the WSL season, London City Lionesses are sitting seventh in the table and three points off the top.

They have won one and lost one of their opening games.

In their first game of the league campaign, they beat Manchester United 2-1, as Putellas made her WSL debut.

But a defeat to West Ham followed and now they're preparing to take on Charlton Athletic on Saturday afternoon.

Sports.title: Forgotten ex-Man United defender finds surprise new club after successful trial
Sports.content:
Tyrell Malacia has a new club after leaving Manchester United in the summer with FC Cincinnati snapping him up.

The Dutchman was released by the Red Devils after joining the club from Feyenoord in 2022.

2 Injuries ruined Malacia's time at Old Trafford, and he became the forgotten man Credit: Getty

The left-back has signed a one-year deal with the MLS side after going on trial with the club last week.

Speaking to the club's website about the deal, General Manager Chris Albright said: “We are excited to add a player of Tyrell's experience.

“He's played at the highest levels of the game and knows the demands of competing at that level.

"His quality on the ball, defensive instincts, and desire to win will add to this group and we're happy to welcome him to Cincinnati.”

Lifeline

Malacia arrived at United for around £15million, and he was seen as the eventual replacement for Luke Shaw.

He played an important role for the Red Devils as they made it to the quarter-finals of the Europa League, starting the majority of the games.

In the Premier League, he rotated with Shaw and ended the season having made 39 of the 50 total appearances he managed for Manchester United.

During that season, he also headed to Qatar with the Netherlands squad for the 2022 World Cup.

But the year ended horribly and began an awful period for the defender.

He suffered a knee injury that required surgery ensuring that he didn't play at all during the 2023/24 campaign.

2 Malacia was released at the end of last season and has been searching for a club since Credit: Getty

The following year saw him return from injury only to be loaned out to PSV Eindhoven in the second half of the season.

During that season, Malacia publicly spoke about his injury hell.

He said: “We spoke to the guy who did my [first knee] surgery and then we made the decision: we had to do something else. I had to start my rehab over, basically… I had one day to be disappointed.

"Then I had to be like, ‘OK, we go again’. I think at the end of the day, everything I did, even if it was a mistake or something, I won’t even see it as a mistake because it’s a lesson.

"I think everything in life is already written for me. I had to go through this whole process to be where I’m at now, so I wouldn’t do anything different."

In the 2025/26 campaign, Malacia managed just 15 minutes for United's first team.

But having now secured a move to Cincinnati, Malacia will hope he can get his career back on track.

Sports.title: Arsenal told they could go invincible again thanks to vital ingredients
Sports.content:
Arsenal told they could go invincible again thanks to vital ingredients

Arsenal have the right manager with the right mindset to go invincible for the second time in the Premier League.

That's the view of former Gunners left-back Ashley Cole who feels they have created the perfect environment for glory.

5 Arteta's side are already winning by any means necessary, as they did last season Credit: Getty

Arsenal, led by the fiercely determined Mikel Arteta, won the title last season by seven points ahead of Man City.

It saw the apprentice finally get the better of the master as Pep Guardiola failed to fend off his fellow Spaniard.

In previous campaigns, the Gunners were superb challengers but gained a reputation for losing their nerve at the vital moment.

Last term though, they were ruthless in pursuit of their first title since 2004, when the team, which Cole played in, went unbeaten and earned their Invincibles tag.

As such, while they lost one extra game last season, they managed to get into the habit of turning draws into wins.

And if they continue to build on that habit with their impressive mindset, Cole doesn't think an unbeaten season is out of their reach having already won all of their first four games.

He told talkSPORT at the launch event of the Topps Flagship Premier League 2026/27 Hobby Box in Fanatics Collectibles on Regent Street: "I don't see why not.

"I think Mikel has had that group now for four or five years. He's been allowed to bring in his own players and take players out.

"I think they've created a great environment where players understand now is about winning. You've got to continue to keep winning.

"They are the champions, so they are going to go into the season, which they've already shown, with a personality, a belief, a desire and a hunger to not just regain the Premier League, but can they do more in the Champions League? They had a taste of that last season and fell a little bit short. They had a great season last year, but you always want to better what you did the previous season.

5 Cole was speaking at the launch event of the Topps Flagship Premier League 2026/27 Hobby Box in Fanatics Collectibles on Regent Street Credit: Topps

5 Arsenal won the Premier League title last season and celebrated in style Credit: Getty

"So, big boots to fill, but I think they've got the players, the squad, the mentality, the environment to do it.

"Can they go unbeaten? It's not easy, but they have got the players and I think they've got the manager with the mindset now. So, who knows?"

Cole, speaking at the Topps Flagship Premier League 2026/27 Hobby Box launch was once a keen collector himself.

Now his son is doing the same and Cole spoke about the joy of a new generation finding his cards.

He added: "I've got big memories of collecting. I think every little bit of pocket money I had, I would go into the local shop and buy the cards and spend the whole day putting them in the sticker books, whether it's a sticker or a card, where you put them in a little case.

"It's definitely something I always did as a child and now I have a son, 10 years of age, and he loves it.

5 Cole opened hobby boxes of the Topps Flagship Premier League 2026/27 set with the SideCards crew at Fanatics Collectibles Credit: Topps

"It's like going back to my childhood and now I help him swap and exchange cards and he also picked me out as well, so that was quite incredible."

Asked about the experience of seeing himself in a collection, he replied: "It's quite crazy really because as a young boy I never thought I'd be in the position where I would play for my boyhood club and then actually seeing myself on a card wearing a shirt. It is absolutely mind-blowing.

"Then 20, 30 years down the line, now I have my own kids and I still see my name and see my card and see my face on the card in different shirts. It's incredible and I look back now and think, I lived out a dream and it's still continuing by having my face on these cards."

Things are a bit different now with Topps innovating within the industry.

Autographed cards and cards with shirt patches inside are now chased by fans and Cole loves that they can now own a piece of their favourite star's history.

He added: "It's incredible how they've evolved and developed.

5 Cole joined fans at the launch event for Topps' Flagship Premier League 2026/27 Hobby Boxes Credit: Topps

"Now you get the opportunity to get a card with an authentic piece of shirt on it. It's mind-boggling to understand that that can fit on a card and you can have a part of that player's journey with the picture signed from the player.

"It's brilliant. I think it just adds a different layer to it and a better layer and now you become part of that player's career as well, which I think is special."

Sports.title: Alexander Isak risks further Newcastle anger after declaring it was ‘easy decision’ to leave
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak risks further Newcastle anger after declaring it was ‘easy decision’ to leave

Alexander Isak has revealed that it was an 'easy' decision to leave Newcastle United and join Liverpool, and he regrets nothing.

The Swedish international departed the Magpies on transfer deadline day to join the Reds in a British record £125million deal last year.



4 Isak has three goals so far in his second season at Liverpool after joining the club from Newcastle in controversial circumstances Credit: Getty

However, the move was far from amicable.

After helping the Magpies win the Carabao Cup and qualify for the Champions League, Isak refused to play in any of Newcastle's pre-season games.

He spent part of the summer training away from the club in an effort to force a move away from Tyneside.

Newcastle rejected a couple of offers from Liverpool and the season started with Isak refusing to play in the first three games of the year.



The striker released a bombshell statement at one point in which he claimed the club had broken some promises to him.

In the end, Newcastle managed to sign Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa, allowing Isak to complete his transfer to Liverpool.



And in his first proper sit-down interview of the season with the BBC, Isak insists he made the right decision.

What has Isak said on his Newcastle exit?

Isak admitted: "[Liverpool] is a massive club, and everything about the club made it an easy decision.



"And the club's ambition and the club's will to get me in as well. It was a big part of it.

Asked if he regretted the switch, he added: "No, never. I would never think like that."

4 Isak was one of the best strikers in the world at Newcastle and is looking to rediscover this form again Credit: Getty

4 Isak is the main frontman for Liverpool under Andoni Iraola with Hugo Ekitike out Credit: Getty



Bouncing back

After missing all of Newcastle's pre-season to force through his move to Anfield, Isak was well short of fitness.

The 26-year-old's first start in the Premier League for Liverpool came at the end of September against Crystal Palace.

He didn't score a top-flight goal until the end of November against West Ham.

Isak then suffered a broken leg while scoring against Tottenham after a Micky van de Ven tackle in a desperate attempt to stop the goal.



But Van de Ven accidentally crunched Isak, and he returned near the end of the year to score one more goal against Palace at Anfield.

Speaking about that injury, Isak said: "[The leg break] was tough. Anyone who had a long injury would know. But on the other hand, when you're in a good place and when you feel good, you don't really tend to look back because it doesn't really benefit you. So I'm just looking forward and feel really optimistic and excited about the season, and what it can bring to us."

4 Isak has already matched his Premier League goal tally from last year Credit: Getty

Mixed start

The opening game of the season saw Isak return to St James' Park for the first time since his move.



He was booed throughout and called a 'rat' by the Toon fans, who rather enjoyed his miss in the second half during the 2-2 draw.

Isak then scored at home to Nottingham Forest and grabbed a double in a 2-0 win over Ipswich Town.

In that match, he looked much more like the Isak of old, but since then, he's blanked against Atletico Madrid and Fulham.

However, Isak believes Liverpool will go on to have a great season.

"Everyone knows that success for this club is winning trophies. I want to score every game. Everyone is different. Some like to set targets and some don't. I'm the one that doesn't."

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso hits out at Chelsea stars for dropping their 'competitive mentality' as Blues boss sends warning after dismal 3-0 defeat by Brentford
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso bemoaned his misfiring Chelsea team after they lost their drive at Brentford – shipping three goals in a drab second-half showing.

Defeat leaves Chelsea winless in three games before the three-week international break, losing away to west London neighbours Brentford for the first time since their promotion to the Premier League in 2021.

Chelsea were undone by three second half goals as Alonso's side failed to test Caoimhin Kelleher after the interval, failing to score for the first time this season.

Speaking post-match, Blues boss Alonso accused his team of lacking 'competitive mentality' – admitting he has a tough job on his hands.

'We dropped our consistency and competitive mentality in the second half,' said Alonso.

'The small details can be decisive. You don't have to give advantage in these kind of games where they do with little, they get a lot and credit to them.

Xabi Alonso hit out at his Chelsea players for dropping their 'competitive mentality' in their 3-0 defeat by Brentford

The Blues go into the international break on the back of no win in three and were second best in west London

'It's about 90 minutes and we have not been able to keep that level throughout these few games at the start of the season. It's something we have to do better.

'It's a process and it's still five games in a competitive Premier League where each game is really hard. We knew it was going to be hard, so (the job) is not going to be easy at all.'

Meanwhile, Brentford boss Keith Andrews believes his side showed the determination which Chelsea lacked.

'We've shown different kind of attributes in the last few weeks where we've had to dig deep, show real great resilience,' said Andrews.

'Our opposition are setting up in a very respectful way to try and nullify what we do then the onus is on us to try and overcome that.

'I felt there was a performance bubbling; I could see it in the players' eyes over the last couple of days.

'The approach has been really focused and I thought in the second half we showed exactly what we are.

'I think there's a really nice connection between the fans and the players and the club in general that is growing all the time. Everyone is enjoying the journey that we're on, especially me.

'I just love watching us play. I love being here. I love feeling that energy from the crowd and the way we play it.'

Sports.title: Chelsea lacked the commitment, intelligence and energy of supposed title challengers in 3-0 defeat by Brentford: Familiar failings haunt Xabi Alonso as we have seen this softness before, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Chelsea may have started their Premier League life under Xabi Alonso with a hint of promise but it’s at places like Brentford’s Gtech Stadium where flaws tend to emerge. Here under west London’s Friday Night Lights, Alonso’s players came up short in a fashion that has become rather familiar.

There is a new coach and some new players at Stamford Bridge but we have seen this softness before. In a poor game that saw Brentford simply more familiar with each other and indeed the details of the task in hand, Chelsea lacked cohesion, intelligence and, most crucially of all, the levels of commitment and energy required of a team supposedly with title aspirations.

Brentford took time to get going themselves but once they did, late in the first half, they were the better team for a distance. Cleverer, quicker, hungrier. Keith Andrews’ team head into the weekend in third spot and will reflect on two goals that come straight from their training ground.

The set piece routine that gave Jaidon Anthony his first Brentford goal looked simple but takes practice. Then, late on, Chelsea were hit with the kind of rapid counter attack that has downed big teams in this part of London before.

Chelsea had some injuries and, as such, both Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck played. They were territorially superior for a while. But they faded dismally as the night wore on and after three games without a win – a draw and two defeats – they may well be in the bottom half by Sunday night

It was a surprise to see Henderson in the Chelsea team. Only hours earlier at Wembley, the England manager had declared him unfit for international duty.

Brentford took time to get going but once they did, late in the first half, they were the better team for a distance

Fabio Carvalho buried Brentford's third in a rampant second half against Alonso' side

Regardless, it was the 36-year-old’s Chelsea debut and the fact he was making it against the team he left in the summer led to a rather predictable reaction from the home fans.

Mind you, he wasn’t the only one. With Chelsea’s Emi Martinez and Valentin Barco being booed simply for being Argentinean, this was not a quiet first half in west London even if the football did nothing to stir the soul.

MATCH FACTS Brentford (4-2-3-1): Kelleher 7; Kayode 6 (Hickey 68, 6), Schuster 8, Ajer 6, Lewis-Potter 7.5 (Malick Diouf 80); Yarmoliuk 6 (Sangare 68, 6), Janelt 6; Anthony 6.5 (Ouattara 81, 6), Damsgaard 6 (Carvalho 87, 7), Schade 6.5; Thiago 6.5. Booked: Igor Thiago. Goals: Anthony 61, Thiago 83, Carvalho 90+3. Manager: Keith Andrew 7. Chelsea (3-4-2-1): Martinez 6; Fofana 6 (Acheampong 71mins 6), Lacroix 6.5, Colwill 6; Neto 6 (Estevao 87mins 6), Henderson 6.5, Barco 6 (Nicoll-Jazuli 97mins), Chavarria 6; Palmer 6.5, Rogers 6.5; Welbeck 6 (Quenda 71mins 6) Manager: Xabi Alonso 5 Referee: Andrew Madley 6

This was, in fact, an awful game in the first half and even the stadium announcer appeared to have a little sarcasm in his voice when he declared at the interval that the score is ‘exactly the same as it was at the beginning’.

With Alonso’s team involved in so many high scoring games so far this season, this had to happen at some point. It was surprising that it was here, though. Games at the Gtech don’t tend to be dull.

Chelsea – missing Reece James and Joao Pedro through injury – also had Danny Welbeck in the team and he and Henderson were among Chelsea’s better players during an open half an hour they shaded. Cole Palmer – back in the England squad – was also prominent.

Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher was required to save well to his right when a mistake from Keane Lewis Potter allowed Pedro Neto to shoot in the 10th minute. At the back end of the half, meanwhile, Morgan Rogers shot powerfully after a run and low cross from Pep Chavarria set him up. Jannik Schuster stood firm to take the shot in his midriff.

At the other end, Brentford took an age to get going. There was none of the home team’s usual energy. On the touchline manager Keith Andrews conducted a constant dialogue with the fourth official. Maybe he was asking him if he fancied a run in the centre of midfield.

As half-time neared there were some Brentford flurries. They found some momentum. Martinez dropped easily enough on a low shot from Yehor Yarmoluik before Kevin Schade's effort was blocked, allowing Lewis-Potter to curl an effort that was well anticipated by the Chelsea goalkeeper.

It was a surprise to see Henderson in the Chelsea team as only hours earlier at Wembley, the England manager had declared him unfit for international duty

Brentford managed to take some of that momentum into the second half and for a while Chelsea were becalmed. Henderson had been like a fulcrum in the first half as his team ticked over but the veteran’s influence waned as Brentford’s energy began to surge and with it their confidence.

Lewis Potter caused Chelsea particular problems with his scurrying runs down the left and it was from a corner on his side that Brentford took the lead.

There was nothing overly fancy about. A delivery to the far post, a header back across from Schuster and a nod from a yard from Anthony. Just shows what happens when you actually keep your eyes on the ball.

Chelsea tried to rally but couldn’t. Barco’s appeal for a penalty with fourteen minutes left was weak and when Schuster sent Kevin Schade clear in the 83rd minute, he was denied by Martinez only for Thiago to gobble up the rebound.

Fabio Carvalho wrapped up proceedings with Brentford's third in the fourth minute of stoppage time. A just reward for the 24-year-old, who spent the last year recovering from a knee injury.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi's own comments about Tottenham's DNA have come back to bite him - they are still yet to replace the goal scoring void left by Harry Kane and Son Heung-min, writes MATT BARLOW
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi's own comments about Tottenham's DNA have come back to bite him - they are still yet to replace the goal scoring void left by Harry Kane and Son Heung-min, writes MATT BARLOW

For a club synonymous with Harry Kane and Jimmy Greaves, Tottenham's ongoing quest for a Premier League goal is an embarrassment.

Greaves, whose 357 English top-flight goals remain a record 55 years after his playing career ended, once joked about suffering a goal drought. 'The worst 15 minutes of my career,' he said.

Kane, the modern equivalent, who beat Greaves to become the club's all-time top scorer and was in overdrive at Bayern Munich last season, has scored more goals (42) than Spurs (35) in 2026.

Roberto De Zerbi knows this rich history only too well. Back in April at his first press conference as Spurs boss, he spoke of his aim to recreate the thrills of Ange Postecoglou's first season.

'The DNA of this club… is to find the goal, to score,' declared De Zerbi and yet here he is five months on with numbers conspiring against him.

Spurs have failed to find the net in their first four Premier League games of this season with the clock ticking towards seven hours.

Roberto De Zerbi said Spurs' 'DNA is to find the goal' - they are yet to score in the Premier League this season

The 47-year-old Italian has never known anything like it.

'No never,' he conceded ahead of the visit of Aston Villa, on Saturday, the last chance before an extended international break. 'I conceded too many goals maybe but (problems) to score, no.'

Quite how Thomas Frank was able to get through an otherwise excellent shift on Match of the Day last Saturday without fielding a single question on goal-shy Spurs is a mystery.

Frank was jeered out of N17 with his team in freefall in February, having been criticised for extreme caution and over-reliance on set pieces for goals, and taunted by Spurs fans singing 'Boring, Boring Tottenham'.

De Zerbi swept in with two years of fluent football at Brighton fresh in the mind, only to run into similar problems once relegation had been averted.

What are your thoughts on that Thomas? Surely, Thomas has pertinent thoughts on that.

Frank hit trouble when he loosened his trademark solid defensive structure in search of more creativity, then found his team leaking goals at an alarming rate, then was floored by an injury crisis and did not recover.

Spurs spent big on reinforcements at the back and in midfield, which will help, but there is still no reliable source of goals to replace the void left by Kane and Son Heung-min in recent years.

There is still no reliable source to fill the void left by Son Heung-min (left) and Harry Kane (right) at the club

Instead, only the hope Omar Marmoush or Savio, signed for a combined cost of £135million, might rediscover their prolific form from days before Manchester City.

Or Dominic Solanke might regain full fitness and stay fit and have a season like he once had at Bournemouth. Or Mohamed Kudus, James Maddison, Mykhailo Mudryk or Dejan Kulusevski might return from their long absences and solve the puzzle.

Of the eight Premier League goals scored under De Zerbi, two came from Joao Palhinha, now at Benfica, and two from Richarlison, now firmly out in the cold, a one-man sideshow having been omitted from the squad because he asked to leave and then refused all offers.

One came from Xavi Simons, in the squad at Richarlison's expense despite a serious knee injury expected to rule him out until next year.

The others have been scored by Mathys Tel, Conor Gallagher and Pedro Porro. Tel, goalless in 457 minutes, started the first three games of this season only to be dropped after a stalemate at Nottingham Forest when Spurs did not have a shot on target.

Someone at the club must be wondering about the wisdom of selling Will Lankshear, a 21-year-old centre forward, who has scored eight in ten games since joining Middlesbrough for £20m in July.

But De Zerbi is not. 'No,' said the Spurs boss when asked if it might go down as a mistake. 'Solanke is a good player. Marmoush is a good player. The Richarlison situation changed in the last five days and was not my decision. Three strikers, how many strikers do you want? I think three strikers are enough.'

Instead, he puts this drought down to 'coincidence' and promised to figure it out. 'Sometimes you have to change everything, sometimes you have to improve what you are doing and sometimes you have to stay calm. We are working to improve and be better but also we have to stay calm because with our performances we could have more than two points.'

De Zerbi remians certain that the likes of Omar Marmoush (pictured) can solve the problem

Former Spurs favourite Rafael van de Vaart has a less flattering view. 'I can't even bear to watch them anymore,' fumed Van de Vaart on the Dutch podcast 'Rondo'. 'I find Tottenham truly awful to watch. When you spend that much money on those players, I find it truly incredible.'

De Zerbi bristled when asked before Tuesday's Carabao Cup defeat at Liverpool if his players had been doing extra shooting practice. 'What do you think?' the Italian replied. 'We are doing it.'

There have been flickers of progress. De Zerbi pointed out 'nine clear chances' at Anfield and spoke of the need for 'a click' whether that is a slice of fortune to secure a win and instill confidence or a combination of players who can find the right chemistry.

Time is on his side. It is September with 34 fixtures to play and no European competition – and no Carabao Cup now either – to interfere with his work on the training ground.

These opening bars of the season can be deceptive.

Four games into last season, Spurs were third with nine points and eight goals scored and Frank had been acclaimed for installing the tactical flexibility absent under Postecoglou.

At the same stage of last season, Aston Villa were next to bottom with two points and no goals, identical to Spurs now. Unai Emery's team ended up in fourth and won the Europa League, their best season this century.

Before Villa's salvage operation none of the previous four teams of the Premier League era who failed to score in their opening four games were relegated either.

Unai Emery's Aston Villa were in the same position last season and salvaged their year to finish fourth in the Premier League

Newcastle in 2005/06 finished seventh. Swansea in 2011/12 and Crystal Palace in 2017/18 finished 11th and Sheffield Wednesday 1994/95 finished 13th.

Spurs and Coventry are newcomers to this slow-to-score roll of dishonour.

Villa have found the net this season albeit just once – Alysson against Forest – and are a point down on the same stage last year.

There are mitigating factors. Emery has been stripped of six of the starting XI from the Europa League final, plus key staff members and are committed to a major rebuilding operation.

Millions can be spent but there are no guarantees. Spurs targeted players with Premier League experience but did not target Premier League goals. In Ollie Watkins and Morgan Rogers, Villa lost Premier League goals. They scored 26 between them last season.

Like De Zerbi, Emery has a heavy workload ahead and will hope his methods can revive Nicolas Jackson to his pre-Chelsea form or conjure something where others could not from the raw talent of Alejandro Garnacho or nurture the expensive potential of Johan Manzambi or Ibrahim Mbaye.

They are two great clubs woven together by different narrative threads but Villa will be keen to avoid the same post Europa League nosedive into a relegation scrap as Spurs.

Sports.title: Unai Emery criticises his own Aston Villa players as Spaniard hits out at side's lack of discipline in search of first Premier League win of the season
Sports.content:
Unai Emery has criticised some of his Aston Villa players for lacking discipline as they seek their first league win of the season. Villa had Joao Gomes sent off on his debut on the opening day of the campaign when they lost 4-0 at Brighton, and Emery took off Nicolas Jackson at half-time of last weekend's home defeat by Nottingham Forest as he feared the forward would receive a second yellow card. Villa have had seven other bookings in their first four Premier League fixtures, as well as three in the Champions League win over Club Brugge, and three more in the Carabao Cup victory at Coventry. Emery said: 'We must control our emotions, individually. We must reduce red cards but also some yellow cards are not necessary. 'Aaron Wan-Bissaka's yellow card at Coventry (for squaring up to Gustavo Hamer) was not normal. He and Jackson are experienced players and they must control it. 'We've spoken about it in the dressing room. It's very important in terms of how we want to build our mentality. We need to focus on playing.' Unai Emery has taken aim at his Aston Villa players for their lack of discipline in the opening weeks of the season Part of the reason former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca lost patience with Jackson was the forward's habit of picking up yellow cards. Jackson has yet to score in the Premier League for Villa since moving from Stamford Bridge for £65million in the summer.

Sports.title: Harry Kane smashes ANOTHER record as Bayern Munich star scores 100th Bundesliga goal - 31 GAMES faster than previous holder
Sports.content:
Harry Kane smashes ANOTHER record as Bayern Munich star scores 100th Bundesliga goal - 31 GAMES faster than previous holder

England captain Harry Kane is continuing to break records – now becoming the fastest-ever player to score 100 goals in the German Bundesliga.

Kane's penalty against Union Berlin on Friday night took him to treble figures in the country in 98 games – a staggering 31 games faster than the previous record holder.

German legend Dieter Muller took 129 matches to score 100 for FC Cologne, with his record coming in 1977.

He also recently became the fastest player in Bayern history to net 150 goals for the club, taking 153 games.

Only one player has reached 150 goals for one club quicker – Cristiano Ronaldo with Real Madrid. He took 149 games.

Kane has scored a goal every 78.5 minutes in the Bundesliga, which is a better rate than both Erling Haaland and Robert Lewandowski.

Harry Kane became the fastest-ever player to 150 Bundesliga goals on Friday evening

Kane would later score his 101st goal in a 7-0 win for his side.

He said upon achieving the feat: 'I'm very proud, scoring 101 Bundesliga goals in such a short time. I've loved every second of it. Playing with Michael (Olise), Lucho (Luis Dias), Jamal (Musiala), I know I'll get chances. Thank you to the team and the club. It's a great stat to have. Let's keep it going.'

The Three Lions skipper, who will next week join up with his country for the first international break since the World Cup, has been a revelation since moving to Germany from Tottenham in 2023.

He cost the Bundesliga giants £100million, and has been their anchorman ever since.

Now 33, many had wondered if he would ever return to England to try and break the record for the most Premier League goals. He is on 213 goals, with Alan Shearer leading the way on 260.

But that seems in doubt, with the forward admitting earlier this year that he is in 'no rush' to depart Bayern.

'No, not for me, I'm very happy,' he said before the World Cup. 'I made that clear to you guys. I'm really settled here. We have a fantastic team - one of the best, if not the best in the world at the moment.

'We have a top, top coach. I'm enjoying my time. The situation is calm.'

Sports.title: NBA icon Shaquille O'Neal towers over Kash Patel as he becomes an FBI special agent in bizarre scene
Sports.content:
NBA icon Shaquille O'Neal towers over Kash Patel as he becomes an FBI special agent in bizarre scene

The FBI has recruited a new special agent that stands above the rest.

On Thursday, the Bureau announced its latest session of National Academy graduates and highlighted one of the members: NBA icon Shaquille O'Neal.

The four-time NBA champion has become an honorary FBI Special Agent and received his stripes from FBI director Kash Patel – dwarfing him in size.

'Congratulations to our newest session of FBI National Academy graduates, session 299 - represented by 265 law enforcement officials from around the country,' Patel said in a post to X.

'This session is historic - FBI was honored to be joined by one of the best supporters of law enforcement in the country - @Shaq - who graduated with this session and became an honorary FBI Special Agent.'

Patel added: 'It's also the first time ever a National Academy session includes two FBI special agents - representing Pennsylvania and North Carolina - making our partnerships out in the field even stronger. Congratulations to all - proud to serve alongside each of you. Mission first.'

Shaquille O'Neal was named an FBI special agent at a graduation led by director Kash Patel

O'Neal then gave a speech to the graduating class of National Academy session 299

O'Neal also managed to add a joke about his on-air NBA analyst partner, Charles Barkley

O'Neal has long been a supporter of law enforcement and the armed forces, with his primary father figure being a US Army Sergeant. He also spent part of his life on military bases in the country and around the world.

The big man gave a speech during the graduation session, thanking all those involved for their efforts.

'Continue to do what you do. Some of you will go back to your regular jobs. Some of you will go to specialized training,' he said.

'Some of you will go do what I do, be undercover. Well, I was undercover. But I just want to say I appreciate you guys so much. Congratulations.

'I'm not here for this, I'm here for you. I want to look at you guys and say I appreciate you, I love you, and thank you very much.'

Of course, O'Neal managed to add in an extra quip during the speech: 'And if you see Charles Barkley, arrest him.'

O'Neal has previously been named a reserve officer in police departments in California, Florida and Georgia.

He will return this fall when Inside the NBA goes back to the ESPN airwaves.

Sports.title: Olympic star Keely Hodgkinson reveals bizarre 'abnormality' after MRI discovery following latest injury scare: 'My body is built differently'
Sports.content:
Olympic star Keely Hodgkinson reveals bizarre 'abnormality' after MRI discovery following latest injury scare: 'My body is built differently'

Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson says an MRI scan has revealed she has an 'abnormality' in her hamstring.

After a suspected tear last year, Hodgkinson discovered she had a 'split' hamstring, giving her two tendons instead of one.

The 24-year-old has continued running despite learning of the anomaly, although she is still trying to determine whether it is a blessing or a curse.

Following her second-place finish behind Switzerland's Audrey Werro in the 800m final at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest earlier this month, Hodgkinson announced she had sustained another hamstring tear at the European Championships in Birmingham a few weeks earlier.

Hodgkinson said: 'My body is quite literally built different. I have two tendons where the tendon tore (last year). So where everyone has one tendon, mine is split, so I have two.

'We’re trying to figure out if it’s a strength or a weakness. So when one of them tore, I still had the other one because it split like this. You don’t feel the injury until later on, when it got a bit tight.'

After a suspected tear last year, Hodgkinson discovered she had a 'split' hamstring, giving her two tendons instead of one

Hodgkinson believes it is something she was born with, adding: 'It’s just how I’m made. We found out last year when I tore it on the MRI scan.

'As a pro, it means that when one is down, I can still run on the other one that works. But as a con, maybe it’s slightly weaker than the other one that’s attached.'

Hodgkinson's primary concern, particularly after two injury-plagued years, including a lay-off lasting more than 12 months, was how it would affect her racing.

'It’s a weird one,' Hodgkinson explained. 'You can still run on them, there’s no danger of it moving (to the other one).

'I haven’t missed any training over the last three weeks. I’ve just had to alter my approach, take my foot off the speed because that’s when it’s most risky, and go at it from a strength perspective. My body heals very, very well, so I couldn’t really feel anything.

'It feels good. I’ve not really felt anything for, like, two weeks now. It’s more the mental side. You’re very hyper-aware, like, "Oh, is that something? Is it not? Do I trust my body to go again?".'

Since claiming Olympic gold in Paris in 2024, Hodgkinson's progress has been repeatedly disrupted by injury. A hamstring problem suffered the following February sidelined her for more than a year before she finally returned to competition.

She made an immediate impact on her comeback in August 2025, winning successive Diamond League races, before carrying that momentum into the following indoor season. Hodgkinson broke the world indoor 800m record in February and added World Indoor gold a month later.

Her outdoor campaign, however, has proved more challenging. The Briton has been beaten three times by Werro this year, including in the race where she surrendered her European title to the Swiss athlete.

Hodgkinson concludes her season on Friday night in London at Athlos, the all-female competition launched by Reddit founder Alexis Ohanian

Hodgkinson recently revealed that a fall while jogging along a Manchester canal during a warm-down left her with cuts to both knees and a jarring impact to her back, an incident she described as turning recent months into a 'battle'.

While she acknowledged the accident may have played a part in the hamstring issue that forced her to miss Diamond League meetings in Zurich and Brussels, Hodgkinson insisted she was not using it as an excuse for her performances.

'Part of me wants to talk about it and then part of me doesn't, because I feel like my words get twisted or people are like "oh, she's making excuses",' Hodgkinson said.

'Going into the Europeans, I thought I was in the best shape ever. But when I fell over, that kind of messed me up way more than I thought it did. I think that's what contributed to my hamstring, because I couldn't really use my quad for a while.'

Hodgkinson concludes her season on Friday night in London at Athlos, the all-female competition launched by Reddit founder Alexis Ohanian.

Sports.title: Loved-up newlyweds Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce seen in rare selfie after Kansas City Chiefs' NFL Week 1 win
Sports.content:
Loved-up newlyweds Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce seen in rare selfie after Kansas City Chiefs' NFL Week 1 win

Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift posed for a sweet selfie with a fan in the wake of the Kansas City Chiefs' Week 1 win over the Denver Broncos on Monday night.

The loved-up pair haven't been seen much together in the wake of their Madison Square Garden wedding in July, but fans were treated to a new snap this week.

The image, which was posted on social media by Texas A&M insider Billy Liucci to his 10,000 followers, showed Kelce - decked in a green polo shirt - with his arm round the man, while Swift took the photo at the front.

Both of the A-listers beamed for the camera as they gave a glimpse into their new married life - and there was certainly reason to be cheerful after Kansas City's dominant opening-day win.

It is understood that the photo was taken after the game, with Travis having showered and changed before meeting up with his now-wife Swift and their pals.

It is unclear whether it was taken at the stadium, or at an alternative venue such as 1587 Prime - Kelce and Patrick Mahomes' restaurant that the group often frequent after games.

Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift posed for a cozy selfie with a fan after the Chiefs' Week 1 win

In the Chiefs' VIP suite, Swift also took a selfie of herself with Pat McAfee on Monday night

For the win over the Broncos, Swift sat alongside her father and Hollywood A-lister Tom Cruise

The reason for Liucci's presence with the love-birds is also unclear - he is the executive editor of TexAgs and a longtime Texas A&M insider, but there is no obvious connection between him and the couple.

The new photo of Travis and Taylor comes on the same week that the Chiefs tight end used his New Heights podcast to gush over his wife's ever-improving football knowledge.

He had previously admitted that she came into their relationship lacking in the details, once believing that players were 'basically out there boxing each other on the field'.

Now, though, she has dived head first into the nuances of her husband's passion, and is regularly seen wildly cheering at games, be it at Arrowhead or further afield.

Speaking to Tom Cruise on this week's bonus edition of New Heights, Kelce said: 'Now she knows everything. She sees the flags coming in, like, "Oh, that might be a defensive hold." [I'm] like, "What'd you say, sweetie?"

Kelce enjoyed a positive night on the field, helping Kansas City to a big win over Denver

Kelce wore his green polo shirt pregame and then changed into it again after the win

'She's like, "That's encroachment." I'm like, "You know what that is?" She's on it now. She's fully engulfed in it.'

Cruise agreed with the sentiment, claiming that Swift was 'schooling me' as they sat together to watch Travis and his teammates beat the Denver Broncos 31-10.

'Just a beautiful couple, in every way,' he added of the newlyweds.

Kelce and Swift got married back in July at an extravagant ceremony at Madison Square Garden, renting the world's most famous arena out for 1,000 of their nearest and dearest.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
