Sports.title: Bruising F1 2026 will not be the end for Russell - Wolff
Sports.content:
Toto Wolff is confident that George Russell can overcome a bruising 2026 Formula 1 campaign and still become world champion in the future.

The Mercedes driver is second and 81 points behind his dominant team-mate Kimi Antonelli with just nine rounds remaining, meaning a maiden crown for the 20-year-old is a matter of time.

It comes despite Russell entering 2026 as the heavy title favourite as he maximised the W16 last year with fourth in the standings and 169 points ahead of seventh-placed Antonelli.

Very few expected Antonelli to make such a strong leap into his sophomore season after a very up-and-down rookie campaign, but he is the one to have capitalised upon the rocket ship Mercedes has delivered for 2026.

“You can have good races, bad races, good years and bad years, but we're talking about the driver that has won everything that you could have potentially won before,” said Wolff of Russell at the Spanish Grand Prix.

“Every single karting championship, Formula 3 in his rookie year, Formula 2 in his rookie year, went into the Williams. We're talking about the top driver.

“We need to find out what is it for him to be able to unleash that potential and of course, there's the psychological side. If you have a run like him this year, you're taking a beating.

“But the great ones, they recover. And I think that George has all it needs to fight for championships and even if that one has maybe sailed, there will be more.”

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

The Spanish Grand Prix was where Antonelli took his second consecutive victory after Monza, which was particularly damaging for Russell as the Italian started 19th with his team-mate on the front row.

It has all led to Russell effectively conceding that “I don’t think I am in the fight” for the title, as eight-time race winner Antonelli is romping towards becoming F1’s youngest ever champion.

A high-pressure situation that Wolff doesn’t think will affect Antonelli, especially thanks to his support network that ensures he remains level-headed for the years to come.

“Kimi from his personality, so grounded, 100% racer, not distracted from anything outside, super family situation and that's why I see no risk that he's losing the plot because he's so dominant,” added Wolff.

Read Also: Formula 1 Russell and Hamilton concede F1 2026 title chances as Antonelli dominates

“Over the next few years, it's something that we will always have our discussions like we have now. What is it that could distract him? What is it that's good for him? What kind of environment he needs? That is the discussion we have.”

“I promise you he's not thinking about it. The way this kid is able to compartmentalise and be the young kid and then get into the car and be the mature racing driver, that's why if Kimi says to himself, I'm not thinking about the championship, he's not thinking about the championship.

“And we are also trying, the parents and myself, the team is saying, you know, this is not finished. There is black swan events. They can come and you're losing something out of your hand when you didn't think it was possible to lose. So he's not going to think about it.”

Sports.title: Haas confident of getting 2027 F1 budget closer to cap with new partner talks
Sports.content:
Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu says the team is making "positive" progress with his team's search for new sponsorship, as the American Formula 1 team seeks to start pushing its yearly budget towards the cap.

F1's smallest team, Haas employs just north of 400 people and has been operating well below the budget cap in both of its iterations. Although the team currently has a title sponsorship deal with Toyota's Gazoo Racing arm, which took over from money transfer company MoneyGram for this year, it is currently looking to further augment its sponsorship portfolio.

Rumours have surfaced that the team is in talks with BWT, currently Alpine's title sponsor, which will move on the team next year as Alpine has a new title partnership with fashion house Gucci planned for 2027. This is not the first time that Haas has been linked to BWT; the Austrian company was suggested as one of its destinations after it ended its deal with Aston Martin at the close of 2021, before it moved to Alpine in search of more pink livery space.

Earlier this year, Komatsu told Sky Sports that a lack of budget was stopping the team from increasing its headcount, and from improving its tooling and infrastructure, and that his job was to find more revenue by attracting new partners to the team.

Speaking over the Madring weekend, Komatsu provided an update and stated that the team was in talks with a few different prospective partners to help bring the team's budget closer to the $215 million cap.

"We're talking to so many prospects; it's getting there. I'd say very positive about next year's budget," Komatsu stated.

"It just helps massively. But I think slowly and surely we are getting our story out there and finding great people. So, yeah, it's good so far."

Asked about the BWT rumours, Komatsu stated that "we're not going to have pink cars, if that's what you are saying!"

Komatsu added that he was not looking to prospective future drivers to make up the shortfall, and that the team was still in a position where it could focus on selecting its 2027 line-up based on performance.

Ayao Komatsu, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Ryo Hirakawa, Leonardo Fornaroli, and Rafael Camara have been conducting tests in previous cars for Haas, as the team assesses potential future drivers; Komatsu estimated that there were five in the running, presumably including current incumbent Esteban Ocon (whose performances have improved of late) and Yuki Tsunoda.

Asked if any commercial factors would have a bearing, Komatsu stated that it would only enter the picture if he had two drivers who were largely inseparable in terms of pace.

"If it's within a tenth, for instance, very, very close, then affiliation package does come into play for sure. I don't think [that will be the scenario]. I think we can choose by performance; we haven't finished the whole programme yet.

"We really want two fast drivers because that's the best way to grow this team. It doesn't matter if it's two Ferrari drivers or two Toyota drivers or two McLaren drivers.

"I mean, Fornaroli, he's a McLaren driver, right? But honestly, it doesn't matter. Whoever is the fastest, that's the best for the team.

"Again, for everybody, 400 people working here, they need to know that we've got the best driver choice that we can get hold of so that these two drivers are getting the best out of the car. Imagine taking somebody half a second off, but extra money. That's not going to be very motivating.

"And also, one position in the championship. That's quite a lot of money, right? For us, like I said, I'm staying consistent. I've always said we take drivers by performance. That's what we're doing."

Sports.title: F1 reveals 2027 calendar as Monaco joins expanded sprint schedule
Sports.content:
F1 has unveiled its 24-race calendar for the 2027 season, increasing the number of sprint weekends to 10, as it kicks off the season in Bahrain and finishes in Abu Dhabi.

The 2027 season is slated to get underway on 14 March with the Bahrain Grand Prix, which returns to its usual opener slot as a double-header with Saudi Arabia, while Melbourne's Australian Grand Prix becomes the third event on the calendar.

Following events in Japan and China, F1 heads to Miami and Montreal in May. The two events remain three weeks apart, but Canada's 23 May date means the race won't clash with IndyCar's Indy 500.

F1 first heads to Europe with the Monaco Grand Prix on 6 June, which will intriguingly receive a sprint race for the first time despite its tight street circuit not allowing any overtaking. It's understood F1 is keen to lean into Monaco's qualifying spectacle by offering two separate qualifying sessions on Friday and Saturday.

Portugal returns to the calendar for the first time since 2021 with a race at the Algarve circuit in Portimao, taking place on 20 June. The British Grand Prix follows on 4 July at Silverstone, followed by rounds in Austria, Belgium and Hungary, the latter bookending the first half of the season on 1 August.

Bahrain is scheduled to host both pre-season testing and the 2027 season opener Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

After the summer break, action continues in Italy on 5 September, followed by Madrid. Alongside Portugal, Turkey also returns to the calendar on 3 October, as the middle leg of a triple-header with Baku and Singapore.

Another triple-header follows in the Americas with Austin, Mexico and Brazil, while the Las Vegas Grand Prix becomes a standalone race on 20 November.

The season is scheduled to close with a double-header in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, both featuring a sprint format.

Monaco one of 10 rounds to organise a sprint race

Monaco is one of 10 sprint races on the calendar, up from six, as F1 management was keen to expand its number for commercial reasons. Bahrain, Australia, Japan, and Abu Dhabi are also set for a sprint debut, while the format returns to Canada, Britain, Italy, Brazil and Qatar.

"Due to the continued success and strong demand for the format, the number of Sprint events has increased from six to ten for 2027, delivering even more competitive action across the season for fans, promoters, broadcasters, and partners," F1 said in a statement.

"Since the Sprint was introduced in 2021, the data shows that total viewership of Sprint weekends is 12% higher than non-Sprint weekends, Sprint Qualifying is up to three times more popular with fans than Free Practice, 82% of attendees at Sprint weekends say it adds value to their ticket, and 75% of F1 fans believe Sprint events add greater value to a season’s calendar."

Portugal will return to the F1 calendar in 2027 Photo by: Mark Sutton / Motorsport Images

Pre-season testing reverts to a single four-day test in Bahrain from 24-27 February.

As for the conclusion of the 2026 season, F1 is adamant Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead as scheduled until further notice. However, Motorsport.com understands preparations are ongoing in Imola to host the season finale on the Abu Dhabi weekend in the likely scenario that neither Middle Eastern race can take place given the ongoing conflict in the region.

F2 has already added an additional race to its Baku schedule, an indication that the single-seater series is aiming to bolster the end of its season.

“The 2027 calendar brings together some of the most iconic circuits and vibrant cities in the world, creating an incredible stage for another unforgettable season of Formula 1," said F1 CEO and president Stefano Domenicali. "We are thrilled to welcome Portugal and Türkiye to the championship and to expand Sprint racing to ten events, giving our fans even more intensity, drama, and the wheel-to-wheel action that make our sport so special."

“The 2027 FIA Formula One World Championship calendar is a strong reflection of the global appeal and continued growth of our sport," FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem added. "With twenty-four Grands Prix across five continents, the return of Portugal and Türkiye, and the opportunity for an expanded Sprint programme, the calendar combines tradition, innovation, and fan engagement while maintaining the highest sporting standards."

2027 F1 Calendar

12-14 March Bahrain (Sprint) 19-21 March Saudi Arabia 2-4 April Australia (Sprint) 9-11 April Japan (Sprint) 16-18 April China 30 April – 2 May Miami 21-23 May Canada (Sprint) 4-6 June Monaco (Sprint) 18-20 June Portugal 2-4 July Great Britain (Sprint) 9-11 July Austria 23-25 July Belgium 30 July – 1 August Hungary 3-5 September Italy (Sprint) 10-12 September Spain 24-26 September Baku 1-3 October Turkey* 8-10 October Singapore 22-24 October Austin 29-31 October Mexico 5-7 November Brazil (Sprint) 18-20 November Las Vegas 3-5 December Qatar (Sprint) 10-12 December Abu Dhabi (Sprint)

*Subject to FIA circuit homologation

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Why F1’s sprint races are leading some fans to switch off | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has repeatedly claimed sprint races are popular among fans, though every poll RaceFans has conducted of its readers has shown the opposite.

The championship has now increased the number of sprint races to 10 on the 2027 F1 calendar but long-time reader DB-C90 doesn’t plan to watch any of it:

I gave up a couple of years ago. First I refused to watch any part of sprint weekends, then I started skipping races in time zones that were too difficult and then finally I just stopped altogether. It’s no longer the pinnacle of drivers taking cars to the edge, the regulations don’t allow any proper innovation, it’s just not the same. Ten sprints will become sprints most events, a good number of events will become three sprint events (one reverse grid) and us long term fans will be replaced by who knows what. At least I now have weekends to myself.

Sports.title: F1 drivers explain why Madring’s hyped Monumental corner failed to impress | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The Spanish Grand Prix promoters set high expectations of the new Madring ahead of its first Formula 1 race last weekend.

“The adrenaline is at 100% every lap” raved one Formula 3 driver in pre-event material issued by the promoters. They promised turn 12, dubbed Monumental, was “set to become one of Madring’s greatest challenges.”

The reality proved somewhat different. The Madring as a whole produced little action of note and Monumental was no exception, aside from Franco Colapinto’s impressive save during qualifying.

Formula 1 drivers were largely unchallenged by the 24-degree banked corner as they couldn’t tackle it at maximum speed. This was for the same reason so many of F1’s great corners have been neutered this year: their power units weren’t up to it.

“I wanted to go flat [out], but then my battery dies,” explained Max Verstappen, “so you add a lift to have better deployment. So that’s my Monumental experience.”

The original design for the Monumental corner featured a straighter, faster approach. But even with the addition of two more turns before it, drivers had to use the Madring’s much-hyped challenge as an energy-saving opportunity.

This was despite the Madring promoters claiming “the circuit is adapted to the new [F1] regulations” which were introduced for 2026.

Although the corner proved unchallenging for F1 drivers, Verstappen suspects it was more demanding for those in junior categories.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“It’s cool, the banking, but I think they should have done it the other way around,” he said. “Initially more banking and then just flatten it out.

“In an F1 car you have so much downforce. I think it’s more challenging in the other categories because it didn’t look so easy flat in other categories.

“For us, plus because our battery dies towards the end, you already slow down a bit. But I guess for the shots it looks great from the outside.”

Lando Norris agreed “it’s not the biggest challenge because you have to just save the battery through the first part of the corner.”

“It would be better if we just had no battery and more power, so in a few years maybe it’ll be more fun. But it’s still a cool feeling, it’s a different feeling.”

Norris suggested increasing the camber on more corners would improve the racing at the Madring. “Cambered corners normally allow you to follow better,” he said. “So, I think next year more corners should be a bit more cambered.”

“It’s a fun corner,” he added, “it could just be better.”

Sports.title: Mercedes risked ‘looking like idiots, like Ferrari did’ at Monza – Wolff | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff wants his drivers to avoid any clash like that between the Ferrari team mates at the Italian Grand Prix.

Charles Leclerc admitted he should not have forced his team mate Lewis Hamilton off the track on the first lap of the race at Monza.

“I can express my opinion now and say this is not on to push your team mate off in turn two,” Wolff told Sky.

However he admitted the Mercedes pair came close to a similar incident at the same corner when Andrea Kimi Antonelli caught George Russell in the final laps of the race. Antonelli ran onto the tyre marbles on the outside of turn two and drifted wide through the same gravel bed Leclerc forced Hamilton into.

“Three or four laps to the end, we had some scary moments between the two of them that we didn’t expect because George had a tyre that was shot and Kimi was a second quicker,” said Wolff.

“Did we expect them to fight like they did? Which could have ended up in a car in a gravel bed. So we could have quickly looked like idiots as well, like the Ferraris looked eventually. So it’s a fine margin.”

Antonelli caught Russell after taking advantage of a Virtual Safety Car period in the second half of the race to switch to a fresh set of tyres. Wolff said the team did not bring Russell in at the same point as he was on a harder compound and did not need a second pit stop.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“It’s absolutely the right thing we did,” said Wolff. “He was on the hard [tyre]. It was predicted to be a one-stop as the better strategy.

“The medium [tyre] was a compromise. We had to put the medium on Kimi because he started on the hard. There was just no way.

“Obviously there’s some couch warriors that will drop their comments after having watched some other material online that are saying that he was penalised [by the team], it’s complete bullshit.”

Sports.title: Social Media: Hamilton denies requesting staff changes at Ferrari | Brief
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has responded to reports claiming he has asked for staff changes at Ferrari.

“I’ve seen some of the stories that have gone out and I want to clear it up here,” he wrote in a social media post. “I’ve never asked for anyone on my team to be replaced.

“Everyone I work with works hard every day, and their dedication is what moves us forward.

“I always try to empower and lift people to be the best versions of themselves or at least see the best in themselves. I may not always achieve that but it’s my intention and what I’m here to do. We all work together and that will continue.”

Sports.title: Video: Verstappen beats amateur rivals in ‘Max vs 100’ kart race | Brief
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen won his race against 100 amateur karters in an exhibition event arranged by Red Bull at Silverstone yesterday.

“When I went to the grid and I saw where I had to start, with 100 karts in front of me, I was a little bit worried,” said Verstappen, who took 14 laps to hit the front. “After my first lap with all the carnage, I did think okay we have got this under control.

“It started to become really fun and once I started getting into a rhythm and was able to overtake them one by one and saw the gap closing, that was really exciting. It was great to just be back in a go-kart again and go back to basics, it reminded me of racing back in the day.

“It’s a really beautiful track and well designed and it was a nice touch to be able to get all the data fed through the radio too. I had a great day and it was good to come out with the win.”

Formula 1

Sports.title: Tsunoda ‘wasn’t hugely disappointed’ when Red Bull dropped him last year | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Yuki Tsunoda said he didn’t feel especially disappointed when Red Bull dropped him at the end of last season.

Red Bull promoted him to their top team at the third round of last season but chose not to extend his contract for 2026.

“When I got told, I still remember, I didn’t feel that much of a huge disappointment or devastated feeling,” Tsunoda told the official F1 channel. “Obviously I was still disappointed and pretty sad that I’m not driving next year, but it’s not like I didn’t expect it.”

Tsunoda said the pressure had been so intense over the second half of last year “I was never able to kind of breathe out much.” Red Bull told him at the penultimate round in Qatar he would be replaced at the end of the year.

While his team mate Max Verstappen went into the final round of the season with a chance to win the world championship, Tsunoda had the largest ever points deficit to a team mate in F1 history. Despite that, he said he could not have tried harder to improve his performance.

“I fought really hard,” he said. “I fought more than ever in that 2025 year. And even if I look back now, I don’t have much regret.

“I gave everything and the outcome is something I didn’t like, obviously, what I heard in Qatar. But honestly, I just gave it everything and okay, if that’s the outcome, yes, I have to accept it.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“It was something that I had to think about in the coming weeks or coming time. But still there was the Abu Dhabi race and still Max was fighting for the championship so my focus was still in Abu Dhabi to make the team happy and help Max as much as possible.”

Despite spending almost the entire season with the team, Tsunoda said he still didn’t understand Red Bull’s RB21 at the end of the year.

“Normally I’m able to understand the car, what I’m driving, what kind of characteristics, obviously [by the] end of the year,” he said.

“But it feels like even after Abu Dhabi I didn’t know what kind of car I was driving. I still don’t understand what was the issue and what kind of things made me struggle to learn about this car and get used to the car.

“I thought the confidence was there, but some races I just somehow lost confidence. I still don’t understand about the car, to be honest.”

Tsunoda said his efforts to emulate Verstappen’s approach to driving Red Bull’s car were not successful.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“One thing about myself, I think if I say completely honestly, is I have a big enough ego to not change my driving style,” he said. “I know what I’m doing in terms of driving and I believe in myself.

“So I never try to change my driving to other drivers even though that driver is competitive and fast. Obviously for Max, it’s a different case, he’s a world champion, he’s proved a lot of things.

“I still learned a lot of things from his driving, so still my core driving is the same, and then sometimes probably [that was the] first year out of any years since I started that I thought about changing my driving style and trying to do something similar to Max.

“But in my perspective, if I just look at data, I didn’t really see a huge difference in terms of driving. What I did most, and what I think now is the biggest mistake last year, was to try to replicate the set-up of what he’s doing.”

Tsunoda found Verstappen’s set-ups tended to exaggerate the handling traits he was already experiencing.

“Even though knowing that sometimes if I felt the car was very oversteery, Max’s car in theory made the car worse – more sensitive in the direction change or made the car slide more – I tended to choose that set-up, even though I was already struggling with this oversteer.

“It could happen sometimes the opposite way as well, even though I was struggling with understeer, and his car was more understeery, I tried to kind of replicate that.”

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Fixing Wrong Jab Before Dubois Rematch
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley has promised Oleksandr Usyk that he is working on his jab, but throwing more left hands will not stop Daniel Dubois from closing his right eye again. Wardley needs an answer for Dubois’ jab before worrying about showcasing his own on October 17 at London’s O2 Arena.

“Fabio, where is your jab? You never jab. Only right hand,” Usyk said.

“With all [Usyk’s] done and all he’s achieved with his background, you can’t dismiss what he’s saying,” Wardley told DAZN Boxing. “But also I’m not him. I haven’t had the schooling he’s had, the background he’s had, the timing that he’s had. Mr Usyk, I’m working on my jab. I promise. I will try and do better for you. “Adjustments need to be made. I have done it before against Frazer Clarke. I’ve proven I can change.”

Wardley is correct about the difference between them. Usyk’s jab operates inside a complete system of footwork, angles, feints and distance control built over hundreds of amateur fights. Wardley cannot reproduce that education during one training camp by increasing his lead-hand output.

His greater concern should be what comes back at him. Wardley repeatedly stood directly in front of Dubois and attempted to slip punches with his chin raised. He was not tucking behind his shoulder or using a high guard to absorb and redirect the jab. That upright posture left his face exposed to Dubois’ ramrod left hand.

Once the swelling impaired Wardley’s vision, Dubois no longer had to search for him. Every jab made the next one harder to detect, while the right hands behind it became increasingly dangerous.

The physical damage was also connected to Wardley’s feet. By the fifth round, they had flattened out and Dubois was forcing him toward the ropes. Wardley lost the room needed to make the champion reset, leaving him trapped at the range where Dubois could jab without taking a counter from a new angle.

Lateral exits matter more in the rematch than a busier left hand. Dubois has struggled against movement and sharp counters thrown over his jab. He is far more comfortable when an opponent remains at mid-range and agrees to trade lead hands with him.

Wardley (20-1-1, 19 KOs) risks turning the rematch into exactly that contest. Trying to install a disciplined, conventional jab may disturb the unusual rhythm that made him dangerous in Manchester.

His early success came through sudden explosions and unconventional angles. The looping right hand dropped Dubois (23-3, 22 KOs) twice, including once within the opening ten seconds. Dubois knew it was Wardley’s primary weapon and still failed to read its delivery.

Wardley points to his rematch with Frazer Clarke as proof that he can change. That adjustment produced a first-round knockout, but an explosive blitz did not require him to sustain a tactical plan across twelve rounds.

Beating Dubois demands something different. Wardley must maintain his defensive posture, move after punching and escape the ropes even when fatigue begins stripping away his discipline. One early right hand may finish Dubois, but Wardley cannot build the entire plan around landing it before his eye closes.

Usyk identified a weakness, but Wardley risks treating the jab as a complete cure. Unless he fixes his posture and ring position first, throwing more left hands will only keep him directly in front of the punch that began his physical collapse.

Sports.title: Richardson Hitchins-Keyshawn Davis Deserves Headliner Treatment
Sports.content:
Richardson Hitchins against Keyshawn Davis is a genuine 50-50 fight that deserves its own main event. These may be the two most naturally talented fighters at 147 pounds, even though neither has proved that talent against an established welterweight.

“I think it’s a great fight. A 50-50 fight,” Hitchins told FightHype. “Two young, athletic fighters, Olympians, undefeated and former world champions. He’s a great fighter and I’m a great fighter. I think it’s a megafight. The winner of this fight should be on the pound-for-pound list.”

The pound-for-pound claim arrives too early, but Hitchins is correct about the competitiveness. He owns the cleaner jab, sharper defensive positioning, and greater experience controlling twelve-round fights. Keyshawn brings heavier combinations, vicious body punching and more willingness to force exchanges.

Both remain diamonds in the rough at welterweight. Hitchins has completed only one bout at 147, while Keyshawn has yet to compete there. They have not earned placement above the current champions, but their natural ability may be greater than anything those belt holders have displayed.

The geography of the fight begins in the center. Hitchins wants enough room to establish his lead hand, make Keyshawn reach and fire straight counters through the openings. Keyshawn must cut off that space rather than follow him. Stepping outside Hitchins’ lead foot would place him close enough to attack the ribs and bring short hooks upstairs.

Hitchins has an answer for that pressure. He regularly uses upper-body clinches to interrupt aggressive fighters before referees separate them and return the action to long range. Keyshawn does his most damaging work when he smothers distance, attacks the body and splits the guard with uppercuts. His success depends upon working before Hitchins can grab and kill the exchange.

Their rhythms are also completely different. Hitchins operates behind measured combinations and prefers a slower fight governed by his jab. Keyshawn changes speed suddenly, exploding with clusters before settling back down. One wants every round conducted at the same controlled pace; the other wants violent stretches that force an opponent to react without thinking.

Neither man has taken clean punches from a proven, full-sized welterweight. Keyshawn must show that his offense remains dangerous at the higher weight. Hitchins must hit hard enough to prevent him from walking through the jab and turning the contest into an inside fight.

The winner would not automatically receive a mandatory position unless a sanctioning body approves an eliminator, but he would become one of the division’s leading title candidates. Matching them now removes the soft transition fights generally used to introduce boxers to a new weight.

That risk is precisely why this is not an undercard attraction. Give Hitchins and Keyshawn twelve rounds at the top of the bill to prove which diamond is ready to become a welterweight champion.

Sports.title: Jesus Ramos Illness Cancels Nursultanov Title Defense
Sports.content:
Jesus Ramos Jr.’s WBC interim middleweight title defense against Meirim Nursultanov has been removed from Saturday’s Isaac Cruz versus Nestor Bravo card in San Diego. Ramos reportedly became ill with a suspected case of food poisoning.

Dan Rafael confirmed the cancellation Friday. PBC had not released its own confirmation when the report was published.

The timing raises unavoidable questions about Ramos’ weight cut. Food poisoning may have caused the illness without any connection to his preparation, but Ramos looked enormous beside Nursultanov at Thursday’s final press conference. He looked closer to a super middleweight than a boxer preparing to reach 160 pounds.

Gastrointestinal illness combined with deliberate dehydration would make completing the cut dangerous. Ramos would have been losing fluids from two directions while still attempting to remove additional water before the weigh-in. Canceling the fight was the responsible decision, but his size raises a longer-term question about how comfortably his body can continue making middleweight.

Nursultanov (20-0, 11 KOs) pays another heavy price. He has spent nearly three years waiting for the WBC opportunity he earned by defeating Julio Alamos in November 2023. Now 33, the Kazakh has lost another training camp and still lacks a confirmed fight date.

The WBC should consider ordering full champion Carlos Adames to defend directly against Nursultanov. Adames has already been prevented from pursuing a unification with WBO champion Denzel Bentley because the sanctioning body wanted him to face the Ramos-Nursultanov winner. Waiting months for the interim defense to be rearranged would freeze all three fighters and further expose the damage created by secondary titles.

The cancellation also removes the most competitive fight beneath Cruz-Bravo. Eumir Marcial (7-0, 4 KOs) against Omar Ulises Huerta (15-1-1, 13 KOs) will now open Saturday’s DAZN broadcast at 8 p.m. ET, Francisco Salazar reported.

Marcial-Huerta offers more resistance than an ordinary prospect showcase, but it cannot replace the divisional importance of Ramos-Nursultanov. Cruz supplies the card’s name recognition. Ramos and Nursultanov supplied its competitive substance and a direct connection to WBC champion Carlos Adames. Without them, the San Diego broadcast has lost the fight serious boxing followers had the greatest reason to watch.

Sports.title: Hamzah Sheeraz Vacates WBO Belt To Avoid Janibek Alimkhanuly
Sports.content:
Hamzah Sheeraz surrendered his WBO belt the instant mandatory challenger Janibek Alimkhanuly stepped up to claim his shot. The abandonment came mere days after Queensberry secured promotional rights through a purse bid, proving this choice had nothing to do with promotional gridlock.

Ring Magazine confirmed Sheeraz officially vacated after Queensberry tabled the winning bid of $1,001,809. Top Rank submitted $820,000, which handed Sheeraz’s own promoter total control over every detail of the event.

Those figures exposed the true commercial worth of this pairing. Neither promoter viewed the bout as box-office gold, and zero outside investors showed up with huge checks. Whining about the purse split looks ridiculous when the open market spoke so clearly.

“This dude talking about money, that’s why he vacated the belt! But in reality, that’s all he’s worth! That dude don’t sell s***, and his biggest fight purse was me. Nobody paying him more than a M. Even with a world title he ain’t nothing,” Edgar Berlanga posted on X

The belt functioned as convenient decorative hardware right until a fearsome southpaw stood opposite in the rankings. Once the trinket stopped serving as a glossy marketing tool and demanded pure combat, Sheeraz tossed it aside like trash.

Janibek represents a nightmare equation for any boxer trying to protect an inflated profile. The Kazakh brings surgical accuracy, power, and a tricky southpaw attack. Defeating him earns praise from diehard purists, yet it moves very few pay-per-view units with casual British sports crowds. Suffering a brutal beating destroys Sheeraz’s drawing appeal before massive domestic paydays materialize.

Frank Warren eliminated every conceivable promotional excuse by putting actual money on the table, outbidding Bob Arum, and locking down the venue, date, and terms. Sheeraz cannot blame rival factions or outside interference. His own promoter handed him the ring on a silver platter, and Sheeraz still bolted for the exits.

Surrendering the hardware frees his schedule for an easier fight that offers fatter checks and minimal physical punishment. Matching him against Chris Eubank Jr. or another familiar domestic name sells out London arenas without forcing him to decipher Janibek’s lethal puzzle.

Official Statement: Hamzah Sheeraz has voluntarily relinquished his WBO Super Middleweight World Championship. The WBO World Championship Committee will issue its ruling on the division on Monday, September 21. pic.twitter.com/vTVq2pL7Qm — WBO (@WorldBoxingOrg) September 18, 2026

Management can celebrate the cynical financial maneuver, but the optics are terrible. Sheeraz exploited the WBO belt to puff up his name, then dropped it the second a genuine killer arrived to take it.

The entire move reveals a fighter maneuvering purely for self-preservation and a cash grab before anyone cracks his chin.

Walking away from the belt right after Frank Warren won the purse bid shows Sheeraz knows exactly what he is. If he had real confidence in his ability, he would have defended the WBO belt against Janibek, unified against another titlist, and forced Canelo Alvarez to face him on champion-to-champion terms. Bailing on the title proves the hardware was only an ornament.

Chasing Canelo through Zuffa is a pipe dream with a short shelf life. Canelo is 36, slipping, and has a dangerous test right in front of him against Christian Mbilli on October 31. Mbilli brings non-stop pressure and heavy artillery. If Mbilli upsets Canelo or tears him up so badly that the Mexican superstar contemplates retirement, Sheeraz’s golden ticket disappears overnight. Signing with Dana White on the assumption of landing a broken, post-prime Canelo is an enormous gamble for a guy whose drawing power in America is nonexistent.

Warren should not give Sheeraz a free pass on his way out the door. Handing an unloyal fighter a hand-picked, tailor-made opponent just lets him walk into a rival stable intact. The promotional playbook dictates feeding an outgoing asset to a live dog who stays with the house.

Putting Sheeraz in with an animal like Osleys Iglesias would be poetic justice. Iglesias is a sledgehammer southpaw who would expose Sheeraz’s defensive holes in three rounds. If not Iglesias, then Diego Pacheco or Lester Martinez would drag him into deep water and drown him. Martinez possesses the inside work and punch output that Sheeraz hates dealing with, while Pacheco has the height, range, and real power to test that suspect beard.

Sheeraz almost certainly has match-making approval or rejection clauses in his deal, which explains why he ducked Janibek in the first place. He will run from anyone with a pulse because taking a loss destroys the Zuffa leverage. If Warren cannot force a killer on him, he will likely sit out, run the clock down, and wait for Dana White to write a check based on inflated hype rather than actual ring merit.

Sports.title: Bakhodir Jalolov Gets Another Soft Touch At 32 Against Solomon Dacres
Sports.content:
Bakhodir Jalolov has spent eight years as a professional without facing a serious heavyweight. His October 17 meeting with Sol Dacres continues that pattern rather than ending it. An Olympic gold medalist of his pedigree should have been hunting top five contenders right out of the gate, yet he remains content taking fights meant for British title-level novices.

British promotional outlets may present Sol Dacres as a major step up, but he is nothing of the sort. Dacres is strictly British level, carries little power with only three knockouts and owns no victories over notable heavyweights. David Adeleye wiped him out in 80 seconds in December 2024. A ten-round decision over Vladyslav Sirenko does not suddenly turn a domestic fighter into a dangerous opponent.

Jalolov (17-0, 15 KOs) will face Dacres (10-1, 3 KOs) on the October 17 Daniel Dubois vs. Fabio Wardley II card at London’s O2 Arena, Dan Rafael reported on X.

Vasiliy Lomachenko fought for a world title in his second outing, and previous Olympic super heavyweight champions treated entry into the pro ranks as an immediate takeover. Anthony Joshua demolished Charles Martin for the IBF belt and stopped Dominic Breazeale by his seventeenth professional appearance. Jalolov possesses superior amateur credentials, yet he has treated the professional ranks like an eight-year paid sparring tour.

The matchup asks if Jalolov can produce an entertaining showing against a cautious, feather-fisted heavyweight. He still fights like an amateur tournament entrant, working behind a stiff jab and straight left before retreating into open space. That approach collected Olympic medals, but it does not make compelling television.

Jalolov displayed the same flaw against Agron Smakici in May. Rather than pin an inferior opponent to the ropes and unload, the Uzbek southpaw retreated to long range. Smakici quit on his stool after seven rounds, but Jalolov did nothing to generate enthusiasm.

Dacres will hide behind a high guard and make Jalolov work for his openings. Adeleye attacked Dacres immediately and blew him away. If Jalolov spends ten rounds potshotting from distance against an opponent who cannot hurt him, the comparison will look terrible.

Years spent drifting between pro bouts and the Uzbek amateur system cost Jalolov crucial development time. Joe Joyce, Zhilei Zhang and Filip Hrgovic left the amateur tournaments behind to pursue real professional tests. Moses Itauma offers an even harsher contrast, generating massive commercial interest in his early twenties by seeking out explosive finishes. Jalolov is 32 and stuck taking soft touches on undercards.

The Dubois and Wardley bill gives Jalolov a massive platform, but promoters have little use for a safety-first heavyweight with zero appetite for danger. Blowing out a harmless domestic gatekeeper is the bare minimum. Jalolov has to prove he wants to be a real professional fighter.

Sports.title: Jai Opetaia Calls David Benavidez’s Cinco De Mayo Bluff
Sports.content:
David Benavidez talked his way into a corner the moment Jai Opetaia accepted his Cinco de Mayo challenge without demanding a single concession. By surrendering location, timing, and promotional perks, Opetaia instantly stripped away every standard excuse fighters use to dodge a dangerous unification.

“I feel like me and Benavidez will fight. He’s got most of the belts at the moment. I really still believe in the undisputed dream,” Opetaia told the Mr Verzace podcast. “All I need is him to sign the contract. Let’s get the fight over the line. Whether the date works for me or not, I’m in my position. These guys are the ones picking the dates. Send me the date. Send me the location. We’ll be there.”

Benavidez climbed into the ring after Opetaia stopped Noel Mikaelian in the ninth round last Saturday at T-Mobile Arena. He called Opetaia the cruiserweight “boogeyman” before presenting himself as the man hired to kill one.

Now Benavidez must turn that television line into an actual fight.

The five-month turnaround presents the first major obstacle. Benavidez is due to challenge WBC cruiserweight champion Michal Cieslak on December 12 in Phoenix. A broken hand, severe cut, or punishing twelve-round struggle would wreck the proposed May timetable. Cieslak is not a ceremonial opponent placed there to introduce Benavidez to 200 pounds.

Opetaia presents an even harsher physical test. Benavidez built his reputation around volume, pressure, and forcing smaller men toward the ropes. Opetaia is an explosive southpaw with cruiserweight power, fast feet, and a lethal counter left hand. Marching forward behind a high guard carries a brutal price against a natural 200-pound champion.

The Australian has also flipped the promotional narrative. Benavidez is being treated as the star granting an opportunity, but Opetaia pursued Gilberto Ramirez, Lawrence Okolie, and Mikaelian long before Benavidez arrived in the division. His interest belongs to the belts rather than the personality holding them.

With both fighters connected to Zuffa Boxing, no network rivalry blocks the match. Sanctioning body politics might create headaches, but Opetaia erased location and timing from the list of outs. Benavidez only needs to defeat Cieslak and put pen to paper.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford Threatens Ryan Garcia After Direct Challenge
Sports.content:
Terence Crawford returned several hours later with an even harsher response to Ryan Garcia’s challenge, claiming the 38-year-old would punish Ryan so severely that witnesses would want the law involved.

“I’ll f*** @RyanGarcia up so bad people going to be calling the law on me talking about child abuse. Like why did you do that to that little boy you knew he was just talking for the entertainment. Here I am,” Crawford posted on X.

Ryan Garcia Dares Terence Crawford To Square Up

Ryan Garcia wants to fight Terence Crawford in the street or in the ring, daring him to settle their feud with bare knuckles. Crawford started it by calling Ryan a fake who only talks tough when his bodyguards are around.

“@RyanGarcia only talk tuff for the internet. He’s know it’s all for show. I promise if I seen him without his security guards and the cameras he’ll be a complete different person. 😂 he say I’m a bully but I was the one they got for the bullies. 😉” Crawford posted on X.

“Okay so let’s square up bro on or off the ring I’m ready to handle this,” Ryan responded.

“I’m bout to go to the gym f**k it! Don’t make me too mad I’ll be 39 in 10 Days dam.😂” Crawford posted on X, reacting to the public challenge.

Crawford mentioning his age serves as a classic two-way insurance policy veteran fighters rely on when engaging younger rivals. First, it is an obvious attempt to shame Ryan in the court of public opinion. By pointing out that he is turning 39 in ten days, Crawford paints the picture of Ryan as an opportunist barking at an older retired man.

Second, it sets up an immediate built-in excuse if they ever step into the ring and things go wrong. If Crawford fights Ryan and wins, he looks like an ageless boxing master who schooled a prime champion twelve years younger than him. If he gets caught by Ryan’s left hook and loses, the narrative shifts immediately to Father Time: Crawford was 39, long past his prime, and stepped off the couch to do it.

Veteran fighters use that trick constantly to protect their pride. It allows Crawford to dismiss Ryan publicly while simultaneously laying down the foundation for an alibi if he decides the money is too big to pass up.

Crawford has now answered Ryan’s invitation with a graphic prediction rather than an offer to negotiate a boxing match. The personal hostility is obvious. The remaining question is whether either man is prepared to turn the threats into a sanctioned fight, where Crawford’s claims would finally have consequences beyond social media.

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol Risks Artur Beterbiev Trilogy For WBO Belt
Sports.content:
Dmitry Bivol rejected a December trilogy against Artur Beterbiev to satisfy the WBO, choosing a single belt over the definitive rivalry of his era. Protecting one sanctioning body strap introduces reckless hazards that could erase the rubber match entirely.

RCC Boxing chief German Titov says Bivol-Beterbiev III is being targeted for April 2027. The fight would serve as the opening attraction at the new 8,000-seat RMK Arena in Chelyabinsk, Russia. Staging the bout there serves regional promoters while shrinking what belongs on a major global stage down to a municipal showroom.

The calendar works aggressively against public interest. Beterbiev reached 41 in January and will enter the ring at 42 by that projected date. That timeline forces Beterbiev into more than two full years of inactivity following their February 2025 rematch. Any victory Bivol manages under those circumstances will trigger claims that he simply ran out the clock on an aging destroyer.

Before any trilogy can materialize, Bivol (25-1, 12 KOs) must first get past Callum Smith (31-2, 22 KOs) on December 12 in Yekaterinburg. Treating Smith as a routine obligation overlooks the physical reality of Bivol’s July elbow surgery.

Bivol operates entirely off his lead arm. His stiff jab dictates distance, controls pace, and sets up his piercing combinations. Smith brings a punishing counter left hook that specifically targets sloppy mechanics. If Bivol carries any hesitation in that surgically repaired joint, Smith has the 6-foot-3 frame, reach, and punching power to exploit it.

Bivol is taking these risks for an organization that previously refused to sanction his defense against Michael Eifert on Russian soil. He is jeopardizing his career-defining bout to appease an alphabet body that could still pull its sanctioning status at the eleventh hour.

Vacating the title would have kept the rubber match on schedule for late 2026 without unneeded detours. Bivol chose the complicated route instead. Between physical recovery, administrative obstacles, and a dangerous puncher in Smith, Bivol is putting his defining moment on the line for plastic and leather.

Ghana News.title: Total value of secured loans hit GH¢31.5bn in quarter 2 2026
Ghana News.content:
BoG Governor, Dr Johnson Asiama

The total value of secured credit advanced and registered in the second quarter of 2026 amounted to GH¢31.5 billion, the Bank of Ghana has revealed in its Second Quarter Brief on 2026 Collateral Registry.

This reflected a substantial year-on-year expansion of 73.4% compared to GH¢18.2 billion recorded in the second quarter of 2025.

According to the report, banks continued to dominate the secured transactions landscape by value of registered credit, accounting for a total value of GH¢19.9 billion, equivalent to 63.1% of total secured credit value registered in the second quarter of 2026.

This is a 36.6% increase over GH¢14.5 billion recorded in quarter 2 2025.

This was followed by other lenders contributing GH¢8.3 billion and accounting for 26.3% of the total value of secured credit.

Comparing quarter one 2026 to quarter two 2026, the total value of secured credit increased by 57.5%. Banks and Rural and Community Banks recorded increases of 21.5% and 12.2% respectively, while Savings and Loans, Micro Finance Institutions and Micro Credit Institutions recorded declines.

Banking Sector Secured Lending

The foreign-controlled banks accounted for a dominant share of secured credit registered by banks in the second quarter of 2026.

Out of the total GH¢19.9 billion registered by banks, foreign-controlled banks registered GH¢14.1 billion, representing 71.1%.

This reflected an increase of 19.3% over the second quarter of 2025 value of GH¢11.8 billion. Indigenous banks, on the other hand registered total credit of GH¢5.7 billion during the review period, corresponding to a year-on-year growth of 112.4% from GH¢2.7 billion recorded in quarter 22025.

According to the Bank of Ghana, the distribution underscores the continued dominance of foreign-controlled banks in secured lending, while also reflecting steady growth among indigenous banks.

Ghana News.title: Ghana needs national dialogue to end political insult culture — Kpebu
Ghana News.content:
Private legal practitioner Martin Kpebu has called for a national dialogue on Ghana’s growing culture of political insults, arguing that arrests and prosecutions alone will not resolve the problem.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story, Mr Kpebu said the controversy surrounding the “Ghana Jollof” TikTok account had exposed a broader problem with political discourse in the country that required collective action.

“The first thing I’m curious about is that we all want this menace of insults against politicians and other people in society to stop. That culture of vitriol, we want to control the vitriol. It’s getting out of hand,” he said.

Mr Kpebu acknowledged that the problem cuts across Ghana’s political divide, saying political actors and commentators on different sides have at various times used language that could be considered offensive.

He cited his own past comments as an example.

“Even me talking to you, for saying Akufo-Addo is ‘manpam,’ which is a song by a musician sung against him to hold him accountable — people say that my hands are also soiled,” he said.

He also referred to remarks previously made by President John Dramani Mahama, including his use of the phrase “Akyem mafia” and an occasion when he said the President jabbed him.

“So it appears we’ve all soiled our hands one way or another. That’s how come I thought that look, this thing is not about handcuffs and police cells and trials. It’s about a national conversation,” he said.

Mr Kpebu said such a conversation could provide an opportunity for political actors and citizens to agree on limits to abusive political discourse.

“So that when we have the national conversation, we’ll call a truce,” he added.

Mr Kpebu acknowledged that the content associated with the “Ghana Jollof” account had been particularly aggressive.

“Ghana Jollof’s vitriol is higher. Nobody has more vitriol than her,” he said.

“The moment I saw that her vitriol is higher, the speed at which she launches the insults, the other guys can’t match her, I said no, let’s do a national conversation.”

He said Barbara Asantewaa Kodua, who is identified by police as the alleged operator of the account, had previously indicated that she would stop if another prominent commentator, Kevin Taylor, was restrained.

“She has stated clearly that if we can rein in Kevin Taylor, she would stop. She said that several times. There was one she even addressed to me,” Mr Kpebu said.

Police have alleged that Ms Kodua is behind the “Ghana Jollof” account and that she paid Salomey Awiti Bafoh and others to help redistribute content. Those allegations are part of the ongoing investigation and have not been established by a court.

Mr Kpebu argued that taking legal action against individuals linked to the account would not necessarily stop the wider phenomenon.

“Yesterday, whilst we were having radio interviews about Salomey in custody, Ghana Jollof was blasting and blasting even the police. So she’s still out there,” he said.

His comments come after Ms Bafoh, a 40-year-old senior nursing officer, was remanded for two weeks by the Adentan Circuit Court after pleading not guilty to a charge of abetment of crime, specifically the alleged publication and circulation of false news. She is expected to reappear in court on September 30.

The prosecution alleges that Ms Bafoh acted as a liaison for Ms Kodua and helped recruit people to redistribute videos associated with the account. Police have also alleged that some of the content could cause fear, alarm or violence.

Mr Kpebu questioned whether continued detention was the appropriate response, arguing that investigators could have relied on less restrictive measures, including the seizure and examination of her phone.

He said the approach could have wider implications for public confidence and democratic freedoms.

The case has already triggered calls for Ms Bafoh’s release and a broader debate over the balance between freedom of expression, public order and accountability for online content.

NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has described the circumstances surrounding her arrest and remand as “very worrying” and called for her release, while maintaining that political insults should not be encouraged.

Government Communications Minister Felix Kwakye Ofosu, meanwhile, has said the government can tolerate criticism and insults directed at President John Mahama but would not ignore statements it considers capable of inciting violence or breaching public order.

Against that backdrop, Mr Kpebu is proposing a broader national conversation as an alternative to relying primarily on arrests, prosecutions and incarceration.

He said the objective should be to confront the culture of political vitriol collectively and establish a more sustainable way of managing disagreements in Ghana’s public discourse.

Ghana News.title: ‘Relax, I’m not contesting you in 2028’ — DVLA CEO tells Zanetor
Ghana News.content:
Chief Executive Officer of the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA), Julius Neequaye Kotey, has dismissed speculation that he is preparing to challenge Klottey Korle MP Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings in the 2028 parliamentary election.

Mr Neequaye Kotey said that although he has the right to contest the constituency if he chooses to, he has not decided to do so in 2028.

“If I’m eyeing that seat, it’s not against any law. I have the right to contest for that seat,” he said.

He added: “For now, I have not made up my mind, so Dr Zanetor should relax. The way she is going around, she should relax. I am not going to contest her.”

Mr Neequaye Kotey, popularly known as “Logas”, said his political involvement in the constituency goes back several decades.

“This is my third time as a constituency executive. At age 17, I was a branch secretary for the NDC in the Korle Klottey Constituency, but I wasn’t allowed to register,” he said.

He said he later served as a polling agent in 2004 before becoming a branch chairman, deputy constituency communications officer and subsequently constituency communications officer.

He is currently the constituency’s Vice Chairman.

Mr Neequaye Kotey also stressed his roots in the constituency, particularly Osu.

“I am an indigene of Klottey Korle. I am from Osu. My hometown is Osu. I cut across all four traditional areas of Osu,” he said.

The DVLA CEO said he has never concealed his political ambitions and would openly declare his intentions if he decided to contest the seat.

“If I want to contest for that constituency seat, I am free. I am good and capable enough to do it, but I have said 2028; I’m not contesting,” he said.

He, however, stopped short of ruling out a possible parliamentary bid beyond 2028.

“I don’t know if the Lord will change my mind for subsequent years, but for 2028, I’m not contesting,” he said.

He added: “Even in 2028, never say never. I can decide to contest; I don’t break any law.”

“For me, I don’t hide my political ambition. If I want to contest, I will say it clearly: I want to contest,” he stated.

Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings has represented Klottey Korle in Parliament since 2017.

Mr Neequaye Kotey was appointed Chief Executive Officer of the DVLA in January 2025 and has since overseen reforms at the authority, including efforts to clear a backlog of driving licences and expand its services.

He also recently disclosed that he had rejected an alleged GH¢4 million inducement linked to opposition to the DVLA’s new number plate reforms and said the matter had been reported to the Office of the Special Prosecutor.

He spoke on Starr FM,

For now, however, Mr Neequaye Kotey says he is not preparing for a parliamentary contest against Dr Agyeman-Rawlings in 2028, while leaving his political options beyond that election open.

Ghana News.title: Insurance sector offers huge job opportunities as Ghana faces actuarial skills shortage — GIU Rector
Ghana News.content:
The insurance industry offers significant employment opportunities for young people, particularly in specialised fields such as actuarial science and statistics, Rector of the Ghana Insurance University College (GIU), Dr Richard Okyere, has said.

He urged WASSCE graduates and other young people with strong interests in mathematics, data and analytical work to consider careers in insurance, saying the sector continues to face a shortage of skilled professionals.

Dr Okyere said Ghana’s low insurance penetration also presented considerable room for growth, creating opportunities for professionals who can help expand the industry and manage increasingly complex financial risks.

“Low insurance penetration implies huge opportunity to grow with high demand for manpower,” he said.

He made the comments while speaking about the admission process and programmes offered by GIU, which was inaugurated earlier this year as a higher education institution focused on developing professionals for Ghana’s insurance and financial sectors.

Dr Okyere said GIU has a distinctive advantage because it is owned by players in the insurance industry, allowing it to maintain a direct link between professional practice and academic training.

“Here, the uniqueness is that there is a bridge between the industry and academia,” he said.

The institution evolved from the Ghana Insurance College, established in 2006 by key industry stakeholders, including the National Insurance Commission, Ghana Insurers Association, Insurance Brokers Association of Ghana and the Chartered Insurance Institute of Ghana.

Dr Okyere said the university had expanded beyond traditional professional insurance training to offer degree programmes in specialised areas.

These include a Bachelor of Science in Actuarial Science with Insurance and Statistics with Insurance.

“These are two specialised areas — actuarial insurance and statistics insurance. We have merged the two areas to produce professionals with both a computational mindset and an underwriting mindset,” he said.

According to Dr Okyere, the programmes are intended to address a shortage of actuarial and other technical professionals in Ghana and across Africa.

He said a stronger pool of local expertise was needed to help insurance companies price products appropriately, assess financial risks and make better-informed decisions.

“The aim is manpower development and the technical expertise to help manage financial risks in our markets,” he said.

He noted that the shortage of local expertise sometimes meant insurance and financial institutions had to rely on professionals from countries including the United Kingdom, South Africa and the United States.

“This does not help the country. This promotes capital flight; the country throws away significant dollars outside the country,” he said.

Dr Okyere said developing local expertise could help retain foreign exchange, strengthen the insurance industry and improve Ghana’s ability to compete in the global financial market.

The Rector said GIU was also incorporating emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, financial modelling, predictive modelling and data analytics into its programmes.

He said the approach was intended to prepare students for changing demands in the insurance and wider financial services sectors.

Graduates, he disclosed, would receive a Bachelor of Science degree jointly issued with the University of Ghana, alongside a professional diploma in insurance administered in collaboration with an overseas professional body.

Dr Okyere said experienced actuaries, statisticians, insurance practitioners, chief executive officers and academics would also be involved in teaching and mentoring students.

He urged parents and prospective students to consider insurance-related programmes as viable career options, stressing that the skills acquired could be applied beyond the insurance industry.

“The university is owned by the market, so the advantage of getting a job is there. Students here will have added leverage,” he said.

According to him, graduates could find opportunities in sectors including banking, pensions, healthcare and manufacturing, where actuarial, statistical, financial modelling and risk management skills are increasingly relevant.

Dr Okyere said GIU’s broader objective was to develop the skilled workforce needed to expand insurance coverage and strengthen financial risk management in Ghana.

He therefore encouraged WASSCE certificate holders with strong analytical and cognitive interests to explore the emerging career opportunities within insurance and related sectors.

Ghana News.title: Newsfile to discuss Ghana Jollof nurse case, cocaine shipment, COVID audit and constitutional reforms
Ghana News.content:
JoyNews’ flagship current affairs programme, Newsfile, will on Saturday, September 19, 2026, examine four major national issues that have dominated public discourse over the past week.

Hosted by Samson Lardy Anyenini, the programme will air from 8:00am to 12:00pm on Joy 99.7 FM, JoyNews and other platforms.

Ghana Jollof case and the free speech debate

The programme will examine the arrest and remand of 40-year-old senior nursing officer Salomey Awiti Bafoh over her alleged links to the controversial “Ghana Jollof” TikTok account.

Ms Bafoh was arrested at her home in Hansua, near Techiman, on September 13 and later appeared before the Adentan Circuit Court, where she pleaded not guilty to a charge of abetment of crime, specifically the alleged publication and circulation of false news under Sections 20(1) and 208 of the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29). She was denied bail and remanded for two weeks, with the case adjourned to September 30.

The prosecution alleges that Ms Bafoh acted as a liaison for UK-based TikTok user Barbara Asantewaa Kodua, popularly known as “Ghana Jollof”, and helped recruit others to redistribute videos produced by Kodua.

The allegations, including claims that some of the videos contained inflammatory statements capable of provoking violence, have not been established by the court.

The case has triggered a wider debate about freedom of expression and the use of state security agencies.

NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has called for Ms Bafoh’s release, describing the circumstances surrounding her arrest and detention as “very worrying” and warning against infringements on free speech.

Newsfile will examine the legal, constitutional and broader democratic questions arising from the case.

3.9-tonne cocaine shipment and Ghana’s security systems

The programme will also turn to the seizure of nearly 3.9 tonnes of suspected cocaine by French customs at the Port of Dunkirk on September 10.

The consignment, concealed in a container carrying plastic waste that had departed from Ghana, was valued at about €225 million.

Six people have since been denied bail by the Kwabenya Circuit Court in connection with the shipment. Four of those accused are linked to the Ghana Revenue Authority and face allegations relating to the handling of Customs scanning procedures at Tema Port.

President John Dramani Mahama has subsequently directed the formation of an inter-agency task force to develop a roadmap for strengthening measures to prevent drug trafficking through Ghana’s borders.

The task force has been given two weeks to submit its recommendations, while 10 people, including four Customs officers, are currently being held as investigations continue.

The programme will examine questions surrounding the shipment, Ghana’s port and border security systems, and the wider implications of the seizure.

COVID-19 fumigation expenditure under scrutiny

Newsfile will further examine questions surrounding COVID-19 fumigation expenditure and the apparent disparity between the Auditor-General’s special audit and figures uncovered by investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni.

The Auditor-General’s special audit reported GH¢96.3 million in COVID-19 fumigation expenditure.

However, documents from the Ministries of Education, Local Government and Transport cited in Mr Awuni’s investigation point to at least GH¢780 million spent on fumigation between 2020 and 2022. The investigation found that Zoomlion Ghana Limited received about GH¢775 million of the amount identified.

The discrepancy has prompted questions about what was captured in the special audit and why some expenditure identified in the various ministries was not reflected in the reported figure.

Vice Chairperson of Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee, Davis Ansah Opoku, has said there is no basis for arrests at this stage, arguing that the immediate priority should be for the Audit Service to explain why expenditure by the Ministries of Local Government and Transport was not captured.

The programme will explore the figures, the audit process and the accountability questions arising from the findings.

Constitutional review and calls for broader consensus

The fourth issue will be the growing debate over Ghana’s ongoing constitutional review process.

The New Patriotic Party has rejected the proposed extension of the presidential and parliamentary terms from four to five years and has called for a Constituent or Consultative Assembly to deliberate on the proposed reforms.

The party has also criticised the scale and process of the proposed amendments, arguing that changes affecting a substantial portion of the 1992 Constitution require broader deliberation.

The concerns extend beyond the NPP. More than 100 civil society organisations, labour groups and professional bodies under the Citizens’ Platform on Constitutional Reform have called for the process to be backed by legislation and clear timelines, while urging greater citizen participation.

The Citizens’ Platform has also rejected the proposed five-year presidential term, arguing that the current four-year mandate can be retained alongside other reforms to improve governance and accountability.

The government, however, has rejected the NPP’s demand for a Consultative Assembly, describing the proposal as without merit and pointing to the fact that the review process has been underway for almost two years.

Newsfile will examine the competing positions, the proposed changes and the broader question of how Ghana should reach consensus on reforms to its constitutional order.

The four issues will form the focus of Saturday’s edition as Newsfile brings together its host and panellists to interrogate developments shaping the national conversation.

Ghana News.title: CPP urges Ghanaians to revive Nkrumah’s vision of self-reliance and industrialisation
Ghana News.content:
The General Secretary of the Convention People’s Party (CPP), Harold Stephen Ato Eshun, has called on Ghanaians to renew their commitment to Dr Kwame Nkrumah’s vision of economic independence, industrialisation and African unity.

He said persistent challenges including unemployment, corruption, economic difficulties, inequality and abandoned projects should prompt the country to critically examine how effectively it controls its resources and determines its economic future.

Mr Eshun made the call ahead of Dr Nkrumah’s 117th birthday on Monday, September 21, saying the occasion should go beyond remembering Ghana’s first President to examining how his ideas could be applied to present-day development challenges.

He said Nkrumah’s vision extended beyond Ghana’s independence from colonial rule to the political and economic emancipation of Africa.

Quoting Nkrumah, he said: “Our independence is meaningless unless linked up with the total liberation of Africa.”

Mr Eshun said the statement reflected Nkrumah’s belief that Ghana’s independence formed part of a wider African project in which Africans would control their resources, determine their economic future and build economies anchored in knowledge, industry and unity.

“Without economic independence, we as Africans remain vulnerable,” he said.

Dr Nkrumah founded the CPP in 1949 after leaving the United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC). The party adopted the slogan “Self-Government Now” and mobilised support for the campaign for independence.

The CPP won the 1951 election, paving the way for Nkrumah to become Leader of Government Business and later Prime Minister before Ghana attained independence on March 6, 1957.

Mr Eshun said the CPP’s history should continue to inform national conversations about self-determination, development and the management of Ghana’s resources.

Mr Eshun said Nkrumah left a legacy of African pride and a belief in the capacity of Africans to determine their own future.

He identified education as another important component of Nkrumah’s development agenda, saying it was regarded as a key tool for national transformation.

According to him, Ghana’s development should also be viewed within the broader context of Africa’s progress.

He said the present generation could advance aspects of Nkrumah’s vision through entrepreneurship, industrial development, technology and the creative arts.

Mr Eshun urged young Ghanaians to establish businesses and industries, while encouraging the use of technology to improve sectors such as education and healthcare.

He also called on journalists and creative practitioners to tell Ghanaian stories to global audiences through journalism, music, film and the arts.

Mr Eshun said commemorating Nkrumah at 117 should prompt Ghanaians to reflect on three questions: “What was his picture of Ghana? What did he leave behind? What will we do with it?”

He said the answers should translate into practical efforts to build a productive, self-reliant and united Ghana.

The call comes as Ghana prepares to mark September 21 as Founder’s Day, a statutory public holiday commemorating Nkrumah’s birthday.

Ghana News.title: Bagbin re-inaugurates African Commission of Health and Human Rights Promoters with GH¢100,000 donation
Ghana News.content:
Speaker of Parliament, Rt. Hon. Alban Kingsford Bagbin, has formally re-inaugurated the African Commission of Health and Human Rights Promoters and launched its Endowment Fund with a personal contribution of GH¢100,000.

The event, held at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra on Thursday, September 17, marked the revival of the Commission, which is seeking to renew its work around healthcare rights, human dignity, accountability and the protection of vulnerable and marginalised groups.

The Commission’s founder, Naa Professor Edmund Nminyem Delle, said its origins date back to 1989, when it was established to respond to human rights concerns surrounding HIV/AIDS and discrimination against people living with the disease.

Professor Delle said its work later expanded to supporting people fleeing persecution and torture, including journalists and others who sought refuge in Ghana.

However, he said the organisation’s activities eventually slowed because of financial constraints, prompting efforts to establish a new foundation for its work.

The Chief Executive Officer of the Commission, Bishop Louis Christian Godson, said its renewed operations would focus on three main areas — advocacy and education, accountability and redress, and policy integration.

He said the Commission would promote patients’ rights, educate the public on healthcare rights, engage healthcare providers, document alleged violations and contribute to policy discussions on health and human rights.

Mental health, access to healthcare, health insurance and environmental health are also expected to receive attention.

Bishop Godson further described illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, as a public health concern and called for stronger scientific research, monitoring and public education on environmental pollution and its potential effects on communities.

A major feature of the re-inauguration was the launch of the Commission’s Endowment Fund, which organisers say is intended to provide sustainable financing for its programmes.

Bishop Godson said the Commission has set a long-term target of raising US$10 billion within five years to establish a financial base for its activities.

He said sustainable funding would be critical to supporting research, legal aid, environmental testing, monitoring and other interventions aimed at advancing health and human rights.

According to him, depending solely on short-term donor grants and irregular funding cycles can undermine the sustainability of advocacy organisations.

Speaking at the event, Speaker Bagbin stressed the importance of institutions that can bridge the gap between policymakers and the realities faced by citizens.

He said organisations working in health and human rights have an important role in bringing the concerns of vulnerable people to the attention of policymakers and other decision-makers.

The Speaker also underscored the need for sustainable financing, likening an institution without adequate resources to a vehicle without fuel.

He cited healthcare interventions, including efforts to support dialysis services, as examples of programmes that can benefit from dedicated and sustainable financing mechanisms.

Speaker Bagbin subsequently declared the African Commission of Health and Human Rights Promoters formally re-inaugurated and its Endowment Fund launched.

The Commission says its renewed work will place particular emphasis on people whose access to healthcare and human rights protections may be affected by poverty, discrimination, disability, social exclusion and other vulnerabilities.

Professor Delle recalled the organisation’s historical engagement with people facing discrimination and health challenges, while Bishop Godson said the revived Commission would continue advocating for people whose rights are violated within healthcare and other social systems.

The organisation also plans to strengthen research and public education as part of its renewed mandate.

The re-inauguration is expected to provide a new platform for the Commission to expand its health and human rights advocacy work in Ghana and beyond.

The event brought together policymakers, civil society representatives, health professionals, human rights advocates and other stakeholders to discuss the intersection of health, human rights and social justice.
