World.title: At least 21 killed after vehicle loaded with explosives rams Pakistan mosque
World.content:
A car-bomb attack on a mosque at a police compound in north-western Pakistan has killed at least 21 people and injured more than 100, officials say.

Fifteen police officers and a four-year-old child are among those killed in the suicide attack, which also involved gunmen firing on the police facility in the city of Kohat in the province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan's APP news agency reported.

Video found by BBC Verify shows the site covered in rubble and people tending to casualties.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police suggested a faction of the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), also known as the Pakistani Taliban, carried out the attack.

A car loaded with explosives rammed into the entrance of the mosque at about 13:15 local time (08:15 GMT), police say. Friday prayers were taking place at the time.

At least six of the attackers were killed in the explosion and the gun battle that followed, according to a Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police spokesperson.

In a post on X, the force said it was "determined to foil the nefarious designs of Fitna-al-Khawarij" - the designation used by officials to refer to the Pakistani Taliban.

The group was set up in 2007 with the aim of enforcing its strict version of Islamic law and is allied with al-Qaeda and the Afghan Taliban.

Pakistan's President Asif Ali Zardari expressed "his best wishes for the swift recovery of those injured in the explosion" in a statement, and called for the "complete elimination" of foreign-backed terrorists.

World.title: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror says he had no doubt she deliberately killed her children
World.content:
The lone holdout juror in the trial of Lindsay Clancy has said he "didn't have any doubts" that she was criminally responsible for killing her three children.

"Based on all the physical evidence, key witnesses and what the prosecution presents, I thought it was enough proof that she knew exactly what she was doing and planned it," Michael Desronvil said in a statement to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

The judge declared a mistrial on 4 September after the jury failed to reach a unanimous verdict following nearly 40 hours of deliberating.

Clancy admitted to the killings but her lawyers argued she had been suffering from postpartum psychosis. Prosecutors said the killings were calculated.

Warning: This article contains distressing details

The 36-year-old was charged with three counts of first-degree murder after strangling Cora, five, Dawson, three, and Callan, eight months, at the family's Massachusetts home before jumping out of the second-floor window.

To find Clancy guilty, jurors had to be unanimously convinced beyond reasonable doubt that she intentionally killed her children and that she did not do so as a result of postpartum psychosis, a rare and serious condition.

The jury - nine women and three men - considered a range of options including not guilty by reason of insanity, manslaughter and first-degree murder.

Several jurors have said following the mistrial being declared that the panel was ultimately divided 11-1 in favour of finding Clancy not criminally responsible.

Desronvil said he believed the evidence presented in court showed she had planned the killings.

"I didn't have any doubts," he said in a statement to CBS on Thursday.

"As I tried to explain different possible theories during deliberation, I kept getting cut off as if I had doubts based on the evidence presented."

World.title: Ryanair boss Michael O'Leary apologises over 'high-fare rapists' remarks
World.content:
Ryanair chief executive Michael O'Leary has said he is "truly sorry" for describing rival airlines as "high-fare rapists".

He had previously refused to apologise to a rape crisis centre which criticised him for the comments.

O'Leary had made the remark earlier this month while talking to journalists ahead of Ryanair's yearly meeting with shareholders.

Following the comments, the Dublin Rape Crisis Centre (DRCC) wrote to him asking for an apology, in a letter seen by the BBC.

O'Leary had originally said that some people were "desperate to get to Ryanair's low fares because they can't afford to fly with the high-fare rapists around Europe".

He subsequently defended his choice of words when asked by a reporter from the Press Association whether the language was appropriate.

"British Airways, Lufthansa, and everybody else's high fares, I'll happily offend them on a regular basis," he had added.

Asked whether it would offend sexual assault victims, he said rape was "a terrible crime".

In a video posted on Friday, O'Leary said that, over the last ten days, he had had "conversations with family and friends, both inside and outside Ryanair".

"I have come to realise however that the word that I used so carelessly has caused considerable upset and offence to a wide number of people, especially to victims and survivors.

"I want to apologise, sincerely and unreservedly, to those people, especially to the survivors."

O'Leary described his choice of language as "careless", and said "it won't happen again".

"I will try to learn from this mistake, and do better in future."

Following O'Leary's first comments, the DRCC's chief executive Rachel Morrogh had written to O'Leary accusing him of trying to get a headline with his comments.

She said the DRCC had received calls from rape victims who were "upset and distressed because of what you said".

She offered O'Leary training on the impact of sexual violence and urged him to apologise.

"I can't imagine you would ever use the term so flippantly again if you truly understood [what] it was like to survive rape," she wrote.

In response, O'Leary had said: "I am quite clear that no remarks of mine could possibly trivialise the heinous crime of rape."

He added that as he had not "trivialised the heinous crime of rape" he would "not be issuing any apology or accepting your offer of training".

It was not the first time O'Leary had offended people while talking about his business.

In 2004, he reportedly called the owners of Stansted Airport "a bunch of overcharging rapists", external in a row over airport charges.

He has also previously called some of his own staff "lazy bastards" and once said to passengers looking for a refund "we don't want to hear your sob stories".

In June, he said the airline would "reluctantly" stop charging parents to sit next to children after a watchdog investigation was opened, but insisted its previous policy complied with laws.

World.title: North Korean anthem played for South Korea at Asian Games
World.content:
Organisers have apologised for playing the North Korean national anthem for the South Korean men's hockey team at the Asian Games in Japan.

South Korea, who thrashed Bangladesh 5-0, looked confused as the incorrect national anthem was played.

South Korea's Yonhap news agency reported that Bangladesh's national anthem followed before South Korea's actual anthem was played.

A stadium announcer did apologise for the mistake.

"This is a really serious problem. When we protested, they said, 'We're sorry. It wasn't that it wasn't prepared; there was a mistake on the part of those responsible for playing it'," South Korea coach Min Tae-seok said.

"But this is something that simply should never happen."

North Korea's national anthem, along with other symbols of the secretive state, are banned in South Korea.

The two countries are still technically at war, after the 1950-53 conflict between the two ended without a peace treaty.

The build-up to the Asian Games, which officially starts on Saturday, has already seen complaints from teams about the quality and amount of accommodation.

A member of the South Korea basketball team posted a video of a leaking pipe and soaked floor in his room, with the caption: "Please help me."

Some teams were also stranded at the airport for up to six hours when they landed this week.

Field hockey at the Asian Games started on Friday and runs until 3 October.

World.title: Marine police rescue two from boat mishap in Akwa Ibom
World.content:
The Police Command in Akwa Ibom State has rescued two persons involved in a boat mishap along the Ibaka waterways in Mbo Local Government Area of the state.

Timfon John, the police spokesperson in Akwa Ibom, disclosed this in a statement in Uyo on Friday.

Ms John, a deputy superintendent of police, said the incident occurred at about 1:30 p.m. on 17 September when a blue W23 speedboat christened “LET’S PRAY” sank while travelling on the waterway.

She said preliminary investigation showed that the boat driver attempted to adjust the boat’s seacock to allow accumulated water onboard to drain.

Ms John said that in the process, waves generated by a passing boat reportedly destabilised the vessel, and caused it to take in water.

The police spokesperson said the driver and the conductor were immediately rescued through the swift intervention of marine police personnel and surveillance patrol team on duty.

ALSO READ: Another boat mishap claims 29 lives in Niger

She said the Commissioner of Police in Akwa Ibom, Baba Azare, commended the marine police personnel for their vigilance, professionalism and prompt response to the issue.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She urged boat operators and passengers in the state to prioritise safety at all times by ensuring that their vessels were seaworthy.

“Avoid overloading, provide adequate life jackets for everyone onboard, and exercise extreme caution while navigating areas with heavy marine traffic,” she said.

(NAN)

World.title: Cross River retirees appeal for pension adjustment, gratuity payment
World.content:
Retirees in Cross River State have appealed to Governor Bassey Otu to review and harmonise their pensions.

The Chairman of the Association of Retirees in the state, Daniel Effiong, made the appeal while speaking with reporters on Friday in Calabar.

Mr Effiong said pension payments had not been adjusted since 2014, despite successive increases in the national minimum wage.

He claimed that some retirees were currently receiving as little as N4,000 monthly, describing the amount as grossly inadequate to meet basic needs, including food and medication.

Mr Effiong said many former state workers were also still awaiting payment of their gratuities several years after retirement.

He said the situation had become increasingly difficult for elderly retirees amid rising living costs and the declining purchasing power of the naira.

The chairman, however, acknowledged the state government’s efforts to ensure regular monthly pension payments and commended the governor for his promise to release another tranche of gratuities before December.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, the N10 billion gratuity payment made by the state government about two years ago had not completely cleared the backlog, leaving many retirees awaiting their entitlements.

Mr Effiong urged the governor to review the existing pension structure and introduce consequential adjustments to bring retirees’ benefits in line with current economic realities.

“Such an adjustment will help cushion the impact of inflation and the rising cost of essential goods and services on elderly former workers,” he said.

Also speaking, the Public Relations Officer of the association, Frank Odey, opposed any proposal to constitute another committee to handle pension payments.

Mr Odey argued that creating another committee could further delay the payment process.

He said the offices of the Auditor-General and Accountant-General had constitutional responsibilities relating to pension payments.

Mr Odey also called for upward adjustments in pensions and gratuities, noting that the declining value of the naira had substantially eroded retirees’ purchasing power.

He said some retirees, particularly those without other sources of income, were facing difficulties paying for accommodation, healthcare, food and other basic necessities.

Mr Odey urged the state government to sustain regular pension payments while taking steps to review pension rates and settle outstanding gratuity obligations.

He said addressing the issues would provide relief to retirees who had spent their working years in the service of the state.

(NAN)

World.title: Tinubu, Bolloré discuss new investments in Nigeria’s film, entertainment sectors
World.content:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has held talks with Vincent Bolloré of the Bolloré Group in Paris over plans to expand the group’s investments in Nigeria’s creative and digital economy.

Mr Bolloré is a French businessman whose interests span media, entertainment, communications, and logistics, with the Bolloré Group holding stakes in major global media companies, including Canal+ and Universal Music Group.

His connection to Nigeria’s media industry has become more significant following Canal+’s acquisition of the MultiChoice Group. PREMIUM TIMES previously reported that Canal+ completed its acquisition of MultiChoice in July, making the African pay-TV company a full subsidiary of the French media group.

MultiChoice operates DStv and GOtv in Nigeria and other African markets. PREMIUM TIMES also reported that MultiChoice Nigeria is now a Canal+ company following the acquisition.

Investment Plan

According to a statement by Bayo Onanuga, the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, the group confirmed plans to deepen the localisation of its operations in Nigeria across film, entertainment, fibre-optic infrastructure and related sectors.

The meeting took place on Thursday as Mr Tinubu continued his working vacation in France.

Mr Bolloré and his executives outlined what the Presidency described as a series of new investments centred on Nigeria.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The executives described Nigeria as the “spearhead of Africa’s cultural renaissance”, citing the global success of Nollywood and Afrobeats, as well as the growing international demand for Nigerian culture.

The group’s plans include greater localisation of its operations, with the Presidency saying this would cover film, entertainment and fibre-optic infrastructure.

Tinubu seeks more local opportunities

Mr Tinubu welcomed the group’s reported plans to deepen its localisation in Nigeria, saying the country’s growing global cultural influence presented an opportunity to bring more production, investment and jobs into the country.

The President reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to economic development, with emphasis on job creation for young Nigerians and investment in digitalisation.

He also said the government would continue to support investments that expand Nigeria’s creative and digital economy, develop local talent and strengthen infrastructure.

PREMIUM TIMES previously reported that Mr Tinubu described Nigeria’s creative economy as a driver of growth, highlighting the role of art, music, film and literature in the country’s global influence.

He said the government would seek to position Nigeria as a base for businesses serving Africa and the wider global market.

Renewed Hope Agenda

Mr Tinubu said the Renewed Hope Agenda was focused on creating an economy where Nigeria’s talent, enterprise, and global cultural reach translate into greater opportunities and improved livelihoods for Nigerians.

The meeting is part of the President’s engagements in France during his working vacation.

World.title: Flamingos beat Ghana 4-2 to maintain winning start at WAFU B
World.content:
Nigeria’s Flamingos maintained their winning start to the 2026 WAFU B U-17 Girls’ Cup with a 4-2 victory over Ghana in a keenly contested Jollof Derby on Friday.

Oluwakemi Adegbuyi put Nigeria ahead in the 33rd minute before captain Harmony Chidi doubled the advantage in first-half stoppage time.

Ghana reduced the deficit through captain Seidatu Wahab in the 62nd minute, but Nigeria restored their two-goal cushion eight minutes later through Mary Dunstan.

Kaosarat Akanji added a fourth for the Flamingos in the 87th minute before Gloria Ameaa scored Ghana’s second in the 90th minute.

Nigeria had to play the final half-hour with 10 players after Elizabeth Adesuyi was sent off in the 59th minute.

Despite being a player down, the Flamingos held firm to secure another important victory and strengthen their position in the competition.

The result comes three days after Nigeria opened their campaign with a 5-0 demolition of Niger Republic. Captain Chidi opened the scoring in that match before Awawu Bashiru doubled the lead, while Ohunene Sunday, Dunstan and Ayomide Rotimi completed the rout late in the game.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The victory over Ghana means the Flamingos have now scored nine goals in their opening two matches, continuing their impressive attacking form in Côte d’Ivoire.

The regional tournament is also serving as part of Nigeria’s preparations for the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Head coach Akeem Busari had said the competition would help his players identify their strengths and weaknesses before the global tournament.

The 2026 WAFU B U-17 Girls’ Cup was switched to a league format following Benin Republic’s withdrawal, with Nigeria, Ghana, Burkina Faso, Togo, Niger and hosts Côte d’Ivoire taking part.

The Flamingos will now turn their attention to their remaining fixtures as they continue their pursuit of regional honours and preparations for the World Cup.

World.title: ‘Armed robbers would soon visit him,’ police officer captured on video telling local council chairman
World.content:
The Police Command in Cross River State has commenced an investigation into an alleged threat by a police officer attached to the Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU) against James Anam, the chairman of Calabar Municipality Local Government Council.

Sunday Eitokpah, the police spokesperson in the state, disclosed this in a statement on Friday.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the officer was allegedly heard in the viral video threatening Mr Anam that “armed robbers would soon visit him” during an altercation with VCRU operatives in Calabar.

Mr Eitokpah, an assistant superintendent of police, said the video, which had been circulating on social media, purportedly captured an altercation between the council chairman and VCRU operatives at an undisclosed stop-and-search point within the Calabar metropolis.

According to him, the incident occurred about three weeks ago during a stop-and-search operation.

He said preliminary information available to the Command indicated that the circumstances surrounding the encounter had not been fully established.

“The Commissioner of Police, Ajo Ordue, has directed a discreet and impartial investigation to establish the facts, circumstances, and conduct of all persons involved,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The police spokesperson said the command has commenced the process of inviting Mr Anam and the concerned VCRU operatives to provide their respective accounts of the incident.

He said the officer was purportedly heard in the video making the statement that armed robbers would soon visit the chairman.

“However, the command has not established the circumstances or intent behind the statement,” Mr Eitokpah said.

He assured the public that the investigation would be conducted professionally and objectively, with due regard to the rights of all parties.

He added that any allegation of misconduct established during the investigation would be dealt with in accordance with extant laws and police regulations.

The command urged the public to refrain from drawing conclusions based solely on the circulating video, noting that the footage might not capture the full circumstances surrounding the encounter.

It appealed to the public to allow the investigation to run its course.

(NAN)

World.title: My successor in 2031 will emerge on merit, not godfatherism – Otti
World.content:
Governor Alex Otti of Abia State says he will neither be a godfather nor impose his successor on the state after serving his second tenure in 2031.

Mr Otti spoke on Thursday in Umuahia while receiving a former governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party, Ngozi Johnson-Chukwunenye, and her supporters into the Labour Party (LP).

He said that leadership succession should be based on identifying the most suitable person for the job, rather than perpetuating a “sit-tight” culture.

He said the person who would succeed him would be better equipped to provide quality leadership to the people.

“The most important thing you can give a people is good governance.

“And once people test good governance, it will be very difficult for them to allow you to take them back.

“So, if you are afraid that we will go back to Egypt, it will never happen and what I can assure you is that, by the time I’m done, the person who will succeed me will be better than me.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I don’t want to be a godfather and I don’t tolerate godfathers.

“We will all sit down, look at everybody and say, who is the best person for this job and then all of us will agree and we will campaign for him.

“He will win and we will take a back seat.”

The governor also reiterated his earlier stance not to seek another elective position after completing his second tenure.

He said his administration’s focus was to provide good governance and create an environment, where younger people could emerge as capable leaders.

“We should stop this sit-tight. It can’t be only you.

“There are smarter, more trained, better-trained, better-equipped younger people; our children. We need to give them opportunity,” he said.

Mr Otti said his administration was already preparing younger people to take over leadership responsibilities through various initiatives, including the Abia Leadership Academy.

He said that over 1,080 young people, between the ages of 16 and 25, had recently graduated from the academy.

“You will see how smart our children are. So, these are the people that will take over from us.

“And they are being trained now for tomorrow; so we can never go back,” he said.

The governor also said the administration’s effort to improve governance and infrastructure would continue, despite criticism.

He argued that development could not be achieved in one day.

He said his administration prioritised the restoration of Aba and Umuahia before extending its interventions to other parts of the state.

“We are now moving into the hinterlands, and we will continue until we reach everywhere; so nothing will stop us,” he said.

He thanked Mrs Johnson-Chukwunenye for joining the party and for remembering less privileged children, including pupils from the School for the Blind.

Mr Otti said such gestures demonstrated concern for vulnerable members of society.

Why I’m backing Otti for second term – Johnson-Chukwunenye

In a speech, the National Vice-Chairman of the LP (South-east), Ishmael Onuoha, said the party’s motto aligned with the ideals expressed in the third stanza of the national anthem.

Mr Onuoha described the party as one committed to the masses and hope for Nigerians.

In a remark, the LP Chairman in Abia, Peter Azubuike, said the growing support for the party was a by-product of Mr Otti’s good governance and performance.

Mr Azubuike said the party was ready for the 2027 elections, urging members to prepare for polling-unit-based campaigns and ensure effective mobilisation at the grassroots.

In a speech, Mrs Johnson-Chukwunenye said that she had closely followed the Otti administration and was convinced by its efforts to clean, light up and restore dignity to Abia.

She said she decided to support Mr Otti’s second-term bid because she believed his administration’s policies aligned with her vision of a government that remembers the poor and promotes equity.

She called for legislation on “continuity and completion” to ensure that successive administrations continued projects inherited from previous governments.

(NAN)

World.title: Mambilla: APC campaign council asks Atiku to quit 2027 presidential race
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council asked urged African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar to withdraw from the 2027 presidential race over ICC arbitration revelations.

The ​‌‌‍​‌‍⁠⁠‌⁠​⁠​‍⁠⁠‌‌​council alleged that proceedings before an International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) tribunal in Paris had raised serious questions about the former vice president’s role in the Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project controversy.

Dele Alake, spokesperson of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, made the call in a statement on Friday in Abuja.

The arbitration involved Sunrise Power and Transmission Company Ltd., its promoter, Leno Adesanya, and the Federal Government over the stalled project in Taraba.

The ICC tribunal ultimately rejected Sunrise’s claims against Nigeria and ordered the company and Mr Adesanya to reimburse Nigeria for 75 per cent of its legal fees and expenses.

The APC council focused on a $500,000 payment made by Mr Adesanya to Jennifer Douglas, who was then married to Atiku, on 30 January, 2003.

According to the tribunal record, the payment was made through China Castle Investments Ltd., an offshore company controlled by Mr Adesanya, into Ms Douglas’ Citibank account in the United States.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The council alleged that the payment was connected to the subsequent award of a build-operate-transfer contract to Sunrise for the Mambilla project.

It also alleged that Atiku and former Minister of Power, Olu Agunloye, worked together to facilitate the contract in spite of objections to the deal.

The APC said the disputed contract was signed in 2003, when Atiku was vice president under former President Olusegun Obasanjo.

It alleged that the contract was not authorised by the Federal Executive Council and subsequently exposed Nigeria to substantial financial claims.

The campaign council cited the tribunal’s observation concerning the timing of the $500,000 payment and the alleged award of the Sunrise contract.

According to the APC, the tribunal noted a “close connection in time” between the payment on 30 January 2003, and the alleged award of the contract on 22 May, 2003.

However, the tribunal record also shows that Mr Adesanya described the payment as part of a foreign-exchange transaction carried out for Atiku.

Reports on the award said the tribunal found that the explanation was not supported by documentary evidence, including records of the underlying naira payment or instructions from Atiku or his aides.

The tribunal did not make a finding that the former vice president received a bribe, according to a report on the final award.

The APC campaign council, however, interpreted the revelations as evidence that Atiku had compromised Nigeria’s interests for personal gain.

Mr Alake said the council’s position was reinforced by the financial implications of the arbitration and the prolonged delay in implementing the Mambilla project.

He alleged that the disputed contract contributed to claims against Nigeria running into hundreds of millions of dollars and a separate claim exceeding $2.7 billion.

The APC Campaign spokesperson also compared the Mambilla dispute with the Process and Industrial Developments (P&ID) case, which involved a multibillion-dollar claim against Nigeria over a gas project.

Mr Alake further criticised Atiku for not appearing to testify before the arbitration tribunal, while former Presidents Obasanjo and Muhammadu Buhari testified in proceedings concerning Nigeria’s defence.

He also cited criticisms of Atiku contained in Mr Obasanjo’s book, My Watch, particularly the former president’s allegations concerning corruption, transparency and national interest.

The APC campaign council urged Atiku to withdraw from the presidential contest, saying the revelations warranted further scrutiny.

It also accused the ADC presidential candidate of bearing responsibility for delays surrounding the Mambilla project and its potential economic benefits to Taraba.

The council said the project, if implemented, could generate substantial economic opportunities for the state and Nigeria.

Atiku has previously denied wrongdoing in connection with corruption allegations concerning the payment and related matters.

(NAN)

World.title: Ex-President Jonathan calls for civil service reform, unified federal-state salary structure
World.content:
Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called for the harmonisation of structures and salaries across the federal and state civil services in the country.

He stated this in Yenagoa on Friday during the foundation-laying and fund-raising ceremony for the Bayelsa State Association of Retired Permanent Secretaries’ Secretariat Complex.

Mr Jonathan commended the retired permanent secretaries for the initiative, noting that the caliber of personnel in the Bayelsa public service compares favourably to their counterparts at the federal level.

Mr Jonathan recalled how, during his tenure as governor of Bayelsa, he restructured the state civil service to introduce Grade Level 17 for directors, who previously retired on Level 16.

He emphasised that establishing a dedicated secretariat for the retired permanent secretaries would serve both retirees and the public, while making a strong case for uniform civil service structures nationwide.

The Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri, represented by the Head of Service, Ebiye Sawyer, pledged government support for the project, praising the retired officials for their vision and dedication.

Earlier, Chairman of the Association, Collins Daniel, described the proposed complex as an institutional edifice designed to embody the legacy of public service.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He explained that the centre would house administrative offices, event halls, conference rooms, and recreational facilities.

Mr Daniel explained that the Bayelsa Association of Retired Permanent Secretaries’ Secretariat Complex is expected to cost N500m and completed in two years.

(NAN)

World.title: CAF Inter-club competitions: Why Nigerian clubs fail
World.content:
By Douglas Baye-Osagie

[email protected]

This season, Nigeria was represented by four clubs on the continent. Rangers International and Rivers United in the CAF Champions League, and Shooting Stars and El-Kanemi Warriors in the CAF Confederation Cup. The story is already familiar – while two have bowed out in their very first game of the tournament, the two that remain now face a heavy North African hurdle. We celebrate qualifiers in June, we get humiliated in September. Rivers United and Shooting Stars are just the latest victims. But the problem is not juju, not luck, not referees. It is systemic. These were teams who had pole position to advance but they refused to do what was needed to get over the line.

The NPFL is now a feeder league for the continent’s smaller leagues. That is how far we have fallen. Our local players have taken their football to African countries whenever the slightest opportunity arises.

We pay our champions peanuts. How can you pay a star striker N150,000 a month and expect him to face a Tunisian defender earning $10,000? Good players don’t stay. They emigrate to Rwanda, Tanzania, Sudan, Kenya, Europe, even Vietnam. We export goals and import regrets. Just look at Shooting Stars – their best two players last season, Ayobami Junior and Tijani Al Ameen, who even made the Super Eagles squad for the Unity Cup derby, have now moved on to clubs in Algeria and Zimbabwe. Think of how much experience and quality is lost by these departures.

Recruitment is corrupt. It’s “man-know-man” football. Players are sacked by cleaners. That doesn’t breed a professional environment. Agents bring their players, commissioners bring their cousins, chairmen bring their clients. Talent is optional.

Some coaches have turned selection into business. If you don’t pay, you don’t play. The best 11 never plays. The richest 11 plays.

We lack tactical preparation. African football has gone scientific. North Africans press with GPS data, video analysis, and set-piece coaches. We do “come out and play” and shout “ginger yourselves” from the bench.

Technically, we are still in 1999. First touch heavy, second touch tackle. Rivers United assistant coach Yemi after the game says there are no strikers in Nigeria. What a way to divert attention from himself and the coaching crew who couldn’t do the needful at home.

Most of our clubs are owned by state governments. Football is treated as a political settlement. A Commissioner for Sports who has never run a kiosk is suddenly managing a club with a continental budget.

Football has left that era. It is now business. Al Ahly is a corporation. Raja Casablanca is a brand. Orlando Pirates is almost a brand of sponsors. We are still a Ministry Department.

No pre-season planning. We start buying players 2 weeks before CAF registration closes. The Fire Brigade Approach. Even the coach who qualified Shooting Stars was not good enough as he was sacked for Salisu Yusuf.

No continuity. A new Governor comes in, sacks the entire management, sacks the coach, sacks 20 players. How do you build a team like that?

We don’t respect away games. You can’t go to Tunisia to defend a 1-0 lead. In Africa, to qualify, you must go to score. North Africans see defense as invitation.

We don’t scout our opponents. They have 50 clips of us. We have zero of them.

Fitness levels are shameful. By minute 70 in North Africa, our players are cramping. Theirs are just starting.

We have no sports psychology. We fear the name “Esperance” and “Wydad” before the bus enters the stadium.

Infrastructure. You train on a bad pitch in Nigeria and expect to play well on a lush green modern hybrid grass in Algiers, Tunis or Morocco. Impossible.

Poor welfare kills motivation. Unpaid bonuses, 6 months salary owed, then you ask a man to die for the badge in Casablanca.

No youth system. Moroccan clubs have academies producing stars for Europe. We have trial grounds every pre-season.

This brings me to ENYIMBA. Why did they succeed where everyone else failed?

In the early 2000s, Orji Uzor Kalu took politics OUT of football. He brought in professionals. He gave Felix Anyansi Agwu a free hand. He paid Enyimba players MORE than the national team. He kept Kadiri Ikhana and later Okey Emordi, bought the best legs in the country – Vincent Enyeama, Obinna Nwaneri, Joetex Frimpong – and did a 6-week close camping in Abia. They didn’t just prepare, they OVER-prepared.

That is how you win Africa back-to-back. Enyimba proved that Nigerian clubs CAN conquer the continent, but only when run like a professional club, not a political campaign office.

And let’s be honest with ourselves – in a fixture that looked like Enugu Rangers were going to have it easy against a Benin Republic club side, it took the luck of penalties to go through. Against a team from Algeria, you don’t win with luck.

Until we sack the political approach and hire professionals, pay professionals, and think like professionals, we will continue to crash out in the first round.

Rangers vs USM Alger and El Kanemi vs Raja Casablanca are not football matches. They are audits. And African football is about to audit us again. We hope and pray they prepare well and live up to the expectations.

World.title: Gombe pledges support for new army formations
World.content:
By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe

GOMBE — Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has pledged the state government’s support for the accelerated take-off of newly established Nigerian Army formations in the state.

Yahaya gave the assurance when a delegation representing the General Officer Commanding, GOC, 3rd Armoured Division, Nigerian Army, paid a courtesy visit to the palace of the Mai Kaltungo, Engr. Saleh Mohammed.

Represented by the Secretary to the State Government, SSG, Prof. Ibrahim Abubakar Njodi, the governor expressed appreciation to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for approving the establishment of the 271 Tank Battalion in Bajoga and 272 Tank Battalion in Kaltungo.

He said the new formations would strengthen the security architecture of the state and contribute to protecting lives and property in the North-East, which continues to face insurgency, banditry and other security challenges.

Yahaya also commended the Federal Government and the state government for their roles in facilitating the conversion of the Snakebite Hospital, Kaltungo, into a National Snakebite Research Centre.

Njodi further commended the Mai Kaltungo for his contributions to the development of the chiefdom and initiatives aimed at improving the welfare of its people.

Earlier, the representative of the GOC, 3rd Armoured Division, and Commander, 301 Artillery Regiment, Gombe, Col. S.O. Bike, said the establishment of the new formations was part of the Nigerian Army’s expansion from eight to 12 divisions.

Bike, who is also Team Lead of the Technical Assessment Team, said the delegation was in Gombe to engage the state government on arrangements for the commencement of operations of the 27 Armoured Brigade and its component units.

He listed the formations as the 27 Armoured Brigade Garrison, 271 Tank Battalion and 272 Tank Battalion.

According to him, the team’s visit to Kaltungo was also to assess facilities provided for the initial take-off of the 272 Tank Battalion.

He commended the Gombe State Government and the traditional institution in Kaltungo for their cooperation and support towards the establishment of the formation.

Responding, the Mai Kaltungo, Engr. Saleh Mohammed, thanked President Tinubu and Governor Yahaya for supporting the establishment of strategic Federal Government institutions in the chiefdom.

He pledged the continued support and cooperation of the people of Kaltungo to the Nigerian Army and the newly established 272 Tank Battalion.

The delegation subsequently inspected a proposed temporary site at a private boarding school designated for the initial take-off of the battalion.

The Technical Assessment Team expressed satisfaction with the facility and commended the Mai Kaltungo and residents of the chiefdom for their efforts in providing a temporary location.

The team also acknowledged the identification of about 90 hectares of land for the permanent development of the military facility, as well as available accommodation for officers.

World.title: FRSC denies 50 recruitment slots for Gombe lawmaker
World.content:
By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe

The Federal Road Safety Corps, FRSC, has dismissed as misleading a viral social media publication alleging that the member representing Balanga/Billiri Federal Constituency of Gombe State in the House of Representatives, Hon. Ali Isah, secured 50 recruitment slots for his constituents.

The Corps, in a statement dated September 16, 2026, signed by its Corps Public Education Officer, Mr Osondu Ohaeri, and obtained by our correspondent in Gombe on Friday, said no appointment letter had been issued to any candidate under its ongoing 2026 recruitment exercise.

The clarification followed the circulation of a social media publication purportedly linking the lawmaker to the allocation of 50 FRSC recruitment slots to his constituents.

According to the FRSC, candidates who have successfully passed various stages of the screening and interview processes have only been invited to designated training schools and the FRSC Academy for further stages of the exercise.

The Corps stressed that such invitations should not be interpreted as appointment letters.

It explained that candidates must still undergo and successfully complete prescribed training, screening, regimentation and other mandatory processes before they can be considered for appointment.

The statement read: “Only candidates who satisfactorily complete all the required stages and emerge without any disqualifying record will be considered for appointment in accordance with established procedures.”

The FRSC further maintained that no political office holder, individual, group or external interest has the authority to confer appointments into the Corps outside its established recruitment framework.

It said the ongoing recruitment exercise, under the leadership of Corps Marshal Shehu Mohammed, mni, was being conducted in accordance with the principles of merit, transparency, due process and institutional integrity.

The Corps urged applicants and members of the public to disregard unverified claims suggesting that recruitment slots had been allocated to particular individuals, constituencies or political interests.

It also warned that such claims could expose unsuspecting applicants to fraudsters who might exploit the perception that FRSC appointments could be secured through political influence, payment or personal connections.

The Corps said it would continue to provide official information on the recruitment exercise through its authorised communication channels, advising applicants to rely only on verified information from the FRSC.

It reiterated that the 2026 recruitment exercise remained subject to the completion of all statutory and administrative procedures, stressing that no candidate should regard himself or herself as an FRSC appointee until the process was concluded and a formal appointment communicated by the appropriate authority.

The FRSC’s position is that no appointment has been issued under the 2026 recruitment exercise and that candidates must complete all prescribed stages before any formal appointment can be made.

World.title: Kalu urges WTO action on food security, investment
World.content:
Hon. Benjamin Kalu (Bende Federal Constituency of Abia State)

By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja

Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has called on the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to deliver concrete outcomes on food security and investment facilitation, warning that prolonged delays could weaken confidence in the multilateral trading system.

Kalu made the call on Friday in Geneva, Switzerland, while speaking at the 57th Session of the Steering Committee of the Parliamentary Conference on the WTO (PCWTO), attended by WTO Director-General, Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala.

The session, co-chaired by Bernd Lange of the European Parliament and Secretary-General of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU), Anda Filip, brought together parliamentarians from national and regional legislatures, trade policy experts, the European Parliament and the IPU.

The committee reviewed developments in multilateral trade negotiations, follow-up actions from the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC14), and outcomes of the PCWTO session held in Yaoundé, Cameroon.

Kalu acknowledged progress on fisheries subsidies and development issues but said the WTO’s credibility would ultimately depend on its ability to deliver tangible outcomes for developing countries.

He expressed concern over the absence of a permanent solution to public stockholding for food security, 13 years after WTO members committed to addressing the issue at the 2013 Bali Ministerial Conference.

According to him, Nigeria had co-sponsored the demand by the African Group, African, Caribbean and Pacific Group and G33 for a permanent solution.

“Thirteen years cannot be explained as an ordinary negotiating delay. Behind every delayed outcome are farmers, workers and families living with the consequences of decisions we defer,” Kalu said.

As an interim measure, the Deputy Speaker proposed that WTO members consider a waiver under Article IX:3 of the Marrakesh Agreement to cover qualifying public stockholding programmes.

He argued that the absence of consensus should not render an existing treaty mechanism unusable when countries were facing pressing food security challenges.

Kalu also raised concerns over the Investment Facilitation for Development Agreement, saying broad support for the agreement had been stalled by a single formal objection.

He called for greater accountability from national parliaments and proposed that participating legislatures submit reports on concrete steps taken to advance PCWTO and WTO outcomes before each Steering Committee meeting.

“Too often, our discussions focus on what Geneva has or has not done. We should devote equal attention to what our own governments and legislatures have done since the last meeting. Accountability must run in both directions,” he said.

The Deputy Speaker further cautioned that improved attendance at parliamentary trade meetings alone would not address the challenge of legislative relevance in global trade governance.

He said many legislatures received briefings only after negotiating positions had already been finalised.

Kalu proposed that future PCWTO sessions focus on specific economic issues, including public stockholding, investment facilitation, the e-commerce moratorium and digital trade rules.

Such an approach, he said, would enable parliamentarians to communicate clear conclusions and areas of disagreement to trade ministers before negotiations.

Kalu, who joined the PCWTO Steering Committee in February 2025, also secured a reaffirmation from the IPU Secretary-General of the organisation’s commitment to working with him towards the successful hosting of the PCWTO event scheduled for Abuja in 2027.

He reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to a fair, credible and development-oriented global trading system.

“Nigeria is not here to add to the diagnosis. We are here to help restore that trust,” Kalu said.

Earlier, Okonjo-Iweala presented an update on WTO reforms, covering decision-making, development, special and differential treatment, fairness and dispute settlement.

She noted that while consensus gives all WTO members an equal voice, its application as unanimity had enabled single objections to block outcomes with broad support.

The WTO Director-General urged parliamentarians to move beyond criticism and propose practical solutions for rebuilding confidence in the organisation, citing transparency and improved notifications as possible confidence-building measures.

She also called for deeper engagement between parliamentarians and Geneva-based trade actors, including national WTO representatives, the Chair of the General Council, reform facilitators and committee chairs.

Okonjo-Iweala acknowledged that the multilateral trading system had not served many developing and poorer countries effectively, while defending the continued relevance of special and differential treatment.

She also stressed the importance of investment facilitation to developing economies and said restoring an effective two-tier dispute settlement system remained part of the WTO reform agenda.

World.title: MTN MIP: Media practitioners urged to strengthen cross-border reporting
World.content:
By Moses Nosike

African journalists need to look beyond crisis-driven coverage and tell more stories about the people and institutions building connections across borders, fellows at the 2026 MTN Media Innovation Summit in South Africa have said.

The call came during a session moderated by one of the MIP fellows Tolulope Ajibola, titled “Storytelling Across Borders: Finding the Untold Nigeria–South Africa Stories,” held as part of the South African study visit for the fifth cohort of the MTN Media Innovation Programme (MIP).

The fellows noted that African journalism often looks beyond national borders when there is a crisis, while stories about entrepreneurs, students, artists, researchers, technology innovators and professionals building relationships across countries receive less attention. They called for more coverage of everyday experiences and relationships between communities in Nigeria and South Africa.

The discussion was part of the two-day summit held at the University of Johannesburg, which brought together 25 senior Nigerian journalists selected from a pool of applicants, alongside South African editors, researchers and media practitioners.

Professor Sifiso Mnisi, Director of the Centre for Data and Digital Communications at the University of Johannesburg, said the summit provided an opportunity for journalists from both countries to examine how media narratives influence relationships between nations and social cohesion.

He noted that perceptions in Nigeria and South Africa are often shaped by news reports, social media and popular culture rather than direct interaction, placing greater responsibility on journalists and editors in shaping how citizens understand one another.

The summit also examined how media practitioners can report conflict without worsening tensions. A session moderated by Progress Godfrey, an MIP 5 Fellow, titled “From Xenophobia to Social Cohesion: Reporting Conflict Without Fueling It,” stressed the importance of historical context, verified information and perspectives from communities working towards reconciliation.

Another session, moderated by Goitsemang Mvula, called for collaborative investigations, regional reporting projects and stronger editorial partnerships to help African audiences understand continental issues beyond national boundaries.

Closing the discussions, Funso Aina, Senior Manager, External Relations at MTN Nigeria, said the summit represented more than a professional development initiative. He noted that by bringing together journalists, newsroom leaders, content creators and communication professionals, the programme has become a platform for strengthening journalism’s role in promoting democratic participation, regional integration and social cohesion.

World.title: West African Youths seek greater role in governance
World.content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Confederation of West African Youths has called for greater youth participation in governance, accountable leadership and policies capable of creating more economic opportunities for young Nigerians.

The Regional President of the organisation, Ambassador Israel Akinola, made the call yesterday in Abuja when a delegation of the group paid a courtesy visit to the National Secretariat of the Social Democratic Party, SDP.

Akinola described the confederation as a platform for African youths committed to promoting effective leadership and governance, saying it had members across West African countries.

He said Nigeria required a new approach to governance, with greater emphasis on citizens’ welfare, accountability and opportunities for young people.

According to him, young Nigerians face challenges including economic hardship, unemployment and limited opportunities to develop and commercialise their skills and ideas.

Akinola, who said he had previously been involved with the SDP, explained that the visit was aimed at engaging the party intellectually on its ideas for addressing the country’s challenges.

He also called for stronger public-private partnerships, saying government policies should have tangible effects on citizens, particularly young people and those at the grassroots.

“We want what will make every African country experience leadership and governance at its peak,” he said.

Akinola criticised what he described as poor governance and alleged misuse of public resources by some political leaders, saying Nigeria needed leaders who would focus on delivering tangible results for citizens.

“We need people who understand what leadership truly is. And we need a government that the citizens would have a direct feeling of. We need a government that poor masses can actually have a direct feeling of,” he said.

He said the confederation was seeking to promote practical solutions to Nigeria’s challenges rather than merely criticising those in government.

Speaking, the SDP presidential candidate for the 2027 election, Prince Adewole Adebayo, thanked the delegation for the visit and highlighted the historical role of West African youth movements in the struggle for independence and self-government.

Adebayo urged the youths to take their engagement beyond political meetings and into communities across the country.

He said meaningful political participation depended on sustained interaction with citizens at the grassroots and polling-unit levels.

The presidential candidate also urged young people to build a common sense of purpose around national development and engage citizens honestly on issues affecting their communities and the future of the country.

Responding, the SDP Vice National Chairman, Senator Ugochukwu Uba, who represented the National Chairman, Professor Sadiq Gombe, said the party was committed to pursuing what he described as a different approach to governance.

Uba said the SDP’s programme was anchored on the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy contained in Chapter Two of the Nigerian Constitution, particularly provisions relating to the welfare and security of citizens.

He said growing interest among young Nigerians in the party indicated increased engagement with its message and policy proposals.

According to him, the party’s recently presented manifesto contains programmes aimed at addressing some of Nigeria’s development challenges.

Uba argued that Nigeria had remained underdeveloped despite its human and material resources, saying leadership and governance remained central to addressing the situation.

He said the SDP was seeking a change in the country’s political culture through what he described as a different approach to governance and national development.

The visit provided an opportunity for the youth organisation and the SDP leadership to exchange views on governance, youth participation, economic opportunities and Nigeria’s development challenges.

World.title: Lagos APC targets millions of votes for Tinubu, Hamzat
World.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

LAGOS — The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress, APC, on Friday inaugurated its campaign council for the 2027 general elections, with party leaders setting ambitious targets for voter mobilisation in support of President Bola Tinubu and the party’s governorship candidate, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat.

The campaign council, comprising more than 1,200 members, was inaugurated at the APC Secretariat on Acme Road, Ikeja, as the party formally commenced preparations for the elections.

The party’s campaign structure lists Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu as chairman, with Hamzat as deputy chairman, while former Senator Musiliu Obanikoro is the Director-General. Rasaq Ajala is the Deputy Director-General and Adekunle Olayinka is the Campaign Secretary.

The inauguration was attended by senior party leaders, including APC Lagos Chairman, Pastor Cornelius Ojelabi; leaders of the Governance Advisory Council, GAC; former governors Babatunde Fashola and Akinwunmi Ambode; Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa; Senator Tokunbo Abiru; Senator Wasiu Eshilokun; former speakers of the state Assembly, Adeleke Mamora and Adeyemi Ikuforiji, among others.

Under the advisory structure, Prince Tajudeen Olusi is listed as Chairman of the Governance Advisory Council, while Sanwo-Olu is Advisory Council Chairman, with Fashola and Ambode as Co-Chairmen.

Other members of the advisory structure include the President’s Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila; Obasa and former Minister of Health, Adeleke Mamora.

The campaign council has directorates and sub-committees covering legal and compliance, party and inter-party affairs, administration and logistics, traditional institutions, diaspora engagement and residents’ associations.

Hamzat urges aggressive mobilisation

Addressing members of the council, Hamzat urged them to intensify grassroots mobilisation and campaign on the basis of the records and achievements of the APC-led administrations.

He highlighted what he described as economic milestones under the Tinubu administration, including tax reforms, increased agricultural and urea production, infrastructure development and efforts to tackle terrorism and kidnapping.

Hamzat said the party should be proud of its candidate and urged members not to be afraid to campaign for Tinubu.

He said: “We should be proud of our candidate. Our President has done the right things for this country. We should be very proud.

“We should not be fearful to go and campaign, because the President has stabilised the economy of this country.”

Hamzat also cited what he described as Nigeria’s trade surplus with the United States, attributing the development to increased agricultural and urea production.

He linked the development of the Lekki Free Trade Zone to Tinubu’s tenure as Lagos governor.

On tax reforms, Hamzat said the administration had undertaken changes to modernise the country’s tax system and commended members of the National Assembly for supporting the reforms.

He urged party supporters to mobilise voters for Tinubu, saying the party should improve on its previous electoral performance in Lagos.

“We have registered 7.3 million people in Lagos. As a member of our party, we cannot be voting only one million. We must do three, four million people to make sure that we galvanise votes for our President,” he said.

Hamzat also canvassed support for APC candidates at the senatorial, House of Representatives, governorship and state Assembly levels.

Speaking on Lagos, he described the state as a major contributor to Nigeria’s economy and highlighted its infrastructure projects, particularly the rail network.

He said the state’s economic importance made it necessary for residents to support candidates who, according to him, understood the state’s history, geography and development needs.

Hamzat said the campaign would be conducted under the banner, “Lagos Forward Together.”

Ojelabi demands grassroots mobilisation

The APC Lagos chairman, Ojelabi, urged all candidates to cooperate with the campaign council and conduct issue-based campaigns in line with the Electoral Act.

He described the inauguration as a milestone in the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections and charged council members to approach the assignment with discipline, accountability and a clear sense of purpose.

Ojelabi cautioned party members against complacency, noting that other political parties would also be working to win the elections.

With 118 days to the presidential election, he said the task before the campaign council was enormous and urged members to take the campaign to communities across the state.

He unveiled the strategy as “Operation Man Your Polling Booths”, with the party targeting mobilisation across the state’s 13,325 polling units.

Obanikoro urges unity

Obanikoro, the Director-General of the campaign council, urged members to work together and set aside personal differences ahead of the elections.

He also highlighted Hamzat’s public-service experience, including his service as a commissioner in Lagos, his work in the Federal Ministry of Works, Power and Housing and his tenure as deputy governor of Lagos State.

Obanikoro described Hamzat’s experience as a strong qualification for the governorship contest and commended the party for supporting his candidacy.

Olusi seeks united campaign

Speaking through former Deputy Governor Abiodun Ogunleye, Olusi commended the party’s leadership and expressed confidence in the campaign structure.

Ogunleye urged party members and political stakeholders to unite and intensify grassroots mobilisation across constituencies.

He said the party’s candidates possessed the experience and capacity required to represent the APC at various levels.

The inauguration ended with party supporters singing and expressing support for Tinubu and Hamzat ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: Cells that cheat Death: New clue to why some cancers return
World.content:
By Sola Ogundipe

Scientists at Israel’s Weizmann Institute of Science have uncovered a cellular mechanism that could deepen understanding of tissue regeneration while offering clues to why some cancers return after treatment.

Published in Nature Communications, the study identified a population of cells that begins the process of programmed cell death but survives to help rebuild severely damaged tissue. Named DARE cells, they multiplied rapidly and replenished nearly half of the damaged tissue within 48 hours in experiments involving fruit fly larvae.

The discovery sheds light on compensatory proliferation, a biological process in which surviving cells multiply to replace those lost through injury. However, the same survival mechanism could potentially enable cancer cells to withstand treatment.

Apoptosis, commonly known as programmed cell death, helps the body eliminate damaged, ageing and unwanted cells. Caspases, a group of enzymes, initiate and execute the process.

Research led by Prof. Eli Arama of the Weizmann Institute’s Department of Molecular Genetics has shown that caspases can also perform functions beyond cell destruction. His team suspected they might contribute to tissue regeneration.

Led by Dr. Tslil Braun, the researchers recreated a classic 1970s experiment in which radiation-damaged fly larvae regenerated functional wings. Using modern genetic tools, they tracked cells that activated the early stages of apoptosis but survived. “We set out to identify cells that push the self-destruct button but survive anyway,” Braun explained.

The researchers discovered DARE cells, which not only survived radiation but multiplied and repaired nearly half of the damaged tissue within 48 hours. They also identified a second population, called NARE cells. Unlike DARE cells, NARE cells had not activated their initiator caspase, although they survived and contributed to regeneration.

The distinction was crucial. When DARE cells were removed, compensatory proliferation disappeared. The researchers also found that signals from dying cells activated DARE cells, triggering rapid tissue repair. The study found that apoptosis begins normally in DARE cells. However, the process stops before the effector caspases can complete cellular destruction.

The researchers linked this interruption to a molecular motor protein that appears to tether the initiator caspase to the cell membrane, preventing activation of the enzymes responsible for completing cell death. When the team silenced the motor protein, DARE cells died and tissue regeneration was impaired.

Arama noted that overactivation of the same protein had previously been associated with cancerous tumour growth, raising the possibility that cancer cells could exploit a similar mechanism to evade apoptosis.

The finding does not establish that this process causes cancer recurrence in humans, but it provides a pathway for further investigation.

The scientists next examined whether DARE cells could pass their resistance to death to their descendants. After exposing the tissue to radiation a second time, they found that cell deaths during the initial hours were half those recorded after the first exposure. Most of the cells that died belonged to the NARE population. Descendants of DARE cells were reportedly seven times more resistant to cell death than cells in the original tissue.

“We wanted to understand whether resistance to death is inherited by the descendants of death-resistant cells that survived the initial irradiation,” Arama said. The finding may help explain how surviving cells acquire characteristics that allow them to withstand subsequent injury. In cancer, however, similar resistance could potentially enable tumour cells to survive treatment and contribute to recurrence.

The researchers stressed that their experiments were conducted in fruit flies, and the relevance to human cancers remains to be established. The study also revealed a feedback system that appears to prevent excessive regeneration.

DARE cells release growth signals that promote the multiplication of nearby NARE cells. In return, NARE cells release signals that inhibit DARE cell growth. This negative feedback loop allows tissue repair to proceed while helping prevent uncontrolled proliferation.

According to Arama, understanding these mechanisms could eventually support efforts to accelerate healthy tissue regeneration and improve cancer treatment strategies. “Many cancers originate in epithelial cells that have lost normal growth control, and many traditional cancer treatments aim to cause them to self-destruct through apoptosis,” he said. “Our findings pave the way for understanding why such treatments sometimes fail and how they could be improved.”

The discovery offers a new perspective on the body’s response to injury. A mechanism that helps healthy tissue recover could, under different circumstances, provide dangerous cells with a means of survival. The next challenge for researchers is to understand how to harness the regenerative benefits without enabling cancer cells to escape treatment.

World.title: ‘We have a responsibility’: Sharks rugby players stand against GBV
World.content:
The Sharks have become the first rugby club to speak out against gender-based violence in South Africa. Like many South Africans, the players also wore black on Friday, in solidarity with the mission to fight femicide.

Their commitment to protect women comes after police discovered nine bodies of women who were sexually assaulted and murdered in the Ekuhuleni district in recent weeks.

SHARKS PLAYERS STAND UP AGAINST GBV

In a video posted on its social media platforms, the Sharks revealed that they would wear black on Friday, 19 September, in solidarity with South Africans fighting GBV.



The club shared: “Gender-based violence (GBV) continues to devastate families and communities across South Africa. Today, we stand in black, in solidarity with every woman and child affected, and with every family carrying the pain of losing someone they love.

“We stand together for a country where everyone can live safely, freely and without fear”

In another post, several prominent Sharks players also publicly addressed the endemic.

Sharks player, Vincent Koch, who has 63 test caps for the Springboks, said, “The senseless killing and violence against women and girls in our country must stop. Every woman should be able to live, walk and live without fear

Mapimpi: “As men, we have a responsibility to speak up, to call it out and to never look the other way”.

Phepsi Buthelezi added, “We want to say that we stand with you. To our sisters and mothers, we see you, we hear you, and we will always love you”.



SPRINGBOK IMPI LEADS THE PACK

Meanwhile, Springboks Impi warrior Sibusiso Kotelo led a peaceful male protest in Johannesburg to show his commitment to taking action and holding perpetrators accountable for GBV.

He shared: “It is our responsibility as men to stand up and protect our women and children. Women should not see men and think of how to survive that encounter. Whether it’s going for a walk. Going into a lift. Getting into an Uber and anything else in between”.

Kotelo added that the men had prayed together and had also presented a petition to the mayor.

He added: “Not for demands but for a partnership with the city council as to what we can collaboratively achieve to ensure a safe environment for our women and children”.

World.title: Anton Taylor scammed by fraudulent visa agent
World.content:
Anton Taylor opens up about being scammed by a visa agent. Images via IG

Actor and comedian Anton Taylor has opened up about having to cancel an upcoming show in Dublin, after he and his pal, Khanyisa JamJam, were scammed by a fraudulent visa agent

The duo, who were expected to perform on stage next weekend, have offered their Irish fund full refunds.

ANTON TAYLOR ON BEING SCAMMED

In a social media post, Anton Taylor and Khanyisa JamJam shared how they were forced to cancel their popular Comedians of National Unity in Dublin, Ireland, after a visa agent fled with their cash.



Anton, a Bishop’s College alumnus, said: “He took us for the biggest ride of our lives”

Anton revealed how he paid the individual – whom they named in the video – over R13 00 to facilitate a visa for himself and his partner

“He ghosted me for six weeks. It’s the silence….he has been linked to numerous scams. It’s the same old story”.

Anton Taylor shared that he had to hire a private investigator to track down the visa agent who was in possession of his passport.

“After saying he would refund us, he ghosted us again!”

TIPS TO HIRING A VISA AGENT

Visa agents, like the one commissioned by Anton Taylor, assist individuals with navigating the visa application process, including preparing paperwork.

However, the actual visa decision is made by the relevant government or consular authority

Before you pay for any assistance with filing for your visa, pay attention to the following tips…

Check they are legitimate: Research the agent or agency, check reviews and verify their business details before paying.

Know what you’re paying for: Get a written breakdown of the agent’s fee, government visa fees and any additional costs.

Never accept a visa guarantee: No agent can guarantee approval. The final decision rests with the relevant embassy, consulate or immigration authority.

Keep copies of your documents: Make copies of your passport, application, supporting documents and anything you submit through the agent.

Get proof of payment and submission: Keep receipts and ask for your application reference number so that you can follow up.

World.title: Arnold Vosloo becomes a dad at 64!
World.content:
Arnold Vosloo has become a first-time dad at 64 years old. Images via IG

Arnold Vosloo has become a father at 64 years old, after his partner, Anika du Toit, gave birth earlier this week.

The couple, who have a 32 age gap, welcomed a baby boy.

The South African-born Hollywood actor filed for divorce from his wife of 27 years last June. Arnold is known for appearing in movies like The Mummy, Blood Diamond, and Darkman, and in series such as LudiK, 24, and NCIS.



ARNOLD VOSLOO WELCOMES BABY AT 64

According to reports, Arnold Vosloo and Anika du Toit welcomed their son, Daniel Reece Vosloo, who was born on 14 September 2026.

The Hollywood actor, who was born in Pretoria, has no children from previous relationships and marriages.

Despite calling the US home for more than three decades, Arnold has settled down in Kleinmond, in the Overberg region, with Anika and their baby.



Arnold and Anika, who are 32 years apart in age, began dating last year. They first met three years ago, when she was on the production team for Arnold’s Netflix series, Ludik.

Arnold Vosloo’s new romance and baby come just months after he filed for divorce from his wife of 27 years, Sylvia Ahi.

The former couple, who met on a blind date, cite “irreconcilable differences.” They had no children together.



The notoriously private star was previously married to American actress Nancy Mulford.

Arnold, who was born in Pretoria, moved to the US in the late 80s, where he became a naturalised citizen. He has expressed a desire to live a “quieter” life in South Africa.

Arnold Vosloo and his partner Anika du Toit.

Images via IG

WHO IS HIS BABY MAMA?

Arnold Vosloo’s baby mama is 32 years old, and 32 years younger than the SA-born Hollywood actor.



She graduated with a BA in drama, theatre and arts from the University of Free State.

Anika has worked on 30 professional productions, including Netflix series Savage Beauty and Ludik, and the movie iNumber Number: Jozi Gold. She is currently working on a TV adaptation of South African author Deon Meyer’s book Blood Safari.

Anika landed a small role on the Showmax series Breekpunt.



She loves travelling around the country, especially to small towns. Her hobbies include gold, hiking and road-tripping.

World.title: DStv gifts subscribers free Premium upgrade – here’s who qualifies
World.content:
DStv has offered Compact Plus subscribers a free upgrade to the Premium package. Image via DStv

DStv has officially rolled out its new system this week, and with it comes a free upgrade for existing subscribers from Compact Plus to its Premium tier.

The pay-per-view TV company, which falls under Multichoice and was recently acquired by French media giant Canal+, introduced the new structure on Thursday, 17 September.

Packages are priced from R99 per month, with the biggest draw card being a dedicated sports package.



Existing customers have been migrated automatically

The new DStv package structure is aimed at giving customers more flexibility and more content, for less, with several packages seeing price cuts while offering expanded channel line-ups.

Customers can also choose packages tailored to what they watch most, from sports and entertainment to movies and series.



Existing Compact Plus subscribers enjoyed an added advantage: as the package was effectively retired from the line-up, customers were promoted to the premium tier at no extra charge.

This effectively means that Compact Plus subscribers get the Premium channel line-up while paying their old prices.

Compact Plus on DStv Stream costs R549 per month, while the decoder-based Compact Plus is listed at R649 per month. DStv Premium costs R799 for streaming and R979 for the standard month-to-month decoder package.



Existing Compact Plus customers will continue to pay R549 for streaming or R649 for decoder while receiving the Premium channel experience, which includes the full bouquet of channels.

MultiChoice told MyBroadband that there is no fixed end date for this arrangement at .present

World.title: Pensioner’s SASSA money vanishes by month-end: Here’s what he wants instead
World.content:
Aaron Kibi has been receiving the SASSA Older Persons’ Grant for less than a year, and the retired homeowner says there’s one change he wants to see: an increase in the grant amount. Person’s Grant for less than a year, and the retired homeowner says there’s one change he wants to see: an increase in the grant.

Kibi, who lives in KwaZulu-Natal, receives R2 400 a month, paid directly into his Capitec Bank account. Between three and five people depend on that income each month, and Kibi says almost all of it goes toward food and groceries. By the end of each month, he says, there is nothing left over.

Despite the shortfall, Kibi confirmed that no one in his household has gone without food in the past month. He describes the grant as helpful, “but it is not enough” to fully cover his family’s basic needs.



Rising food prices remain his biggest worry

Kibi’s biggest financial concern right now is the cost of living, particularly the climbing food prices. He is one of roughly 18 million South Africans currently receiving a SASSA grant, many of whom report similar pressure as inflation continues to squeeze fixed incomes.

He has not applied for any additional government support, noting that he did not qualify for other assistance. Owning his own home offers some financial cushioning, but with several dependents relying on a single grant, Kibi says the money simply does not stretch far enough.

SASSA’s service gets a good review

Despite wanting a higher payout, Kibi praised the agency’s service delivery, rating its communication with recipients as “very good” and reporting no problems accessing his payments. Living under five kilometres from services, he avoids the added transport costs that burden recipients elsewhere.



Kibi believes the grant plays an important role beyond his own household. In his words, SASSA “assists in poverty alleviation and needy people”, a sentiment he says reflects why the system matters despite its shortcomings.

His story reflects a common theme among grant recipients: a system that runs smoothly on the administrative side but leaves many pensioners counting rands before the month is out.

World.title: Orlando Pirates transfer news: Full list of 13 new signings
World.content:
Orlando Pirates have announced another new signing, taking their total number of arrivals to 13 ahead of what promises to be a demanding season.

The Buccaneers have been the busiest club in the PSL transfer market, bringing in more new players than any other top-flight side as they prepare to compete across five different competitions.

Following several high-profile departures during the off-season, head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou and the Pirates hierarchy have moved quickly to rebuild the squad and add depth in key positions.



Bulelani Sigomoshe is the latest player to join the Soweto giants after making the move from Milford FC. His arrival follows that of Bheki Mabuza, who was signed earlier this month.

Orlando Pirates have had a busy transfer window

Not all of the new arrivals have had to wait long to make an impression. Thapelo Mokobodi and Gamphani Lungu have already caught the attention of Pirates supporters with their performances and have established themselves as important members of the starting XI.

With the season still in its early stages, it remains to be seen how many of the 13 new signings will go on to become key players for the Buccaneers.

Bulelani Sigomoshe – 26-year-old right-back, signed from Milford FC.



Kabelo Kgositsile – 22-year-old winger, signed from Baroka FC.

Sebastian Pedersen – 27-year-old striker, signed from Sundal.

Thapelo Mokobodi – 23-year-old midfielder, signed from Stellenbosch FC.

Mthetheleli Mthiyane – 25-year-old midfielder, signed from Stellenbosch FC.

Sbangani Zulu – 24-year-old defender, signed from Richards Bay FC.



Bohlale Ngwato – 20-year-old winger, signed from Siwelele FC.

Neo Rapoo – 20-year-old left-back, signed from Siwelele FC.

Aphiwe Baliti – 24-year-old left-back, who has remained at Siwelele FC on loan.
