World.title: Azcatitlan Codex returns to Mexico after 186 years, on loan from France
World.content:
A monumental illustrated account of Aztec history — from the Mexica migration to the Spanish conquest of Tenochtitlán — is back in Mexico for the first time in 186 years under a loan agreement with France’s national library.

The centuries-old Azcatitlan Codex, on loan through Dec. 6, chronicles the origins, expansion and collapse of the Mexica world. Tenochtitlán was the island capital of the Mexica empire, built on Lake Texcoco where Mexico City now stands.

The document left Mexico in 1840 and remained in Europe through a succession of private and institutional collections. It has been held by the National Library of France since the 1890s, making its temporary return a rare cultural and diplomatic event for Mexico.

The loan is not a repatriation — unlike Mexico’s 2024 recovery of three 16th-century codices and Spain’s 2023 return of a Tlaquiltenango Codex fragment, which was expected to fetch more than US $100,000 at auction before Spain’s Civil Guard withdrew it.

But it comes as Mexico continues to seek the return of pre-Hispanic and colonial-era objects that left the country in earlier centuries, and after President Claudia Sheinbaum described codices in France as a top priority for recovery before French President Emmanuel Macron’s 2025 visit.

Instead, Sheinbaum and Macron agreed to a temporary, reciprocal exchange to honor the 200 years of diplomatic relations between their two countries.

Where to see the Azcatitlan Codex

The Azcatitlan Codex arrived in Mexico City this month for an exhibition at the National Museum of Anthropology, while Mexico has sent the Boturini Codex to Paris for display at the French national library.

The exchange is part of the Great Franco-Mexican Festival, a binational cultural program featuring nearly 200 activities, according to a joint release from Mexico’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Culture Ministry and National Institute of Anthropology and History.

The Azcatitlan Codex is a significant record of the Mexica, the Nahuatl-speaking people often called Aztecs. “Aztec” is widely used for the empire centered on Tenochtitlán, while “Mexica” more specifically identifies the people who founded and ruled it.

Created in the Valley of Mexico in the late 16th or early 17th century, the manuscript combines Mesoamerican pictorial writing with European paper, bookbinding and Spanish text.

The manuscript is divided into three broad sections: the Mexica migration from Aztlán; the reigns of Tenochtitlán’s rulers; and the 1519 arrival of Spanish forces led by Hernán Cortés, the conquest and evangelization.

The codex’s images have made it a particularly vivid source. One scene depicts Cortés and Spanish conquistadors, accompanied by Indigenous people carrying loads. Another depicts Mexica warriors defending Tenochtitlán’s great pyramid.

Tres grandes momentos atraviesan las páginas del Códice Azcatitlan: la migración desde Aztlan, la historia de Tenochtitlan y los primeros años de la Nueva España. En el marco de la Gran Fiesta Franco-Mexicana, el Museo Nacional de Antropología presenta por primera vez en México… pic.twitter.com/wF8hjc3PO3 — Secretaría de Cultura (@cultura_mx) September 18, 2026

The museum is exhibiting the original under low light, opened to pages four and five. They depict eight Indigenous groups setting out to find the site where Huitzilopochtli instructed them to found Tenochtitlán, El País reported.

Photographic reproductions of the remaining pages are displayed on the wall of the anthropology museum, located in the capital’s Chapultepec Park.

The exhibition also includes 25 archaeological and ethnographic objects and facsimiles of nine manuscripts, including the Codex Mendoza, the De la Cruz-Badiano Codex and the Boturini Codex.

The Boturini Codex, also known as the Tira de la Peregrinación, traces the Mexica journey from Aztlán to Tenochtitlán. It belongs to Mexico’s National Library of Anthropology and History and is due to return from France in December, when the Azcatitlan Codex will also return to Paris.

The temporary exchange is part of wider efforts to preserve, digitize and recover Indigenous documentary heritage, such as the digital public release of the Florentine Codex, a 12-book encyclopedia of Mexica life compiled by Nahua scholars in the 16th century.

With reports from BBC.com, El País and Deutsche Welle

World.title: Peso slides toward 17.3 to the dollar after US Fed’s first rate hike since 2023
World.content:
The peso depreciated on Friday morning and was on track for its worst weekly performance since March, as traders continued to react to the U.S. Federal Reserve’s decision to raise interest rates.

The tightening of U.S. monetary policy has eroded the appeal of assets denominated in local currency, a trend that became evident as soon as the Fed announced its decision on Wednesday morning.

The peso had weakened to 17.32 to the dollar Friday morning, and hovered at 17.229 to the dollar by 2:00 p.m., down nearly 6 centavos from Thursday’s close of 17.1706. Market analysts projected a trading range of between 17.08 to 17.28 pesos per dollar for Friday’s session.

The Fed’s decision on Wednesday to raise its benchmark rate by 25 basis points, bringing it to a range of 3.75% to 4%, interrupted an eight-month pause that saw the U.S. rate remain between 3.50% and 3.75% since December.

The peso lost 0.58%, or 10 centavos, against the dollar that same afternoon.

Gabriela Siller, director of Financial Analysis at Banco BASE, said the fall of the peso is directly linked to the Fed decision, as well as the possibility of another rate cut in the United States this year.

“This is relevant because of carry trade operations, where the interest rate differential between Mexico and the U.S. is important,” she said.

The carry trade is an investment strategy in which investors borrow money in a currency with a low interest rate to invest in another currency or asset with a higher rate.

“With the rate cut, traders get a lower return, because the rate differential is the net return after paying off the loan,” Siller explained.

The Fed’s decision reduced the interest rate differential between Mexico and the U.S. to 250 basis points, a historic low not seen since December 2015. Mexico’s benchmark rate sits at 6.5% and the Bank of Mexico is expected to hold the rate steady at its meeting next week.

If the Fed announces another rate hike before the end of the year, as anticipated, this differential will be at 225 points, representing even lower returns for investors.

As such, the peso’s value would be impacted by the relative unattractiveness of peso-denominated investments.

These expectations are also related to the recent inflation trend in Mexico.

As of August, inflation stood at 3.26%, remaining within the central bank’s target range, a situation that contrasts with the United States, where inflationary pressures remain more persistent, suggesting the Fed will continue with a more aggressive posture.

With reports from El Economista, Forex.com and El Financiero

World.title: 59 million liters of stolen fuel seized in Guanajuato state, the largest such bust in Mexican history
World.content:
Listen to this article

Authorities confiscated 59 million liters of stolen fuel, the largest single-site seizure in Mexico’s history and five times larger than the March 2025 bust in Tamaulipas that led to 14 arrests, including six members of the Navy.

The operation, which was triggered after a July 3 arrest involving a tanker truck loaded with stolen fuel, occurred at a property located in the small community of La Fragua in the San José Iturbide municipality, Guanajuato state, alongside Federal Highway 57.

Las indagatorias para combatir a redes delictivas vinculadas al contrabando de combustible llevaron a la #FGR a cumplimentar órdenes de cateo que derivaron en el hallazgo de más de 59 millones de litros de hidrocarburo en #Guanajuato. Más ▶️ https://t.co/1aA8iguFlJ pic.twitter.com/D6A7lUbh4n — Guanajuato (@FGR_Gto) September 18, 2026

State and federal agents seized 10 tanks containing suspected fuel (diesel, regular gasoline and premium gasoline), three tanker trucks, containers used to transport fuel, and documentation. No arrests had been reported as of Friday morning.

State officials said the amount of hydrocarbon material discovered — roughly equivalent to the amount seized in all of 2025 — is so large that its identification and handling will have to be carried out by specialized personnel to prevent spills and fires.

The July 3 incident in which a person was arrested while unloading approximately 30,000 liters of stolen fuel at a gas station in San Luis de la Paz, Guanajuato, prompted an investigation that led to another arrest weeks later at an LP gas dispensing station in Dolores Hidalgo.

As the suspects were unable to provide documentation establishing traceability, a judge issued a search warrant after investigators identified the storage facility in La Fragua as the likely source.

Guanajuato Security Minister Juan Mauro González Martínez said that the seizure goes beyond the volume confiscated.

“Investigating possible irregular fuel operations allows us to reduce the risk of fires, explosions and spills, while also protecting our communities and the environment,” he said. “It also disrupts potential sources of funding for criminal organizations.”

The facility was equipped with access roads, both asphalt and metal, for the movement of trucks and rail vans, as well as large-scale containers with a capacity for up to 80 million liters. All materials have been turned over to the Federal Attorney General’s Office (FGR).

For now, the authorities have not publicly established the origin of the 59 million liters seized, a task the FGR will undertake.

Prosecutors will also seek to determine who was in charge of the mega-operation, which is located just outside La Fragua, a community of fewer than 400 people. Current ownership remains unverified.

A small fuel storage facility was authorized there in 2013. Ownership changed hands several times by 2020, by which time it had expanded and was legally established as a Petroleum Products Storage and Supply Terminal.

At the time, the facility was operated by Gas Natural del Noreste, in partnership with ExxonMobil and Grupo Gasolinero Orsan and had been granted permits from the Environment Ministry and the federal Agency for Safety, Energy and Environment.

This latest bust is the fifth this year in Guanajuato related to stolen fuel, though the previous four pale in comparison:

55,000 liters of fuel were seized during a Feb. 25 joint operation across three towns;

Twin operations in Apaseo el Grande on March 31 netted 99,000 liters of fuel.

State police seized a tanker truck carrying 21,000 liters of fuel near Pénjamo on Aug. 27.

A clandestine tunnel providing access to a Pemex pipeline was discovered and neutralized.

With reports from El País, La Jornada, Zeta, El Financiero and Periódico Correo

World.title: El Jalapeño: National Palace overrun by feral cats, Sheinbaum admits
World.content:
All stories in El Jalapeño are satire and not real news. Check out the original article here.

MEXICO CITY — In an unexpected admission during a routine morning address, President Claudia Sheinbaum confirmed that the National Palace’s administrative functions have been severely disrupted by an unmanaged population surge of its feline residents.

While the palace was originally reported to house 16 felines — all legally classified under Mexican law as “living fixed assets” — unregistered stray populations have ballooned, leaving cabinet members, visitors and security personnel navigating a sprawling feline hierarchy that operates outside government oversight.

The crisis reportedly escalated when an attempt to introduce a newly adopted puppy, Rollo, aimed at providing emotional well-being support to palace staff, was immediately thwarted by a coordinated blockade of senior orange tabbies occupying the primary garden corridors.

“We attempted to establish a balanced workspace for all four-legged personnel,” Sheinbaum explained, adjusting her podium microphone to avoid disturbing a sleeping calico. “However, the current asset distribution leans approximately 98% feline, and they have made it clear that additional canine integration will require extensive inter-departmental negotiation.”

Palace officials admitted that several key historic rooms have effectively been ceded to the animals. The famous courtyards now run on cat schedules, with high-level diplomatic meetings routinely paused to accommodate lap inspections by roving kitties. Staff members trying to process official paperwork report that several desktop keyboards remain indefinitely occupied by napping felines.

Despite the territorial challenges, the administration confirmed it has no plans to evict the current residents, citing their permanent legal protections. Instead, the government is considering creating a specialized feline mediation task force to negotiate shared corridor access before upcoming foreign dignitary visits.

World.title: Officials report 43% drop in Guanajuato homicides: Friday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Listen to this article

Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

📉 Guanajuato homicides down 43% this year : At Friday’s mañanera in Irapuato, National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa reported an average of 3.2 homicides per day in Guanajuato in August, 75% lower than in February 2025, the state’s most violent month under Sheinbaum. The daily average for the first eight months of 2026 was 4, a 43% year-over-year decline. This year is on track to be the state’s least violent since 2017.

: At Friday’s mañanera in Irapuato, National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa reported an average of 3.2 homicides per day in Guanajuato in August, 75% lower than in February 2025, the state’s most violent month under Sheinbaum. The daily average for the first eight months of 2026 was 4, a 43% year-over-year decline. This year is on track to be the state’s least violent since 2017. 🚔 10,699 arrests in Guanajuato since October 2024 : Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said 172 of the people detained through Aug. 31 were “priority targets.” In the same period, authorities also seized more than 6 tonnes of drugs and over 2,000 firearms, and dismantled two methamphetamine labs.

: Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said 172 of the people detained through Aug. 31 were “priority targets.” In the same period, authorities also seized more than 6 tonnes of drugs and over 2,000 firearms, and dismantled two methamphetamine labs. ⚖️ Suspect arrested in murder of Spanish student : García Harfuch confirmed that a man known as “El Trompas,” identified as Francisco Javier Meléndez, was detained Thursday in Cuautla, Morelos, in connection with the murder of Claudia Tacoronte Aguilera, a 21-year-old Spanish exchange student.

: García Harfuch confirmed that a man known as “El Trompas,” identified as Francisco Javier Meléndez, was detained Thursday in Cuautla, Morelos, in connection with the murder of Claudia Tacoronte Aguilera, a 21-year-old Spanish exchange student. 📞 Sheinbaum says her call with Trump was “very good”: Sheinbaum said she spoke to the U.S. president about trade issues on Wednesday. She said differences have not yet been resolved, but that good progress is being made.

Why today’s mañanera matters

President Claudia Sheinbaum held her Friday morning press conference in Irapuato, a city in Guanajuato, a state that in recent years has been Mexico’s most violent in terms of total homicides.

At the mañanera, federal security officials took the opportunity to outline the progress that has been made in combating violence in the state. Much of the violence in Guanajuato is related to organized crime, and, in particular, a long-running turf war between the Jalisco New Generation Cartel and the Santa Rosa de Lima Cartel.

Also of note at today’s mañanera was Security Minister Omar García Harfuch’s confirmation that a man known as “El Trompas” was detained in connection with the murder in Cuautla, Morelos, of Claudia Tacoronte Aguilera, a 21-year-old Spanish woman who was studying at the Autonomous University of the State of Morelos on an exchange program.

In addition, Sheinbaum spoke briefly about her trade-focused call on Wednesday with U.S. President Donald Trump. The call came less than two weeks after Trump asserted that Mexico has “nothing” the United States needs — apart from “hot tamales” and “tomatoes” — and therefore the U.S. could cease trading with its southern neighbor. In reality, Mexico supplies a wide range of goods to the U.S., and the economies of the two countries are highly integrated.

Homicides down 43% in Guanajuato this year

National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa reported that there was an average of 3.2 homicides per day in Guanajuato in August. Figueroa highlighted that the daily average in August was 75% lower than that in February 2025, the most violent month in Guanajuato since Sheinbaum took office in October 2024.

She reported that there was an average of 4 homicides per day in Guanajuato in the first eight months of 2026, a reduction of 43% compared to 2025. Data presented by Figueroa showed that 2026 is on track to be the least violent year in Guanajuato since 2017.

More than 10,000 arrests in Guanajuato since Sheinbaum took office

García Harfuch reported that more than 10,600 people were arrested in Guanajuato between Oct. 1, 2024 — the date Sheinbaum was sworn in as president — and Aug. 31, 2026.

Of the 10,699 people detained in the state in the period, 172 were “priority targets,” García Harfuch said.

He also reported that over 6 tonnes of drugs and more than 2,000 firearms were seized in Guanajuato between October 2024 and August 2026. In addition, two methamphetamine laboratories were dismantled, García Harfuch said.

Suspect arrested in Morelos femicide case

García Harfuch reported that federal and state security forces detained Francisco Javier “N” on Thursday in connection with the murder of Tacoronte. The suspect has been identified as Francisco Javier Meléndez in media reports. He was detained in Cuautla, a city around 40 kilometers southeast of Cuernavaca, the capital of Morelos.

García Harfuch first reported the arrest in a social media post on Thursday evening.

On Friday morning, he said that “preventing femicides and addressing violence against women” is a “priority” of the federal government.

En #Morelos, autoridades federales y estatales detienen a un hombre por el feminicidio de una joven de nacionalidad española. https://t.co/mLtMcbL8ch pic.twitter.com/jyLFGK6NtE — Secretaría de Seguridad y Protección Ciudadana (@SSPCMexico) September 18, 2026

Sheinbaum discloses ‘very good’ call with Trump

Sheinbaum told reporters that she spoke to Trump on Wednesday.

“It was a scheduled call,” she said, adding that she often speaks to the U.S. president without publicly announcing their discussions.

“Why? Because we’re making progress on trade issues,” Sheinbaum said.

She said that differences over trade have not yet been resolved, but stressed that good progress is being made.

Reuters reported on Sept. 11 that “Mexico and the United States are racing to reach a bilateral trade deal before the U.S. midterm elections,” which will take place on Nov. 3. As part of a bilateral deal, Mexico is seeking the reduction — or ideally the elimination — of U.S. tariffs on Mexican steel, aluminum and vehicles.

On July 1, the United States announced that it had declined to renew the USMCA in its “current form,” although the three-way pact remains in effect.

Sheinbaum said her call with Trump was “very good.”

“… The Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco and Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard were with me in the conversation,” she added.

By Mexico News Daily chief staff writer Peter Davies (peter.davies@mexiconewsdaily.com)

World.title: A mountain, a legend and a dream: Chavela Vargas’ Tepoztlán home
World.content:
The story goes that when Chavela Vargas, the iconic singer of Mexican ranchera music, visited Tepoztlán in the state of Morelos, she was captivated by the mountain known as Chalchitépetl. She was amazed by its beauty, but more importantly, Vargas was struck by the fact that she had dreamed of that exact formation many times, despite never having seen it before. After seeing the mountain, she decided to make the town her home.

“She came, knocked on the door, and asked what she had to do to live here, and that is how she ended up staying,” said Gerardo Ramírez, the manager of Casa Chavela.

How Chavela chose her home

Vargas, who was Costa Rican by birth and famous for her declaration, “We Mexicans are born wherever the hell we want,” arrived in Mexico at age 17 and began her career singing in cantinas. She was later discovered and mentored by the iconic Mexican singer José Alfredo Jiménez. Vargas was a close friend — and perhaps more — to figures like Frida Kahlo, Diego Rivera, Joaquín Sabina and Federico García Lorca, and she became a major icon for the LGBTQ+ movement.

Vargas arrived in Tepoztlán in 2007, by which time she was already a legend whose career was celebrated throughout Latin America and Europe. The house she chose was located on the Tepoztlán-Cuernavaca Federal Highway and belonged to Emma Teresa Ortiz, known as “Monina.” At the time, the property was called Quinta Monina. There were once two other houses on the property, which were also inhabited by artists, including the famous actress María Eugenia Llamas.

When Vargas arrived at Quinta Monina, she requested changes to the house that reflected her strong personality and creativity. Today, the building has become a landmark of Mexican architectural design.

An architectural gem

The initial design of Casa Chavela was straightforward, with a large hallway connecting the kitchen, living room, dining room and two bedrooms, as well as a terrace. This was later transformed at Vargas’ request. Today, the house is a blend of volcanic rock — typical of Tepoztlán construction — and large windows with orange ironwork that bathe the interior in light, reminiscent of functionalist architecture.

“The reason all the ironwork is this orange color is that, when Chavela moved into this house, she asked for the terrace to be enclosed with glass, which has become a distinctive feature of the house,” Ramírez explained.

In 2020, the Romero family — comprising architects, designers and engineers — purchased the property and remodeled it using local materials, inspired by Vargas’ original ideas.

They replaced the tiles, added two rooms and expanded the orange ironwork windows to the bedrooms and dining room, giving the house openness and light. In terms of decoration, the home features ocote pine crafts from the nearby town of Ocotitlán, and Vargas’ iconic jorongos (traditional Mexican woolen garments) hang on the walls. Her famous equipal — a handcrafted, pre-Hispanic-style armchair — lined in bright colors, can also be admired.

A place for art, inspiration and creativity

The surrounding gardens contain more than 60 trees that the owners have added in recent years, while preserving the original vegetation. A Y-shaped pool and numerous totems made from traditional clay from Amayuca, Morelos, add to the house’s unique atmosphere.

A podium in the shape of a kiosk crowns the garden and is used for ceremonies such as weddings. Furthermore, as the land slopes down, an area of old stables appears; these now serve as rooms for artists in residence.

Further down is a huge open living room that serves as a cultural space for concerts, meetings and exhibitions. While Casa Chavela welcomes guests through Airbnb and by renting out rooms like a hotel, it also has a social purpose: It offers free lodging to artists in residence.

Since 2022, five artists have completed residencies of between two and three weeks, donating their work to the house collection. Many of these pieces were inspired by Vargas, though the work can cover any topic.

Vargas spent her final years in this house, from 2007 to 2012. During this time, she found peace and formed a profound relationship with the mountain of her dreams, Chalchitépetl. After a complicated and magnificent life, she found a place of contemplation here, as well as the strength to overcome her struggles. Casa Chavela is undoubtedly imbued with the personal magic and spirit of her personality.

Ana Paula de la Torre is a Mexican journalist and collaborator for various outlets, including Milenio, Animal Político, Vice, Newsweek en Español, Televisa and Mexico News Daily.

TANZANIA · AFCON 2027, 19 SEPTEMBER 2026

Key Facts —The headline — Tanzania’s AFCON 2027 stadium program is in its final phase: the Benjamin Mkapa Stadium renovation is about 95 percent complete, and Arusha’s new Samia Suluhu Hassan Stadium has passed 80 percent. —The newcomer — Dodoma has broken ground on a US$136 million, 32,000-seat stadium, giving the capital its first international tournament venue. —The islands — Zanzibar’s renovated Amaan Stadium is ready, and the 36,500-seat Fumba/Maisara complex is under construction as the archipelago’s first major sports facility. —The clock — CAF required venues at 80 percent readiness by August 2026 and conducts its full readiness audit in late 2026. The tournament runs 19 June to 17 July 2027. —The tickets — Official AFCON 2027 ticket sales are expected to open between August and October 2026 via CAF’s portal. Tanzania’s group matches on 20, 24 and 28 June 2027 will be the hottest seats.

Ten months before kickoff, Tanzania is quietly winning its part of the AFCON 2027 construction race. One stadium is essentially done, a second is nearly there, a third just broke ground — and Zanzibar is building the first major arena in its history.

AFCON comes to East Africa for the first time in 2027, co-hosted by Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda. Photo: Bantu Gazette

Benjamin Mkapa Stadium, Dar es Salaam — the fortress is nearly back

The 60,000-seat national stadium in Temeke District closed for six months of deep renovation and is now about 95 percent complete, according to government figures reported by The Citizen in early September. The core of the work is a brand-new hybrid pitch — the old turf and several layers of sub-soil were removed entirely to meet CAF’s drainage and surface standards for tropical coastal rain — plus rebuilt VVIP areas and new seating. The government allocated TZS 179.8 billion (about US$68 million) for the program. Mkapa is expected to stage the tournament’s biggest Tanzanian nights, including knockout matches.

Samia Suluhu Hassan Stadium, Arusha — the new icon passes 80 percent

Purpose-built for AFCON at a cost of US$112 million, Arusha’s 30,000-seat arena has passed the 80 percent mark, with its V-shaped canopy roof complete and seats going in. The faceted facade mirrors a tanzanite gemstone, found only in the Arusha region. Built by China Railway Construction Engineering Group since April 2024, it targets completion in 2026 and will give the safari capital group-stage football beneath Mount Meru.

Dodoma — the capital enters the map

The newest project is also the boldest: a US$136 million, 32,000-seat stadium in Dodoma, officially commissioned this year. It is early-stage — around 10 percent complete — but it brings top-flight international football to the seat of government for the first time. Whether it hosts tournament matches or serves as a training and legacy venue will be decided in CAF’s final venue allocations.

Zanzibar — island football, twice over

Zanzibar offers AFCON’s most unusual stage. The historic Amaan Stadium (15,000), China’s first stadium project in Africa back in 1970, was fully renovated and re-inaugurated in December 2023 — minutes from UNESCO-listed Stone Town. Nearby, the Fumba/Maisara Sports Complex (36,500 seats, TZS 388.8 billion) is rising as the first major sports facility in the archipelago’s history, with its foundation stone laid in September 2024.

The CAF clock and what it means for fans

CAF set an 80 percent readiness threshold for August 2026 and runs its full venue audit in late 2026. Tanzania’s core venues are on or ahead of that line; the regional picture is mixed, with Kenya’s Talanta Stadium past 90 percent and Uganda investing over US$600 million across stadiums and support infrastructure. The three hosts are also discussing a joint “Pamoja visa” so fans can move freely between Nairobi, Kampala, Dar es Salaam and Zanzibar during the tournament. World.title: PayJustNow Mobile Launches on Cell C as Weaver Fintech Bets on Rewards
World.content:

One email, every weekday morning. African markets, politics and business — filed from our newsroom in Rio.

SOUTH AFRICA · FINTECH, 18 SEPTEMBER 2026

Key Facts —The launch — PayJustNow Mobile, Weaver Fintech’s own mobile virtual network operator (MVNO), began a soft rollout to selected customers on 27 August 2026. —The network — The service runs on Cell C’s network. Cell C has positioned itself as South Africa’s preferred MVNO host, adding Dolphin Mobile in July and now PayJustNow Mobile. —The hook — Airtime and data rewards are tied to customer behaviour on PayJustNow, the country’s largest buy-now-pay-later app, with more than a million Google Play downloads. —The backdrop — Weaver skipped its interim dividend in August after bad-debt costs jumped 62 percent to over R1 billion. The fintech arm still grew revenue 30 percent. —The base — Weaver serves 5.1 million customers, up 17 percent year on year, and holds about R1.1 billion in cash and unused facilities.

South Africa’s biggest buy-now-pay-later company is now also a mobile operator. Weaver Fintech has quietly switched on PayJustNow Mobile, a phone service that rewards good repayment behaviour with airtime and data — and it is doing so while tightening lending after a bad-debt shock.

PayJustNow Mobile turns the BNPL app’s five-million-strong customer base into a distribution channel for mobile services. Photo: The Rio Times archive

A soft launch, not a splash

There was no launch event and no advertising campaign. PayJustNow Mobile began rolling out to selected customers on 27 August 2026, according to industry trackers, with tech outlet MyBroadband confirming the service on 1 September. Weaver Fintech, the JSE-listed group formerly known as HomeChoice International, had flagged a “soft launch” of the product in its interim results in mid-August.

The service is a mobile virtual network operator: Weaver owns the customer relationship, the brand and the rewards programme, while the calls and data physically run on Cell C’s network. It is the second MVNO to join Cell C in two months, after Dolphin Mobile went live on 22 July. Cell C, which stopped building its own radio network years ago and now roams on partner infrastructure, has made hosting MVNOs a core business.

Why a lender wants to be a phone company

The logic is retention. PayJustNow’s model depends on customers repaying on time and coming back for the next purchase. Mobile service gives Weaver a monthly touchpoint that credit alone cannot provide — and a rewards currency that costs little but feels valuable. Early details indicate airtime and data benefits tied to customer behaviour on the platform.

The move follows a playbook proven elsewhere on the continent: fintechs and banks use connectivity to lock in ecosystems. It also diversifies revenue at a moment when the core lending business needs tighter, not looser, growth.

The bad-debt backdrop

The launch lands in Weaver’s hardest credit cycle in years. In the six months to the end of June, group revenue grew 10 percent to R2.8 billion, but debtor costs surged 62 percent to just over R1 billion and the credit loss ratio climbed to almost 25 percent, from 21 percent. Headline earnings slipped about 9 percent to R272 million, and the board skipped the interim dividend to preserve cash.

A technical failure at DebiCheck, the bank-authenticated debit-order system, made some paying customers look like defaulters — a problem chief executive Sean Wibberley says has been resolved. Weaver cut its targeted approval rate from 81.4 to 75.8 percent, shortened loan terms, and slowed new lending growth from 15 percent in the first quarter to 6 percent in the second. July arrears measures improved 13 percent, the first sign the turn is taking hold. We covered the credit squeeze in detail when the results broke in August.

The engine underneath

For all the credit pain, the fintech division — the part PayJustNow Mobile now extends — lifted revenue 30 percent and fee income 43 percent, and it generates 94 percent of the group’s trading profit. Customer numbers rose 17 percent to 5.1 million. That base, plus R1.1 billion in cash and unused facilities, is what Weaver is betting on: a captive audience for mobile services, digital banking and whatever comes next. Rival digital banks such as GoTyme, which we profiled this month, are chasing the same customer from the banking side.

Wibberley expects consumer finances to stay strained through the second half, with transport and food costs squeezing households. The mobile bet suggests Weaver thinks the winners of that squeeze will be the platforms that own the most everyday touchpoints — and few are as everyday as the phone itself.

Frequently Asked Questions What is PayJustNow Mobile? It is a mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) run by Weaver Fintech, the company behind the PayJustNow buy-now-pay-later app. The service sells SIM-based mobile plans with airtime and data rewards linked to customer behaviour, and it runs on Cell C’s network. When did PayJustNow Mobile launch? The soft rollout to selected customers began on 27 August 2026. Weaver Fintech had announced a beta launch in its interim results earlier in August. A full public launch date has not been confirmed. Which network does PayJustNow Mobile use? Cell C. The operator has become South Africa’s main MVNO host and added its second fintech-flavoured partner in two months, after Dolphin Mobile launched on the same network on 22 July 2026. Why is a BNPL company launching a phone service? Retention and data. A monthly mobile plan keeps customers inside the PayJustNow ecosystem, and rewards for on-time repayment support the credit book. The fintech division already produces 94 percent of Weaver’s trading profit, and mobile adds a fee-based revenue line that does not depend on lending.

World.title: Nigeria’s BOI Development Bond Raises About US$206 Million
World.content:
NIGERIA · MARKETS

Key Facts — What happened BOI, Bank of Industry, sold a five-year naira bond, closing at about 274.19 billion naira (US$206 million).

— How big The offer started at 250 billion naira (US$188 million) and was enlarged after strong demand.

— Who bought Pension funds, banks, insurers, asset managers and other institutions, with NSIA and IFC reported as anchor investors.

— Who advised Chapel Hill Denham led the deal, with FCMB Capital Markets, RMB Nigeria and Quest Merchant Bank also involved.

— The catch A 17.60% fixed rate is costly money, so returns depend on BOI lending the cash well.

— What comes next Final allotment details await regulatory approval, and officials hope BOI funding can reach 1 trillion naira (US$752 million).

The Bank of Industry sold more than it planned to local pension funds, banks and other large investors, advisers FCMB Capital Markets and RMB Nigeria said.

Nigeria’s Bank of Industry (BOI) has raised about 274.19 billion naira (US$206 million) through its first domestic bond. The BOI development bond pays a fixed 17.60% a year and matures in 2031.

How the BOI development bond came together

BOI, whose roots date back to 1959, is owned by the federal government and gives long-term loans to businesses. It had already borrowed abroad before this first local bond.

The bond was issued through BOI Financing SPV Plc, a special-purpose company, under BOI’s US$1 billion Multi-Currency Instruments Programme. It is the bank’s first bond in Nigeria’s domestic market.

BOI first offered 250 billion naira (US$188 million). The offer was oversubscribed within five working days, according to BOI’s managing director, Olasupo Olusi.

BOI then used a “green-shoe” option, which lets an issuer sell extra bonds when demand is high. The final size rose to about 274.19 billion naira (US$206 million) at 18 September 2026 rates.

Reports round the final figure slightly differently, at 274.18 or 274.19 billion naira (about US$206 million either way). The signed documents put it at 274.1868 billion naira (US$206 million), according to MarketForces Africa.

BOI said on 3 September 2026 that it had completed closing the deal. Advisers say it is the largest bond by a Nigerian development finance institution, based on public market data.

Who arranged and bought the bond

Chapel Hill Denham was lead issuing house and bookrunner. FCMB Capital Markets was a joint issuing house and bookrunner, and RMB Nigeria and Quest Merchant Bank also advised.

FCMB Capital Markets’ managing director, Ikechukwu Omeruah, said the deal “highlights the depth of Nigeria’s domestic debt capital market”.

RMB Nigeria’s Chidi Iwuchukwu said it “demonstrates the ability of Nigeria’s capital markets to mobilise long-term capital at scale”. RMB earlier advised BOI on its first Eurobond, a bond sold abroad.

Buyers included pension fund administrators, banks, insurers, asset managers, development finance institutions and companies. Two outlets report the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority (NSIA) and the International Finance Corporation (IFC) as anchor investors.

The bond pays interest twice a year, BusinessDay reported. No principal is repaid for the first two years, then repayments are spread over the remaining term.

Why investors wanted it

Analysts point to the high return and BOI’s close links to the state. BOI is owned by the federal government, so investors see its risk as close to Nigeria’s own.

Muda Yusuf of the Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise said it has “more or less a sovereign guarantee”. That is his view, not a formal guarantee.

Yusuf also noted that the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) now plays a smaller role in funding businesses through intervention schemes. He said BOI can help “fill that gap more effectively”.

Charles Sanni of Cowry Treasurers said the bond lets fund managers spread money beyond federal government securities. He added that it pays more than comparable government paper.

Olusi also credited President Bola Tinubu, who approved incentives for investors. A 100 billion naira (US$75 million) fund approved for BOI will help lower loan costs for manufacturers.

Olusi called the response “a vote of confidence not only in BOI, but also in the capacity of Nigeria’s domestic capital market”. He said the aim is to turn that confidence into more lending.

Why this matters for expats and investors

For foreign investors and expats with naira savings, this deal shows local institutions can fund large, long-term projects. That can mean more naira bonds to choose from later.

Local manufacturers and suppliers may also gain. BOI says the money will fund firms in priority sectors, including industrial growth, import substitution and local value addition.

Still, returns in naira must be weighed against currency moves when converted into dollars. The high fixed rate also reflects Nigeria’s expensive borrowing environment.

Olusi has said the industrial financing gap is estimated at more than US$35 billion a year. Manufacturing is about 7.2% of gross domestic product (GDP), against a national goal of 25%.

What is not yet known

BOI said detailed subscription figures and final allotments would come after regulatory approval. The exact amounts bought by NSIA, IFC or pension funds have not been published.

BOI has also not published a detailed plan showing which firms or sectors will receive the money. Only broad priority areas are public so far.

Minister of State for Industry John Owan said BOI’s development finance could reach 1 trillion naira (US$752 million) this year. No timetable or further bond series has been confirmed.

What comes next for the BOI development bond

Investors will now watch how quickly BOI lends the money and how those loans perform. Secondary-market trading of the bond will also give a signal on pricing.

Muda Yusuf said the deal could encourage other development finance institutions to borrow at home. A steady, well-run rollout of lending would help make the BOI development bond that model.

Frequently Asked Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the BOI development bond?

It is a five-year, 17.60% fixed-rate bond due 2031. BOI raised about 274.19 billion naira (US$206 million) with it.

Who can invest in the bond?

This series was sold to institutional investors such as pension funds, banks and insurers. Individuals mainly gain exposure indirectly, for example through their pension fund.

Why did BOI issue this bond?

BOI wants long-term naira funding to lend to businesses in priority sectors. It also adds local money to its existing international funding.

Sources: Bank of Industry statement, 3 September 2026; FCMB Capital Markets; RMB Nigeria; African Law & Business; MarketForces Africa; BusinessDay; Daily Trust.

World.title: York Timbers Restructuring Hands Sabie Lodge and Farms to Shareholders
World.content:
SOUTH AFRICA · BUSINESS

Key Facts — What happened York’s board approved unbundling Stadsrivier Vallei and Mbulwa Estate to shareholders, in a 17 September 2026 announcement.

— What is being split off Stadsrivier is a farm business, and Mbulwa is a 38-hectare lodge estate near Sabie.

— Cash picture Cash from continuing operations should rise 25% to 30% for the year to 30 June 2026.

— The catch Earnings per share from continuing operations should fall by 54% to 59%.

— Not a sale The assets go to existing shareholders, not to an outside buyer, and no price was given.

— What comes next Full-year results are due on or about 30 September 2026.

The Sabie-based timber group will give shareholders its Mbulwa lodge estate and Stadsrivier farm business. Cash from its core operations is rising, but earnings per share are falling.

Pine plantations and fields near Sabie, Mpumalanga, where York Timbers is based (Photo: M J Hurter, CC0 via Wikimedia Commons)

On Thursday, 17 September 2026, York Timber Holdings said it will separate a Sabie lodge and a farm business. The York Timbers restructuring hands both to shareholders rather than selling them to a buyer.

What York announced

York Timber Holdings, listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), published a trading statement on the exchange’s news service. It was issued from Sabie, Mpumalanga, on 17 September 2026.

The board said it will pursue several options to restructure the group. As part of that, it approved the unbundling of Stadsrivier Vallei and Mbulwa Estate to shareholders.

An unbundling means the company passes a business directly to its own shareholders. The board said the plan still depends on a final structure and on legal, regulatory and corporate approvals.

What the two businesses are

Stadsrivier Vallei is York’s agricultural arm. The group’s website says it runs an avocado packhouse, built in 2004, in Mpumalanga.

Mbulwa Estate is a 38-hectare lodge on the Mount Anderson Pass above the Sabie Valley. Its website says York Timbers owns it.

The estate was once the home of American mining magnate Charles Engelhard Jr, according to the lodge. Guests now come for its views, forest setting and closeness to Kruger National Park.

Why the York Timbers restructuring shows up as ‘held for sale’

Under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), assets a company plans to give away or sell are grouped separately. York has therefore labelled both businesses ‘assets held for sale’ in its 30 June 2026 accounts.

That label is an accounting rule, not a sale agreement. York has not named any buyer, price or sale of either business.

What stays with the timber group

Engineering News describes York as a solid wood processor. Its website says the group manages about 89,700 hectares of land in Mpumalanga, including Stadsrivier Vallei.

Of that land, about 59,600 hectares are pine and eucalyptus plantations. York also runs a plywood plant in Sabie with a yearly capacity of 130,000 cubic metres.

After the York Timbers restructuring, the group would be more tightly focused on trees and wood products. That is a reading of the plan, not a company statement.

Cash rises while earnings fall

At 18 September 2026 rates, cash from continuing operations should be R182.3 million to R189.6 million (US$11.2 million to US$11.7 million). A year earlier it was R145.9 million (US$9.0 million).

Cash from all operations, including the two departing businesses, should be R166.9 million to R174.2 million (US$10.3 million to US$10.7 million). The comparable figure was R147.6 million (US$9.1 million).

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and tree-value changes should be R158.7 million to R166.7 million (US$9.8 million to US$10.3 million). York compares that with R160 million (US$9.8 million) a year earlier.

Profit per share tells a weaker story. Earnings per share (EPS) from continuing operations should be 27.40 to 30.73 cents (US$0.017 to US$0.019), down from 66.63 cents (US$0.041).

Headline earnings per share (HEPS), which removes some one-off items, should be 29.37 to 32.65 cents (US$0.018 to US$0.020). That compares with 65.50 cents (US$0.040) last year.

The two businesses being separated lost money in the year. They are expected to post a loss of about 9 cents (US$0.006) per share, against a small profit a year earlier.

The core loss behind the numbers

York also reports ‘core’ earnings, which strip out changes in the value of its growing trees. On that basis, continuing operations should show a loss of 4.90 to 4.95 cents (US$0.003) per share.

The year before, the core loss was 0.86 cents (US$0.0005) per share. York said the figures have not been reviewed by its auditors.

Why this matters for expats and investors

York shareholders, including those holding through South African funds, may later receive a stake in the two businesses. How that works depends on the final structure.

Investors living abroad should check with a tax adviser once the details are out. Unbundlings can have different tax effects in different countries.

For people who visit or live near Sabie, Mbulwa’s ownership may change. York has said nothing about how the lodge will be run after the split.

What is not yet known

York has not said how the unbundling will be structured or when it will happen. It has not given a value for either business.

It has not said whether the separated businesses will be listed on the JSE. It has also not said what other restructuring options the board is considering.

York has not said whether jobs at the lodge or the farm business will be affected by the change of ownership.

What to watch next

The full-year results, due on or about Wednesday, 30 September 2026, should replace these ranges with final numbers. A detailed shareholder document on the unbundling would follow if the plan goes ahead.

York said it will update shareholders as the process moves forward.

Frequently Asked Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

Is York Timbers selling the Sabie lodge?

Not to an outside buyer. The board approved unbundling Mbulwa Estate and Stadsrivier Vallei to York’s own shareholders, subject to approvals.

Why are the assets called ‘held for sale’?

It is an accounting label under IFRS 5. It applies to assets a company plans to separate, including by unbundling.

When will York publish final results?

York expects to release results for the year to 30 June 2026 on or about 30 September 2026.

Sources: York Timber Holdings trading statement on JSE SENS, 17 September 2026; Engineering News; News24; York Timbers and Mbulwa Estate websites.

World.title: King Long Hanlink Tanzania Deal Puts Bus Aftercare in Focus
World.content:
TANZANIA · BUSINESS

Key Facts — What happened King Long and Hanlink agreed a partnership to supply buses in Tanzania, The Citizen reported.

— Where The partnership was presented at an event in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania’s largest city.

— Hanlink’s role Its finance chief said Hanlink will handle sales, after-sales service, technical support and genuine spare parts.

— Operators’ demand The bus owners’ association asked for a strong spare-parts and service network to limit costly downtime.

— The catch No prices, order numbers, contract value or delivery dates have been made public.

— What comes next Watch for first confirmed orders from Tanzanian bus operators and for financing packages with lenders.

A Chinese bus maker gains a local partner — and operators say spare parts and service matter as much as price.

The Magufuli Bus Terminal at Mbezi Luis, Dar es Salaam’s hub for long-distance coaches (Photo: Josephgodfrey, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

Chinese bus maker King Long has teamed up with Hanlink Company Limited, The Citizen reported on 18 September 2026. The King Long Hanlink Tanzania deal aims to supply buses to the country’s passenger transport sector.

What the King Long Hanlink Tanzania deal covers

King Long, based in Xiamen, China, has partnered with Hanlink Company Limited to supply buses in Tanzania. The Citizen says the aim is durable, affordable and efficient buses.

The deal pairs King Long’s manufacturing experience with Hanlink’s knowledge of the local market. It targets buses built for long-distance travel and heavy daily use.

The partnership was presented at an event in Dar es Salaam this week. Michuzi Blog, a Tanzanian news site, reported on King Long’s Tanzania launch on 17 September 2026.

No contract value, bus prices or order numbers have been made public. So far, the details come from speeches at the event.

Who King Long and Hanlink are

King Long was founded in 1988 in Xiamen, in China’s Fujian province. The company says it has exported vehicles to more than 150 countries and regions.

Its website describes it as part of Xiamen King Long Motor Group. The Citizen reports that the maker has been present in Africa for more than two decades.

Hanlink sells Chinese trucks and machinery in East Africa. Its Tanzania website lists Sinotruk trucks, XCMG construction machinery, Heli forklifts and Great Wall vehicles.

Hanlink Mobility Tanzania opened in Dar es Salaam on 26 June 2026, according to a Citizen business supplement. It was presented as an authorised Sinotruk distributor, with King Long buses in its range.

Hanlink’s chief financial officer, Manuel Ma, said the firm operates in Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda. He said this gives King Long a regional platform.

What bus operators are asking for

Operators set a clear test for the partnership. Abdallah Kiongozi, chairman of the Tanzania Association of Bus Owners (Taboa), put after-sales service first.

“Operators need reliable access to spare parts and technical support,” he said. He warned that a bus stuck in a workshop waiting for one part costs operators and passengers alike.

Mr Kiongozi also named fuel efficiency and financing as key concerns. He urged the companies to work with financial institutions on affordable financing packages.

Salim Mohamed, managing director of bus operator Ratco, called the partnership timely. “Durability is very important because these vehicles are used intensively, on long-distance routes,” he said.

He added that operators should weigh maintenance and after-sales support alongside the purchase price. Operators, he said, want reliability, comfort and manageable running costs.

What the two companies promise

The Citizen quoted King Long chief executive Ding Ming Bin as calling Tanzania an important market in the company’s East Africa strategy. He described the deal as more than a product launch.

“The partnership would support the long-term development of transportation in Tanzania and East Africa,” he said, according to the newspaper.

Mr Ma said Hanlink would strengthen sales, after-sales services and technical support. He also promised better access to genuine spare parts.

At its June launch, Hanlink named CRDB Bank, NBC Bank, NMB Bank and NCBA Bank as financing partners. It is not yet clear whether these arrangements will cover King Long buses.

A busy field of Chinese buses

King Long enters a market where other Chinese makers are already active. In July 2025, Golden Dragon, another Xiamen bus maker, handed over 200 buses for Dar es Salaam’s bus rapid transit (BRT) network.

Those buses serve the network’s second phase, run by the local operator Mofat. The Citizen reported that 151 of them had arrived by late August 2025.

As reported, the King Long Hanlink Tanzania partnership focuses on long-distance travel and intensive daily use. That points to private intercity operators rather than the city’s BRT fleet.

The brand is also not new to Tanzanian roads. One local operator told Michuzi Blog it has used King Long buses since 2018 — what is new is the local partner.

What it means for expats and investors

For expats who travel between Tanzanian cities by coach, the practical effect depends on service quality. Better spare-parts supply could mean fewer breakdowns and cancelled trips.

For investors, the deal shows Chinese dealers bundling trucks, machinery and buses under one local roof. Firms in logistics, construction or mining may need fewer separate suppliers.

Local banks could also gain business if bus financing packages follow, as Taboa requested. None has been announced for King Long buses so far.

What is not known

Several key details are missing. No prices, order volumes or delivery dates for King Long buses have been published.

It is also unclear how large Hanlink’s service network in Tanzania will be. Descriptions of its regional footprint differ, from three countries to six.

The first confirmed orders from Tanzanian operators should show, in the coming months, how far the partnership delivers on its promises.

Frequently Asked Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the King Long Hanlink Tanzania deal?

It is a partnership under which Hanlink will sell and service King Long buses in Tanzania. The Citizen reported it on 18 September 2026.

Is King Long supplying Dar es Salaam’s BRT buses?

No confirmed report says so. The 200 BRT buses handed over in July 2025 came from Golden Dragon, another Chinese maker.

What do bus owners want from the deal?

Taboa asked for reliable spare parts, technical support, fuel-efficient buses and affordable financing through local lenders.

Sources: The Citizen, 18 September 2026 and 29 August 2025; Michuzi Blog; King Long company website; Hanlink Tanzania website; Bus-News.

World.title: Accra Tests Aayalolo Contra-Flow Lanes to Speed Up City Buses
World.content:
GHANA · INFRASTRUCTURE

Key Facts — What happened GAPTE has started studying whether Aayalolo buses can run against traffic in a spare lane.

— Where first The assessment began on the Kinbu-Adenta corridor, a busy route into central Accra.

— Trial result GAPTE’s managing director says a trial cut travel time from nearly two hours to about 45 minutes.

— The fleet The plan would support the deployment of 126 repaired Aayalolo buses.

— The catch No completion date, cost or start date for any lanes has been announced.

— What comes next The findings will go to the Transport Minister for consideration.

Accra’s public bus operator wants its buses to use an empty lane on the other side of the road. A study now tests whether that is safe and workable.

Traffic on a main road in Accra, Ghana’s capital (Photo: Elegant Machines, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

Accra’s public bus authority has begun a feasibility study into an Aayalolo contra-flow system on busy city routes. The work started on the Kinbu-Adenta corridor, Citi News reported on 17 September 2026.

What the Aayalolo contra-flow study will test

The Greater Accra Passenger Transport Executive (GAPTE) runs Aayalolo, the state-backed bus service in Ghana’s capital. It is carrying out the study with the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) of the Ghana Police Service and other partners.

GAPTE Managing Director Daouda Awudu explained the idea to Citi News on Thursday, 17 September 2026. “When you say contra-flow, we are talking about a traffic management system that would ease congestion in a particular area,” he said.

In practice, the plan is simple. Where one side of a road has spare space, Aayalolo buses could use a lane there against the normal flow.

Awudu said the study will look at the possible risks of the system. It will also recommend ways to reduce those risks.

A promising trial on the Kinbu-Adenta route

According to Awudu, a trial on the Kinbu-Adenta route cut travel time from nearly two hours to about 45 minutes. The state broadcaster GBC carried the same figure on 18 September 2026.

The trial figure comes from GAPTE itself. No independent data on the trial, such as its length or the number of trips, has been published.

Awudu said the contra-flow system, together with dedicated bus lanes, would support the deployment of 126 repaired Aayalolo buses. The goal is to stop those buses from being caught in the same traffic as everyone else.

GBC reported that the results will be sent for evaluation and possible use if they are found to be workable. No timeline for that decision has been given.

Not a motorbike escort plan

Awudu also rejected reports that the buses would be escorted by police motorbikes. He said such an arrangement is not a contra-flow system.

That point matters because the idea has been in the news for weeks. On 8 September 2026, Local Government Minister Mahama Ayariga proposed a peak-hour lane for Aayalolo buses, according to MyJoyOnline.

Ayariga suggested reserving one lane on the less busy side of some roads for the buses from 6 am to 9 am. He also proposed that MTTD motorbike officers lead the buses to warn oncoming drivers.

Ayariga said the earlier approach of permanent dedicated lanes had not worked well. A senior MTTD officer, Assistant Commissioner of Police Alexander Kwaku Obeng, publicly backed the proposal, Rainbow Radio reported on 9 September 2026.

A bus service trying to recover

Aayalolo was launched in 2016 as a bus rapid transit service, with 245 buses bought for the system. By January 2026, only 80 of those buses were running in Accra, GAPTE told GhanaWeb.

Awudu said then that 60 buses had gone to Kumasi and 10 each to Takoradi and Tamale, on earlier ministry orders. GAPTE said it was working to bring buses back and repair others.

In April 2026, then Local Government Minister Ahmed Ibrahim asked a new GAPTE council to revive Aayalolo for 24-hour service. Easing congestion around Kinbu was among his priorities, the Daily Graphic reported.

Aayalolo managers have also said that buses stuck in traffic lose money. When dedicated lanes existed between Circle and Tesano, the buses saved riders up to 30 minutes, according to the Daily Graphic.

Why this matters to expats and investors in Ghana

Traffic in Accra is a daily cost for people who live and work there. A faster, more reliable bus would make longer commutes from suburbs such as Adenta more practical.

For employers, bus reliability affects staff punctuality and the cost of company transport. For property investors, better bus links can make outer districts easier to rent or sell.

The study is also a test of how well Ghana’s agencies work together. Road space, police enforcement and bus operations sit with different bodies, and a contra-flow lane needs all of them.

Visitors and expats who rely on ride-hailing or private cars would also feel the effect. Buses that move freely at peak hours could take some pressure off the wider road network.

What is not yet known about the Aayalolo contra-flow plan

GAPTE has not said when the study will finish or which corridors will be assessed after Kinbu-Adenta. It has not published the cost of the study or of any lane changes.

It is not yet clear whether police escorts will play any part in the final design. Awudu’s comments suggest GAPTE favours lane changes over escorts, but the final choice rests with the government.

Figures for the working Aayalolo fleet have also varied between reports this year. The study reports themselves refer only to 126 repaired buses.

The findings will go to the Transport Minister, currently Joseph Bukari Nikpe. How quickly his ministry acts on them will decide whether commuters see any change soon.

Frequently Asked Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Aayalolo contra-flow system?

It is a proposal to let Aayalolo buses use a spare lane on the opposite side of a busy road, moving against normal traffic.

How much time did the Kinbu-Adenta trial save?

GAPTE’s managing director says travel time fell from nearly two hours to about 45 minutes. No independent data on the trial has been published.

Who decides whether the plan goes ahead?

GAPTE will send its findings to the Transport Minister for consideration. The study is being done with the police traffic department, the MTTD.

Sources: Greater Accra Passenger Transport Executive statements via Citi News, 17 September 2026, and GBC, 18 September 2026; MyJoyOnline; Rainbow Radio; GhanaWeb; Daily Graphic; Ghanaian Times.

World.title: Libya Power Cuts Last Up to 36 Hours in Parts of Tripoli
World.content:
LIBYA · BUSINESS

Key Facts — What happened A Tripoli restaurateur told Reuters that outages in his southern district can last up to 36 hours.

— The cost He said generators cost him about 10,000 dinars (US$1,575) a day and losses reached about US$40,000.

— Fuel prices Black-market diesel has reached as much as 11 dinars (US$1.73) a litre, against a subsidised 0.15 dinars (US$0.02).

— The utility GECOL declared a blackout that also cut water from the Great Man-Made River, Reuters reported.

— The catch GECOL’s new chairman promised in late August to end the cuts within 10 to 15 days.

— Still unknown GECOL has published no current national outage figure, and it did not answer Reuters’ interview request.

A new chairman at the state power company promised in August to end the cuts within about two weeks. In September, businesses still run on generators and black-market diesel.

Libya power cuts in Tripoli’s Qasr Bin Ghashir district can last up to 36 hours, a restaurateur told Reuters on 17 September. Naseem Al-Akkari said he spends about 10,000 Libyan dinars (US$1,575) a day on generators.

A 36-hour outage in one Tripoli district

Naseem Al-Akkari owns a chain of restaurants in Tripoli, the Libyan capital. He told Reuters that this summer’s heatwaves caused him an estimated US$40,000 in losses in a few months.

“The generator has to run to prevent goods from spoiling,” he said. The power went out more than ten times during his interview with Reuters.

In Qasr Bin Ghashir, a southern district of Tripoli, outages can last up to 36 hours, Akkari said. That is one owner’s account of one district, not an official figure.

In Benghazi, in the east, pastry shop manager Sufian Boushaala told Reuters the cuts forced his family business to lay off staff. Some days it closed completely.

Why Libya power cuts are so costly for businesses

Akkari said the long outages mean spending about 10,000 dinars (US$1,575) a day on generators. All figures here use 18 September 2026 rates of 6.35 dinars to the US dollar.

Subsidised diesel costs 0.15 dinars (about US$0.02) a litre. Reuters reported that the black-market price has surged as high as 11 dinars (US$1.73) a litre.

That is about 73 times the official price. Petrol queues in both eastern and western Libya can now stretch up to two kilometres, Reuters reported.

The state fuel distributor, Brega Petroleum Marketing, has set up a mobile refuelling station with a limit of 300 litres per vehicle. Even so, queues can still last hours.

What GECOL has said

The state-owned General Electricity Company of Libya (GECOL) runs the national grid. Reuters said water from the Great Man-Made River Project was cut off after GECOL declared a blackout.

GECOL did not respond to a Reuters request for an interview. Its most recent public statements came in August and early September.

On 18 August 2026, GECOL’s general assembly named Bashir Al-Marash as chairman, replacing Mohamed Al-Mashai, the Libya Herald reported. On 26 August, Al-Marash said the cuts should end for all of Libya within 10 to 15 days.

Those 15 days ended around 10 September, yet a week later Reuters still found long outages in Tripoli. GECOL also reported a partial blackout in western Libya on 31 August, after two major transmission lines tripped.

On 4 September, GECOL said it had reconnected a 150-megawatt unit at the Zawia power plant, west of Tripoli. It had earlier announced the start of the first unit at the new South Tripoli station.

Heat, old equipment and smuggled fuel

Reuters linked the crisis to this summer’s heatwaves, global energy disruptions, ageing infrastructure and widespread fuel smuggling. Jalel Harchaoui of Britain’s Royal United Services Institute also pointed to shortfalls in natural gas production.

US watchdog The Sentry estimated that fuel smuggling costs Libyans about US$6.7 billion a year. Brega said nine fuel tanks in Tripoli destroyed in 2014 are still not repaired.

The UN envoy for Libya, Hanna Tetteh, called the outages a “striking paradox” in an August briefing. Libya spends about US$1 billion a month on fuel imports, Reuters reported.

On 1 July 2026, the state news agency LANA reported that demand had passed 7,000 megawatts. It said some areas faced cuts of more than eight hours a day.

What is not known

There is no current, official national figure for how long outages last. The 36-hour figure comes from one business owner; LANA’s eight-hour figure dates from July.

Protesters blocked roads and burned tyres in Tripoli in late July, Al Jazeera reported. It is not confirmed whether new protests have followed in September.

What this means for expats and investors

For anyone running a shop, restaurant or workshop in Libya, backup power is now a major running cost. Owners should budget for a generator, fuel storage and closed days.

Investors should note that Libya holds North Africa’s largest proven oil reserves yet still imports costly refined fuel. The split between rival governments in the east and west adds operational risk.

Expats in Tripoli or Benghazi should plan for long outages and hours-long fuel queues. The same lesson applies elsewhere in Africa and Latin America: check the grid, not just the resources.

What to watch next

The key signs are new generating units reaching the grid, fuel supply to power stations and any GECOL update on outage schedules. Cooler autumn weather should also ease demand, though no forecast has been published.

Frequently Asked Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

How long do Libya power cuts last?

It varies by area. A Tripoli restaurateur told Reuters in September that cuts in his district can last up to 36 hours. In July, state media reported cuts of more than eight hours a day in some areas.

What has GECOL promised?

Its new chairman, Bashir Al-Marash, said on 26 August 2026 that the cuts should end within 10 to 15 days. That period has passed, and outages continue.

Why is fuel so expensive for Libyan businesses?

Subsidised diesel is scarce because of smuggling and supply problems. Black-market diesel has reached as much as 11 dinars (US$1.73) a litre, Reuters reported.

Sources: Reuters, 17 September 2026; General Electricity Company of Libya statements via Libya Herald, August–September 2026; Libyan News Agency (LANA), 1 July 2026; Al Jazeera.

World.title: Ghana Horticultural Seed Roadmap Aims to Lift Vegetable Farming
World.content:
GHANA · AGRICULTURE

Key Facts — What happened The Ministry of Food and Agriculture launched the National Horticultural Seed Roadmap in Accra on 17 September 2026.

— Time frame The roadmap sets strategic priorities for the next three to five years.

— Main goal More farmers should get quality seeds and seedlings suited to Ghana’s soils and climate.

— Who spoke Deputy Minister John Setor Dumelo and Inge Tenniglo of the Netherlands Embassy addressed the launch.

— Related push Two days earlier, Ghana launched a tomato plan aiming for 400,000 tonnes a year.

— The catch No budget, funding source or measurable seed targets have been made public.

The Ministry of Food and Agriculture wants vegetable farmers to get better seeds and seedlings, but it has not yet published a budget.

A vegetable farm in northern Ghana (Photo: Ibn Shiraz, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)
