Ghana’s Ministry of Food and Agriculture launched the Ghana horticultural seed roadmap in Accra on Thursday, 17 September 2026. Its formal name is the National Horticultural Seed Roadmap, and it sets vegetable seed priorities for three to five years.

What the roadmap says it will do

The ministry says the roadmap aims to increase the availability and use of improved planting materials. These are seeds and young plants suited to Ghana’s farming conditions.

Work will focus on strengthening local seed production and the companies that produce seed. It also aims to widen farmers’ access to quality seeds and seedlings.

A third goal is to support new crop varieties adapted to Ghanaian conditions. The roadmap also sets out responsibilities, timelines and financing arrangements for putting the plan into practice.

The launch brought together government agencies, seed companies, research institutions, farmer groups and development partners.

Who spoke at the launch

Deputy Minister for Food and Agriculture John Setor Dumelo spoke for the ministry. He called the roadmap “an important step towards building a stronger and more responsive seed system.”

He said the new system should respond to farmers’ needs and help the horticulture sector grow.

Inge Tenniglo, representing the Netherlands Embassy, said the Netherlands would keep supporting Ghana’s horticulture sector. She described the roadmap as “laying the foundation for the future of Ghana’s horticulture sector.”

How it fits with other recent moves

The roadmap follows several related steps this year, most of them aimed at seed quality.

In June 2026, the ministry inaugurated a National Seed Council under the Plants and Fertilizer Act, 2010 (Act 803). Alhaji Abubakari Mumuni chairs the council.

The council advises the minister on seed policy and oversees rules for seed production, certification and distribution. At its inauguration, Dumelo said the government was trying to reduce seed imports.

He also said spending on fertiliser, irrigation and machinery works best when backed by a reliable seed system. That argument sits at the centre of the new roadmap.

On 3 September 2026, the ministry, the Netherlands Embassy and private partners launched a three-year Business Seed Partnership. It aims to improve farmers’ access to quality vegetable seed and support local seed businesses.

The World Bank’s Food System Resilience Programme is also listed among that partnership’s backers. The partnership was launched at the University of Ghana in Legon.

It builds on the Ghana Seed Partnership, a Dutch-backed group of 13 organisations launched in Accra in October 2025. Members include seed firms East-West Seed, Rijk Zwaan, Enza Zaden and Bakker Brothers, plus Wageningen University and Research.

The tomato link

On 15 September 2026, Food and Agriculture Minister Eric Opoku launched the Ghana Tomato Self-Sufficiency Initiative in Anloga, Volta Region. It is run with a private company, FarmMate Limited.

The first phase targets about 100,000 tonnes of tomatoes in the 2026/2027 season. The first phase covers more than 10,000 acres, and the longer goal is about 400,000 tonnes a year.

Organisers say Ghana spends about US$400 million a year on imported fresh tomatoes and tomato paste. Imports rise most during the dry months from December to July.

Farmers in the scheme receive a production package worth about GH₵20,000 (US$1,748) per acre, at 18 September 2026 rates. Good seed matters here because yields depend heavily on the variety planted.

That makes the seed roadmap and the tomato plan closely linked. Both depend on farmers getting the right seed at the right time.

Why the Ghana horticultural seed roadmap matters to expats and investors

For people living in Ghana, vegetable prices often jump in the dry season when supply falls. More reliable local seed could, over time, help farms produce more steadily through the year.

For investors, the government and its partners point to seed production, commercial nurseries and tomato processing as areas to develop. Dutch seed firms and development partners are already active in the sector.

Returns will depend on funding, clear seed rules and farmers’ ability to pay for better seed. Those conditions are still being set.

The tomato plan also includes processing. Officials say up to 200,000 tonnes a year could eventually be turned into tomato purée and other products.

What is not yet known

The ministry has not published a budget for the roadmap or named who will pay for it. It has not released target volumes, crop lists or the full roadmap text.

It is also not clear which agency will lead day-to-day work or how progress will be measured. Earlier seed plans in Ghana have not always been fully carried out.

What to watch next

The first signs will be funding announcements, the full roadmap text and progress on seed testing and certification. Watch also for whether tomato farmers in the new scheme can get enough quality seed on time.

If money and clear targets follow, the roadmap could help Ghana grow more of its own vegetables in the years ahead.

Frequently Asked Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Ghana’s National Horticultural Seed Roadmap?

It is a three- to five-year plan launched on 17 September 2026. It aims to give vegetable farmers better access to quality seeds and seedlings.

Who is supporting it?

The Ministry of Food and Agriculture leads it. The Netherlands Embassy has said it will keep supporting Ghana’s horticulture sector.

Has funding been confirmed?

No. The roadmap includes financing arrangements, but no budget figure has been made public.

Sources: Ghana Ministry of Food and Agriculture launch, 17 September 2026, as reported by MyJoyOnline and Ecofin Agency; Graphic Online; Ghana Netherlands Business and Culture Council; The High Street Journal.

World.title: Man’s drivers license disqualified for 1 year; fined $700 for reckless driving and failing to provide urine sample – Says he didn’t have to pee at the time
World.content:
Man’s drivers license disqualified for 1 year; fined $700 for reckless driving and failing to provide urine sample – Says he didn’t have to pee at the time

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 45-year-old IT manager has been fined a total of $700, plus court costs, and disqualified from driving for one year after pleading guilty to reckless driving and failure to provide a specimen.

Lee Liu, a resident of Sandhill, appeared before Senior Magistrate Mannon Dennison in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Friday, where he pleaded guilty to both traffic offences.

The charges stemmed from an incident around 5:10 a.m. on Thursday, September 17, when police officers conducting a checkpoint on the Philip Goldson Highway reportedly noticed a white car swerving across the highway.

A police constable signalled the driver to stop and, according to the prosecution’s facts, observed that Liu appeared intoxicated, had difficulty standing and was speaking with slurred speech. Police said Liu admitted that he had been drinking, telling the officer, “Yes, but I just want to go home.”

Liu was taken to a police station and initially agreed to provide a urine specimen for alcohol analysis. Police alleged that when the time came to provide the sample, however, Liu refused, saying he no longer wanted to give it.

In court, Liu explained that he had been driving around potholes on the highway, which he said accounted for the manner in which he was driving. Regarding the urine sample, he told the court that he did not feel the need to urinate at the time.

He was fined $500 plus $5 court costs for failure to provide a specimen, payable by November 30, 2026, or three months’ imprisonment in default. For reckless driving, Liu was fined $200 plus $5 court costs, payable by October 31, 2026, or two months’ imprisonment in default.

Liu was also disqualified from driving for one year, effective September 18, 2026. Belize’s Motor Vehicles and Road Traffic Act provides that a person who, without reasonable excuse, fails to provide a required blood or urine specimen commits an offence and, upon conviction, is subject to a 12-month disqualification from holding or obtaining a Belize driving licence.

When ordered to surrender his driver’s licence, Liu told the court that he did not have it with him and believed he had misplaced it at home. Senior Magistrate Dennison ordered him to surrender the licence at the Sandhill Police Station by 5:00 p.m. Friday.

He may apply in writing after 90 days seeking to have his driving privileges reinstated.

World.title: Bulridge Belize hiring full time Sales Representative in Georgeville
World.content:
Bulridge Belize hiring full time Sales Representative in Georgeville

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Bulridge Belize is looking to add a full time Sales Representative to its team in Georgeville Village, Cayo District.

The company is seeking a candidate who is computer literate and has knowledge of Microsoft Office and QuickBooks.

Applicants should also have strong communication and customer service skills, pay close attention to detail, work well as part of a team and demonstrate honesty in the workplace.

The position is full time and based in Georgeville.

Interested applicants are asked to submit their resume to [email protected].

The deadline to apply is September 28.

World.title: Belize showcases new airlift, resorts and Eco-Tourism in New York
World.content:
Belize showcases new airlift, resorts and Eco-Tourism in New York

By Zoila Palma: Minister of Tourism, Youth, Sports and Diaspora Relations Anthony Mahler participated in a series of media and tourism events hosted by the Belize Tourism Board in New York on Thursday, September 17, 2026.

The events highlighted Belize’s expanded airlift options, new accommodation offerings and its growing reputation for eco-sustainable tourism.

The day began with a broadcast video interview between Minister Mahler and James Shillinglaw, Editor-in-Chief of Insider Travel Report, followed by a media breakfast attended by more than 20 prominent writers and editors from publications including Fodor’s Travel, Travel + Leisure, AFAR, Forbes, National Geographic, Condé Nast Traveler and Parade Magazine.

The event also provided Belizean hoteliers and tour operators with an opportunity to network with international travel media.

Minister Mahler later participated in a desk-side briefing with Amy Virshup, Executive Travel Editor at The New York Times, who expressed interest in Belize’s tourism developments, particularly expanded connectivity with BermudAir and plans for new marine sanctuaries.

Also attending the engagements was Eluide Miller, Deputy Mayor of Belize City and Administrator at NICH. During the afternoon, Minister Mahler and Michelle Bowers-Flowers, Director of Marketing and Communications, met with executives and digital marketing teams from Development Counsellors International, FINN Partners and TM Americas, who presented upcoming campaigns aimed at promoting travel to Belize during the upcoming Blue Season.

The day concluded with Minister Mahler’s participation in the United States Tour Operators Association (USTOA) New York City Mixer.

USTOA CEO Terry Dale welcomed associate members, including destination marketing organizations and airlines, as well as tour operators from the New York area.

World.title: Government of Belize advances Digital skills through Marketing and CRM Training in Corozal
World.content:
Government of Belize advances Digital skills through Marketing and CRM Training in Corozal

By Zoila Palma: The Government of Belize, through the Investment Policy and Compliance Unit (IPCU) of the Office of the Prime Minister, in collaboration with the Corozal Think Tank, has advanced efforts to strengthen digital skills among young Belizeans through a Digital Marketing and CRM Training programme.

Today, a graduation ceremony was held in Corozal following the completion of the programme earlier this year.

The initiative targeted young and early-career participants ages 15 and up, along with a small group of adult learners, providing them with digital competencies aligned with international certification standards.

Participants received training in industry-standard platforms including Canva, Shopify, Zoho CRM, Zapier, AdRoll and Taboola, while covering digital marketing strategy, content creation, social media marketing, e-commerce, customer relationship management, marketing automation, analytics and search engine optimization.

A total of 41 students from the Corozal District successfully completed the course, with most coming from Chunox St. Viator Vocational High School. Participants reported gaining practical skills in digital marketing, content production, social media management, e-commerce platforms, CRM systems and analytics.

The programme also incorporated soft skills such as communication, teamwork, time management, professional presentations and self-confidence, with participants reporting greater preparedness to engage with potential employers.

The graduation ceremony was attended by Minister of Human Development, Family Support and Gender Affairs Thea Garcia Ramirez, IPCU Director Lincoln Blake, Corozal ITVET Chairman Froylan Gilharry, Chunox St. Viator Vocational High School Principal Marconie Moh and Corozal Think Tank member Juan Carlos Menzies.

Christian Junior, head trainer from UK-based Rhics Ltd., which provided the training, participated virtually.

The programme forms part of efforts to equip Belizeans with skills relevant to the country’s growing digital services sector, including business process outsourcing, micro-businesses and public-sector digital transformation.

World.title: Belize makes historic debut at 2026 Americas Food & Beverage Show
World.content:
Belize makes historic debut at 2026 Americas Food & Beverage Show

By Zoila Palma: Belize has concluded its historic debut at the 2026 Americas Food & Beverage Show, marking the country’s first-ever participation with a dedicated Country Pavilion at the Miami Beach Convention Center.

Over three days, Belizean exporters engaged in business-to-business matchmaking, product showcases and networking with buyers, distributors and industry representatives from the Caribbean, United States, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

The participation generated interest in Belizean products and opened opportunities for exporters to access new international markets.

Belize also took the spotlight on the show’s official Beverage Stage, with Cuello’s Distilleries Limited showcasing its Belizean spirits through a live presentation and sampling session, followed by Caribbean International Brewery Company Limited, which highlighted its products and Belize’s growing beverage industry.

The seven exporters representing Belize were Cuello’s Distilleries Limited, Aqua Mar Belize Ltd, National Fishermen Producers Co-operative Society Ltd. (Natfish), Coco Fruta Ltd., ESADE Limited, Silk Grass Farms and Caribbean International Brewery Limited.

The Belize Country Pavilion was supported by BELTRAIDE representatives Monique Usher, Deputy Executive Director, and Zain Hernandez, Export Business Advisor.

BELTRAIDE said the event provided a valuable platform for Belizean businesses to build international connections and showcase the quality and diversity of locally produced goods.

World.title: PM Briceño: ‘Within five years, you’re going to see a major difference in this country; Five-year MCC clock starts
World.content:
PM Briceño: ‘Within five years, you’re going to see a major difference in this country; Five-year MCC clock starts

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Belize has officially moved from planning to implementation of its US$125 million Millennium Challenge Corporation Compact, beginning a five-year clock to complete major reforms and investments in education and energy.

Prime Minister John Briceño said Friday that work in both sectors will have to proceed simultaneously because Belize has only five years to deliver the projects.

“We only have five years, so we have to be simultaneously doing several things,” Briceño said.

On the education side, one of the immediate priorities will be the continued transformation of Belize’s Technical and Vocational Education and Training system, including establishment and operationalization of a National Training Agency.

The original compact requires the National Training Agency to operate as an autonomous institution responsible for planning and oversight of the TVET system, while sector skills councils are to connect training more closely to the needs of employers and the labour market.

The wider Education Project also includes teacher and school-leader training, national student assessments, strengthened teacher licensing, increased access to free secondary education and work-based opportunities such as apprenticeships.

MCA-Belize Chief Executive Officer Dr. Marcia Mahler Bouloy said the first year will involve continued work with ministries, educational institutions and other stakeholders, along with procuring consultants and carrying forward work already started during the preparation phase.

“What happens immediately is a continuation of our collaboration with the different ministries, agencies, university sectors that we have been working with,” Bouloy explained.

She said establishing the national training body and moving ahead with consultancies in the energy sector are among the activities that must be completed early if the compact is to remain on schedule.

Accountability and transparency mechanisms, she added, will continue throughout the five-year implementation period.

The energy component will meanwhile focus heavily on the new high-voltage submarine cable linking Ambergris Caye to the mainland transmission system, along with modernization of Belize’s electricity regulatory framework.

The compact was first signed on September 4, 2024. Under the agreement, its formal term lasts five years from its Entry into Force.

MCC is providing US$125 million, while the Government of Belize has increased its own contribution to approximately US$54.94 million.

Asked what Belizeans should expect by the end of those five years, Briceño pointed to both the shortage of skilled workers and the country’s energy challenges, saying he expects the investments to produce noticeable changes.

“Within five years, I have every confidence that you’re going to see a major difference in the development of this country,” the Prime Minister said.

World.title: Judge explains Juan Carlos Novelo acquittal in Leslie Verde murder: Key witness unreliable, circumstantial case fell short
World.content:
Judge explains Juan Carlos Novelo acquittal in Leslie Verde murder: Key witness unreliable, circumstantial case fell short

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Nearly two months after Juan Carlos Novelo was found not guilty of murdering his common-law wife, Leslie Margarita Verde, High Court Justice Candace Nanton has released a 29-page judgment explaining why the Crown’s circumstantial case failed to prove that Novelo was her killer.

Justice Nanton acquitted Novelo on July 20, 2026, following a judge-alone trial. At the time, she indicated that her detailed reasons would follow in writing. The decision sparked protests in Caye Caulker, where Verde’s relatives and supporters demanded an explanation for the verdict.

In her written ruling, Nanton made clear that there was no dispute that 32-year-old Verde had been unlawfully killed. Medical evidence from a doctor established that she died from asphyxia caused by neck compression and that the injuries were intentionally inflicted.

The crucial question, however, was whether the Crown had proven beyond reasonable doubt that Novelo was the person who inflicted those injuries.

The prosecution’s case relied heavily on Verde’s minor daughter, whose identity BBN is withholding. The child testified that she heard noises from her mother’s bedroom, peeped through an opening near the attic and saw Novelo beside her mother. She also claimed that she later saw him move her mother’s body behind the bedroom door.

But Justice Nanton found that the child’s evidence contained “material inconsistencies,” significant differences from earlier accounts and portions that were implausible when compared with the other evidence.

The judge noted that the inconsistencies went to the heart of the prosecution’s case rather than minor details. As a result, she said she could not safely rely on substantial portions of the child’s testimony — including the claims that she saw Novelo touching Verde and later moving her body.

That finding significantly weakened the Crown’s circumstantial case.

Surveillance evidence established that Verde returned home at approximately 4:29 a.m.; Novelo was at the residence and left around 5:28 a.m. He returned at approximately 8:16 a.m., went inside and shortly afterward left carrying beers. Verde was discovered dead closer to midday.

However, Dr. Blanco could not establish an exact time of death, meaning the remaining evidence did not prove that Verde necessarily died during a period when Novelo was the only person who could have killed her.

Justice Nanton said circumstantial evidence must form a coherent chain pointing to guilt as the only reasonable conclusion. Once critical portions of the minor’s testimony were rejected as unreliable, she found that the remaining evidence did not establish beyond reasonable doubt that Novelo caused Verde’s death.

Importantly, the judge stressed that the acquittal was not based on accepting Novelo’s version of events.

Novelo had given an unsworn statement maintaining that Verde was alive when he left their home and that during their eight-year relationship he had never harmed her. Justice Nanton said she did not need to rely on that account because the weakness was already present in the Crown’s case.

“The weakness identified is a failure of proof in the Crown’s case and does not arise from the Court accepting the Accused’s account,” the judgment stated.

Verde, a mother of three, was found unresponsive inside her Caye Caulker home on November 4, 2023. Police initially reported bruising around her neck and no signs of forced entry. Novelo was arrested and charged with murder days later.

Following his July acquittal, Verde’s family and other Caye Caulker residents staged a peaceful protest demanding answers, specifically calling for the written judgment explaining how the court arrived at the not-guilty verdict.

World.title: US$20M shifted from education to energy as MCC moves to fund new San Pedro submarine cable
World.content:
US$20M shifted from education to energy as MCC moves to fund new San Pedro submarine cable

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Twenty million U.S. dollars originally earmarked for education under Belize’s MCC Compact has been shifted to the energy sector, with Prime Minister John Briceño saying the Government will put up additional money to ensure that the education objectives are not sacrificed.

Officials explained the change Friday as the US$125 million Millennium Challenge Corporation Compact formally moved into its five-year implementation period.

When the compact was originally approved in 2024, US$73.8 million in MCC funds was budgeted for the Education Project and US$21.7 million for the Energy Project.

Following a U.S. Government foreign-assistance review, the compact was modified in July 2026 to move US$20 million from education into energy, primarily to accommodate major new electricity infrastructure, including a new 69-kilovolt submarine transmission cable to Ambergris Caye.

MCC’s current breakdown lists US$53.8 million for the Education Project and US$41.7 million for the Energy Project.

Briceño said Friday that the shift should not result in education programs being lost because the Government of Belize has stepped in to cover the funding gap.

“I don’t think there’s an impact because we are going to be filling the void or the shortage of the money,” the Prime Minister said.

Belize has now committed approximately US$54.94 million of its own money to the overall compact, up from the US$40.65 million contribution contemplated when the original agreement was signed.

MCC Acting Vice President Jason Small said Belize’s contribution is more than five times the minimum country contribution that MCC would ordinarily require, calling it a tangible demonstration of the Government’s commitment to completing the projects.

The urgency on the energy side centres heavily on Ambergris Caye.

Briceño told reporters that the existing submarine cable supplying San Pedro from the mainland had already reached the end of its expected lifespan in 2019.

“So there’s a sense of urgency to get that done,” Briceño said.

The Prime Minister said the project will involve more than the submarine cable itself, noting that new transmission infrastructure will also have to be developed from the Bomba area.

The modified compact officially provides for a new 69-kilovolt submarine transmission cable to Ambergris Caye, along with regulatory reforms aimed at modernizing the electricity sector and reducing wholesale electricity costs.

Briceño said the wider goal is to reduce Belize’s vulnerability to imported electricity and eventually place the country in a position where it can produce enough electricity domestically to meet its needs and potentially export power into the Central American market.

World.title: US appeals court puts brakes on TCN deportations
World.content:
An image shared by US White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt depicting people boarding a deportation flight in January 2025. (Photo: @PressSec / via X)

WASHINGTON, United States (AFP) — A United States (US) federal appeals court on Friday broadly upheld a lower court ruling restricting a Trump administration policy of deporting undocumented migrants to countries that are not their own.

The three-judge panel of the US Court of Appeals for the First Circuit said people facing “third-country” deportations must be given effective notice ahead of time about where they are being sent to allow them to raise concerns about potential persecution.

Congress has made it US policy not to deport people to countries where their lives would be in danger or they could be subject to torture.

READ: No start date as yet to TCN agreement — Johnson Smith

“An individual’s right to contest removal to a country based on a fear of persecution in that country means little if one does not receive prior notice of the intended removal destination and a meaningful opportunity to contest that destination,” said Judge Seth Aframe, writing for the unanimous three-judge panel.

Department of Homeland Security (DHS) policy “would deny access to that protection to a substantial swath of noncitizens who are sent to third countries with no notice of their destination,” the judge said.

The Trump administration is expected to appeal the case to the conservative-dominated Supreme Court.

Donald Trump campaigned for president promising to expel millions of undocumented migrants from the United States and has taken a number of actions aimed at speeding up deportations since returning to the White House.

The Trump administration has defended third-country deportations as necessary since the home nations of some of those who are targeted for removal sometimes refuse to accept them.

World.title: Father clueless if daughter was intimate with Pastor Kevin Smith
World.content:
This combo photo shows deceased pastor Kevin Smith and Taneka Gardener who was killed at Smith's church in a 2021 incident.

KINGSTON, Jamaica — The father of Taneka Gardner, the 39-year-old woman who had her throat slashed on October 17, 2021, at the Pathways International Restoration Ministries in Albion, St James, told a defence attorney on Thursday during cross-examination that he had no knowledge of his daughter being in a romantic relationship with the late pastor of the church, Dr Kevin Smith.

The murder trial of Andre Ruddock, the man accused of killing Gardner, got underway in the Home Circuit Court in Kingston on Thursday after a seven-member jury was empanelled on Wednesday.

Ruddock, under instructions from Smith, allegedly cut Gardner’s throat during what is widely believed to be a sacrificial killing.

Attorney-at-law Venice Brown, who along with Anthony Williams is representing Ruddock, appeared to have known something about a romantic relationship between Smith and Gardner, as the few questions she posed to the witness were mainly centred on that topic.

Brown asked the father if his daughter was involved romantically with Smith and he responded, “I don’t know about that one.

Brown right after suggested to the father that his daughter was in a romantic relationship with the pastor, however, trial Judge Leighton Pusey pointed out to her that the witness already indicated that he knew nothing about the alleged romance and prompted her to move on to the next question.

The next question to the father was if his daughter had any known medical conditions before she died.

“No, madam,” the father said to the attorney, who had no further questions.

During examination-in-chief, prosecutor LaToya Bernard asked the father a series of questions to establish for the seven jurors that he actually buried his daughter and that she was in fact dead.

The father shared that he received a call on October 18, the day after the incident, which prompted him to go to the church in Albion.

“I just went there because I heard what happened. I saw the police and the yellow tape. A lot of police and yellow tape, caution tape. I saw the tape blocking the entrance to the church. No madam, I didn’t go over to the church when I saw the caution tape,” he said.

He explained that he then proceeded to a location he referred to as Mango Walk, where his cousin resided. He explained that both of them went to the Freeport Police Station where he spoke to a detective inspector.

“I left for the Delapenha Funeral Home in Montego Bay, St James, to see the body because they said the body was there. They took out the body and showed it to me. It was Taneka Gardner, my daughter. I saw a slash on her throat. Workers from Delapenha were there with me. My cousin didn’t come inside.

“On November 19, 2021, I was called to come to St Catherine at Archer’s Funeral Home in Spanish Town. When I got there I was early so I waited until they opened. I went inside and a policeman spoke to me and took me to a room where the doctor was going to perform the autopsy. Taneka Gardner’s body was on a table and I was asked to identify her and I identified her as Taneka Gardner to the doctor as well as the police,” he said, explaining that he last spoke to his daughter about four days before she was killed.

After Gardner’s father left the witness stand, Corey James, the second witness, took up his position to give the jurors his chilling account of what occurred at the church on that fateful day in 2021.

“>He confirmed knowing Ruddock — the accused — very well as both of them had been attending the church together since 2014.

James, who is a livestock farmer, confirmed that Smith was the head of the church and that other members including himself and Ruddock were given various roles and functions.

He shared that while Ruddock was a security guard and Smith’s bodyguard, he on the other hand was given the role of getting Smith dressed and shaving his head.

“I helped Dr Smith get dressed before services,” he told the court.

James said that on the day of the incident, there was not supposed to be any service at the church because the day before, on Saturday, October 16, 2021, there was a “special ceremony”.

So, on the Sunday while he was cooking and resting, he had no intentions of going to church. However, his wife ran upstairs to him and told him something. He got out of bed and started to get ready to head down to the church. Asked by prosecutor Bernard why he, his wife and others got ready for church, James explained that Pastor Smith made a Facebook post where he informed his congregants of a flood and instructed them to come to him for safe haven.

“After she spoke with me we got ready, my wife, myself, our daughter and one of her friends, her friend’s mother and a nephew,” he said.

“Dr Smith made a post on Facebook. It was not his first time. He would post on his timeline on Facebook. Dr Smith made a post that a flood was coming. I am not sure what flood it was, but that was what he said, and we should come to the church for a safe haven. Yes, I did believe that a flood was coming, and I got ready and went to the church. When I reached the church it was between 1:00 pm and 3:00 pm. My family and friends travelled with me.

“When I got there, there were other individuals there. I was in yellow shorts, a blue hoodie, and I had a white sheet covering myself. Dr Smith said we should all cover ourselves with a white sheet. Everyone who travelled with me had a white sheet. When I got to the church, I saw others covered in white sheet. The covering up with the sheet was something new that started on the 16th, the day before at the special ceremony.

“I went on the boardwalk and was going inside the building. Dr Smith was at the top of the step at the main entrance of the building. Yes, I spoke with Dr Kevin Smith, and he spoke to me. I entered the building and sat down on the ground. He told us all to sit on the ground, cover ourselves with the sheets and not look in his face. Around 12 individuals [were in the building]. Mr Michael Brown, my wife’s cousin, was also at the church. Dr Smith started speaking. We started throwing food stuff outside. We threw away sanitary napkins, tissue and other stuff out the front of the building.

Because of COVID-19, Dr Smith was telling us the world was coming to an end,” James said, pointing out that the pastor was frequently telling them to take their money out of the bank.

He said Smith told them to throw out the food and other stuff because they were from Babylon.

While James and others threw out the items, he explained that a bottle fell from a table and broke on the ground inside the church.

He told the court that Smith informed them that those who were on the opposite side of the bottle would have to die in order for them to enter into the Kingdom.

“He said he got a revelation. I was on the opposite side, and Dr Smith said to me that in order for me to come over on the other side, my throat has to be cut. I was confused when he mentioned that to me. I spoke to Dr Smith, and he said I was a demon and that I should come out of the sanctuary. After I was told my throat would be cut, Kevaughn Plummer approached me with a knife, and he was trying to put the knife under my throat. I rest my finger under my neck to push away the knife. The knife was right under my chin. Dr Smith said I should get out.”

He said that when he turned around to walk outside, he felt someone stab him in the back, causing him to run out on the pavement.

“I felt like something was running down in my back. I wiped my back, and when I looked, I saw blood. Mr Smith was standing at the entrance of the door when I turned around. He said something to me. I spoke to Andre Ruddock and asked him if he could tie the white cloth around my back. He did not tie it, but Aldeane Campbell tied it for me. There were a lot of people outside the fence on the road, including my mom, sister, nephew and other people I would call friends. They wanted to come on the compound. The gate was closed, so they weren’t able to come over.”

The witness said he remained at the church because his wife and his daughter were still inside.

While on the outside of the church building, James said he could hear things being smashed and broken on the inside.

“It was still bright, so it was maybe around after 3:00 pm. Persons were shouting on the outside, ‘it’s Israel God, Israel King’. This was on the outside of the fence on the roadside. He shared that Smith took out a piece of paper with names on it. Among the names on the list were Taneka Gardner.

He appointed two archangels, Ruddock and another man and gave them two knives. He then instructed them to go to the church gate and not let anybody else in unless their names were called.

When Gardner was called, she entered and signed 999 beside her name on the paper. She was given instructions, including to kneel down.

“When Kevin Smith called Taneka Gardner’s name, Andrew Ruddock and Kayon Ramsey opened the gate and let her in. The people on the outside of the gate, I could see them over the picket fence. When Taneka Gardner was allowed to come on the inside, she was covered in the white garment. White cloth was tied around her head. I could see her face when she came in. Her head was covered as well. She had a suitcase in her hand, a mini suitcase. She came in with it and Kevin Smith asked her where she was going with that bag. One of the young men took it from her and went back to the gate with it.

“Kevin Smith said, ‘Taneka Gardner, your blood is not clean’. He was speaking very loudly. He continued to speak to her. He asked her, ‘do you believe that I am God? Do you believe I can heal you?’ She said Yes. He went further and he said, do you believe that if you die I can bring you back to life? She shouted on the top of her voice and said yes. Dr Smith gave a command. He said, ‘Archangel, cut her throat.’ He appointed Kayon Ramsey and Andre Ruddock as Archangel Gabriel and Michael.

“I was looking directly in the direction of Andre Ruddock. I watched Andre use his elbow to nudge Kayon Ramsey, but Kayon did not move. Andre Ruddock ran off from the gate and ran towards Taneka Gardner. Miss Taneka Gardner was kneeling down, and Andre Ruddock put the knife at her throat, and he was rubbing her throat with the knife. I just saw her foot kicking, and I could hear a gargling sound, like the blood was rushing down her windpipe as if she had fluid in her mouth, like when you put water in your mouth and gargle. He was rubbing the knife at her throat for about a minute before he brought her down to the ground. Mr Smith said to him to cut her head right off. While Andre Ruddock was cutting her throat, a cow was coming down from up the top,” he said, telling the court that it was at that time Smith switched focus from Gardner and told Ruddock and Ramsey to kill the cow.

The witness explained that Ruddock then got up from where Gardner was, while Ramsey chased down the cow.

“Taneka Gardner was just lying there. You could see the white sheet with what appeared to be blood and it was also on the sheet that Andre Ruddock had on,” he said.

World.title: 10 things only a Westwood High girl would know
World.content:
In this April 15, 2011 file photo, students of Westwood High School at an Earth Day expo put on by the Environmental Foundation of Jamaica and held at Devon House in St Andrew. (Photo: Bryan Cummings)

Westwood High School is known for producing talented, well-educated and poised young ladies. The institution, which has been in existence for more than a century, can credit much of this to its vibrant culture and traditions.

Observer Online spoke to a number of the Stewart Town, Trelawny-based school’s alumni to find out some of the things that every Westwood girl would know.

1. Jippi Jappa hat and wearing all white

Westwood High is one of the few schools in Jamaica where students wear hats as part of their uniform. The tradition, which has its roots in English school customs, has been passed down and retained by the institution over the years. The Jippi Jappa hat, also known as a Panama hat, is worn by the young ladies along with their uniforms. Students are not permitted to wear the hat past the principal’s building.

Students are also expected to have a set of white clothing outside of their regular uniform. This is worn on occasions when they are not required to be in uniform, except on Friday evenings and Saturdays.

2. The Jacaranda tree

The Jacaranda tree was one of the familiar landmarks on the Westwood campus and a popular meeting spot for students during break time. The ladies gathered beneath the tree to catch up with friends, relax and enjoy each other’s company. With its vibrant purple blooms and towering structure, the tree provided both a scenic and comfortable setting. Unfortunately, the tree has been cut down, but it remains a memorable part of the Westwood experience.

3. Observing silence

Silence is a familiar part of life at Westwood. Students are expected to observe silence during prep or study time, meal times and intervals. For many old girls, learning when to talk and when to remain quiet was simply part of the discipline and routine of school life.

4. Sarcasm and lapsing

Westwood ladies are known for their quick wit and, according to old girls, their ability to dish out a healthy dose of sarcasm. They also participate in what is known as “lapsing”. This is when a word is mispronounced and other students repeat the word or phrase, often drawing attention to the mistake. For Westwood girls, it is all part of the banter and camaraderie that develop among students.

5. Knife and fork

Table manners are a big part of the meal-time experience at Westwood. Students are expected to eat their meals using a knife and fork and to follow proper dining etiquette. This includes knowing how to conduct themselves at the table and, in some cases, asking permission before doing things such as chewing bones at the table. For many students, these lessons extended beyond the dining hall and became part of the poise and etiquette associated with being a Westwood girl.

6. Day girls and boarders

Westwood is one of the few schools in Jamaica that offers a boarding option for students. Those who live on the school compound are referred to as boarders, while students who travel to school are called ‘day girls’.

7. Walking to church

Boarders are expected to walk to church on Sundays. The girls are divided based on denomination and walk together to their respective churches. For many boarders, the walk to church is a familiar part of the Westwood boarding experience.

8. Out-of-bounds areas

The ladies of Westwood know that there are certain areas of the school that they are not allowed to enter. These include the teachers’ steps and staff rooms. Students are expected to know and respect these boundaries, with venturing into out-of-bounds areas likely to result in disciplinary action.

9. Students not allowed in stores without parental supervision

If a young lady wanted to enter a store while wearing her uniform, she had to be accompanied by a parent. If she entered a store without a parent and misbehaved, any report made to the school could result in her being reprimanded when she returned. The rule meant that students were expected to remember that their behaviour while wearing the Westwood uniform reflected on the school.

10. Silence as punishment

Silence was also used as a form of punishment at Westwood. Students who misbehave could be required to observe silence. The punishment was intended to give students time to settle down, reflect on their behaviour and regain their composure.

– Carlysia Ramdeen

World.title: Market Bag: Tomato now $500 as food prices continue to climb
World.content:
KINGSTON, Jamaica — Food prices continue to surge at the Coronation Market this week amid worsening drought conditions which have affected agricultural supplies across the country.

Among the more expensive items at the market are lettuce, selling for $1,500 per pound, and Scotch bonnet peppers at $700 per pound. Sweet peppers are going for $600 per pound, while carrots and tomatoes are selling for $500 per pound. Onions, sweet potatoes and Irish potatoes are each priced at approximately $400 per pound.

Speaking on the latest episode of Market Bag with host Carlysia Ramdeen, Andre Barnaby of the Kingston and St Andrew Municipal Corporation pointed to changing weather patterns as one of the major challenges affecting market supply and prices.

“I’d say the biggest challenge right now that we’re facing is climate change so the variation in the weather. So at times or different times of the year, we have large yields and like now for example, in the drought period, we have like way less in terms of supplies. So that affects the overall, that’s like the biggest challenge we face because it also affects price,” Barnaby said.

Catch the latest episode of Market Bag on all Jamaica Observer digital platforms.

World.title: Reggae Boyz squad named for opening Nations League games
World.content:
Jamaica’s Reggae Boyz Leon Bailey (left), Damion Lowe (second left) and Demarai Gray (partially hidden) celebrate with Jon Russell after he scored against Guatemala during the Concacaf World Cup Qualifier at the National Stadium on Tuesday, June 10, 2025. (Photo: Observer file)

Head Coach Rudolph Speid has named his Reggae Boyz squad for the first two games of their 2026-2027 Concacaf Nations League campaign.

Jamaica, drawn in Group B, will open the first round at the National Stadium against Guatemala on Friday, September 25, before welcoming Honduras four days later on Tuesday, September 29.

Speid has selected a 24-man squad for the assignment.

It will see the return to the Reggae Boyz squad for a number of players who last represented Jamaica in the failed World Cup 2026 qualifying campaign. Among them are goalkeeper and captain Andre Blake, wingers Leon Bailey and Tyreece Campbell, defender Richard King, midfielders Kasey Palmer and Karoy Anderson, and forward Renaldo Cephas.

The top two teams from the two Nations League preliminary groups will qualify for the finals where they will be drawn alongside the ranked teams- two-time defending champions Mexico, the USA, Canada and Panama in the quarterfinals.

World.title: WATCH: Tensions flare at meeting over Charles’ Barking Lodge aquaculture project
World.content:
ST THOMAS, Jamaica — A sensitisation meeting over a controversial aquaculture project in Barking Lodge, St Thomas erupted in chaos Tuesday as tensions boiled over amid continued opposition to the development near a primary school in the community.

The meeting, held at the Barking Lodge Primary and Infant School, the institution located behind the proposed fish ponds, ended abruptly when Member of Parliament for St Thomas Eastern Rose Shaw and her team walked out.

Dr Michelle Charles, the former St Thomas Eastern Member of Parliament and director of St Thomas Farms Limited, the company behind the project, had organised the sensitisation meeting for the development which was suspended due to a lack of environmental permits.

At the meeting, an overview of the project was presented along with environmental and safety measures that will guide the development.

WATCH: Charles defends Barking Lodge aquaculture project, addresses safety concerns

Clive Williams, director of the National Fisheries Authority, said the organisation determined that the project was conducted according to agricultural standards and was indeed feasible.

“When we looked at the site, the water source that is available, the proximity to the community, we realised that the project is feasible… We don’t see any challenges of it having an adverse effect on the environment and the community,” Williams said.

Despite Williams’ assurances, tensions flared as critics of the project maintained their skepticism, while Shaw accused the chairman of the meeting of having a political agenda.

“I am utterly disgusted with what is taking place… a politician is cheering the meeting,” Shaw said.

The meeting subsequently erupted in a shouting match before ending prematurely, and even the police had to be called in to quell tensions.

Charles has described the initiative as having the potential to become one of the first major commercial aquaculture operations on Jamaica’s eastern side. She said responsible investment of this nature could contribute to job creation, skills training, infrastructure improvements and sustained economic growth in an area that has experienced limited commercial development since the decline of the sugar industry.

According to Charles, consultations were held with the school’s principal before construction of the ponds began, and student safety has remained a priority throughout the planning process.

World.title: ‘Mommy, them want me turn cruff”
World.content:
BICKERSTETH, St James — The lament of a 10-year-old student struck a chord with residents Thursday after thieves ransacked Bickersteth Primary and Infant School, making off with computers and tuck shop supplies in the fifth break-in there in just seven years.

“Mommy, them people yah want me turn cruff,” was how the boy reacted to news of the break-in, his mother told the Jamaica Observer.

The mother, who asked not be named, said her son, a grade five student, cried on the verandah of their house as he was told that school would be closed on Thursday and Friday because of the crime.

“I told him ‘Son, you nah turn cruff, we will stand with you’,” she related to the Observer.

Cruff is a Jamaican colloquial term for individuals who are deemed lazy, lack ambition, or have poor social etiquette.

The mother is among parents and residents who are now expressing anguish over the situation at the school.

“I usually send him out before me, but he has to stay home with his sister today,” the distraught mother said.

On Thursday morning, school administrators turned up to see windows and doors at the school pried open and items missing.

“They ripped the grill out the wall, broke the window and came in,” Principal Robert Gordon said. “Not even [Hurricane] Melissa did a job like that, the place was ransacked.”

Category 5 Melissa left widespread destruction across western and south-western parishes last October.

Principal Gordon said Thursday’s early morning break-in was the fifth in seven years.

“Last year, this time, they broke into the school twice, but that individual was held. We lost some equipment as well — computers and food items,” Gordon said.

He speculated that the robbery may be connected with others committed in western Jamaica in recent times.

“Based on what is happening now and the series of schools — Bogue Hill, Retrieve, Anchovy — it seems like they are just going through and hitting schools in a series,” Gordon said.

A man who gave his name as Anglin, described the break-in as disheartening.

“I have four daughters and all of them went through here. The last one was head girl at Anchovy, one got 11 subjects at Mount Alvernia, but this is the ground where it all started,” he said.

“This is heartbreaking, man,” he added.

On Thursday, following an emergency meeting of the school board, several members of staff were seen engaged in cleaning-up activities while listening to gospel music amid the sound of power tools as work was ongoing to replace a damaged window.

“We are trying to fix back as best as possible, even though it might be temporary, but we want to secure the area from the elements because rain may fall and the entire area is ripped out and we don’t want the office to be compromised any further,” Principal Gordon told the Observer.

“The gentleman that is working now is a community person; he’s from the area, his children came to school here. We called him, he dropped what he was doing, and he’s here and we are very appreciative of that,” Gordon said, adding that the school will be closed for the rest of the week while they work to sort things out. However, online classes will be held.

“One of the things we looked at is the impact it will have on the students seeing the school ripped apart and that could have a long-term impact on their mental psyche,” the principal explained.

“We said, ‘Okay, let’s sort of fix back the school in a way, because these children are very young, they are very impressionable, and we have to be mindful of what they see’,” he added.

“We have spoken to the teachers and we have asked them to send out work for the students to do virtually,” he revealed.

On Wednesday, Education Minister Senator Dr Dana Morris Dixon acknowledged that schools, particularly in western Jamaica, are being plagued by break-ins since the start of the academic year.

“The west has gone through a lot of trauma for us to be dealing with theft of computers for these schools and these children, it is really heartbreaking,” she lamented during the weekly post-Cabinet news briefing.

She said the series of robberies has resulted in her reaching out to the national security minister and police commissioner for assistance.

World.title: ‘It’s a fallacy’
World.content:
ROBINSON... we’re far from being in a good position in the economy

Opposition spokesman on finance Julian Robinson has dismissed as a “fallacy” the rosy picture of the Jamaican economy presented by Finance Minister Fayval Williams during Wednesday’s post-Cabinet media briefing.

Among other things, Williams noted that the rate of recovery from the fallout caused by Hurricane Melissa, which destroyed large swathes of south- and north-western parishes last October, was 18 months ahead of earlier projections by the Planning Institute of Jamaica (PIOJ).

However, Robinson is pointing to inflation running at nearly eight per cent and a $30-billion tax revenue shortfall as signs of a struggling economy.

In a video released by the Opposition People’s National Party (PNP) on Thursday, Robinson suggested that the finance minister was merely trying to put a positive spin on the situation. He reminded that in the last quarter the Government’s own projection for revenues was $28.7 billion lower than projected.

“It’s important to note that these projections were done in March 2026, which is after Hurricane Melissa, so they would have factored in Melissa and they would have made their projections,” he said.

Robinson pointed out that the revenue shortfall of nearly $30 billion forced the Government to go back to the market to borrow $30 billion but the Administration was unable to raise the full amount.

“To give this impression that the economy is doing great is really a fallacy,” he declared.

The Opposition spokesman also highlighted what he described as the cost of living pressures facing Jamaicans. He cited that at nearly eight per cent, inflation was “way above the Bank of Jamaica (BOJ) target range of four to six per cent”.

“I anticipate that when the BOJ’s monetary policy committee meets, they will be looking to raise interest rates to try and tame inflation,” he stated.

Were the central bank to take such a decision, Robinson conceded that this would put more pressure on businesses which will have to pay more on their loans, and on consumers, who will have to pay more on their mortgages and the various loans they are carrying.

“We’re far from being in a good position in the economy, we’re actually seeing the highest rates of car repossessions; we’re seeing bad loans at banks at elevated rates. So it indicates that there’s significant consumer pressure being faced, people are struggling to meet their basic obligations,” said Robinson.

Anticipating talk from some quarters that the cost of living pressure is being driven by factors outside Jamaica’s control, such as the higher cost for fuel and electricity as a result of the Middle East war, Robinson said while that is true, there are things within the control of the Government that would lessen the pressure on Jamaicans.

“The Government has the control to determine how much imported oil we use, it has been an absolute failure on the part of this Government to increase the amount of renewables that have been added to the grid,” Robinson argued.

“In the 10-and-a-half years that they have been in office, they have added no renewables to the grid,” he said, adding that what was in fact added since 2016 started under the previous PNP Administration with Phillip Paulwell as energy minister.

Pointing out that it took the Jamaica Labour Party Government eight years to issue a request for proposal for renewables, the Opposition spokesman said those companies that have been selected cannot sign private purchase agreements with Jamaica Public Service Company because the company’s contract is in limbo (its licence expires in July 2027).

He asserted that while we cannot control the price of oil, we can determine how much oil we import by building out more renewables. In this regard, he said the Government has failed; a failure with a direct impact on cost of living.

“Because, if we’re less dependent on oil, it improves our financial position and it means the impact is less on consumers,” he said.

Robinson also argued that the minister pointing out that the economy is recovering faster than projected masks certain uncomfortable realities.

“We’re underspending the capital budget. Our capital budget is required to build out schools, hospitals, roads, etc, we’re underspending that,” he reiterated. He argued that such spend is important to ensuring that there’s growth in the economy “because there’s a direct link between your capital budget and economic growth and for the last five years we have underspent it”.

Robinson pointed out that when the capital budget is underutilised, the money is shifted to recurrent expenditure such as wages and salaries. “This makes the fiscal situation look a little better but it does not account for the fact that we have been woefully underspending the capital budget,” he insisted.

He lamented that the vast majority of Jamaicans most affected by Hurricane Melissa — either at the individual or small business level — have received no assistance from Government. This, he said, has made it difficult for them to recover, resulting in lower tax revenues. He insisted that Government has taken too long to get help to those who are most in need.

In her take on the economy, Williams highlighted that in the quarter following the hurricane, the economy contracted 7.1 per cent, then 4.1 per cent in the next quarter and just 2.9 per cent in the quarter after that. She said the 2.9 per cent projection should be finalised by the Statistical Institute of Jamaica by the end of September.

The finance minister argued that the shrinking year-on-year numbers are themselves proof that the economy is recovering, adding further that “an economy in decline produces deepening figures, not improving ones”.

Williams urged Jamaicans to remember that immediately after the hurricane, PIOJ projected that the country would not get back to its pre-Melissa level of output until the last quarter of 2028. She noted that the PIOJ now expects that the economy will begin to see growth by the second quarter of 2027 — “six quarters earlier, a year-and-a-half earlier”. According to her, the PIOJ “has been able to revise their forecast because the out-turn keeps getting better”.

World.title: ‘There are no decent parties left’: Sham elections underscore Putin’s grip on Russia
World.content:
But other opponents of the Kremlin say Navalnaya’s strategy is giving credibility to sham elections that are only held to justify Russian President Vladimir Putin’s maximalist war against Ukraine and tighten his grip on Russian society.

“To whoever comes to us with a sword — do not expect mercy,” Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said in a campaign ad for Putin’s United Russia party, alongside NHL superstar Alex Ovechkin and the propagandist Margarita Simonyan, who runs the state broadcaster RT.

Putin’s veterans

The Kremlin’s response to the opposition suggests it is worried that people are growing tired of the war.

By removing anti-war candidates from the ballot and promoting pro-war voices, Moscow seeks to overstate public support for the invasion of Ukraine, says Ivan Preobrazhensky, a Russian political scientist based in Prague. “By electing them, people are effectively endorsing the policies of the ruling party and the government,” he told POLITICO, even though voters have no real alternative.

Yabloko received between 1% and 2% of votes in previous parliamentary elections and was seen as “politically dead” by the Kremlin, according to Maxim Reznik, a former party leader in St. Petersburg. By allowing it to run, Reznik said, the Kremlin “wanted to show that just 1.5% of Russians oppose war.”

But reports in Russian media suggested that Yabloko’s recent positioning as “the only peace party,” as well as its advocacy for an immediate ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, had boosted its electoral support. The Nezavisimaya Gazeta reported on a July poll from an unnamed agency giving Yabloko a rating of 9.4%. Faridaily, an outlet founded by independent journalist Farida Rustamova, reported that internal government polling put the party around 5.5%.

World.title: European leaders prepare public for ‘intensified threat’ from Putin
World.content:
The warnings underscore a growing sense of anxiety in Europe amid fast-proliferating incidents of airspace violations and sabotage attempts in recent months. NATO allies have repeatedly said they see the attacks as pressure from the Kremlin to reduce their support for Ukraine but have muted their response over fears of escalation.

French President Emmanuel Macron summoned party leaders and 2027 presidential candidates for an emergency meeting on Friday to talk about Ukraine, Iran and the growing energy crisis.

He called Tusk’s warnings “sound and well-documented” as he announced a new critical infrastructure protection plan, adding: “In recent weeks … the Russian hybrid threat against Europeans and France has intensified.”

Guillaume Lacroix, leader of the Radical Party of the Left, left the meeting saying: “At the age of 50, I have rarely felt such vertigo.”

“It is no coincidence that the Polish prime minister is speaking out so strongly,” Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said Friday. “We need to take that warning very seriously … we must consistently demonstrate that we do not accept this and that we will take action if necessary.”

On Thursday, Finnish President Alexander Stubb told his country it was “worth mentally preparing for something to happen” including sabotage and Russian drones.

World.title: Australia following Canada as EU associate member is ‘pure speculation,’ says Commission
World.content:
Asked whether the meeting could provide an opportunity to discuss the associate membership idea with Australia, Podestà dismissed the suggestion.

“We have a very strong and close relationship with our Australian partners,” she said. “All the rest is pure speculation, and we’re not going to enter into that.”

Von der Leyen pitched Canada as a potential first EU “associate member” during her State of the Union address on Wednesday. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has welcomed the ambition behind closer EU-Canada ties but has stopped short of endorsing the proposed status.

European Parliament President Roberta Metsola subsequently said countries such as Australia and New Zealand could potentially follow Canada.

But Commission spokesperson Olof Gill stressed that Brussels is currently focused solely on developing the idea with Ottawa.

“What we’re focused on here is putting flesh on the bone on this idea,” Gill said, adding that the Commission is working with member states and Canadian partners to establish what the concept could look like in practice. “All other discussions are subsequent to that.”

World.title: Germany gets its first F-35 as Europe’s fighter plans fall apart
World.content:
But without the FCAS, Berlin is left without an obvious European successor.

“We want and need to maintain nuclear sharing,” Pistorius said ahead of the handover. The F-35, he argued, is currently “the only aircraft in the world” capable of fulfilling that mission.

Under the NATO nuclear-sharing program, Germany and other select allies have aircraft that can carry U.S. nuclear bombs, although the decision to use them remains with Washington.

The first F-35s will remain in the United States for training, with German pilots and technicians preparing for operations before more jets are sent to Büchel in late 2027. Full operational capability is expected by 2030.

Berlin currently operates around 80 Tornados, and some missions will migrate to the Eurofighter Typhoon. But the collapse of FCAS has opened a longer-term gap in Germany's plans for its combat-air fleet.

During June's Berlin Air Show, Pistorius said Berlin is weighing whether to acquire additional F-35s as a “bridge” option after the FCAS failure, to join an existing international sixth-generation program or to develop a national effort headed by Airbus.

World.title: Macron to call emergency G7 meeting as energy prices spike and Russian hybrid attacks mount
World.content:
“The situation we face is serious. It is serious due to the international situation and the consequence of wars that we endure,” Macron said. “In this context we need to stay united.”

France’s dire fiscal outlook, which has prompted the government to pursue a €54 billion budget squeeze next year, will make it difficult for the state to massively subsidize increasingly expensive energy bills. Macron told reporters, however, that the government was working on targeted assistance proposals.

Macron also said he was seeking to firm up French access to oil and gas supplies during recent meetings with leaders from Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. He added that he’d discuss France’s trade in petroleum products and liquefied natural gas with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney when the two meet on Sunday.

The president said France was stepping up efforts to protect critical infrastructure and defense production sites amid the uptick in cyberattacks and the intensified threat of so-called hybrid attacks from Russia, including recent ones on a Ukrainian passenger train and at Leipzig airport in Germany. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned Thursday that Russia was planning to target Ukraine’s European allies using drones or rockets.

Among those in attendance were center-right former Prime Minister Edouard Philippe, centrist Gabriel Attal, conservative candidate Bruno Retailleau, center-left Raphaël Glucksmann, Greens leader Marine Tondelier and Socialist Party chief Olivier Faure. Far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, who has a commanding lead in the polls, was represented by her party’s president, Jordan Bardella, while far-left hopeful Jean-Luc Mélenchon was represented by a high-ranking lawmaker from his party, Manuel Bompard.

The politicians who spoke to reporters after the meeting acknowledged the gravity of what had been discussed. Guillaume Lacroix, the head of a small left-wing party, wrote online that the stakes of the three-hour briefing had made his head spin.

World.title: Ukraine’s NATO envoy calls for more air defense donations
World.content:
“We need to stop viewing assistance that enables Ukraine to defend itself as purely a matter of supporting Ukraine. It is also in NATO’s own interest … the more drones and missiles Ukraine can destroy in its own airspace, the fewer will cross the borders of neighboring NATO countries,” the envoy added.

Getmanchuk underlined that Western countries still have stocks of interceptor missiles to donate, including missiles close to the end of their service lives.

“There is hardly a better way to decommission them than by using them in the Ukrainian sky,” Getmanchuk said.

Kyiv is proposing a workaround: allies hand over interceptors from their existing stocks now, and Ukraine replaces them later with missiles it has already ordered.

“It’s a swap — not a donation. What we need is to get through this winter,” Getmanchuk said.

Ukraine is placing substantial orders, using both partner funding and the EU’s €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan. These contracts cover not only hundreds of Patriot interceptors — both PAC-2s and PAC-3s — but also European systems, including SAMP/T and Aster 30 missiles, IRIS-T and others.

World.title: EU to ban metal scrap exports to India, Egypt on environmental grounds
World.content:
The EU exported nearly 19 million tonnes of scrap metal in 2025, accounting for over half the bloc’s total recyclable raw materials exports.

Egypt and India respectively bought over 1.3 million and 850,000 tonnes of scrap metal.

Last-minute concerns over the EU’s trade deal with India led the European Commission to withdraw planned export duties on aluminum scrap earlier this month.

India is a major importer of aluminum scrap. The country last year exported over 350,000 tons of aluminum scrap alone.

The executive was due to present an instrument to slow exports of cheap aluminum scrap to buyers outside the single market, keeping prices down for aluminum producers and users within the bloc. The European aluminum sector has pushed for priority access to local scrap.

EU industry chief Stéphane Séjourné said, however, that the EU would scrap the measure after it became clear it would only cover around half of the bloc’s aluminum scrap exports and decided to pursue a solution “entirely independent” of trade policy instruments.

Egypt and India will still be able to export other scrap materials, including paper, wood, rubber, and textile waste.

The Commission will consult on the suggested country exemptions until October 16, before adopting the final list in November, as required under the regulation.

World.title: British MPs to tackle UK crisis — why it does so badly in Eurovision
World.content:
The British entry is currently selected internally by the BBC, one of the world’s largest public broadcasters, and chosen from the third biggest record industry on the planet, behind the U.S. and Japan. It also automatically qualifies for the contest’s final because the BBC is one of the largest contributors to the event’s organizer, the European Broadcasting Union.

Despite this, the U.K. has repeatedly finished in the bottom half of the leaderboard over the past 15 years, with only one exception: Sam Ryder, who claimed second place in 2022 with ‘Space Man.’

The committee is expected to hear from figures from the BBC and the music industry to establish whether the U.K.’s track record is “the result of bad song choice, weak performance … or something else,” Dinenage told the BBC.

The British broadcaster has yet to announce its entry for next year’s event, which will take place in May 2027 in Burgas, Bulgaria.

The contest has been overshadowed in recent years by boycotts from multiple nations over Israel’s participation, following the Oct. 7 2023 Hamas attack and subsequent Israeli military offensive in Gaza. Dutch broadcaster AVROTROS and Ireland’s RTÉ have already announced that they will not be taking part in next year’s contest.

World.title: Trump threatens to ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House
World.content:
President Donald Trump has said he is banning three major news organisations, CNN, MS NOW and Politico, from the White House with immediate effect, accusing them of publishing “fake news”, “fiction” and “lies”.

 

It is not yet clear what the ban will entail. Trump also warned that restrictions could be extended to other media outlets.

In a post on his Truth Social platform on Friday, the president said the three outlets “constantly write or report fiction and lies” about his administration, although he provided no specific examples.

President Trump writing on Truth Social via Truth Social

The move is the latest test of First Amendment protections guaranteeing freedom of the press in the United States.

It is also the latest move by Trump’s second administration to restrict press access. He has already tightened controls over which journalists can join the White House press pool, the small group of reporters who accompany the president into restricted spaces such as the Oval Office and aboard Air Force One.

CNN is part of the traditional five-network television pool that travels with and covers the president. It is not yet clear whether the new ban will affect that arrangement.

In 2025, Trump restricted Associated Press access to some presidential events after the news agency continued to use the name “Gulf of Mexico” rather than Trump’s preferred “Gulf of America”. AP subsequently launched legal action over the restrictions. The case remains ongoing.

During Trump’s first term, CNN reporter Kaitlan Collins was barred from a White House Rose Garden event after officials said questions she asked the president earlier that day were "inappropriate" for the venue.

While it is extremely rare for a US president to bar an entire news organisation from the White House, previous administrations have also imposed restrictions on individual outlets. President Richard Nixon restricted access for The Washington Post during the Watergate scandal in the 1970s.

World.title: As Russia strikes Kyiv and Kharkiv, Russian cooling tower hit by drone
World.content:
Russia has launched attacks on several areas of Ukraine, with two killed in Balakliia in Kharkiv and missiles launched at the capita, Kyiv.

 

In a post on Telegram, the head of Balakliia's military administration Vitalii Karabanov gave an update on the damage and loss of life: "Sadly, the consequences of this attack are terrible. Early reports indicate that two people have been killed in the strike. I extend my deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of those killed."

There have been further attacks on the Kyiv on Friday evening. Ukrainian media reports the city has been hit by ballistic missiles.

The Mayor of Kyiv, Vitali Klitschko, posted on Telegram at 19:32 local time (18:32 CEST) warning of the strikes, which read: "Air defense forces are working in the capital. Kyiv is under ballistic fire. Stay in shelters!"

Meanwhile, there have been repeated attacks on central Odesa, with strikes twice in quick succession. The second hit during the rescue operation. Local media reports 10 people have been injured in the attacks.

An office building on fire, in the aftermath of Russian strikes on central Odesa. Odesa Oblast Military Administration

In Russia, a drone hit a cooling tower of the Kursk Nuclear Power Plant early on Thursday. The International Atomic Energy Agency reported Friday that it was aware of the strike on the Kursk plant, adding that the power station remained operational at the time, but that there was no fire and operations had continued.

The IAEA reports that that a cooling tower of the Kursk Nuclear Power Plant in the Russian Federation was hit by a drone early on Thursday.

In the post, the Director General of the IAEA, Rafael Grossis warned against further attacks near nuclear infrastructure, and reiterated the need for "maximum military restraint to prevent the risk of a nuclear accident".

World.title: Irish Finance Minister says Hormuz closure, not Ukraine, causing energy crisis
World.content:
The closure of the Strait of Hormuz and Trump's war with Iran are causes behind the turmoil in the energy markets, not Ukraine's attacks on Russian diesel refineries. That is the message Irish Finance Minister and Deputy Prime Minister (Tánaiste), Simon Harris, shared with Euronews in an exclusive interview

 

Harris pushed back against recent remarks made by US President Donald Trump, who blamed Ukraine's strikes on Russian diesel refineries for creating a shortage. Oil prices are hovering around $108 per barrel.

"The reason there's a major energy crisis in the world right now is because the Strait of Hormuz is closed," Harris said on Euronews' interview programme 12 Minutes With. "I always make the point, and I would make it again today, that the greatest economic intervention we could see is de-escalation in the Middle East," he added.

He noted that this became evident during the summer, when there was a brief moment of respite in the conflict. "We saw a very rapid fall in the commodity markets and therefore a benefit at the pump."

Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil and gas facilities are squeezing Moscow’s oil output and having an impact globally, as Russia is one of the world’s largest oil producers, but experts agree the current energy crisis is primarily caused by the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz – the transit route for 20% of the world's oil and gas supplies.

The situation has escalated after Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline, also known as Petroline, following drone attacks earlier this month from Iran-backed allied Houthis and Iraq.

"From an economic perspective, I'm very concerned [after] what we've seen on oil markets in recent days," Harris said. "I'm also very concerned about the fact that we aren't seeing de-escalation; we're actually seeing an escalation and indeed more fronts in terms of complications opening up regarding energy."

Windfall tax on the table

It is against the backdrop of mounting energy costs that finance ministers from eurozone countries gathered in Dublin on Friday, rushing to mitigate the rising prices and discussing measures to mitigate the impact on citizens.

One of the ideas circulating among EU ministers at the meeting is a windfall tax for firms profiting from energy price volatility, following calls from several member states to consider this measure.

"Some energy companies are making extraordinarily large profits on the back of this energy crisis," Harris said, noting that they are not doing so by "being innovative," but "because of the chaos that we're seeing in the energy markets as a result of the Strait of Hormuz being closed."

Without pre-empting possible outcomes of the talks, Harris said he would be having an initial conversation on such a tax with ministers in Dublin. Ireland currently holds the rotating EU Council presidency, allowing it to set the work programme and Council meeting agenda.

"It's likely that we will ask the European Commission to further examine this and that we would formally discuss it in Brussels at the next formal [Economic and Finance Council] meeting in October."

World 'cannot become numb to loss of life'

Harris stressed that, aside from the economic importance of ending the Middle East conflict, the world can not turn a blind eye to the human toll either.

"I think while I'm obviously speaking in the capacity of a finance minister, we should never become numb to the loss of life in war, whether that's the loss of life in Ukraine, whether it's the horrific genocide we've seen in Gaza, whether it's a situation in the Middle East more broadly," he said. "We need to see a de-escalation of conflict more broadly in the world."

On settler violence seen in the West Bank against Palestinians, the Tánaiste argued in favour of a tougher stance on Israeli settlements, which are illegal under international law.

"I'm massively pro-European, but I think when it comes to Gaza, it's been disappointing, to put it mildly, that more hasn't been done at that coordinated level," Harris said.

Several European countries, including Ireland and more recently the United Kingdom, have announced national bans on the import of all goods produced in illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

"Member states are listening to their public and are moving ahead, but we would always rather see action at an EU level because we think it's more impactful."

The EU’s top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, recently put forward an EU-wide ban on trade with illegal Israeli settlements as a "principled stance" for the bloc, comparing illegal settlements in the West Bank to Russia’s occupation of Crimea.
