World.title: England can build on World Cup ‘spirit’, says Tuchel
World.content:
London – Thomas Tuchel said England will build on the “fantastic spirit” of their World Cup campaign as he targets glory on home soil at Euro 2028.

The England boss was speaking at Wembley after naming a 27-man group for a four-game Nations League camp, starting with a clash against world champions Spain on September 26.

It comes just nine weeks after the end of the World Cup, where England conceded two late goals in a painful semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold and Chelsea forward Cole Palmer were the headline picks after both were controversially overlooked for the World Cup.

Tuchel also included Liverpool’s teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, uncapped Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite in his first squad since the tournament in North America.

A number of players who were in the World Cup squad including John Stones, Djed Spence, Dan Burn, Jordan Henderson and Dean Henderson missed out through injury.

Former Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Tuchel said he did not see the Nations League as a new start, instead focusing on continuity.

“I feel that it’s not a new beginning that we are starting now, so we build on a solid and very valuable foundation, and the target is to win the home Euros,” he told reporters on Friday.

Euro 2028 will be co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales, and Ireland.

The German said his side’s ultimate failure at the World Cup had left him unfulfilled but stuck by his squad picks.

“I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic,” he said.

“I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.”

Tuchel said Palmer had impressed for Chelsea early in the season.

“He has his numbers back, he has assists back, he has decisive goals back, so that’s why he’s in the squad and I think he has a point to prove,” he said.

“The same goes for Trent. He was never off the list, he was never in a non-selectable class, and he has this chance to show, to be the best version of himself.”

Tuchel said it was his “duty” to play Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo after he failed to feature for a single minute at the World Cup.

The England boss welcomed the challenge of taking on Spain at Wembley.

“We feel the gap is closing and we feel that we are close and we want a proof of point,” he said.

“The stadium is sold out, it will be very exciting, the motivation cannot be higher to play against the world champions.”

England also play the Czech Republic twice and Croatia once during the upcoming international window.

World.title: Anti-Assad music star makes triumphant return to Syria
World.content:
Damascus – Syrian singer Assala Nasri has made a triumphant return to Damascus with a sold-out concert following 15 years of exile due to her opposition to ousted ruler Bashar al-Assad.

Thousands of fans welcomed the 57-year-old, known mononymously as Assala, at a venue in the Syrian capital where she bowed and opened the show with songs hailing the Syrian people.

“Souls of my heart, I missed you,” she repeatedly said to endless cheers on Thursday night.

“My loves, my people, I swear, until this moment I could not believe that I am among you. I want to tell you how much I dreamt of this.”

There was a heavy security presence for the concert, after some religious conservatives launched a campaign calling for its cancellation.

Half of the show’s proceeds will be donated to charity.

Syria’s new Islamist authorities, who overthrew Assad in 2024, have welcomed Assala. Culture Minister Mohammed Yassine Saleh has dubbed her “the daughter of Damascus”.

Joining her on stage, he said her return was that of “every honest Syrian and every free person”.

– ‘Moving forward’ –

Assala was among the first artists to express support for the peaceful anti-Assad protests that erupted in 2011, refusing to partake in events supporting his government.

She was booted from the Syrian artists’ union for her stance and was the target of media campaigns.

She went into exile, living in Cairo with her family and playing shows in various Arab countries.

The bloody repression of the protests led to a 13-year civil war that killed more than half-a-million people.

At Assala’s show, small Syrian flags rippled in time with the music, with many in the crowd unable to hold back their tears.

“I never thought this day would come. It’s like a beautiful dream,” concert-goer Sawsan Wadha, 56, said.

“We are very happy that our country is moving forward,” added 40-year-old Lynn Nahas.

On her new record, “The Syrian Album”, Assala covers folk songs from all 14 of Syria’s provinces as an homage to her country’s cultural diversity.

She sings for the cities scarred by war, but also for the coastline in mourning after last year’s killing of hundreds of members of Assad’s Alawite minority, and for Druze-majority Sweida, which also saw sectarian violence.

– Recovery through art –

Assala’s piercing, powerful voice rang out as she made her way through the album’s tracks at Thursday’s concert.

She also performed fan favourites like “Samehtak” and “Sandooq”, with the jubilant, tearful crowd singing along.

Assala and her family only returned to Damascus this week. An antiques dealer in the capital returned the oud, or Oriental lute, that had belonged to her father, a celebrated musician.

Conservative Muslim figures had expressed criticism in the run-up to the concert.

Egyptian preacher Hani Dahab, who lives in Syria, launched a social media campaign with the slogan “Cancel the Sinful Concerts”. He accused the culture ministry of seeking to “give society a secular character”.

Syrian Salafi preacher Abdul Razzaq al-Mahdi condemned what he called a “concert of music and debauchery”, while a group of preachers in Damascus called on the culture minister to take into account “the religious identity of society”.

While not addressing the critics directly, Assala said at the show that “recovery will only happen with art and music”.

Syria has seen a cultural boom since 2025, but also the rise of preachers and conservative religious movements in public spaces and at universities, raising fears of restrictions on freedom.

Farah Al-Atassi, political advisor to the government, said poetry, language and thought were “an integral part of Syrian identity”.

“This is the Syria that we know and that will endure,” she told AFP.

World.title: UNESCO can be ‘moderator’ in AI debate: chief to AFP
World.content:
Paris – UNESCO chief Khaled el-Enany has proposed in an interview with AFP that the UN culture and education agency become a facilitator in the worldwide wrangling on the risks of artificial intelligence.

“I believe we are uniquely positioned to make UNESCO a true moderator in this global debate,” he said as he prepared to welcome Pope Leo XIV, a key advocate for international AI governance, in Paris next week.

The UN educational, scientific and cultural organisation has long stressed that its remit covers more than heritage, looking to advance in areas ranging from access to education to the ethical use of artificial intelligence.

The debate over the potential dangers of self-improving algorithms has surged in recent weeks, with some researchers warning the technology could end humanity, and leaders of AI companies suggesting development needed to be slowed down.

US President Donald Trump has on the other hand called the fears a “hoax”.

Enany told AFP: “There is a risk that it will get out of control if we don’t intervene.”

“This break, this dialogue that has taken place over the past few weeks, is something very positive,” he added in the interview on Thursday.

He said the cultural agency had found an “indispensable partner” in the pontiff, who is to visit the UNESCO headquarters in Paris on Friday next week at the start of a four-day trip to France.

“This visit will be the beginning of a very solid partnership to strengthen and protect human dignity in this industrial revolution,” Enany said.

It will be the first visit by a pope to UNESCO headquarters since John Paul II in 1980.

– AI ‘must be governed’ –

Pope Leo, the first US pope, this week warned against delegating to algorithms decisions that should be taken by humans alone.

In his first major document, the encyclical “Magnifica Humanitas” (Magnificent Humanity), published in May, the pope issued a call to “disarm” AI in order to “prevent it from dominating humanity”.

Enany said UNESCO had long been concerned with regulating AI, in 2021 issuing a “Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence”.

The guide warned about the risk of violations of privacy and the concentration of technological power in the hands of a few states or companies, and well as potential effects on democracy and the environment.

AI is “an extraordinary tool, but one that must be governed in an ethical, inclusive, and fair way,” Enany said.

Trump has since returning to office withdrawn the United States from UNESCO, alleging that it is biased against Israel and promotes “divisive” causes.

China — one of the major global AI players — has become the agency’s largest donor.

Trump had already ordered a departure from UNESCO in 2017 during his first term, before President Joe Biden reestablished US membership.

As the United States rejoined in 2023, then US secretary of state Antony Blinken said it was key Washington was present at UNESCO for decisions “that actually matter”, including on “rules, norms and standards for artificial intelligence”.

China was among countries to oppose the move.

World.title: Bahrain’s Ramsis Engineering expands into Iraq with Basra office
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Bahrain-based Ramsis Engineering has opened a new branch in Basra to serve Iraq’s growing energy and industrial sectors.

The new office will put the mechanical engineering firm closer to its clients and partners in southern Iraq, where the majority of the country’s oil, gas, and heavy industrial activities are located.

Ramsis stated that its Iraq operations would concentrate on manufacturing, maintenance, and specialized engineering services, building on its expertise in the oil and gas, petrochemical, aluminum, power, and desalination sectors.

The Basra opening establishes the company’s local foothold as Iraq invests in oilfield development, gas processing, and large industrial infrastructure.

Ramsis offers mechanical engineering, building, manufacturing, maintenance, and oilfield services to industrial operators.

World.title: Most Asian stocks track Wall St rally, yen drops after BoJ rate hike
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks mostly rose on Friday in line with a rally on Wall Street as a drop in oil prices eased inflation concerns, while the yen dropped against the dollar even after the Bank of Japan hiked interest rates to a three-decade high.

The Federal Reserve’s lift in borrowing costs this week provided some relief to traders concerned that policymakers were not moving quick enough to address a spike in inflation that could deal a blow to the world’s top economy.

That has been helped by news that Saudi Arabia was moving to restore within days about half of crude shipments disrupted by the stoppage of its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea.

The conduit, even more important since the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz by Iran, was shut last week after being targeted by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.

Crude prices, which had soared around a fifth in September, have fallen around five percent from recent highs, with West Texas Intermediate dipping below $100 for the first time since last Friday. WTI was down more than one percent Friday and Brent lost two percent.

The surge in oil this month has been among the main catalysts for rising inflation since the United States and Israel began their war on Iran at the end of February.

And the latest fall-off provided some much-needed support to stocks.

Seoul, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Taipei, Mumbai and Bangkok all advanced, although there were losses in Singapore, Wellington, Jakarta and Manila. Sydney was barely moved.

London, Paris and Frankfurt dipped.

The latest moves in oil and the Fed’s action reassured investors and kept the 10-year US Treasury bond yield — a key indicator of borrowing costs throughout the world’s biggest economy — back below five percent.

Japan’s Nikkei was also helped by a drop in the yen against the dollar that came in the wake of the BoJ’s well-telegraphed decision to lift rates to their highest level since 1995.

Pressure has increased on officials to further tighten monetary policy as a spike in oil prices caused by the Middle East crisis — which shows little sign of ending anytime soon — is expected to keep putting a floor under inflation.

“Given that underlying CPI inflation has been approaching two percent and financial conditions have been accommodative, the bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate,” the BoJ said on its website.

But the yen slipped to more than 157 to the greenback, compared with around 156 earlier.

Stephen Innes at Quintex Intel suggested traders were jolted by the fact that the hike was not unanimous, passing by a 7-2 majority.

“For a market looking for evidence that the BoJ could shorten the distance between hikes, those dissents mattered,” he wrote.

“Traders were looking for signs that the Bank could move faster from here, yet two members were already arguing that even today’s move had come too soon.”

Focus will now turn to Governor Kazuo Ueda’s news conference due later in the day.

“Attention should fall on the forward swaps curve and the Bank’s guidance around the pace and urgency of further tightening,” wrote Chris Weston at Pepperstone.

“The market will be looking for confirmation that further normalisation remains firmly on the table, while assessing whether the Bank sees any urgency to move again.”

World.title: KBR and AKT sign engineering deal for Iraq’s West Qurna gas capture project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – KBR and AKT have signed a contract to complete the comprehensive engineering design for Iraq’s West Qurna Gas Capture Project, which advances Basrah Gas Company’s efforts to collect associated gas and minimize flaring in southern oilfields.

KBR will offer engineering expertise for the design work in partnership with AKT, since the project is part of Basrah Gas Company’s (BGC) larger gas collection initiative.

The project aims to collect associated gas generated with crude oil from West Qurna, which would otherwise be burnt, enabling more of the resource to be processed and consumed domestically.

Expanding gas capture is critical to Iraq’s attempts to prevent flaring, enhance local gas supplies, and make better use of its energy resources, especially as the country seeks to reduce its dependency on imported gas and fuel for power production.

The West Qurna development is one of many gas projects now underway in southern Iraq, where some of the country’s major oilfields are located and significant amounts of associated gas are generated.

KBR said that the deal strengthens its role in gas monetization and energy infrastructure projects in Iraq and the broader Middle East.

The companies did not disclose the contract’s amount or the timeframe for completing the detailed engineering design.

World.title: Iraq PM to meet Trump in New York as US ties shift to investment
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi will visit the United States next week to address the UN General Assembly and meet with President Donald Trump, as Baghdad aims to pivot its relationship with Washington away from security cooperation and toward long-term commerce and investment.

According to government spokesperson Haider al-Aboudi, Al-Zaidi will give Iraq’s presentation to the UN General Assembly in New York, as well as meet with Trump and other international leaders.

He is also slated to attend an economic-related conference of the United States Chamber of Commerce.

The trip comes barely two months after Al-Zaidi’s first official visit to the United States, during which Baghdad announced 48 agreements and collaborations with American corporations spanning energy, infrastructure, technology, healthcare, and finance.

During discussions in Washington and Houston, Al-Zaidi advocated for more US investment in Iraq and met with leaders from key American corporations.

According to the US Chamber, the agreements and memorandums announced during the visit were worth more than $60 billion and included corporations such as Chevron, ConocoPhillips, GE Vernova, Google, JPMorgan Chase, and PepsiCo.

Al-Zaidi also met with Chevron officials in Houston as Iraq explored agreements for large oilfields and new export infrastructure aimed at diversifying the country’s pathways to international markets.

The current visit takes place only days before the conclusion of the US-led coalition operation in Iraq on September 30.

Al-Aboudi regarded the date as a watershed moment for Iraqi sovereignty, stating that relations with Washington will shift toward long-term economic collaboration, boosting Al-Zaidi’s desire to make investment and private-sector links the basis of the next phase of the Iraq-US relationship.

World.title: Palestinian state more distant than ever, a year after recognition
World.content:
Ramallah – When France, Britain and other Western powers last year recognised a Palestinian state, entrepreneur Adam Bader felt a sense of hope.

“I was happy when I heard about it,” said Bader, 27, who lives in the occupied West Bank’s city of Tulkarem, which has seen repeated Israeli raids in recent years.

“Now a year on, we’re not seeing any improvement. On the contrary,” he said. “The situation is getting worse by the day and no one can do anything.”

A year after the recognition, Palestinian statehood in real, tangible terms looks more distant than ever.

Israeli settler violence has soared, Palestinians are being pushed into ever-smaller areas and the Palestinian Authority has only been weakened.

French President Emmanuel Macron, vowing to find a new path forward amid global outrage over Israel’s offensive in Gaza, on September 22, 2025 led a special UN summit to recognise a Palestinian state.

Ten countries, also including Britain, Canada and Australia, recognised Palestinian statehood, bringing the number of UN member-states doing so to around 157, more than four-fifths of the UN membership.

But Israel, which enjoys support from the United States, adamantly rejects Palestinian statehood, and has stepped up efforts to isolate the Palestinian Authority of president Mahmoud Abbas.

While Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stopped short last year of formally annexing the West Bank, observers say unofficial annexation is creeping as his right-wing government approves an unprecedented number of settlements.

“Recognition makes the two-state solution a reality politically and diplomatically, but unfortunately on the ground it still depends on the illegal behaviour of Israel, which is not implementing international resolutions,” Omar Awadallah, deputy foreign affairs minister of the Palestinian Authority, told AFP.

Ines Abdel Razek, a Palestinian political analyst, said that recognition of a state of Palestine amounted to little without measures to support its existence and counter Israeli actions.

“The two-state solution’s become a diplomatic refrain to avoid looking at reality in the face,” she said.

– ‘No future’ –

Across the West Bank’s limestone hills, thousands of Israeli flags line roads used by Israeli settlers, with the occasional graffiti “No future in Palestine” stencilled on walls, as a call for Palestinians to leave.

Netanyahu argues that a Palestinian state would be a “reward for terrorism” after Hamas on October 7, 2023 carried out the deadliest attack ever on Israel, which responded with a massive military operation in Gaza.

“As long as I am prime minister, an Iranian-controlled Palestinian state will not be established — neither in Gaza nor in Judea and Samaria. Period,” Netanyahu said last month, using the biblical name for the West Bank.

Iran, which the United States and Israel attacked in February, backs Hamas in Gaza. The Palestinian Authority, centred in the West Bank, is led by Fatah, Hamas’s archrival.

Ahead of the anniversary, Israel ordered the closure of the UK consulate serving Palestinians from Jerusalem, angered after Britain led France and Canada in sanctions over rising attacks by settlers.

Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, explaining the move, said Britain’s Labour government was attempting to “force upon Israel” a Palestinian state but the attempt was “doomed to fail”.

– Rising attacks –

The Palestinian Authority, established in the 1990s, has been starved of cash in part by Israel’s decision not to give it customs revenue it collects on its behalf, and struggles to pay its civil servants.

Israel has objected to the Palestinian Authority’s historic payments to families of imprisoned or slain Palestinians, including those who carried out attacks against Israelis.

In early 2025, Israel built nearly 1,000 gates in the West Bank, at the entrances of nearly all villages and towns, which it closes on occasion to control Palestinian movement.

Palestinians have also decried a policy of “maximum land, minimum Arabs” whereby settlers push out isolated herder communities from rural areas in order to establish settler outposts.

The UN says extremist settlers have been responsible for an average of six attacks per day on Palestinians and Palestinian property in the West Bank in 2026.

Palestinians complain that Israeli perpetrators of violence are almost never brought to justice, and are protected by the army.

Defence Minister Israel Katz has called for police to take over civilian matters from the military in the West Bank, a move observers see as a further step towards annexation.

Sameh, a software engineer in Nablus, still sees last year’s move as a positive sign, but concedes the difficulties.

“There is still a big distance between international recognition and seeing that recognition translated into reality on the ground,” he said.

World.title: SC questions alcohol prohibition law, points to 5 'evils'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Questioning the efficacy of prohibition,

Friday pointed to five "evils" associated with the ban on liquor - revenue loss, money spent on its enforcement, corruption in police, illegal distilling, and result-ant drug menace - while also referring to a number of hooch tragedies in Gujarat and other states over the years.

A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said this while quashing Rules 18A and 18B of Maharashtra Poisons Rules restricting purchase of methanol and making it mandatory to add bitterant and colourant to it before selling to non-drug manufacturers. The rules were framed following the deaths of 93 people from spurious liquor containing methanol in Mumbai in 1991.

While allowing the plea of various chemical manufacturing companies, including Indian Chemical Council, the bench dwelled upon the efficacy of the prohibition policy.

The court said recent hooch tragedies in Bhavnagar (Gujarat) and Sagar (MP), which claimed 13 and 15 lives respectively, were a reminder for the authorities to wake up and act.

"History bears eloquent testimony to the fact that complete alcohol ban often drives the liquor trade underground, increasing the prevalence of unregulated, lethal brews. The state of Gujarat has a strict prohibition policy... It has witnessed at least 10 major mass hooch tragedies since the state's formation and independence, claiming the lives of over 600 people," the bench said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





SC rejected Maharashtra govt's plea and said the rules had no rational nexus with the objective sought to be achieved to prevent hooch tragedies. The court said it was not doubting the intention of the state but intention solely would not pass the test of manifest arbitrariness.

"The state failed to indicate that this practice of putting such additives would discourage or rather dissuade continuous usage of methanol or affect its chemical composition so it cannot be used in making spurious liquor. Further, the state has also failed to indicate how mixing of the additives would definitively prevent deaths. Another question that is left unanswered is how the respondent plans to prevent manufacturing of spurious liquor by the use of other adulterants," the bench said.

NEW DELHI: Amid the charge from the opposition that Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill targets institutions run by minorities, especially Christians, Union home ministry asserted Friday that the amendments do not regulate charity but the entry of foreign money into a "sovereign space", which Centre is fully entitled to protect, and emphasised the law at its core is a "national-security" legislation.A team of MHA officials led by home secretary Govind Mohan briefed the joint committee of Parliament - which is scrutinising the bill and held its first meeting - on different facets as it faced questions from MPs, with Mohan insisting the bill is not against any community, sources aware of the details said.He said concerns over national interest, internal security and law and order are the main drivers of the bill. It was introduced by govt in Parliament's budget session and sent to the committee for scrutiny amid stiff protests from opposition parties and Christian groups, who had met home minister Amit Shah to convey their concerns.After the meeting, the panel's chairperson, Sanjay Jaiswal, expressed confidence that it would be able to submit its report in the winter session of Parliament.MPs from BJP-led NDA and opposition parties presented conflicting views.BJP's Nishikant Dubey suggested India had a history of foreign money being used to influence issues of national interest and asked why Ford Foundation was allotted prime property in Lodhi Estate when over 1,400 NGOs linked to foreign funding were closed down under different laws before FCRA was enacted in 1976.Rockefeller Foundation was a key financial support behind an elite cultural and intellectual organisation in central Delhi, he said.Sources said DMK's P Wilson reiterated the charge that the amendments target Christian groups, which make up the majority of religious organisations with an FCRA licence, and was supported by other opposition MPs. Some alleged that these organisations were being targeted as they had empowered Dalits and women in south India.Opposition MPs slammed the proposed amendments as draconian, saying even if an organisation surrendered its FCRA licence, it still allowed assets to be seized.Jaiswal, sources said, flagged protests against the Kudankulam nuclear plant in TN and Sardar Sarovar Dam in Gujarat. BJP circles have argued that foreign-funded NGOs tried to disrupt the two critical projects of national interest under the veneer of environmental concerns.According to data shared by MHA, TN has the highest number of organisations with FCRA registration (2,102), followed by Maharashtra (1,578), Karnataka (1,355) and Delhi (1,218). Foreign contribution increased to Rs 22,974 crore in 2024-25 from Rs 17,832 crore in 2015-16.Out of the total foreign contribution received in 2024-25, 57% (Rs 13,071 crore) was for social purposes, 30% (Rs 6,933 crore) for educational, and only 8% (Rs 11,841 crore) for religious. Under the head of religious purpose, 73% went to Christian groups followed by 17.8% for Hindu organisations, with a little over 1% to Muslims. US and UK at Rs 12,113 crore and Rs 2,414 crore respectively were the two highest contributors.

World.title: 25% youths in 250 districts not in education or jobs: Survey
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In nearly 250 districts, more than 25% youth (15-29 age group) are neither engaged in any productive work, nor are they pursuing education or any sort of training for work, highlighting a gap in human capital utilisation.

The situation is of particular concern in northern India, especially in states such as Bihar, UP, Haryana, Punjab and West Bengal, where nearly two-thirds of districts have around a quarter of the young population categorised as NEET (not in employment, education or training), showed the first-ever district-level periodic labour force survey (PLFS) for 2025, released by statistics ministry Friday.

In Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Assam and Telangana in nearly half the districts, 25% young population is categorised as NEET (not in employment, education or training).

A recent Niti Aayog report pegged the number of NEET youth in the country at nearly nine crore, with govt clarifying that these people cannot be crudely termed as unemployed.

In around 25 districts, NEET is below 10%, including Kabirdham, Rajnandgaon and Uttar Baster Kanker in Chhattisgarh; Chamba in Himachal Pradesh; Ernakulam in Kerala; and Mandla in Madhya Pradesh. Nabarangpur in Odisha had the lowest NEET rate of 4.1%.

The ministry's report covered around 600 districts in major states and UTs. In some cases, it clubbed a few adjoining districts and treated them as a single unit.

Lowest unemployment rates across India

Generally, high unemployment rate among youth is attributed to their participation in education or their engagement with skilling or vocational programmes. NEET, however, represents those people who are not enrolled anywhere with any educational institution and have also withdrawn from the labour force altogether. This is either due to them attending to domestic unpaid duties, care work in the case of women or those who have stopped looking for work due to no suitable work being available, or in some cases, preparing for exams or having leisure.

For young women, nearly three-fourth of total districts surveyed recorded a NEET rate of more than 25%, highlighting the burden of unpaid domestic chores and societal expectations.

World.title: Presumption of guilt doesn't make prosecution case 'gospel truth': SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a judgment that will impact as many as nine penal laws, Supreme Court has ruled that the stringent provisions of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act providing for presumption of guilt of the accused must not persuade trial courts to believe the prosecution's case to be the "gospel truth".

A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and N V Anjaria gave this ruling while setting aside concurrent judgments of a Delhi court and Delhi HC convicting a man, whom a woman had falsely accused of sexually assaulting her minor daughter in a Kalkaji slum in south Delhi in 2015. It said the accusation was part of a long-standing feud over water the woman had with him.

The bench said both the trial court and HC appeared to have been swayed by the presumption of guilt provision in

and overlooked glaring discrepancies and loopholes in the mother's testimony despite these being highlighted by the accused during cross-examination.

Writing the judgment, Justice Anjaria said presumption of guilt in Pocso Act did not operate to eliminate evidence standing in favour of the accused.

The statutory presumptions cannot be read to mean that the prosecution version is liable to be treated as gospel truth in every case," he said.

The presumptive provision cannot unburden courts from "discharging their essential duty to analyse the evidence on record in light of the features emerging in a particular case", he added.





This ruling will potentially impact provisions of presumption of guilt against the accused, or casting reverse burden on them, in eight other laws - Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, Prevention of Corruption Act, Wild Life (Protection) Act, Essential Commodities Act, Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, Customs Act, Foreign Exchange Management Act, and Negotiable Instruments Act, which were specifically mentioned in the 42-page judgment.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Justices Mishra and Anjaria said, "The court should not mechanically accept the ipse dixit of the prosecution riding on the provisions regarding presumption of guilt to give a stamp of approval to every prosecution even if they are absurd or improbable in its story."

It said the provision, or the rule of reverse burden requiring the accused to prove his innocence, did not change the rule of standard of proof as normally applied in criminal cases.

World.title: Where thinking beats mugging up
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Hands hovered over buzzers as students listened intently to each question, ready to hit the button before their competitors. Every few moments, a buzzer broke the silence and another answer was put to the test.

But points were not won through recall alone, as the questions pushed students to reason, judge, analyse and think beyond the obvious.

The questions came thick and fast. "If a meteor crashes on the Moon and an astronaut is 1,000km away, when will they hear the sound?" A student quickly buzzed in with the answer: they wouldn't - sound cannot travel through the vacuum of space.

Then came a word puzzle: "Which word becomes shorter when you add two letters to it?" Buzzers went off again.

The answer was "short" - add "er" and it becomes "shorter".

That was the scene at the auditorium of DPS RK Puram on Friday as students went head to head in the semi-final and final rounds of the AM/NS India Times Critical Thinking Championship 2026, conceived and conducted by Times Foundation. The Nav Ratna prize distribution ceremony was held soon after, during which chief guest Brajesh Pathak, deputy chief minister of Uttar Pradesh, handed over certificates to the winners.





Pathak, who spoke of the "immense effort" involved in reaching so many schools and students, urged participants to never stop asking questions. "Human beings are not machines meant to follow the same routine. We have the ability to think, understand and show the world a new direction," he said.

The championship has been designed to encourage students to move beyond rote memorisation and develop the ability to question, analyse information and arrive at conclusions independently.

The students who reached Friday's rounds had already made their way through a much larger field. From thousands of participants, 140 were shortlisted for written and oral assessments. The field was then narrowed to 36 students for the buzzer rounds, with nine winners emerging.

The gathering included their parents, DPS teachers and other representatives.

"Critical thinking is very important for the younger generation because students need to learn to ask questions, reason and analyse before reaching conclusions.

We see this initiative not as a one-off event but as a long-term process," said Vikas Yadvendu, head, CSR, AM/NS India.

Impact catalyst Aruna Goenka said, "Critical thinking is the need of the hour. With young people exposed to so much information through social media, they can sometimes lose sight of their own judgement or be misled. So, such initiatives are important."

DPS RK Puram principal Anil Kumar said, "This initiative encourages children to think, reason and analyse.

Over 10 lakh students have participated across languages, and next year, we aim to reach one crore."

Over the past six months, TCTC reached more than one million students from over 20,000 schools, spanning Grades III to XII across 28 states and eight Union Territories, with the programme conducted in 14 languages.

But amid those numbers were students from different corners of the country, each with their own interpretation of what it meant to think critically.

Bhanvi, a Class V student from Kerala, summed it up simply: "Critical thinking is not agreeing with something just because everyone thinks it is right. Don't always listen to others. Use your own mind." Aaryahi Hazarika, a Class IV student from Assam, said it helped people find solutions carefully, while Sarah from Kashmir described it as the ability to "think out of the box". Divisha, a Class IV student of DPS East of Kailash, described it as "finding solutions by thinking with our own minds" rather than blindly following others.

British citizen Jagtar Singh Johal, who was granted bail

NEW DELHI/LONDON/BATHINDA: Delhi HC on Friday granted bail to British citizen Jagtar Singh Johal, who is charged with targeted killings and conspiracy linked to Khalistan Liberation Force (KLF), taking note of his âlong period of incarcerationâ and acquittal in one of the cases. News of his bail sparked celebrations at his home in Dumbarton, Scotland, and among UK-based activists who have been campaigning for his release.His brother Gurpreet Singh Johal, a solicitor in Dumbarton, where Johalâs wife Gurpreet Kaur Johal also lives, said, âThe past two years have been an expensive rollercoaster, contesting bails at Supreme Court and back to the high court in India. Now, all I can think about is Jagtar walking out of prison. We have waited so long and fought so hard for this moment. Whenever evidence against Jagtar is tested in court, judges find what weâve said all along, which is that there isnât any. âJohalâs MP Douglas McAllister, who has been campaigning for his release, described the news as âamazingâ. âNow itâs time to bring him home.âScotland-born Johal, arrested shortly after his 2017 wedding, was named as an accused in eight cases of attempted murder in Punjab and booked by NIA under UAPA.He was acquitted in one of the cases last year.HC heard Johalâs bail appeals in the remaining seven case together Friday and said, âWe find the appellant has remained in custody for more than eight yearsâ¦ Only 40 witnesses have so far been examined and we are informed there are another 123 witnesses whose testimony is yet to be recorded... Trial is certainly not likely to conclude any time soon.âOn NIAâs claim Johal was a flight risk as a foreign national, HC ordered Johal to surrender his passport and barred him from joining any WhatsApp group or other social media platform where anti-national material was uploaded or circulated or propagated.It rejected NIAâs claim certain witnesses alleged they were threatened and that, if released, Johal might influence the trial.NIAâs cases against Johal arise from a series of allegedly targeted murders and attempted murders in Ludhiana and Jalandhar in 2016-2017. Two cases pertain to the killing of Amit Sharma, president of Shri Hindu Takhat in Ludhiana in Jan 2017, and the attempted murder of Jagdish Kumar Gagneja, RSS vice-president in Punjab, in Jalandhar in Aug 2016.The probe was transferred from Punjab Police to NIA after the offences were identified to be a part of a âtransnational conspiracyâ. NIA accused Johal of being an âactive memberâ of the âterrorist gangâ KLF.Gurpreet Singh Johal told BBC News, âWe are still waiting for the order and a report. We expect he wonât be allowed to leave India without permission... But at last we see some light at the end of the tunnel that he will be at least at liberty.âNoting Johal was acquitted of all charges in one case, he said, âJagtar is innocent and is arbitrarily detained. There is a lot more that has to be done from UK govt. They have not done enough.âDan Dolan, deputy executive director of Reprieve, a UK legal rights organisation campaigning for Johalâs release, said, âWhile this judgment is welcome as Jagtar should not be in prison a day longer, we must now watch closely to ensure this order is actually implemented and not obstructed in any way.âChris Esdaile, senior legal adviser at REDRESS, a London NGO that pursues legal claims on behalf of survivors of torture around the world that also campaigned for Johal, said, âThis is a welcome development but it canât undo the intolerable suffering caused by nine years of arbitrary detention without a fair and timely resolution.â

World.title: Bombay High Court permits BMC to cut over 1,200 mangroves for Versova-Madh Island bridge
World.content:
The Bombay High Court has permitted the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) to cut 1,237 mangroves to build a bridge that connects Versova and Madh Island in the western suburbs of Mumbai.

The bridge is expected to reduce the distance of travel between Versova and Madh Island from 22 km to 1.5 km.

The court on September 17, 2026, set conditions including the plantation of 39,000 mangroves over 9 hectares, monitoring for 10 years, deposit of ₹1.42 crore, and an undertaking. The order came from a Bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna.

The Bench held that the project is for infrastructure and for residents, stating that is not for a particular company.

The Bench also held that the project improves connectivity between Madh Island and suburbs in Mumbai, giving relief from delays due to congestion on roads in the capital city. It added that the distance between Versova and Madh Island will reduce from 22 km to 1.5 km after completion of the project.

The BMC filed a plea as the proponent of the project., stating that it had obtained clearance for the bridge over Malad creek. The BMC had first sought permission to cut 560 mangroves and later raised the count to 1,237 following a re-assessment.

In its order, the Bench recorded that the BMC will plant 39,000 mangroves over 9 hectares of land with forest of mangroves. It said the BMC will plant these at the site and at places in the area. Further, the BMC will monitor the plantation for 10 years.

The Bench said the BMC will deposit ₹1.42 crore, accepting the undertaking. It said the corporation will face consequences in law if it breaches the said undertaking.

Permitting the construction of the bridge, the Bench said the court's intervention on mangroves with safeguards and measures for restoration would serve the interest of residents. It added that the petition was entertained on the basis of the commitments and the undertaking from the BMC.

World.title: U.S. appeals court rejects Trump policy allowing swift deportations to third countries
World.content:
A U.S. federal appeals court rejected on ​Friday (September 18, 2026) a policy adopted by President Donald Trump’s administration that allows authorities to ⁠rapidly deport migrants to countries other than their own without giving them a chance to raise safety concerns.

Ruling in a case that is likely headed to the Supreme Court, a three-judge panel of the Boston-based 1st ‌U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals largely upheld a February decision by a lower-court judge that declared the Department of Homeland Security’s policy unlawful.

The ruling came in a class-action ‌lawsuit filed by migrants subject to deportation orders that has become a key test ‌of ⁠what due process protections the government must provide before removing people to countries with which ⁠they have no connection.

“This decision confirms that due process and the protections Congress enacted against persecution and torture cannot be circumvented by putting someone on a plane to a country that was never part of their removal proceedings,” Trina ​Realmuto, a lawyer for the plaintiffs at ‌the National Immigration Litigation Alliance, said

Under Mr. Trump, the administration has entered into a series of agreements that have allowed it to send more than 25,000 migrants to at least 29 third countries, in many cases Mexico, according to Third Country Deportation Watch, a project run by Refugees ‌International and Human Rights First.

The Trump administration is expected to appeal. Earlier in the ​same case, the administration twice convinced the Supreme Court to lift a preliminary injunction protecting migrants’ due process rights, clearing the way for eight men to be deported to ⁠South Sudan.

DHS had no immediate comment.

Trump’s third country deportations pose risk of abuse and incarceration

Under the third-country deportation program, DHS adopted a policy in March 2025 that would allow migrants to be sent to such countries if immigration authorities have credible diplomatic assurances they ‌will not be persecuted or tortured there.

The policy called for only minimal notice before a migrant could be sent to a third country that had not given the State Department such assurances.

Third country deportations

U.S. District Judge Brian Murphy, an appointee of Democratic President Joe Biden, set aside the policy and concluded that it failed to protect migrants’ due process rights and could lead to their swift deportation to unfamiliar and potentially dangerous countries, without notice.

On appeal, the Trump administration contended that ‌Judge Murphy’s order if left intact would usurp its authority to execute potentially thousands of valid orders of deportation to third countries.

But ​U.S. Circuit Judge Seth Aframe, writing for Friday’s panel, said Judge Murphy adopted a “sensible” interpretation of the immigration law requiring migrants be given a “meaningful” chance to raise any ⁠concerns before they are deported.

“DHS’s proposed interpretation would deny access to that protection to a substantial swath ⁠of noncitizens who are sent to third countries with no notice of their destination,” Judge Aframe wrote. “We decline to adopt such an interpretation.”

The panel included two Biden appointees, including ‌Judge Aframe, and a judge appointed by a Republican president.

However, the 1st Circuit overturned one part of Judge Murphy’s ruling on procedural grounds. That part of the ruling concerned whether the government must ​first try to deport migrants to countries they have ties to before sending them to third countries.

World.title: Trump to meet with Venezuela's interim President Rodriguez in New York on Sept. 22
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump will have a meeting with ‌Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez in New York ​on Tuesday (September 22, 2026), a senior U.S. official said, in what will be the first in-person meeting between the two leaders since Washington ousted ‌former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January.

Mr. Trump’s meeting with Ms. Rodriguez, Mr. Maduro’s former deputy, will be ‌on the sidelines of a reception ‌that ⁠the Republican President will be hosting, U.S. ⁠ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz told reporters in a briefing call on Friday (September 18, 2026).

“The president will host a UN General Assembly leaders’ reception. ​There, he’ll participate ‌in a pull-aside with the acting president Rodriguez of Venezuela,” Mr. Waltz said. He did not give any details of what they might discuss.

The ‌Venezuelan Communications Ministry, which handles all press queries ​for the government, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Last month, ⁠the U.S. and Venezuela signed an energy agreement that would allow the U.S. to take partial ‌control of Venezuela’s vast oil reserves, betting that American companies can help revive the South American nation’s battered energy industry.

Venezuelan Opposition leader Maria Corina Machado is facing a growing dilemma over when to return home to rally support amid reticence ‌from the Trump administration about her homecoming.

Ms. Machado left the ​country late last year to receive the Nobel Peace Prize, after largely living in ⁠hiding since a contested 2024 election. She sought to ⁠cultivate Mr. Trump as an ally well before Mr. Maduro’s removal. But since the ouster, Mr. Trump ‌has repeatedly expressed support for Ms.Rodriguez.

World.title: U.S. troop deaths during Iran war exceed Pentagon count by at least four: report
World.content:
More U.S. troops have died ​during the U.S.-Israeli war ⁠with Iran than the Pentagon has publicly disclosed, the Washington ‌Post reported on Friday (September 18, 2026).

Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth ‌denied the report.

The Post, ‌citing ⁠five unidentified officials, ⁠reported that there had been at least 22 military fatalities, four ​more than were listed ‌in the data available on the Pentagon’s public database.

The newspaper also reported, citing ‌another unidentified official, that not ​all of the undisclosed deaths were directly tied ⁠to the months-long conflict but involved U.S. personnel ‌who were in West Asia amid ongoing hostilities.

Mr. Hegseth, in a post on X, called the report “a complete LIE.”

The Post did not ‌immediately respond to a request ​for comment. In its story, the newspaper said ⁠the Pentagon had declined to address ⁠its questions about the discrepancy in casualty accounting.

World.title: Waste of public money amid economic crisis: U.P. Congress on PM’s birthday celebrations
World.content:
Uttar Pradesh Congress unit chief Ajay Rai on Friday (September 18, 2026) accused the BJP-led State government of wasting public money on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday at a time when a portion of the country is facing floods and economic crisis persists across the country.

“The entire country saw how birthday of Prime Minister Narendra Modi was celebrated with pomp and ceremony. Lamps were lit across the country and government funds were wasted. This has been done at a time when hundreds of villages in U.P. And other states have been cut off due to the devastation caused by severe floods, there is destruction across the country, people are not getting food or water, they are not getting medicines, and Modi ji is celebrating his birthday,” said Mr. Rai, addressing the media in Lucknow.

Mr. Rai alleged that 500 bikes were given in Varanasi with a deal that the people who ride them will have to pay ₹700 per day

The Congress state chief said: “Crores of lamps were lit across the country, and at least Rs. five would be spent on lighting one lamp. Several videos are going viral in which it can be seen that children are collecting oil, the leftover oil from the lamps that were lit is being collected by children. A little girl in a viral video can be seen collecting oil and saying that she will use it to cook dinner.”

He said the Prime Minister should be ashamed that there is no oil in these children’s homes to cook food. “And you are spending crores of rupees on your birthday. Poor people do not have money, they do not have money for medicines, in fact you should light lamps in their homes,” he said.

Further, Mr. Rai accused the BJP of being responsible for collapse of the economy, stating that neither employment nor jobs are being provided in the country by the government. “The government says that GDP has increased. But, the reality is there is neither employment nor jobs in the country and Uttar Pradesh,” he added.

World.title: Trump signs Russia sanctions bill into law
World.content:
U.S. ​President ⁠Donald Trump on ‌Friday (September 18, 2026) ‌signed ‌the ⁠Russia ⁠sanctions ​bill ‌into law, the White ‌House ​said ⁠in a ‌statement. The Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act seeks to impose steep levies on Moscow and its top energy buyers, including India and China.

“On Friday, September 18, 2026, the President signed into law: H.R. 5334, the “Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026,” which authorizes and expands statutory sanctions, tariffs, and prohibitions on Russia and extends existing sanctions on Iran,” the White House said.

The House of Representatives on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) passed the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which seeks to impose sanctions on Russia’s leadership and energy sector — as well as on collaborators in Moscow’s defence industry and its so-called shadow fleet.

The Act also authorises President Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries buying Russian oil and gas, including China and India.

The law gives Mr. Trump wide discretion over implementation, including which countries face tariffs, the tariff rates imposed, and whether sanctions provisions are waived.

The law comes into effect within 30 days of signing by the President and requires him to impose duties of up to 100% on goods imported from countries that are the top five purchasers of Russian crude oil or natural gas by total volume during the 12 months preceding enactment.

A country is exempt from the gas-related duties if its Russian gas imports accounted for less than 15% of Russia’s total exports during the applicable period and it has taken “significant steps” to reduce those imports.

The legislation targets Russia’s “shadow fleet” and other foreign persons involved in supporting Russian energy production or sanctions evasion, including vessel owners, operators, managers, insurers, and other parties engaged in covered activities.

Zelenskyy thanks Trump, members of U.S. Congress

Ukrainian President ​Volodymyr Zelenskyy early ‌Saturday ​(September 19, 2026) thanked Mr. Trump for signing ‌the Russia sanctions ‌bill ‌and ⁠members of ⁠Congress for supporting it and ensuring ​its ‌passage.

“The best way to honour Lindsey’s ‌memory would ​be to implement the provisions ⁠of this law ‌fully and as quickly as possible,” Mr. Zelenskyy said, referring ‌to the ​lawmaker who championed the bill, ⁠the late Senator ⁠Lindsey Graham.

With PTI, Reuters inputs

World.title: U.S. and Denmark reach deal on Greenland: Trump
World.content:
The United States, Denmark and Greenland have entered into an agreement ⁠for the U.S. to develop a significant military presence on Greenland, while prohibiting U.S. adversaries from building their own bases on the island, Donald Trump said on Friday on Friday (September 18, 2026). This comes after months of threatening to take island by force from the NATO ally.

In a Truth Social post, the U.S. President ‌wrote that no U.S. enemies would be able to make sensitive investments on the island without the approval of the United States and that the agreement had ‌no expiry date.

“At my direction, we worked with representatives of Denmark and Greenland to ‌guarantee ⁠that the United States will FOREVER have the complete ability to do what ⁠is necessary in Greenland in order to secure and defend the security of Greenland, and the United States of America,” Mr. Trump wrote.

The announcement suggests he was pleased with the outcome of the negotiations, and that he may not revive his territorial claims, at least ‌in the near future. He said, without elaborating, that the U.S. would soon be ​rolling out a large military presence on the island, which already hosts one Space Force base in its remote northwest.

“This is a dream come true ⁠for the United States of America,” Mr. Trump wrote.

Deal to be signed next week, still needs parliamentary action: Denmark

The office of Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said the Greenland deal with the U.S. will be signed by three governments next week during the United Nations General Assembly. However parliamentary action is still needed by the Danish and Greenland governments before it can be enforced.

Mr. Frederiksen said in a statement that “the agreement recognizes the sovereignty and territorial integrity” of Greenland and Denmark and upholds both people’s right “to self-determination.” The PM’s office said that the agreement would strengthen North Atlantic and Arctic security.

Rubio says deal addresses security concerns

In a separate statement, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that the deal “permanently and completely” ​addressed Washington’s national security concerns with respect to the island. “Greenland will forever be part of the strategic defense area of North America and exclude any adversary from ⁠it and the surrounding area,” he wrote.

A State Department official, speaking on condition of anonymity to discuss ⁠specific terms, said the deal prohibits non-NATO countries from building a base in Greenland, and will allow only the U.S. and its allies to make unspecified “sensitive investments.”

Much was ‌unclear as of Friday night (September 18, 2026), including whether any new U.S. bases would be constructed as a result of the agreement. Trump’s Truth Social posts about negotiations or agreements often lack context or specifics.

The U.S. already has nearly total overflight and basing rights in Greenland due to a 1951 treaty.

It was also unclear how the agreement would be received in Greenland, an autonomous territory of Denmark. The island’s residents aspire to independence and have bristled at US attempts ‌to assert hegemony.

The ‌official said the agreement grants the U.S. permanent access, basing and overflight rights, and would continue to apply even if Greenland becomes independent.

World.title: 21 killed in car bomb blast in northwestern Pakistan
World.content:
At least 21 people, mostly policemen, were killed and 78 others injured in a suicide blast at a mosque during Friday prayers near the police lines in Kohat district of Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, police said.

The blast occurred at the mosque located near the old Police Lines in Kohat, around 60 kilometres southwest of the provincial capital Peshawar, they said.

According to police, an attacker rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into the mosque premises, following which an exchange of fire with armed militants took place.

District Health Officer Kohat Dr Nasir Hussain said 21 people, including 16 police personnel and five civilians, were killed and 78 others injured in the explosion.

A little-known militant group, Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, claimed responsibility for the attack. The group, an alliance comprising the Hafiz Gul Bahadur Group, Harakat Inqilab-e-Islami Pakistan and Lashkar-e-Islam, was formed in April 2025.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hamid said that an explosives-laden vehicle rammed into the gate of the old police lines, triggering an explosion followed by gunfire.

“The vehicle hit the gate and then exploded, and firing also took place,” Hameed said, adding that another blast occurred at the Special Branch building during the exchange of fire with terrorists.

The blast occurred during Friday prayers, leaving a crater outside the mosque and severely damaging its exterior, while a wall also collapsed.

Most of those wounded were worshippers. Video footage from the site showed the bodies of worshippers lying inside the mosque.

According to the Central Police Office in Peshawar, seven armed militants entered the police lines, where police and the Counter-Terrorism Department engaged them in a gun battle.

Six militants have so far been killed, including bombers and snipers, the official said.

Security officials said security forces and police had cordoned off the area.

The injured, including police personnel, were shifted to the District Headquarters Hospital, where an emergency was declared, hospital Medical Superintendent Tahir Ali Shah said.

According to Rescue 1122 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa spokesperson Bilal Ahmad Faizi, rescue teams reached the site shortly after receiving the information and launched a rescue operation.

Police said the Kohat-Hangu Road had been closed to all traffic and additional police contingents had been deployed near the police lines.

Rescue officials said nearby buildings were also damaged in the blast.

Following the blast, provincial police chief Hameed sought a report from the district’s regional police officer. He directed authorities to ensure timely and best possible medical treatment for the injured.

“Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police stands as an iron wall against terrorism, and such cowardly attacks cannot weaken our resolve,” he said.

President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif have condemned the incident and vowed that the complete elimination of foreign-sponsored terrorists was “essential for national security”.

Mr. Sharif also sought a report on the blast from the concerned authorities. He also directed authorities to expedite relief operations, state-run Radio Pakistan reported.

KPK Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also condemned the blast, saying the “entire nation stands with the security forces to eradicate terrorism.” Provincial Chief Minister Sohail Afridi also sought a report from the police chief into the blast.

Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terror activities, particularly in its Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan provinces in the past few years.

World.title: 15 cops among 21 martyred in blast at Kohat Police Lines, more than 80 injured
World.content:
PESHAWAR: At least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred on Friday when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines, followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities, according to senior police and district health officials.

District Health Officer Dr Nasir Hassan Afridi confirmed the toll to Dawn, adding that more than 100 people were injured, with three in critical condition.

According to officials, SP Traffic Akbar Shinwari and Dr Israel Orakzai, head of the children’s department at DHQ KDA Kohat, were among those martyred in the attack.

Police said at least one attacker was holed up inside the compound and a clearance operation was underway.

In a separate statement, the CTD said the Additional IG CTD reached the site of the Kohat attack.

An exchange of fire between CTD personnel and the terrorist was ongoing, the department said, adding that the AIG had entered the police lines to take part in the operation and lead the personnel.

Later in the evening, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed visited the police lines as the clearance operation continued. According to a statement, the IGP met GOC Kohat, the regional police officer, the district police officer Kohat and other officers and personnel present at the site.

The attack

According to IG Hameed and police statements, the attack began when a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED) detonated at the boundary wall near the mosque inside the Kohat Police Lines.

At least seven attackers then breached the compound and headed towards the CTD and Special Branch buildings. Six attackers, including a suicide bomber, were killed by law enforcers, according to a police statement.

At least one attacker was subsequently cornered, prompting police personnel to launch a clearance operation. At around 3:30pm, police said the operation was “in its final stages”.

“The operation will continue until the complete elimination of Fitna-ul-Khawarij,” the IG was quoted as saying, adding that the police’s morale remained high.

Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

Earlier, television footage from the scene showed citizens gathered beside a building with a collapsed wall, digging through the rubble and helping the injured. The blast caused extensive damage to the mosque.

The attack was claimed by the Hafiz Gul Bahadur-led Ittehadul Mujahideen.

Separately, KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi sought a detailed report on the incident, saying the targeting of innocent citizens was “deeply regrettable and unacceptable,” as per a statement issued by his office.

Residents gather on a street leading to a police facility, where ambulances are parked following a suicide attack in Kohat on September 18. — Reuters

He directed authorities to ensure immediate treatment for the injured. “The nation’s morale cannot be dampened by cowardly acts of terrorism,” he was quoted as saying.

The funeral prayers for 15 police personnel martyred in the Police Lines blast were offered in Kohat later in the evening, after which their bodies were transported to their native districts of Kohat, Karak, Lakki Marwat, Bannu and Mardan in Rescue 1122 ambulances.

In 2010, 20 people, mostly the relatives of policemen, were killed and more than 90 injured in a remote-controlled bomb blast inside a police colony located just behind the Kohat Police Lines.

Condemnations pour in

President Asif Ali Zardari, condemning the incident, vowed that the complete elimination of foreign-sponsored terrorists was “essential for national security”.

President Zardari wished the injured a swift recovery.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif sought a report on the blast from the concerned authorities. He also directed authorities to expedite relief operations, Radio Pakistan reported.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also condemned the blast, praying for the recovery of the injured.

“The entire nation stands with the security forces to eradicate terrorism,” he said in a statement.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said in his condemnation that terrorists’ “cowardly acts cannot weaken the nation’s resolve”.

A statement posted on his ministry’s X account said Naqvi expressed grief over the loss of lives in the attack and extended condolence to the bereaved.

“The nation is standing with the families of the martyrs in this moment of grief,” he was quoted as saying.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi also strongly condemned the suicide attack in Kohat and expressed his condolences over the deaths of police personnel and civilians.

In a video message, he said the people of KP had sacrificed more than 80,000 lives for Pakistan and continued to bear the brunt of the fight against terrorism.

“Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is Pakistan’s frontline province in the war against terrorism,” he said, adding that peace in Islamabad and the rest of the country was due to the sacrifices made by the people of the province.

He also criticised those who, he said, labelled the people of KP as terrorists, saying such remarks reopened their wounds and disrespected their martyrs.

Referring to comments by the chief minister of another province, Afridi said it was regrettable to suggest that the threat to Pakistan came from its other provinces rather than India. He said KP and the other provinces were patriotic and had made sacrifices for the country.

“Pakistan is our country, and we will not allow any conspiracy to succeed,” he said, adding that efforts to create division, prejudice and hatred among the people would be thwarted.

United Kingdom’s High Commissioner in Pakistan said she was “appalled by the horrific attack” in Kohat.

“Nobody should face violence in a place of worship“,” she said, adding that her thoughts were with those injured and those who lost loved ones in the attack.

China’s embassy in Pakistan said it was “deeply saddened” by the terrorist attack. It condemned the attack and added that it extends “deepest condolences to the deceased victims and sincere sympathies to the breaved families”.

Russia’s embassy in Pakistan also strongly condemned the attack.

“This terrible tragedy, which claimed numerous lives, once again underscores the need for concerted efforts to combat terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. We hope that those responsible for this heinous act will be identified and brought to justice.”

The mission added that their hearts go out to the families and friends of the victims. “We wish a speedy recovery to all those injured.”

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs1.65 per litre, HSD by Rs0.88 per litre
World.content:
The government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Rs1.65 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs0.88 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs389.14 per litre while HSD will cost Rs424.04 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable from Sept 19 (Saturday) to Sept 21 (Monday).

According to Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA), the increase is primarily linked to higher petrol and diesel prices in the international market.

The regulator said the prices were revised based on international market rates, premiums and other relevant factors.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

The government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices, including requiring markets to close by 9pm and cutting fuel allocations for official vehicles by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

A statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said owners of two- and three-wheelers would receive relief of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles up to 800cc would receive the same relief on a monthly quota of 30 litres.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Govt to stop anyone marching on Islamabad 'in every possible way', says Naqvi
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said on Friday that the government would stop anyone from marching towards the federal capital “in every possible way” and file contempt of court proceedings against those who violated a recent Islamabad High Court (IHC) decision.

He was addressing a press conference in Islamabad alongside other officials.

The interior minister’s remarks came in the wake of PTI’s call for a nationwide protest , including in Islamabad, on September 27 to demand the release of party founder Imran Khan and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

Last week, the administrations of the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad started preparations to counter the PTI’s announced countrywide protest, including a request for detention of activists, arranging containers, seeking additional personnel and procuring anti-riot gear.

At the outset of his press conference on Friday, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said a detailed meeting had been held to discuss the upcoming protest call and the law and order situation. Officials from all provinces and federal law enforcement agencies had also attended the meeting.

“In light of the detailed IHC judgment, there is no possibility of ravaging the federal capital or any other province,” he said.

The minister said that if anyone took to the streets, the government would first pursue legal action by filing a contempt petition against them for violating the IHC order.

At the same time, he said, “We will stop the marchers in every possible way.” All law enforcement agencies had been informed of the decision “with all clarity”, Naqvi added.

He said weapons had been used and losses suffered in protests in the past.

“This time, we are communicating very clear rules of engagement to our law enforcement agencies. They will not remain silent if a bullet is fired at them,” he said.

He urged the protesting party’s leadership to hold demonstrations in their respective provinces and cities. “Plans for locking down the capital or charging into another province will never be allowed,” he said.

“It is our responsibility to stop this protest to ensure the protection of the lives and property of the capital’s residents,” the interior minister said.

The interior minister drew a distinction between a political protest aimed at pursuing political interests and a violent campaign involving people armed with weapons.

“There is complete clarity. The organisers of this march will be held accountable if even a single life is lost,” he said.

Naqvi said there were still some “sensible” voices within the opposition and hoped they would reconsider their decision. “There is only loss in it, no sort of gain at all,” he added.

He reiterated that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had repeatedly invited the opposition from the floor of parliament to hold talks on all issues. “If you want to resolve matters through violent mobs, we are ready for it,” he said.

The interior minister reaffirmed that the government had finalised its preparations and all law enforcement agencies were ready.

“We will not allow people to spread turbulence as happened in the past,” he said.

In a detailed judgment issued today, the IHC ruled that any activity resulting in infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights amounts to a violation of the Constitution.

It warned that public office holders responsible for such violations would also be deemed to have breached their oath of office.

The court also held that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the fundamental rights of other citizens.

Kohat attack

Commenting on the attack in Kohat, Naqvi said security agencies had been fighting terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

“We have to focus on this, rather than making strategies for mobilising masses, arranging transport and collecting money,” he said.

“After such incidents, it doesn’t suit you to call for long marches and, on the other hand, lift the dead bodies of martyrs,” he added.

He further said the KP chief minister and his cabinet should work towards eradicating terrorism with the same spirit with which they were carrying out campaigns for long marches.

Earlier today, at least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines. More than 80 people were injured, according to the officials.

The incident was followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities, according to senior police and district health officials.

World.title: Trump bans media outlets CNN, MS NOW, Politico from White House
World.content:
President Donald Trump said on Friday he was banning three major news ​outlets – CNN, MS NOW and Politico – from the White ‌House, in his latest move to crack down on the independent press.

He wrote that he was banning the outlets for allegedly “reporting ​FAKE NEWS” in a move that is likely to ​be challenged as conflicting with the US Constitution’s First ⁠Amendment guarantees of free speech and a free press.

“Media ​Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report ​FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America,” he wrote. “Other Fake ​News Media Outlets to follow.”

CNN, MS NOW, Politico and ​the National Press Club did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

He has ‌repeatedly ⁠urged broadcasters to drop comedy or news programs he dislikes or which have joked about or criticised him or his administration. He has also called on the Federal Communications ​Commission to strip ​stations of ⁠licenses after criticizing news and other programming.

Trump’s early legal wins against broadcasters have given way to defeats and retreats as courts and newsrooms act to protect press freedom.

At the end of July, the Justice Department withdrew subpoenas issued to New York Times (NYT) journalists who had written articles about the security of Trump’s presidential aircraft.

The president has also filed defamation suits targeting The New York Times over articles and a book about the origins of his fortune, and the Wall Street Journal over an article about a salacious letter he sent to Jeffrey Epstein.

Last year, he banned the Associated Press from ​the usual pool of reporters that cover his ​movements ⁠because the news agency did not adopt Trump’s preferred name for the Gulf of Mexico, which Trump has instructed executive ⁠branch ​employees to refer to as the ​Gulf of America.

Earlier cases involving ABC and CBS ended in December 2024 and July 2025 with the broadcasters promising to pay $15 million and $16 million, respectively.

Trump sued ABC for defamation over statements about a civil judgment against Trump in a sexual assault case.

He took CBS to court for allegedly misleading viewers by airing different clips of the same answer from an interview with 2024 Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris.

World.title: IHC rules infringement of fundamental rights breaches Constitution ahead of PTI’s Sept 27 protest
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that any activity resulting in infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights amounts to a violation of the Constitution, warning that public office holders responsible for such violations would also be deemed to have breached their oath of office.

The ruling came in a detailed 37-page judgment on a petition concerning the proposed nationwide PTI protest towards Islamabad on September 27, 2026. PTI had announced the march to demand release of party founder Imran Khan and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

A citizen, Waqas Ahmed, had challenged the planned move on the grounds that the protest could disrupt routine life, traffic and business activities in the federal capital.

A three-member bench headed by Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and comprising Justice Muhammad Asif and Justice Muhammad Azam Khan issued the judgment.

The bench had announced its short order on September 14 after hearing Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Awan, Additional Attorney General Amir Rehman, the advocate generals of the four provinces and Islamabad, and counsel for the petitioner, Barrister Akhter Cheena.

The court described the case as requiring an “unusual degree of constitutional balance” between the right of political parties and citizens to assemble peacefully and express dissent, and the rights of other citizens to life, liberty, dignity, free movement, trade, business, property, and access to hospitals, educational institutions, courts and workplaces.

“The question is not whether a political party is entitled to protest. It plainly is, subject always to the Constitution and law,” the judgment observed.

The court held that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the fundamental rights of other citizens.
